this is the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa). Those of middling or inferior capacity, being deluded and ignorant, are unable to awaken to or illuminate [their nature]; they remain submerged in the three realms, wandering through birth and death.
For their sake, the World-Honored One Śākyamuni established teachings throughout the heavens and among humans to provide proof and manifest the path of wisdom. Do you all understand?
A monk asked, "How can one escape birth, old age, sickness, and death? The Master said, "The green mountains have never moved; drifting clouds come and go as they please.
Another asked, "When a king goes forth to battle, what is it like? The Master said, "Outside the Chongming Gate, one does not ask about Chang'an.
[The monk] asked, "How can one have an audience with the Son of Heaven? The Master said, "A blind crane descends into the clear pond; the fish [flee] from beneath its feet."
Guo asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The business of the donkey has not yet departed, and the business of the horse has already arrived.
Guo said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The auspicious vapor stirs constantly at night; the spiritual essence is rarely encountered during the day.

Xuefeng had a verse to send to Shuangfeng, the last line of which read: "When the thunder ceases, its sound does not stop. The Master [Yunmen] offered a different version: "The thunder resounds, yet nothing is heard."
When Shengfeng heard this, he said, "On the peak of Lingyun Mountain, the ancient moon appears. Later, Feng asked, "The ancients said, 'Three before, three after.
What is the meaning of this? The Master replied, "A fish in the water; a bird in the sky. Feng asked, "What is its intent?
The Master replied, "High enough to shoot; deep enough to fish. A monk asked, "In all other quarters, there is a mixture of [the sacred and the profane]."
[The monk] ate. He asked, "I do not know how you, Master, are. The Master said, "Only in Min is there something extraordinary; it stands majestically, guarding the edge of the sea.
[The monk] asked, "Having fought long on the battlefields, why have you not achieved fame and merit? The Master said, "When the Sovereign possesses the Way, the three borders are at peace;
what need is there to laboriously build the Great Wall ten thousand li away? [The monk] asked, "When the weapons of war are laid aside and one surrenders oneself to return to court, what then?"
The Master said: "Compassionate clouds universally moisten boundless lands; when withered trees have no flowers, what can be done? Changsheng asked:

"Before the primordial chaos was divided, from where did sentient beings come? The Master said: "It is like a pillar conceiving a fetus. [Changsheng] asked: "After it was divided, what was it like? The Master said:
"It is like a fragment of cloud touching the vast clarity. [Changsheng] asked: "I do not know whether the vast clarity itself is touched by the cloud or not? The Master [remained silent].

[The monk] did not answer. [The monk] said, "In that case, do sentient beings not come? The Master also did not answer. [The monk] said, "When one has reached the state of utter purity, free from even a single speck, what then?
The Master said, "This is still the flow of the eternal and constant. [The monk] asked, "What is the flow of the eternal and constant?
The Master said, "It is like a mirror that is constantly bright. [The monk] asked, "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "There is. [The monk] said, "Such as..."
"What is this matter of going upward? The Master said, "Bring me a broken mirror, and I shall see you. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?
The Master said, "Planting crabapples at the bottom of a well. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "This year’s peach and plum are precious;
each fruit is worth a thousand pieces of gold. A monk asked, "The *maṇi* jewel does not conform to the colors of its surroundings. I wonder, what does it do?"
"What color is it? The Master said, "White. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then it follows the colors of the multitude. The Master said, "The Zhao jade was originally without flaw;
Zhang Yi deceived the Lord of Qin. He asked a monk, "Where are you going? [The monk] said, "I am going to Xuefeng. The Master said, "I have a letter;
may I send it to Xuefeng for you? [The monk] said, "Please do so. The Master took off one of his sandals, tossed it before him, and the monk immediately—
He went to Xuefeng. Xuefeng asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I come from Lingyun. Xuefeng asked, "Is Lingyun well?
He said, "He has a message for me. Xuefeng asked, "Where is it? The monk took off one of his sandals and tossed it before Xuefeng.
Xuefeng then desisted.
Chan Master Shou Shan Shi Jie of Fuzhou once studied under Dongshan. Dongshan asked, "Where is your place of origin, Venerable?
The Master replied, "If you are asking in earnest, Master, I am a native of Min. Dongshan asked, "What is your father’s name?"
The Master said, "Today, having received this question from the Honored One, I have been driven to forget what came before and lose track of what follows.
Later, while presiding over the assembly in the Dharma Hall, he addressed the monks: "Venerable seniors, fortunately there are words of truth with which to exhort you, my brothers.

You should each examine yourselves thoroughly. When all sentiments of ordinary and sage are exhausted, the true and eternal nature is revealed. It requires only that you momentarily cast off all prior delusions and mental attachments."
Free from defilement, the mind is like empty space. At some future time, one will come to recognize a little of what is good and what is bad.
The Military Governor of Min asked Shoushan, "How old are you? The Master said, "I am the same age as empty space. He asked, "How old is empty space?
The Master said, "It is the same age as Shoushan."
A monk asked Master Yaoshan of Ruzhou, "What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, "The mid-winter is bitterly cold.
The monk asked, "What is the master’s deepest place? The Master said, "Wait until your tongue falls to the ground, and then I will tell you.
The monk asked, "What is the sixteen-foot golden body? The Master said, "The judge renders his verdict; the official revises it."
Changqing asked, "Regarding the ancestral vehicle of the predecessors, how is it discussed here?
The Master said, "I have made a vow not to fail the former sages. Changqing said, "How do you not fail the former sages? The Master said, "I do not reveal it.
Changqing said, "If that is so, I ask the Master to lead me through this statement. The Master said, "Where have you come from? Changqing said, "Right there—where have you come from?"
The Master sighed once.
Chan Master Wenju Huiri of Chongfu Monastery in Guohan, Quanzhou, was the son of the Huang family of Fuzhou.
He possessed extraordinary qualities from birth. Upon reaching adulthood, he served as a jailer in the county prison, yet he frequently abandoned his duties to visit Shenguang and An of Xiyuan.
At two locations, the officials were unable to restrain him. Later, he visited Wansui Ta Tan-kong and shaved his head;

however, he did not don the *kāṣāya* robe nor receive full ordination, wearing instead a sash made of various colored silks. He then visited Guanzhi, who said, "I am not your teacher; go and pay your respects at Xiyuan.
The Master carried a small green bamboo staff and entered the Dharma Hall of Xiyuan; from afar, the Head of the Monastery saw him and smiled.
He said, "Enter the Nirvana Hall. The Master responded with an assent and entered, carrying his rattan staff. At that time, there were about five hundred monks suffering from an epidemic.
The Master tapped them one by one with his staff, and each rose as soon as he was tapped. The King of Min honored him deeply and established a monastery for him to reside in.
Thereafter, many miraculous events occurred. He passed away during the Qianning era of the Tang dynasty.
When Xuefeng led his assembly to visit Master Fuhuang of Taizhou, he asked, "There are currently two hundred people staying here for the summer retreat;
is this permissible? The Master took his staff, drew a line, and said, "If you cannot apply it, then speak. Xuefeng then desisted.
A monk asked Master Lushui of Luzhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Do you see the flower garden railing in front of the courtyard? The monk was speechless.

Chan Master Yuanming of Wenshu Monastery in Guangzhou was the son of the Chen family of Fuzhou. Having attained the essential meaning under Daomai, he later traveled to Xuefeng to seek further instruction;

there, he realized that the Dharma has no disparate flavors. He once journeyed to Mount Wutai and beheld a manifestation of Mañjuśrī, whereupon he established a monastery in that location, naming it after the Bodhisattva.
During the Kaibao era, the Imperial Commissioner for Military Affairs Li Chongju went there on patrol and provided protection.
In the south, while entering a monastery, he beheld an image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and asked a monk, "Why does Kṣitigarbha extend his hand?
The monk replied, "The jewel in his hand was stolen by a thief. Li then asked the Master, "Since it is Kṣitigarbha, why would he be robbed by a thief?
The Master said, "He has been caught today. Li bowed in gratitude. He passed away in the Chunhua era at the age of one [hundred].
136. Chan Master Yan’yang Shanxin of Xinxing in Hongzhou, a successor of Chan Master Zhaozhou Congshen.
When he first visited Zhaozhou, Zhaozhou asked him: "Bring nothing at all."
"How is it at such a time? Zhaozhou said, "Put it down. The Master said, "Since you have brought nothing at all, what is there to put down?
Zhaozhou said, "If you cannot put it down, carry it away. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Later, while residing [at his monastery], a monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "A clod of earth. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "The ground is shaking. The monk asked...
"What is the Sangha? The Master said, "Eating porridge, eating rice. "Question: What is the water of Xinxing? The Master said, "The river before you. "Question:
How does one manifest form in response to things? The Master said, "Bring me the bed over here.
The Master often had a snake and a tiger following him; he would give them food from his own hand.

A monk asked Chan Master Huijue of Guangxiao Monastery in Yangzhou: "The flower of awakening has just blossomed, pervading all of Sahā. Since the Patriarchal Seal came from the West, what matter should be discussed?

The Master said: "When sentiment arises, wisdom is obstructed. The monk said: "This is the meaning of the Teachings. The Master said: [This is the meaning of the Teachings.]* *Note: The Master’s second response is recorded as "This is the meaning of the Teachings" (此是教意), which appears to be a repetition of the monk's own statement, likely indicating that the Master was acknowledging the monk's understanding of the doctrinal perspective.*
“What kind of clothing are you wearing? [The Master asked. [The questioner] asked: “What is it like when a single blow shatters empty space?
The Master said: “When weary, then rest. The Master asked the Chancellor Song Qichu:

“Do you understand how to speak? Song said: “If it were ‘speech,’ it could not be applied. The Master said: “Is it that there is something which cannot be applied, or is it that there is nothing which cannot be applied? Song said: “Both.”
"Not so," the Master said. "Is it that one cannot grasp it? Song was speechless. The Master led the assembly out;
seeing a pillar, he joined his palms and said, "How do you do, World-Honored One? A monk said, "The Master is the pillar. The Master said, "Weeping until the blood flows is of no use;
it is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring. While traveling by boat, a monk asked, "From afar, I have come to seek refuge..."
The Master asked, "What is your intention? The Master said, "The authorities are strict; they do not permit me to make arrangements. [The monk] asked, "Is there no expedient means?
The Master said, "For now, you may stay one night in the fire-storage room. When the Master arrived at Chongshou, Fayan asked, "Where have you recently come from?
The Master said, "Zhaozhou. Fayan said, "I have heard that Zhaozhou has the story about the cypress tree in front of the hall. Is this true?"
The Master said, "There was none. Yuanzhen said, "Everyone who comes and goes says so. When a monk asked, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
the Master replied, 'The cypress tree in the courtyard. How can you say there was none? The Master said, "The former master truly did not say such a thing."
"Preceptor, do not slander the former master," [the Master] said. A layman asked, "What can be done about old age? The Master said, "How many years of age are you?
He replied, "Eighty. The Master said, "One may indeed be called old. The man asked, "Ultimately, what of it? The Master said, "Even at a thousand years, it would still not have ended.
A layman asked, "I have killed oxen throughout my life; will there be any karmic retribution for this? The Master said, "No."
[The monk] said, "Why is there no offense? The Master said, "Kill one and receive one in return.
A monk asked Chanshi Feng of Guoqing Monastery in Longzhou, "Are the intent of the Patriarchs and the intent of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said:
The rain nourishes the three types of grass so they flourish; the spring breeze does not wrap the head. [A monk] asked, "Ultimately, are these one or two?
The Master said, "Auspicious clouds rise in competition; the mountain caves remain unimpaired. [Another] asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Stands, tables, chairs, fire-bowls, and windows. [Another] asked, "What is an ordained person? The Master said, "Copper heads and iron jaws."
[He appeared with] the beak of a bird and the body of a deer. [The monk] asked, "What is the fundamental matter of one who has left the household life? The Master said, "Good morning;
take care at night. [Another] asked, "Before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds bring him flowers?"
The Master said, "It is like a person from Shanfu sending money and goods to an iron ox. [The monk] asked, "Having seen it, why does it not bite the flower?
The Master said, "A wooden horse travels eight hundred li at the break of dawn. [The monk] asked, "How does one subdue the mind throughout the twelve periods of the day?
The Master said, "Striking ice to seek fire; one would not encounter it even after kalpas. [The monk] asked, "The twelve divisions of the teachings are for the purpose of cessation..."

Regarding the meaning of "weeping": it is to depart from the act of stopping the weeping. I request a phrase from the Master. The Master said: "A two-horned woman on the summit of a solitary peak asks:
'What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master says: 'Śākyamuni is the Ox-head jailer;
the Patriarch is the horse-faced *āpāṇa*. Question: "What is the meaning of the [Patriarch’s] coming from the West? The Master said: "The east wall strikes the west wall."
Question: "What is the phrase that cannot be broken? The Master said: "Not separated by even a hair's breadth. At that time, people looked up to him from afar.
A monk asked Chan Master Mumen Chonglang of Wuzhou: "When the crane is released from its cage and departs with the snow, what then?"
The Master said, "I say that 'not being of one color' is because the Vajra has fallen over. A monk asked, "Since it is the indestructible body of the Vajra, why did it fall over?
The Master struck the meditation bench and said, "Walking, standing, sitting, and lying down.

As the Master was about to pass into nirvana, he spoke a verse: "For thirty years I have dwelt at Mumen; throughout this time, not a single moment was spent in artificial effort. If there is anyone..."
When asked, "What is the meaning of my coming from the West?
he simply raised his eyebrows. Master Xinjian of Wuzhou did not ordain junior monks. A monk asked him, "Venerable Sir, you are old;
why do you not keep a boy to attend to you? The Master said, "There is one who is blind and deaf; go find such a person for me. When the monk took his leave, the Master questioned him.
"Where are you going? he asked. "I am going to Kaiyuan Temple in the Prefecture," he replied. The Master said, "I have a letter I wish to entrust to the Abbot of that temple.
Can you take it there? "I would be honored to do so," he replied. The Master said, "I imagine you will find yourself at a loss once you get there."
A monk asked Master Duofu of Hangzhou, "What is the single grove of bamboo at Duofu?
The Master said, "One stalk, two stalks, leaning. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Three stalks, four stalks, curved.
The monk asked, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? The Master said, "There are many who harbor doubts about this. The monk asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, [silence].
"Concealing the Head within the Moon.
Master Xi Mu of Yizhou ascended the hall. A layman raised his hand and said, "The Master is nothing but a donkey.
The Master replied, "I am being ridden by you, old monk. The man was speechless. Three days later, he returned and said, "I..."
Three days prior, Jia had been wearing a thief's clothes. The Master picked up his staff and drove him out.
Chan Master Changtong of Xuedou in Mingzhou, a dharma heir of Chan Master Chongshen of Changsha, was a native of the Li clan of Xingzhou. He visited Changsha, who asked: "Where are you from?"
The Master said, "A person from Xingzhou. Deshan said, "I say you did not come from there. The Master asked, "Has the Master ever lived here before?
Deshan assented. Thereupon, he was permitted to enter the room. After [the Master] had resided there, a monk asked, "What is the secret chamber?
The Master said, "It does not allow even the breath of wind to pass through. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the secret chamber? The Master said, "All the sages seek it."
Seeing yet not seeing, the assembly prostrated. The Master said: "A thousand sages cannot conceive it; ten thousand sages cannot deliberate upon it.

Whether heaven and earth perish or do not perish, whether empty space encompasses or does not encompass—everything is beyond compare; throughout the three periods of time, it cannot be raised as a topic. He asked: Question: [What is this?]
"What is the place from which the Buddhas of the three periods emerge? The Master said, "He is unwilling to acknowledge that you exist within the three periods.
After the monk had remained silent for a long while, the Master asked, "Do you realize it? [The monk replied,] "If not, then for now, contemplate that which cannot be grasped as a Buddha;
it is ever-present within the temporal moment. When consciousness is exhausted and effort vanishes, it arises in a flash—this itself is already an injury to it, let alone words and phrases."
In the seventh month of the year Yichou (1085), blessed by Heaven, he manifested his passing. He was seventy-two years of age.
His stupa was erected at the southwest corner of the temple.
As for Master Zhuyou’s Dharma heir, Master Shiti, when an attendant requested that he take a bath, the Master said: "Since one does not wash away dust, nor does one wash the body, you..."
"How is it? he asked. The monk replied, "The Master should go first; I will bring the soap pods. The Master laughed heartily.
A newly arrived monk stood before him for a short while and then departed. The Master said, "What was there to justify his departure?
The monk returned once more. The Master said, "He has justified himself. The monk asked, "After he has justified himself, what then? The Master said, "He can be buried."
[The monk] said, "O Blue Heaven! O Blue Heaven! The Master said, "Just now it was so; even now, it is still not quite right. The monk then went out.
One day, seeing an attendant carrying an alms bowl toward the hall, the Master called to him. The attendant responded, "Yes? The Master asked, "Where are you going?
The attendant said, "I am going to the hall for the midday meal. The Master said, "How could I not know that you were going to the hall for the midday meal?"
The man said, "Aside from this, what else would you say? The Master said, "I am simply asking you about your fundamental matter.
The man said, "If the Master asks about my fundamental matter, I am truly going to the hall for the midday meal.
The Master said, "You do not fail in being my attendant."
A monk asked Master Shengguang of Taizhou, a successor of Chan Master Zihu Zong, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Lychees of Fuzhou;
*stathona* trees of Quanzhou. The monk asked, "What are the two characters for 'Buddha-dharma'? The Master said, "If you wish to speak, then speak."

[Zhao] said, "I request the Master’s Way. The Master said, "The pierced-eared barbarian monk smiles and nods his head; Longhua comes to illuminate [me]. The Master grabbed him and said, "What is this?
Zhao said, "Do not err. The Master then let go of him. Zhao said, "I have long admired the Radiant Light (Shengguang). The Master remained silent. Zhao then took his leave.
As the Master saw him off at the gate, he asked, "Once we part from here, where shall we meet again? Zhao gave a shout.
[The monk] rebuked him and departed.
Master Fushi of Zhangzhou ascended the hall and said: "I, this mountain monk, have opened a divination shop; it can determine people's wealth or poverty and settle their life or death. A monk asked:
"Setting aside life and death, as well as wealth and poverty, and not falling into the five elements—please, Master, speak directly. The Master [replied]: [He laughed and departed.]
It is said: "Gold, wood, water, fire, and earth.
A monk asked Master Zitong, "What is the realm of Zitong? The Master said, "Can you put sand into your own eyes?
The monk said, "I do not even recognize this great and wonderful realm of Zitong. The Master said, "I do not conceal this matter. That monk—
[The monk] was about to leave. The Master descended from his meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Today there is a fine case;
I have not yet received so much as a single coin for it. [The monk] replied, "Fortunately, I am a monk. The Master pushed him away and said, "Calamity does not come alone."
When the monk Huo visited Master Riyong Yuan, the Master clapped his hands three times and said, "A fierce tiger stands in the gateway;
who is there to oppose it? Huo replied, "A swift hawk soars toward the heavens; who can catch it? The Master said, "Both are difficult to withstand."
Huo said, "Stop for now; there is no need to resolve this public case. The Master brandished his staff and returned to the abbot's quarters.
Huo was speechless. The Master said, "This fellow is dead!"
The monk Guannan Daowu was a successor of Chan Master Chang of Guannan.
While passing through a village and countryside, he heard a shamanist musician playing for a deity who proclaimed, "Consciousness has no self.
Upon hearing this, Daowu suddenly attained enlightenment. Later, he went to visit the aforementioned Guannan, who certified his understanding. He subsequently traveled to the gate of Deshan.
The flavor of the Dharma became even more profound. After he took up residence, whenever he ascended the hall, he would wear a lotus-shaped hat, don a cassock, and hold a ritual tablet.

Accompanied by the beating of drums and the blowing of flutes, he would call out, "Master Lu Sanlang! The spirit knows it, the non-spirit does not know it; the spirit comes from within emptiness and returns to within emptiness.
Having said this, he would immediately descend from his seat. At other times, he would say: "The drum of Guannan is struck; the song of Deshan is sung! [Monk: [Question] [Master: [Response]
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master made a gesture with his fan and said, "Yes.
At another time, he held a wooden sword across his shoulder and performed a dance. A monk asked, "Where did you get the sword in your hand? The Master threw it to the ground.
The monk then picked it up and placed it back in the Master's hand. The Master asked, "Where did you get it? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "I grant you three days."
[The Master] turned inward and selected a turning phrase from below; the monk likewise had no response.
The Master himself stepped in on his behalf, holding a sword across his shoulder and performing a dance, saying: "Only by doing thus can one succeed.

When Zhaozhou visited the Master, the Master was wearing a leopard-skin loincloth and holding a *jiaoluo* staff, waiting at the main gate with one foot raised. As soon as he saw Zhaozhou, he shouted a loud greeting.

The Master stood up. The Governor said, "Be careful and attend to yourself. The Master responded with a single "Amen" and departed. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master descended from his meditation seat, performed a woman’s bow, and said, "Thank you for coming from afar; there is nothing to offer as a reception. He asked Guankui, "How is it? Guankui said, "No rank. The Master said, "Is it like empty space? Guankui said, "It is not. The Master said, "If it is not like empty space, what is it? Guankui remained silent. The Master said, "You have been living in a ghost cave for thirty years! Guankui then bowed. The Master said, "I knew you were a man of great capacity. Guankui then left. When the Monk Luóhàn of Zhāngzhōu first visited Guānnán, he asked, "What is the source of the Great Way?
Guānnán struck him once with his fist, and the Master immediately attained realization. He then composed a song, saying: "In the seventh year of Xiántóng, I first entered the Way; wherever I went..."
Meeting him, he spoke of not knowing; a mass of doubt swirled within his heart like a winnowing basket. For three springs he found no joy, dwelling only among the forests and springs.
Suddenly encountering the Dharma King seated upon his mat, he laid bare his doubts before the Master. The Master rose from the mat like a *nāga*.
Baring his shoulder and placing his fist against his chest, he struck out a single blow; the mass of doubt was shattered like a startled wildcat. Raising his head, he beheld the newly risen sun;
from that moment on, with every step firm and resolute, he has remained constantly joyful until this very day.

Hearing only the full rumbling of a satisfied belly, he no longer wanders east or west to carry his almsbowl. He further composed a verse, saying: "A guest at leisure within the universe... (The text continues with "人").
In the interim, he became a wild monk; let others laugh as they will, for he roams freely wherever he goes.
This was the nun Chan Master Liao Ran of Mount Moshan in Ruizhou, a successor of Chan Master Dayu of Gao’an. Once, when Guankui Xian arrived, he asked her: "If you were truly equal [to him], then—"

As he was about to take his seat, Mazu pushed over the meditation bench and entered the hall. Mazu sent an attendant to ask, "Elder, did you come here to sightsee, or did you come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma?

Mazu asked, "Elder, where did you depart from today? He replied, "The crossroads. Mazu said, "Why didn't you pave it over? Xuefeng had no reply.
At the beginning of the interview, he prostrated and asked, "What is Mount Me? The Master said, "It does not reveal its peak. He asked, "Who is the master of Mount Me?
The Master said, "He is neither male nor female. Xixi then shouted, "Why do you not transform away? The Master said, "I am no spirit."
"It is not a ghost. What has it transformed into? At this, Xi submitted to his teaching. He served as the head gardener for three years.
A monk came to pay his respects. The Master said, "You look quite ragged. The monk replied, "Even so, I am still a lion cub.
The Master asked, "Since you are a lion cub, why are you being ridden by Mañjuśrī? The monk was speechless. Another asked, "What is the ancient [Way]?"

"Is it the Buddha-mind? The Master said, "The world collapses and perishes. [The monk] asked, "Why does the world collapse and perish? The Master said, "It would rather be that my own body does not exist.
[He was a successor of] Venerable Tiantong of Hangzhou.

The master remained there, yet he had no one to converse with. After the visitor had departed, the master sighed and said, "Though I possess the physical form of a man, I lack the spirit of a man.
It would be better for me to abandon this hermitage and travel to various regions to seek out wise teachers.
That night, a mountain deity told him, "There is no need to leave this place; a Bodhisattva in a physical body will arrive to preach the Dharma for you, Master."
More than ten days passed, and indeed a deva and a nāga arrived at the hermitage. The Master welcomed them with prostrations and related the previous events in detail.

The nāga raised one finger to indicate the matter, and the Master attained great enlightenment on the spot. From then on, whenever students came to inquire about the Dharma, the Master would simply raise one finger;
he had no other teaching or proclamation. There was a young boy who served him, who, whenever he saw someone asking a question, would likewise respond by raising a finger.
A man said to the Master, "The novice monk also understands the Buddha-dharma; whenever he is questioned, he always raises his finger just as you do, Master.
One day, the Master secretly tucked a knife into his sleeve and asked the novice, "I have heard that you understand the Buddha-dharma—is this true?
The novice replied, "Yes. The Master asked, "What is the Buddha? The novice raised his finger. The Master severed the finger with the knife, and the novice cried out.
He called out for him to come out. The Master summoned the boy; the boy turned his head back. The Master asked, "What is the Buddha? The boy raised his hand, yet no finger-tip was visible.
At this, he attained sudden and great enlightenment. As the Master was about to pass away, he said to the assembly, "I have obtained the 'one-finger Zen' of Tianlong;
I have used it throughout my life and it is not yet exhausted. Having spoken these words, he entered nirvana.
During a vegetarian feast at the residence of Chen Cao,
the Prefectural Governor of Muzhou and Senior Secretary,
who was a Dharma heir of the Venerable Master Chen of Muzhou— the fifth generation descendant of Nanyue— he picked up a steamed cake and asked a monk, "In Jiangxi and Hunan..."
"Is there still this [other thing]? He asked. The Official said, "What did you just eat, Minister? The Official replied, "I struck the bell to thank it for its resonance.
Then, during a vegetarian feast, he personally went to distribute the cakes. One monk extended his hand, intending to receive one, but the Official withdrew his hand.
The monk was speechless. The Official said, "As expected, as expected. He asked a monk, "I have a matter to discuss with you, Venerable Sir."
[The Master] said, "Shut your dog's mouth! The official pinched his own mouth and said, "I have committed a transgression. [The Master] said, "One who recognizes their error must surely reform it.

The official said, "If that is so, may I beg for the use of your seat’s mouth to eat my food? On another occasion, while serving food to the monks during a vegetarian feast, [the Master] said, "The Seat-Holder (the Master) is bestowing this food.
A monk said, "It possesses the three virtues and six flavors. The official said, "Wrong! The monk was speechless.
Furthermore, while ascending the tower with his subordinates, he saw several monks approaching. One official remarked, "Those coming are all traveling monks.
The Master said, "They are not. The official asked, "How do you know they are not? The Master replied, "Wait until they arrive; we shall examine them.
A moment later, the monks reached the front of the tower. The Master suddenly called out, "Venerable Upādhyāya! and all the monks raised their heads. The Master said to the officials, "Not..."
Xindao also composed a verse for a Chan practitioner, saying: The Chan practitioner possesses the primordial pivot; that primordial pivot is neither existent nor non-existent.
If one wishes to comprehend the intent prior to the pivot, all attempts will fail at the very point of the phrase.
Chan Master Daoyan of Changqing in Shengzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Guangxiao Jue.
A native of Luzhou, he first attended Guangxiao and immediately attained realization of his subtle teachings.
He received the tonsure at Mount Daguan in Hunan. As his influence for conversion flourished, he went forth to reside at Changqing. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Maitreya entered the monastery this morning and attained perfect enlightenment this evening. He spoke a verse, saying: 'The dharmas of the three realms, high and low—I say they are all mind.
Apart from these various mental phenomena, there is nothing else to be found. Look at him speaking thus; it is truly..."
"Kill the alert one! Compared to my disciples, you are still dull-witted fellows. Therefore, when the Way is seen in a single thought, the emotions of the three periods of time are exhausted;
it is like a seal stamping clay—there is no before or after. Sons of the Buddha, the matter of birth and death is great; you must quickly realize it. Do not treat it as trivial.
That the karmic consciousness is vast and boundless is simply because you are deluded about yourself and pursue external objects. When the World-Honored One was about to enter nirvana, Mañjuśrī..."

[The monk] made a special request for the Wheel of Dharma to be turned once more. The World-Honored One exclaimed, "In the forty-nine years I have dwelt in this world, I have not spoken a single word.
You ask me to turn the Wheel of Dharma once more; have I ever turned the Wheel of Dharma before?
However, at this time, amidst the assembly, I establish this exchange of guest and host out of necessity, solely for the sake of beginners. A monk asked: [What is the meaning of this?]
"What is the realm of Changqing? The Master said, "Look at how you tread upon it. A student asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Today is the third day of the third month. The student did not understand. The Master said, "Cease, cease! There is no need to speak;
my Dharma is subtle and difficult to conceive. He then descended from his seat. In the second year of the Xianping era, he passed away.
*Wudeng Quanshu*, Volume Eight;
*Wudeng Quanshu*, Volume Nine. Xuefeng asked, "What are you doing?
[Shigong] said, "If I had not reached Caoxi, how would I have known that [the Way] is not lost? Xuefeng said, "The Great Master of Caoxi..."
"Do you still recognize me, Master? The Master asked, "Do you recognize me now? He replied, "I do recognize you; how could I not be able to?
The Master said, "Though there may be many horns, one qilin is enough. Xian asked again, "Since you left Caoxi, Master, when did you arrive here?
The Master said, "I, however, know exactly when you left Caoxi. He replied, "Xiqian [does not know]."
[The monk] came from Caoxi. The Master said, “I also know where you have come from. The monk replied, “Master, as you are a person of great stature, please do not speak so hastily.
The Master then desisted. One day, the Master raised his whisk and asked, “Is there such a thing as this at Caoxi?
The monk replied, “Not only at Caoxi; even in the Western Heavens it does not exist. The Master asked, “Have you ever been to the Western Heavens? The monk replied, “No.”
"If you have arrived, then it exists. The Master said, "That is not yet it; speak further. [The monk] said, "Master, you too must speak half of it;
do not rely entirely on this student. The Master said, "I do not refuse to speak to you, but I fear that in the future there will be no one to take it up.
The Master then sent Qian to deliver a letter to Nanyue, instructing him: "Once you have delivered the letter, return quickly. I have something for you."

[Zhaozhou] presented his axe. Yanquan said, "I am staying on the mountain; come with me. When they arrived there, before Yanquan had even presented the letter, Xuanzang asked, "When one does not admire the various sages and does not prize one's own spiritual essence, what then?
Yanquan said, "Your question is too high-flown. Why not ask about things below? Xuanzang said:
"I would rather suffer in the depths of saṃsāra for eternal kalpas than seek liberation from the various sages. At this, Nanyue stopped. (Xuansha said:
"The Great Stone was toppled by Nanyue, and even until now he cannot get up. Chang then turned back. The Master asked: "Why have you returned so quickly? Did your letter reach?"
Xuan said, "Your letter has not been delivered, nor has your message reached me. On the day I departed, I was granted by the Master the promise of a 'pickaxe';
I request it now. The Master extended one leg; Xuan immediately prostrated himself. He then took his leave and went to Mount Heng.
When Shenhui of Heze came to visit, the Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Caoxi. The Master asked, "What is the essential meaning of Caoxi?"
He straightened his body and stood up. The Master said, "You still have some rubble left. He replied, "Does the Master not have any genuine gold to give people here?
The Master said, "Even if there were, where would you put it? (Xuansha said, "As expected. Yunju Xi said, "As for Xuansha saying 'as expected,' is that genuine gold or rubble?
A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The price of rice in Luling."

Mojia: Having transmitted the Dharma to Shitou, the Master ascended the hall on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month of the Gengchen year of the Kaiyuan era of Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang dynasty.
He addressed the assembly, then sat in the full lotus posture and passed away.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at his original mountain, which Emperor Xi Zong certified as the "Stupa of Chan Master Hongji’s Return to Truth."

The First Generation Dharma Heir of Chan Master Qingyuan Si was Chan Master Shitou Xiqian of Nanyue, a native of the Chen family from Gaoyao in Duanzhou. When his mother first became pregnant with him, she had no desire to consume meat.
Although the Master was still a mere infant, he required no nursemaid; once he reached adulthood, he was self-assured in his word and promise. Scholar Dong...
The Liao people fear ghosts and spirits and frequently perform licentious sacrifices, killing oxen and pouring out wine as a habitual practice.
Whenever the Master went there, he would destroy the shrines and take the oxen back with him; this occurred nearly a hundred times over the years. Later, he entered Caoxi and received ordination.

Following the Master’s passing, he fulfilled his final instructions by visiting Qingyuan, whereupon he adjusted his robes and followed him. (These words regarding their meeting are recorded in the preface to the chapter on Qingyuan. One day, Qingyuan asked the Master:
[The monk] said, "People say there is news from Lingnan. The Master said, "People do not say there is news from Lingnan.
[The monk] asked, "If that is so, from where do the Great and Small Collections of the Canon come? The Master said, "They all go forth from right here. He then returned to his original state.
At the beginning of the Tianbao era of the Tang dynasty, the Master arrived at Nanshi Temple on Mount Heng. To the east of the temple was a rock, shaped like...
He built a hermitage atop the terrace, which was then known as the Hermitage of Master Shitou.

While studying the *Zhao Lun*, upon reaching the passage, "Only the Sage can regard the myriad things as himself," the Master struck the table and said: "The Sage has no self; there is nothing that is not his own self.
The Dharma-body has no form; who can speak of self and other? Within this, the perfect mirror shines with spiritual illumination, and the myriad phenomena..."
"The essence is profound and manifests spontaneously; object and wisdom are not one. Who would say there is coming or going? How sublime these words!
Thereupon, he closed the volume and fell asleep unconsciously. In a dream, he saw himself and the Sixth Patriarch riding together upon a tortoise, swimming within a deep pool.

Upon awakening, he examined this in detail. "The numinous tortoise" refers to wisdom (*jñāna*). "The pond" refers to the ocean of nature (*prakṛti-samudra*). "I and the Patriarch ride together upon this numinous wisdom to roam the ocean of nature.
He then composed the *Cantong qi* (Mysterious Agreement on the Same Source), saying: "The mind of the Great Immortal of the land of India was secretly transmitted from east to west.
Human faculties are either sharp or dull, but the Way has neither Northern nor Southern patriarchs. The numinous source is bright and pure; its branches and tributaries are obscured."
The continuous flow is fundamentally delusion; even to accord with principle is not yet awakening. In every gate and all objects, there is mutual interpenetration and non-interpenetration.
When they interpenetrate, they further involve one another; otherwise, they abide in their respective positions. Form is originally distinct in its substance and appearance;

sound is fundamentally different as pleasure or pain. Darkness accords with words of superior and middle grade; clarity manifests in phrases of pure and turbid tone. The nature of the four great elements returns to itself, like a child finding [its mother].

Its mother consists of the heat of fire, the movement of wind, the moisture of water, and the solidity of earth; the colors of the eyes, the sounds of the ears, the fragrances of the nose, and the saltiness and acidity of the tongue.
Yet, relying upon each individual dharma, they are distributed according to the roots and leaves; from beginning to end, one must return to the source. Use the common language of honor and humility;
when there is light within, do not meet with darkness; when there is light within darkness, do not [meet] with light.
Beholding one another, light and darkness face each other like successive steps. All things possess their own efficacy; one should speak of their function and their place.
In affairs, there is the joining of lid and box; in principle, there is the meeting of arrow-tips. To receive the words, you must realize the source; do not establish your own narrow rules.
If you do not meet the Way upon seeing it before your eyes, how can you know the path as you set foot upon it? Advancing forward is neither near nor far; delusion merely separates one by a mountain.
He Gu: I respectfully address those who have penetrated the Source. Do not let the light of time pass in vain. Ascending the Hall: My Dharma-gate has been transmitted by the Buddhas of the past.
It does not concern itself with meditative concentration or diligent effort; it seeks only to realize the Buddha’s knowledge and vision. Mind is Buddha; mind, Buddha, and sentient beings;
enlightenment, awakening, and affliction—these names differ, but their substance is one. You should know that the essence of your own spiritual mind...
Free from the extremes of annihilation and permanence, its nature is neither defiled nor pure; it is profoundly still and perfect, such that ordinary beings and sages are of one essence.

Its application is boundless, transcending mind, intellect, and consciousness. The three realms and six paths are merely manifestations of one’s own mind; like the moon in water or an image in a mirror, how could they have arising or ceasing?
If you can know this, there is nothing that is not fully provided. Daowu asked, "Who has attained the essential meaning of Caoxi? The Master replied:
[The Master] said, "Only those who have realized the Buddha-dharma can attain it. A monk asked, "Does the Master yourself attain it?
The Master said, "I do not. The monk asked, "Why not? The Master said, "I do not understand the Buddha-dharma. A monk asked, "What is liberation? The Master said, "Who has bound you?"
[The monk] asked, "What is the Pure Land? The Master said, "Who defiles you? [The monk] asked, "What is Nirvana?
The Master said, "Who gave birth and death to you? The Master asked a newly arrived visitor, "Where have you come from? [The visitor] replied, "From Jiangxi.
The Master asked, "Have you seen the Great Master Ma? [The visitor] replied, "I have. The Master then pointed to a piece of firewood and said, "How does the Great Master Ma compare to this?"
The monk had no reply. The Patriarch returned and related this to Mazu. Mazu asked, "How large was that wooden stake you saw?
He replied, "It was of immense size. Mazu said, "You have great strength. He asked, "Why? Mazu said, "From Mount Heng, you carried a single wooden stake back here;
is this not having great strength? A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "Ask the dew."

The Pillar said, "I, a student, do not understand. The Master said, "I, moreover, do not understand. Dadian asked, "An ancient said, 'To say there is a Way, or to say there is no Way, both are slanders.
I beg the Master to eliminate them. The Master said, "There is not even a single thing. What would you have me eliminate?
The Master then asked, "Close off your throat, lips, and mouth, and tell me what you have to say. Dadian said, "I have nothing of this. The Master said, "If it is so..."
