"Does one who eats still possess eyes? The monk had no reply. In the sixth month of the Jia-chen year of Emperor Mu-zong’s Changqing era, he told his disciples, "Prepare hot water for a bath;
I wish to depart. Thereupon, he donned a bamboo hat, took up his staff, and put on his sandals, leaving one foot hanging.
Before it even reached the ground, he passed away. He was eighty-six years old. His disciples erected a stupa at the mountain monastery. By imperial decree, he was posthumously titled "Zhi" (Wisdom).
Chan Master Tong’s stupa was named Miaojue (Wondrous Enlightenment).
A monk from Jiangling came to visit Chan Master Dachu of Tanzhou. The Master asked, "When did you set out from Jiangling?
The monk lifted up his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*). The Master said, "Thank you for coming from afar; go on down. The monk circumambulated the meditation seat once and then departed. The Master—

The Master said, "If it were not so, how could one know for certain the true nature of the eyes? The monk clapped his hands and said, "If one were to kill someone, it would have been a mistake to judge the various quarters [of the teaching].

The Master said, "You have grasped the principles of the Chan school quite well. [The monk] related this to Danxia. Danxia said, "That may be acceptable regarding the Dharma path of Dayuan, but here with me it is not so.

[The monk] asked, "I wonder, how is it done here? Danxia said, "It is still three steps ahead of Dayuan. The monk bowed. Danxia said, "There are many who mistakenly judge the various quarters. Dongshan said, "Had it not been Danxia, it would have been difficult to distinguish."
Jade and Stone).
When Chan Master Dadian Baotong of Ling Shan in Chaozhou first visited Shitou, Shitou asked, "Which one is your mind?
The Master replied, "The one that perceives these words is it. Shitou then shouted at him and sent him out. After ten days had passed, the Master asked again, "As for what happened previously..."
"It is not that. "Apart from this, what is the mind? Mazu said, "Set aside your raising of eyebrows and blinking of eyes, and bring me the mind.
Nanquan said, "There is no mind to be brought. Nanquan said, "Originally there is a mind; why do you say there is no mind?

To say there is no mind is nothing but slander. At these words, Mazu attained great enlightenment. On another day, while standing in attendance, Nanquan asked, "Have you been practicing *chan* (dhyāna)?"
A Zen monk was a "white-trampling" (unregistered) monk from the local prefecture or county. The Master said, "This is a Zen practitioner. The monk asked, "What is Zen?
The Master said, "Raising an eyebrow and blinking an eye. The monk said, "Setting aside raising an eyebrow and blinking an eye, show me your original face.
The Master said, "Please, Reverend, examine me setting aside raising an eyebrow and blinking an eye. The monk said, "I set [it] aside..."
[The Master] finished. The Teacher said, "You have presented it. The Head asked, "Since you have presented it, what is my mind like?
The Teacher said, "It is no different from the Master’s. The Head said, "That does not concern you. The Teacher said, "Fundamentally there is nothing. The Head said, "You, too, are without anything."
The Master said, "Since there is no object, it is the true object. Tou said, "The true object cannot be apprehended;
such is the meaning of the scope of your mind's perception. You must guard and uphold this with great care. After the Master took up residence, students gathered from the four quarters.
He ascended the hall and said, "A student of the Way must recognize his own original mind. Only by pointing out the nature of the mind can one see the Way. I see that many of our contemporaries..."

To recognize only the raising of eyebrows, the twinkling of eyes, a single word, or a moment of silence, and to suddenly grant approval based on these as the essential core of the mind—this is truly not yet understood.
I shall now clearly explain it for all of you; each of you must listen and receive it.

Simply eliminate all deluded movements of thought, conceptualization, and intellectual measurement, and that is your true mind. This mind is neither the sensory objects nor the state of clinging to stillness.
At the time of silence, there is no interaction at all. This very mind is the Buddha; it does not await cultivation or refinement. Why is this?

Responding to conditions and illuminating accordingly, it functions with a clear, limpid autonomy. When one exhaustively investigates the locus of its functioning, it is ultimately ungraspable. To call this "wondrous function" is precisely the fundamental mind.
One must guard and sustain it with great care; it must not be treated lightly. A monk asked: "When those within [this state] meet one another, how is it?"
The Master said, "From the beginning, you were not in the center. The official asked, "What is it to be in the center? The Master said, "Do not act as if you are questioning Han Yu.
One day, when I visit you, I shall ask: 'How many years of age are you? The Master then held up his rosary and asked, "Do you understand?
The official replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "One hundred and eight beads, day and night. The official did not comprehend this and returned home. The following day, he came again.

He came to the gate and saw the Head Seat (Śrāmaṇera). He raised the previous conversation and asked, "What is the meaning? The Seat knocked his teeth three times. When he saw the Master, he repeated the previous question;
the Master also knocked his teeth three times. The Official said, "It turns out that the Buddha-dharma is not of two kinds. The Master said, "What principle is this?
The Official said, "Just now, when I questioned the Head Seat, it was also like this. The Master then called out to him.
"Head Seat," the Master said. "Is this how you would respond? The Head Seat replied, "Yes. The Master then struck him and expelled him from the monastery.

On another day, Master Wen addressed the Master, saying, "Disciple, the affairs of the military prefecture are numerous. I beg the Master for a single word regarding the essential points of the Buddha-dharma.
The Master remained silent for a long while. Master Wen was at a loss. At that time, Sanping was serving as the attendant; he struck the meditation seat three times. The Master—
[The Master] asked, "How so? Ping said, "First move with concentration; afterwards, extract [the being] with wisdom. The official then said, "The style of your Gate, Master, is lofty and steep.
I have gained an entrance through your attendant. A monk asked, "The waves of the sea of suffering are deep;
what shall serve as a boat or raft? The Master said, "Use wood as a boat or raft. The monk said, "If that is so, one will cross over. The Master said, "..."
The blind remain blind as before; the mute remain mute as before. One day, while walking along a corridor with Yanghezi, the Master encountered a monk who came to pay his respects.
The Master struck him across the mouth with Yanghezi and asked, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I do not understand."
The Master said: "Old Wild Fox Dadian never fails anyone.
Chan Master Changzi Kuang of Tanzhou went to pay homage at the Patriarch’s stupa at Caoxi; upon his return, he visited Shitou.
Shitou asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Lingnan. Shitou said, "At the head of Mount Dayu, there is a shop of merit—has it been completed yet?"

The Master said, "He has been accomplished for a long time; he simply lacks the 'dotting of the eyes' (the final realization). Baizhang said, "Do you not wish for the dotting of the eyes? The Master replied, "I request it at once.
Baizhang then lowered one foot. The Master prostrated himself. Baizhang asked, "What principle have you perceived that you prostrate yourself?
The Master said, "According to what I have seen, it is like a single drop of snow upon a red-hot furnace. (Xuange said: Now tell me, did Chang [Baizhang]...)

The Master asked, "Does one who possesses eyes respond? Or does one who lacks eyes respond? If he possesses eyes, why did he ask for the Way to have his eyes opened? If he lacks eyes, it has been said that his attainment of the Way has long since been perfected. How do you judge this?
Fadelen (Fadeng) spoke on his behalf, saying, "The Master may indeed be called 'blinded by cataracts. A monk visited. He circumambulated the meditation seat once and stood there with a solemn air.
The Master said, "If this were the Dharma-seat of Shitou, not even a single drop would be needed. The monk again circumambulated the meditation seat once. The Master said, "But rather, it is thus..."
At that moment, the monk did not readily state his place of origin. The monk then departed. The Master called after him, but the monk paid no heed.

The Master said, "This fellow still lacks instruction. The monk turned back and asked, "There is a person who does not receive it from another, who does not receive instruction, and who does not fall into stages;
would you grant your approval of such a one? The Master said, "Meeting him is not meeting him; if you meet him, there must be something."
The monk then stepped back three paces. The Master, however, circumambulated the meditation seat once.

The monk said, "Not only is the eye of the school made clear, but the lineage of the teacher is also well-founded. The Master then struck him three times with his staff. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from?

The monk replied, "From the Kòngshí Hermitage on Mount Jiuhua. The Master asked, "Who is the abbot of that hermitage? The monk replied, "A venerable elder under Mazu. The Master... [proceeded as above].
[The monk] asked, "What is its name? [The Master] said, "I do not know its dharma-name. The Master said, "He does not know it; you do not know it either.
[The monk] asked, "Where are the eyes of a venerable elder? The Master said, "If the Abbot himself had come in person, he too would have had to receive a blow of the staff today.
[The monk] said, "Fortunately, we encountered the Master who let me off. The Master said, "A hundred years from now, even a single monk will be difficult to find."

When Layman Pang arrived, the Master ascended the seat and gathered the assembly. Once they were settled, the Layman stepped forward and said, "Each of you should examine yourselves well," and then stood to the right of the meditation platform.
At that time, a monk asked, "Without touching the master of the house, I ask the Master to respond to my question. The Master said:
"Do you know Master Pang? [The monk] said, "I do not. The layman then seized him by the collar and said, "Alas! Alas! The monk had no reply. The layman then let him go.
A short while later, the Master asked again, "Did that monk just now receive a blow of the staff? The layman said, "I will wait until he is willing before I do so.
The Master said, "The Layman sees only the sharpness of the chisel's point, but does not see the squareness of the chisel's head. The layman said, "That being so..."
"What kind of talk is this? I myself might get away with it, but if outsiders hear it, it will certainly not be good.
The Master said, "What is so bad about it? The Layman said, "Master, you see only the sharpness of the chisel's tip; you do not see the keenness of the adze's head.

When Li Xingpo arrived, the Master asked, "Do you remember the events when we were in Jangzhou? The Lady said, "Were it not for you, Master, I would not know. The Master said, [and she replied: "I remember clearly."
[The Master said,] "There is much falsehood and little reality. The old woman said, "What is there to hide? The Master said, "I am mindful that you are a woman;
therefore, I let you off with a blow from my staff. The old woman said, "I have never seen any fault in the Venerable Elder. The Master said, "Where does the old monk’s fault lie?
The old woman said, "If the Teacher has no fault, how could I possibly have one? The Master said, "As for one who has no fault, what is he like?"
Ba raised his fist and said, "In this way, everything becomes inverted. The Master said, "Truly, there is no place for concealment.
When the Master saw a monk, he seized him and said, "A lion cub belonging to the lineage of jackals! The monk made a gesture with his hand as if brushing his eyebrows. The Master said:
"Even so, you still lack the roar. A monk seized the Master and said, "You are biased in favor of using this one particular turn of phrase.
The Master gave him a slap. The monk clapped his hands three times. The Master said, "If you see it as being of the same wind, would you be willing to act like this?"
[The Master] said, "In the end, it does not depend on another. The Master made a gesture of plucking his eyebrows. The monk said, "There is still a roar missing.
The Master said, "I suspect it does not depend on another. While a monk was bowing in greeting, the Master said, "Every step is a place for you to realize proof.
Do you know this? The monk said, "I do not know, sir. The Master said, "If you knew, what would I be capable of doing?"
[The Master said: "No. The monk bowed. The Master said, "I am not fit for this; you are the one who is suitable.
Tianhuang Daowu Chan Master of Jingzhou was a native of the Zhang family of Dongyang in Wuzhou. His divine countenance was exceptionally distinguished, and he possessed innate wisdom from childhood.
At the age of fourteen, he earnestly sought to leave the household life, but his parents would not permit it. Consequently, he reduced his meals until, by day, he could barely...

He ate but one meal a day, and his physical form became emaciated and haggard. His parents, having no other recourse, finally granted their permission. He received the tonsure under a virtuous master from Mingzhou.
At twenty-five, he went to Zhulin Temple in Hangzhou to receive full ordination. He cultivated the pure conduct of a *brahmacārin* with such diligence that he was esteemed for his heroic vigor.
Whether during wind and rain or in the darkness of night, he sat in meditation among burial mounds with body and mind in tranquil stillness, free from all fears.

One day, while traveling through Yuhang, he first visited Guoyi of Mount Jing to receive the Dharma of the Mind. He served him diligently for five years, after which he went to study under Mazu, who reaffirmed his previous understanding;
the Dharma was without differing explanations. Having stayed there for two summer retreats, he then visited Shitou and posed this question: "Apart from..."
[The monk] asked, "Having set aside both concentration and wisdom, by what dharma do you instruct people? Baizhang said, "In my place here, there are no servants.
What would you have me abandon? The monk asked, "How can one attain clarity? Baizhang said, "Can you grasp empty space?

The monk said, "If that is so, then from this day forward, I shall not follow [your path]. Baizhang said, "I wonder, at what time and from where did you come? The monk replied, "Daowu is not [the one who knows]."
The man from that region said, "I have known for some time where you came from. The Master asked, "Why do you falsely accuse me with stolen goods?

The man replied, "Your very body is present here. The Master said, "Even if it is so, how ultimately will you show this to future generations? The man replied, "Tell me, who is the 'future generation'?
From this point on, the Master attained sudden enlightenment, exhausting the depths of the words of the two former masters under whom he had studied.

Having attained the realization that there is nothing to be grasped, he later settled at Mount Ziling in Dangyang, Jingzhou. Disciples followed him in such numbers that their shoulders brushed against one another;
men and women from the capital arrived like moths drawn by the wind. At that time, the head monk of Congye Monastery reported these circumstances to the regional governor.
They escorted him into the city. To the left of the commandery was Tientang Temple (Tianhuang Si), a renowned monastery that had been destroyed by fire.
The presiding monk, Lingjian, intending to restore it, said, "If we can secure Master Wuzu as the chief fundraiser, he will surely bring us prosperity."
He then went secretly at midnight to offer a sorrowful plea. [The Master] arrived carried on a shoulder litter.

At that time, the Right Vice-Director of the Chancellery, Lord Pei, the Governor of Jiangling, bowed his head and inquired about the Dharma, paying him the utmost respect. The Master had never before welcomed or seen off guests; regardless of their rank, whether noble or humble, he would simply have them sit and bow to them.
Lord Pei’s devotion increased all the more, and from this, the Dharma path of Shitou flourished. A monk asked: "If..."
"What is this profound and wondrous teaching? The Master said, "Do not say that I understand the Buddha-dharma. [The student] said, "What can be done about the doubts and stagnations of this student?
The Master said, "Why do you not ask the old monk? [The student] said, "I have already asked just now. The Master said, "Go; this is not where you may find rest.
In the fourth month of the Dinghai year of the Yuanhe era of Emperor Xianzong of the Tang dynasty, the Master manifested illness and issued his final instructions.
The disciple had previously announced that his end was near. When the final day of the month arrived, the assembly went to inquire after his illness. The Master suddenly called out to the head cook.
As the cook approached, the Master asked, "Do you understand? The cook replied, "I do not understand. The Master picked up his pillow, threw it to the ground, and immediately passed away.
He was sixty years old, with thirty-five years of summer retreats (*varṣa*). On the fifth day of the eighth month of that year, he was interred in a stupa at Dongjun.
The Master Shili of Jingzhao Prefecture asked Stonehead, “What is the student’s fundamental matter?
Stonehead said, “Why do you seek it from me? He replied, “I do not seek it from the teacher. Stonehead asked, “Have you ever lost it?
At these words, the Master realized its essential meaning.
Chan Master Huilang of Zhaoti Temple in Tanzhou was the son of the Ou-yang family of Qiuxiang in Shixing.
He first went to visit Mazu. Mazu asked, "What do you seek by coming here? He replied, "I seek the Buddha’s knowledge and vision. Mazu said, "The Buddha has no knowledge or vision;
knowledge and vision are merely demons. Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from Mount Heng. Mazu said, "Since you have come from Mount Heng, you have not yet recognized [the Buddha]."
"The essential heart of Caoxi. You should return there quickly; it is not fitting for you to go elsewhere. The Master returned to Shitou and asked, "What is the Buddha?
Shitou said, "You have no Buddha-nature. The Master said, "What about all the wriggling, sentient beings? Shitou said:
"Even wriggling insects and sentient beings possess Buddha-nature. Daowei asked, "Why then does Huirang not have it? Daohui replied, "It is because you are unwilling to accept it.
Upon these words, the Master attained faith and entry. After he took up residence, whenever students arrived, he would always say, "Go away, go away!
You have no Buddha-nature. His manner of engaging with practitioners was roughly like this (at that time, he was called "Daolang").
When Chan Master Zhenlang of Xingguo Temple in Changsha first visited Shitou, he asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Shitou replied, "Ask the pillar. Zhenlang said, "I do not understand. Shitou said, "I do not understand either."
The Master suddenly attained realization. After he had taken up residence, a monk came to pay his respects. The Master called out, "Elder! The monk responded, "Yes.

The Master said, "You have failed me. The monk asked, "Why do you not discern [me]? The Master then rubbed his eyes and stared at him; the monk was speechless (at that time, he was known as Xiao Lang).
Chan Master Shilou of Fenzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "I do not yet recognize my original nature; I beg the Master for a skillful means to point it out.
The Master said, "Shilou has no ears. The monk said, "I myself know that I am at fault. The Master said, "The old monk also has his faults."
The monk asked, "Where does the Master's fault lie? The Master said, "The fault lies in your being in the wrong place. The monk bowed, and the Master struck him.
He asked another monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From the land of Han. The Master said, "Does the ruler of the land of Han respect the Buddha-dharma?
The monk said, "How miserable! Fortunately I encountered you to ask me this; had you asked anyone else, disaster would have ensued. The Master said, [and struck him].
"What is it? [the monk] said, "People themselves do not even exist; what Dharma could there be to value?

The Master said, "How many years of summer retreat have you completed since receiving the precepts? He replied, "Thirty years. The Master said, "Excellent! You truly do not see people," and then struck him.
Chan Master Fo-tuo of Famen Temple in Fengxiang Prefecture habitually held a string of prayer beads and recited three names:
first, Śākyamuni; second, Yuanhe; and third, Buddha. As for all others, he would say, "What are they? They are just broken bowls."
He would pass over one bead and, having finished the string, begin again; his conduct was extraordinary, and people of the time could not fathom it.
One day, Master Shuikong saw a monk in the corridor and asked, "How is the matter of the present moment?
The monk remained silent for a long while. The Master said, "Is it enough just to do this? The monk replied, "Adding a head atop a head. The Master struck him and said, "Go! Go! It was already done.

Later, while the master was confusing the men and women of the household, Chan Master Jì of Dàtóng in Lǐzhōu arrived with his assembly. Just as they were about to meet, the master pulled the meditation seat around and sat facing the wall.
Mihu stood behind him for a short while; as he was about to return to the guest quarters, the master said, "It is."
This was indeed so. If he had not tested and refuted him, later on Mi would have been subjected to humiliation. [One day], Mi asked his attendant to bring some rice.
When the rice was brought, Mi pulled the meditation seat toward himself and sat down. The Master then walked once around the meditation seat and returned to his quarters.
Mi then pulled the meditation seat over and led the assembly out. Later, the Master visited Layman Pang. The Layman said, "Do you remember when I was in my mother’s womb?"
There is a saying; I will cite it for you, Master. You must by no means attempt to explain it through intellectual reasoning. The Master said, "That is still a matter of past lives.
The Layman said, "I told you not to resort to intellectual reasoning. The Master said, "This is a startling statement; how could one not be afraid?
The Layman said, "According to your understanding, it may indeed be called startling. The Master said, "By not employing intellectual reasoning, it instead becomes [the truth]."

[The Master] applied the principle of reasoning. The Layman said, "Not only separated by one or two lifetimes. The Master said, "As for a monk who merely eats his rice gruel, let him be subject to whatever scrutiny he desires.
The Layman snapped his fingers three times. One day, when the Master saw Layman Pang approaching, he immediately shut the door and said, "An old man of many knowledges;
do not come to meet me. The Layman said, "Sitting alone and speaking to oneself—whose fault is this? The Master...
He immediately opened the door and was just about to step out when the officer seized him, saying, "The Master knows much; I know much.

The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment our mutual knowledge of much, as for closing the door and opening the door, or rolling it up and stretching it out—how much difference is there between them? The officer said, "This one question alone [is enough]."
"Anxiety kills people. The Master remained silent. The layman said, "To be clever and end up clumsy. A monk asked, "How can this Dharma-gate be transmitted and maintained?
The Master said, "Winter is cold and summer is hot; people know this for themselves. The monk said, "If that is so, then I have received your entrustment.
The Master said, "The stubborn and dull-witted lack wisdom; the energetic and eloquent are mostly foolish. [The monk] asked, "Throughout the twelve periods of the day, as..."
"What accords with the Way? The Master said, "Do you recognize the twelve hours? The monk asked, "What are the twelve hours? The Master said, "Zi, Chou, Yin, Mao.
The monk bowed. The Master presented this verse: "In the midst of the twelve hours, what thing is distinct? Zi, Chou, Yin, Mao—I shall now explain them.
If you understand that all phenomena are but mind, they are empty; Then Śākyamuni and Maitreya will be resolved from this point on."
The Third Generation under Qingyuan:
Chan Master Daowu Shanzhi of Daowu Mountain in Tanzhou, a successor of Chan Master Yanshan Yuan of Yaoshan, was born into the Zhang family of Haihun in Yuzhang. In his youth, he relied upon Panyue.

Furthermore, having received instruction and been ordained, he joined the dharma assembly at Yaoshan, where he secretly attained the seal of the mind. One day, the Mountain asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "I have come from wandering the mountains. The Mountain said, "Without leaving this room, quickly bring it here! The Master said:
The crow on the mountain peak has a head like snow; the fish swimming in the bottom of the stream are never at rest. After the Master left Yaoshan, he went to see Nanquan.
Nanquan asked, "What is your name, *śrāmaṇera*? The Master replied, "Zongzhi. Nanquan said, "How can you establish a school where wisdom does not reach?
The Master said, "One must absolutely avoid speaking of it. Nanquan said, "If one speaks of it, horns will surely grow. (3)

Later, while the Master and Yunyan were mending robes on the rear rack, Baizhang saw them and asked, "The other day, Zenith (Zhizhu) said, 'Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking;
if you speak, horns will grow. How should one practice in such a state?
The Master then withdrew his body and entered the monks' hall. Baizhang returned to the abbot's quarters. When the Master came back to mend the robes again, Yunyan said:
The Master’s disciple, Yañ, had just arrived. Why did he not respond to the Master? The Master said, "You are remarkably quick-witted.
Yañ did not understand and asked Nanquan, "Why did that Zen monk (Zhìtóuduō) just now not respond to the Master?

I do not understand; I beg the Master for an instruction. Nanquan said, "He was, in fact, acting within the realm of the 'different species' (yílèi). Yañ asked, "What is meant by 'the different species'?"
"Walk among the heterodox. Quan said, "Do not let the Way reach where wisdom cannot; one must strictly avoid becoming attached to the Way.
If you become attached to the Way, then 'horns' will grow upon your head. You must simply walk among the heterodox. Yan also did not understand.

The Master, knowing that Yunyan had not realized it, said, "This man's karmic conditions do not lie here. They then returned together to Yaoshan. Yaoshan asked, "Why have you returned so quickly? Yan—
Yunmen said, "It is simply because our karmic conditions do not coincide. Deshan asked, "What kind of karmic conditions? Yunmen recounted the previous conversation.
Deshan said, "How did you understand that moment? Yunmen then turned to leave. Deshan had no reply, whereupon he laughed heartily.
Yunmen then asked, "What is it like to walk among those of different species? Deshan said, "I am weary today; come back at another time."
Yan said, "I have come back specifically for this matter. Shanshan said, "Go for now. Yan then departed.
While the Master was outside the abbot’s quarters, hearing that Yan had not attained realization, he unconsciously bit his finger until it bled. The Master then came down and questioned Yan.
The Master’s senior brother went to ask the Abbot, “What is the meaning of that karmic connection?

Yanguan said, “The Abbot did not tell me. The Master then bowed his head. [A monk asked Yunju,] “The instruction was ‘Above all, do not speak of it. What is the meaning of this? Yunju said, “These words are most poisonous. [The monk asked,] “What are the most poisonous words? Yunju said, “A single blow of the staff kills both dragons and snakes.
When Yunyan was about to pass away, he sent a letter to take leave of his teacher. After the teacher had finished reading the letter, he said to Dongsan Mi:
The Master (Shishibo) said: "Yunyan did not realize there was a 'me' and regretted not having spoken to him [at that time].

Nevertheless, even so, he still does not violate the lineage of Yaoshan. (Xuange said: "When the ancients spoke thus, did they know it existed or not? Furthermore, Yunyan did not understand at that time;
tell me, where exactly was his lack of understanding? Yaoshan ascended the hall and said: "I have a single phrase that I have never yet spoken to anyone."
The Master came out and said, "I have come along with you. A monk asked, "How would you explain the single phrase of Yaoshan?

Yaoshan said, "It is not something that can be expressed in words. The Master said, "He has already finished speaking. One day, as the Master was going out carrying his rain hat, Yunyan pointed at it and asked, "What do you use this for?
The Master said, "I have a place where it is used. Yunyan said, "What if you suddenly encounter a black wind and a violent rain?"
"How is it when [the guest] arrives? The Master said, "He is covered. Yank asked, "Does he still accept being covered?
The Master said, "Even though it is so, there is no leakage. Miaoshan asked Yunyan, "What serves as the seat for Bodhi?
Yunyan replied, "Non-action (wuwei) serves as its seat. Yunyan then asked Miaoshan. Miaoshan said, "The emptiness of all dharmas serves as its seat. Furthermore—
Question: "Master, what do you do? The Master said: "If he sits, I let him sit; if he lies down, I let him lie down.
There is one person who neither sits nor lies down—speak quickly, speak quickly! Shan then withdrew. Miaoshan asked the Master:
"Where have you come from? The Master said: "I have come to visit the sick. Miaoshan said: "How many people are ill? The Master said: "There are those who are ill, and there are those who are not."
Deshan said, "The one who is not ill—could that be Zen Master Zhidu? The Master said, "Whether it be illness or non-illness, neither concerns him at all.
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Deshan said, "Even if I were to speak, it would have nothing to do with him.
A monk asked, "When there are no clouds ten thousand miles away, that is still not the original sky. What is the original sky? The Master said, "Today is a fine day for sunning oneself."
Mai: Yunyan asked, "How has the family style of you, my junior teacher, been lately? The Master said, "What would it be worth for you, elder brother, to point it out?
Yunyan said, "It has been quite some time since that was not the case. The Master said, "The roots of the teeth still have a trace of rawness.
[Another] asked, "What is the place of exertion in these present times? The Master said, "A thousand people, ten thousand people call out..."
"Not looking back; only then will there be a slight degree of resonance. [A monk] asked, "What is it like when the fire suddenly breaks out? The Master said, "It can burn the great earth.
The Master then asked the monk, "Setting aside the stars and the flames, what is the fire? [The monk] said, "It is not something other than the fire.
Another monk then asked, "Do you see the fire, Master? The Master said, "I see it. [The monk] asked, "From where does this seeing arise? The Master said:
Setting aside walking, standing, sitting, and reclining, he posed a separate question:

A donor presented a loincloth to Yashan, who held it up and showed it to the assembly, saying, "Does the Dharma-body still possess the four great elements? If anyone can speak to this, I will give him this loincloth."
The Master said, "The nature of the ground is not emptiness; emptiness is not the nature of the ground. This is the element of earth; the other three elements are likewise.
Yunshan said, "I give you a waist-cloth. The Master pointed to a *fó-sāng* flower and asked a monk, "How is this like that?"
[The monk] said, "I have truly reached the point where my hair stands on end. The Master said, "Ultimately, how is it? [The monk] said, "It is the one under Daowu's gate.
The Master said, "The Great King of Ten Li; Yunyan is unwell. The Master then said, "Apart from this leaking shell, where shall we meet?
Yunyan said, "We shall meet at the place of neither arising nor ceasing. The Master said, "Why do you not say 'it is not'?"
"In the state of neither arising nor ceasing, one does not even seek to see their marks. While Yunyan was mending his shoes, the Master asked, "What are you doing?
Yunyan replied, "I am mending what is already worn out with what is already worn out. The Master said, "Why do you not say that what is worn out is not worn out?
The Master heard a monk reciting the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra*, which says: "Eight thousand bodhisattvas and five hundred śrāvakas all desired to follow [him]."
From Wenshushi: A monk asked, "Where have you been? The monk had no reply, so the Master struck him. The Master went to Wufeng.
Wufeng asked, "Do you still recognize the old master Yaoshan? The Master said, "I do not recognize him. Wufeng said, "Why do you not recognize him?
The Master said, "I do not recognize him; I do not recognize him. [Another] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The Master said, "I have never encountered such a thing in this eastern land. Once, when a vegetarian feast was being prepared for Yaoshan, a monk asked, "I wonder, will the late master still come?
The Master said, "Why do you all go to the trouble of preparing a feast?
Shishuang asked, "Master, a single piece of bone—when struck, it rings like bronze. Where has it gone? The Master called to his attendant. The attendant responded.

"Yes," [the Master] replied. The Master said, "When will that ever be? It will be as long as it takes for a donkey to grow horns. In the ninth month of the *wuyin* year of the Taihe era of Emperor Wenzong of the Tang dynasty, he manifested illness and suffered.
The assembly of monks came to inquire after his health. The Master said, "There is receiving without retribution; do you understand this? The assembly was all somber and distressed.

Ten days later, as he was about to depart, he said to the assembly, "I am to go westward; by principle, there shall be no moving east. Having finished speaking, he passed away. His *jia* (funeral rites) were performed.
He obtained several fragments of the holy relics and erected a stupa for them at Daowu. Later, Lei moved them to the southern slope of Mount Shishuang.
Chan Master Tansheng of Yunyan in Tanzhou was the son of the Wang family of Jianchang in Zhongling.

He left home to become a monk at Shimen in his youth and studied under Baizhang for twenty years, yet the karmic conditions did not harmonize. Thereafter, he visited Yaoshan, who asked him, "Where have you come from?"
Baizhang arrived. Mount said, "What words or phrases did Baizhang have to show to his disciples? The Master replied, "He usually said, 'I have a single phrase that possesses a hundred flavors.
Mount asked, "If it is salty, it is the flavor of salt; if it is bland, it is the flavor of blandness;
if it is neither salty nor bland, it is the ordinary flavor. What is this phrase that possesses a hundred flavors? The Master had no reply. Mount said:
"But what can be done about birth and death right before one's eyes? The Master said, "There is no birth and death right before one's eyes.
Sansheng said, "How long have you been at Baizhang? The Master said, "Twenty years. Sansheng said, "Even after twenty years at Baizhang, you have not eliminated your worldly airs.
On another day, while standing in attendance, Sansheng asked again, "What further Dharma did Baizhang teach? The Master said, "Sometimes..."
"Regarding the Way: eliminate it beyond the three phrases; realize it within the six phrases. Shanshan said, "Three thousand miles away, I am glad there is no connection.
Shanshan asked again, "What further Dharma do you speak? The Master said, "Sometimes when I ascend the hall and the assembly has taken their places..."
He drove them all away at once with his staff. He then called to the assembly, and as they turned their heads, Baizhang asked, "What is this?
Dongsan said, "Why did you not say so earlier? Today, because of you, I have been able to see my elder brother Hai.
At these words, the Master attained sudden realization and prostrated himself. One day, Dongsan asked, "Apart from being at Baizhang, where else have you been?"

The Master asked, "Have you ever been to Guangnan? He replied, "I have heard it said that outside the eastern gate of the city of Guangzhou there is a large rock, which has been moved by the provincial governor.
Is this true? The Master said, "Not only the provincial governor; even if all the people of the country were to move it together, it would not budge.
The Master asked again, "I have heard that you are skilled at performing with the lion. Is this true? The Master said, "It is. The Master asked, "How many times have you performed it?"
The Master said, "I have handled it six times. The other replied, "I have also handled it. The Master asked, "How many times has the Abbot handled it?
He replied, "I have handled it once. The Master said, "One is six; six is one. Later, he went to Mount Gui (Miaoshan), where Miaoshan asked him:
"I have heard that the Elder plays with lions at Yaoshan; is this true? The Master said, "It is. The monk asked, "When playing for long, is there a time to set it down?
The Master said, "If you wish to play, you play; if you wish to set it down, you set it down. The monk asked, "When it is set down, where is the lion?"
The Master said, "Set it aside! Set it aside! Question: "Where have all the sages of the past gone? The Master remained silent for a long while and then said, "What? What? Question:
"When one is absent for even a moment, as if being a dead man, what then? The Master said, "It is best to bury him. Question:
"Between the person who maintains great assurance and that other [person], are they one or two? The Master said, "A single function."

[The Master] held up a piece of silk; one was a single segment, the other was two segments. (Dongshan spoke on his behalf, saying: "It is like a person grafting a tree. While the Master was brewing tea, Daowu asked him:
“To whom shall I give this fried cake? The Master said, “There is someone who wants it. [The attendant] asked, “Why do you not tell him to fry it himself?
The Master said, “Fortunately, there is someone here. The Master asked Shishuang, “Where have you come from? He replied, “From Mount Huai. The Master said, “How long have you been there?
He replied, “I have spent the better part of the winter and summer there. The Master said, “In that case, you must have grown quite large.”
[Daowu] said, "Even though he is right there in the midst of it, he does not know. The Master said, "In his house, there is neither knowing nor cognizing. Shishuang had no reply.

(When Daowu heard this, he said, "How can one attain such a state where there is no Buddha-dharma, body, or mind? Later, after taking up residence [at Dongshan], he ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying, "There is a man’s son who, when questioned, has nothing he cannot answer.
Dongshan stepped forward and asked, "How many things are there in his house?"

[The Master] asked about the scriptures. The Master said, "There is not even a single character. [Shan] asked, "How is it that you possess such vast knowledge? The Master said, "Day and night, I have never slept.
Shan said, "May I ask about a certain matter? Would it be acceptable? The Master said, "If one could speak of it, one would not speak of it. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from?
[The monk] replied, "I have come to offer incense. The Master said, "Do you see the Buddha? [The monk] replied, "I see him. The Master said, "What kind of Buddha?"
[Daowu] said, "The view of the lower realms. The Master said, "Ancient Buddhas, ancient Buddhas. Daowu asked, "Of the Great Compassionate One’s thousand hands and eyes, which one is the True Eye?
The Master said, "It is like a person at night reaching behind with their back to feel for their pillow.
Daowu said, "I understand. The Master said, "How do you understand it? Daowu said, "Everywhere on the body is hand and eye. The Master said, "To speak of it is already too much."
Shaduo said, "I can only get it eighty percent. Wuzu asked, "What about you, Elder Brother? Shaduo replied, "My whole body is hands and eyes.
While sweeping, Wuzu said, "You are being far too diligent. Shaduo said, "You must know that there is one who is not so diligent.
Wuzu said, "In that case, there would be a second moon. Shaduo held up the broom and asked, "Which one is this?"

[When] Yue asked, "I shall go," Xuansha heard this and said, "That is precisely the second moon. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from conversing upon a rock.
The Master said, "Does the rock nod its head as well? The monk had no reply. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "It was precisely when he had not yet spoken that it nodded its head.
While the Master was making straw sandals, Dongshan approached him and said, "May I beg for the Master's eyes?"
The Master said, "To whom have you given yours? Dongshan replied, "Liang-jia has none. The Master said, "Even if you had one, where would you put it?
Dongshan was speechless. The Master said, "Is that which begs for eyes itself the eye? Dongshan replied, "It is not the eye. The Master then shouted and sent him out. A nun bowed in prostration.
The Master asked her, "Is your father still alive? She replied, "He is. The Master said, "He is advanced in years."
[The monk] said, "I am young. [Dongshan] said, "At eighty years of age, you have a father; do you know him? The monk said, "Is it not one who comes in this manner?
The Master said, "One who comes in this manner is still but an offspring. (Dongshan spoke on his behalf: "Even one who does not come in this manner is likewise an offspring.
A monk asked, "When a single thought flickers up and one immediately falls into the realm of Māra, what then? The Master said, "It is because of you..."
"From what did it come when it came from the Buddha-realm? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "Do you understand? He said, "I do not.
The Master said, "Do not say that you cannot realize it; even if you were to realize it, it would still only be a matter of left and right.
When the head of the monastery returned from visiting the stone grotto, the Master asked, "You went inside that stone grotto; why did you return just as you were? The head had no reply.
[Dongshan] replied, “That place has already been occupied by someone. The Master said, “Why would you go there again? Dongshan said, “One must not let human relations be severed.
On the twenty-sixth day of the tenth month of the Xinyou year of the Huichang era of the Tang Emperor Wuzong, [Baizhang] manifested illness.
Having ordered his body to be washed, he summoned the administrator and instructed him to prepare a vegetarian feast, saying, “Tomorrow there will be...”

The Elder departed; he passed away peacefully on the evening of the following day at the age of sixty. Upon cremation, more than one thousand *śarīra* relics were obtained, which were enshrined in a stone stupa.
He was posthumously titled Great Master Wuzhu, and his stupa was named Jingsheng.
Chan Master Decheng of Huating in Xiuzhou was of lofty character and peerless capacity.
Having received the seal of his mind from Yaoshan, he shared a bond of spiritual fellowship with Daowu and Yunyan. Upon departing from Yaoshan, Yaoshan said to him:
"You gentlemen should each take charge of a region and establish the school of Yaoshan. I, Zishu, am by nature simple and rustic;

I delight only in mountains and waters, seeking to divert my own feelings, and possess no other ability. In the future, should you encounter a sharp and talented presiding master (zuozhu) at the place where I reside, send one such person to me.
If he is worthy of being refined, I shall transmit to him all that I have attained throughout my life, thereby repaying your kindness."

Parting from his late master, he traveled to Huating in Xiuzhou, where he took to a small boat and spent his days according to circumstances, receiving the crowds of people coming and going from all directions.
At that time, no one knew of his lofty conduct, so he was called the Boatman Monk.
One day, while sitting idly by the riverbank with his boat moored, an official asked him, "What is the Master's daily practice?"
The Master held up his oar and asked, "Do you understand? The official said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The oar sweeps through the clear waves;
the golden-scaled fish are rarely encountered. He once had a verse that said: "For thirty years I have sat upon the fishing platform; From hook to hook, I have often caught yellow eels.
The golden-scaled fish has not been met, and my efforts have been in vain; I shall gather in my line and go back home. A thousand feet of line...
Hanging straight down. When a single wave stirs, ten thousand waves follow. At night, when the water is cold and still, the fish do not bite;

the boat returns empty under the bright moon. For thirty years I have roamed the seas; the water is clear, the fish appear, yet they do not swallow the hook. The fishing rods are worn out, so new bamboo is planted;
one must not allow the task to end merely because success has been achieved. There is a great fish, its majesty beyond measure, blending with—

How wondrous is this melting embrace and inclusion! It can transform and give forth wind and thunder. How could one ever catch it by casting a line below? Others merely watch as the lotus blossoms are gathered.
Its fragrance long lingers, clinging to the breeze that circles the fingers; redness reflects from both banks upon a single boat. How could it ever stain the void?
When asked about my livelihood, I say it is simply this boat; sons and grandsons each wager their own karmic conditions.
"Not by earth, not by heaven; remove the raincoat and there is nothing to transmit. Later, Daowu arrived at Jingkou and encountered Jiashan ascending the hall.
A monk asked, "What is the Dharma-body? Jiashan replied, "The Dharma-body has no form. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma-eye?
Jiashan replied, "The Dharma-eye has no flaw. Daowu could not help but let out a laugh. Jiashan then descended from his seat.
[Dongshan] asked Wugu: "I have just been responding to this monk's words; there must have been something incorrect that caused you, Reverend, to laugh.
I hope you will not withhold your compassion and instruct me. Wugu said: "The Master is equally one who has appeared in the world, yet you still do not yet have a teacher.
Dongshan said: "In what way was I incorrect? I hope you will explain it for me. Wugu said: "I, for my part..."
He did not say anything. [Zhaozhou] requested that the Master go instead to Chanzi at Huating. Shanshan asked, "What is this man like?
I said, "This man has not a single tile above him and not a needle’s point of ground below him. If you, Master, wish to go, you must go in disguise."
Zhaozhou dispersed his followers and packed his belongings, proceeding directly to Huating. As soon as he saw him, Zhaozhou asked, "Virtuous One, in what monastery do you reside?
Shishuang said, "I do not reside in a monastery; if I were to reside, it would not be like this. Zhaozhou asked, "If it is not like this, what is it like?
Shishuang said, "It is not the Dharma of the present moment. Zhaozhou asked, "From where have you learned this? Shishuang said, "It is not something grasped by the ears or the eyes."
When he arrived, the Master said, "A single phrase that fits the head is a tethering stake for ten thousand kalpas. He then said, "The fishing line hangs down a thousand feet;
the intent lies in the deep pool. Three inches away from the hook—why do you not speak? As Shanzhao was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him with an oar and knocked him into the water.
As soon as Shanzhao climbed back onto the boat, the Master said again, "Speak! Speak! As Shanzhao was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him once more. Shanzhao...
He attained a sudden and great awakening, whereupon he nodded his head three times. The Master said, "The line on the tip of the pole is for you to play with;
yet, by not disturbing the clear waves, its meaning is naturally distinct. Daowu then asked, "When casting the line and throwing the hook, what is your intention, Master?

The Master replied, "The line hangs in the green water; whether it floats or sinks is beyond the reach of thought. Daowu said, "Your words carry the source but leave no path; your tongue speaks while—"
[Shishuang] did not speak. The Master said, "The waves of the river have been fished through until at last the golden-scaled fish is encountered.
Shishuang then covered his ears. The Master said, "So it is, so it is. He then instructed him, saying, "In the future, you must leave no trace where you hide your body;
do not hide your body where there is no trace. For thirty years I was at Yaoshan, and I clarified only this matter. You have now attained it. Hereafter..."
"Do not dwell in cities, provincial capitals, or villages. Go instead into the deep mountains;
at the edge of your mattock, seek out one or two [true heirs] and ensure that the lineage continues without interruption. When Shanshan was about to depart, he looked back again and again.
The Master then called out, "Dārali! Shanshan turned his head. The Master held up his oar and said, "You thought there was something else. Thereupon, he overturned the boat and entered the water.
Shi. Chan Master Huisheng of Bishu in Xuanzhou went to visit Dongshan. The Master asked, "What have you come for? Dongshan replied, "I have come to attend upon the Master.
The Master said, "If it is for the sake of attending, why do you move these two pieces of skin [your lips]? Dongshan was speechless.
A questioner asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A cat climbing a pillar. The questioner said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "Go ask the pillar."
Cen Master Baiyan of Ezhou in Huguang was visited by Dongshan and his senior companion, Master Mi. The Master asked, "Where have you two venerable monks come from?
Dongshan replied, "From Hunan. The Master asked, "What is the surname of the Military Governor? Dongshan said, "He has no surname."
The Master asked, "What is its name? He replied, "It cannot be named. The Master asked, "Is there no one who manages affairs? He replied, "There is naturally the Chancellor's Secretariat.
The Master asked, "Is there no coming and going? He replied, "There is no coming and going. The Master said, "How can there be no coming and going? Shan shook his sleeves and departed.
The next morning, the Master entered the hall and called to the two senior monks, saying, "Yesterday, when the old monk was facing the Kalyāṇamitra..."
Lanxi’s turn of phrase did not accord with him, so he was unsettled all night. He now requested the *śrāmaṇera* to provide another turn of phrase;
if it pleased the old monk, he would open the gruel and stay together for the summer retreat. Lanxi said, "Please ask the Master. The Master said:
"How about coming and going? Shanshan said, "It would be too dignified for you to do so. The Master then opened the rice gruel and they spent the summer retreat together.
When the novice Gao of Lizhou first visited Yaoshan, the Mountain asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from Mount Heng. The Mountain asked, "Where are you going?
The Master replied, "I am going to Jiangling to receive the full precepts. The Mountain asked, "What is the purpose of receiving the precepts? The Master replied, [silently].
[The Master] said, "I wish to escape birth and death. Mount [Shan] said, "There is one person who does not receive the precepts, and for whom there is no birth and death to escape.
Do you know this yet? The Master said, "If that is so, then what use are the Buddha’s precepts? Mount Shan said, "This śrāmaṇera still has his teeth hanging from his lips.
The Master bowed and withdrew. Daowu came forward to stand in attendance. Mount Shan said, "Just now there was a lame-footed śrāmaṇera..."
The śrāmaṇera replied, "He has a little bit of breath. I said, "One must not yet place full trust in this; you must further examine him before it is settled.

That evening, as he was ascending the hall for the formal discourse, the Master called out, "Where was that śrāmaṇera from this morning? The Master stepped forward from the assembly and stood there. The Master asked:
"I have heard that Chang'an is very bustling. Do you know this? The Master said, "In my country, all is peaceful. Fayan (in a variant version) said, "[Who] says so?

Shan said, "Did you obtain this from reading the sutras, or did you obtain it from seeking instruction? The Master said, "I did not obtain it from reading the sutras, nor did I obtain it from seeking instruction.
Shan said, "There are many who do not read the sutras and do not seek instruction; why is it that they do not obtain it? The Master [remained silent].
He said, "It is not that one cannot speak of it; it is simply that one is unwilling to accept it. Master Shishuang looked at Daowu and Yunyan and said, "Do you not believe what I have said?
One day, the Master took his leave of Yaoshan. Yaoshan asked, "Where are you going?
The Master replied, "I am causing some disturbance in the assembly, so I shall go to the side of the road and pitch a thatched hut there to provide tea and soup for those who pass by. Yaoshan said:
"The matter of birth and death is great. Why do you not receive the precepts? The Master said, "Knowing such matters as these, one simply rests;
what further would you call 'precepts'? Deshan said, "Since you are thus, you must not leave my side. From time to time, I wish to see you.
After the Master had stayed at the hermitage, he returned one day and encountered rain. Deshan said, "You have come. The Master said:
Shishan said, "It is quite damp. The Master said, "I do not beat this drum or play these pipes. Yunyan said, "There is no hide;
what drum could one beat? Daowu said, "There is no drum; what hide could one beat? Shishan said, "Today there is truly a magnificent musical performance.
[The Master] asked: "In a single phrase, is there anything that cannot be encompassed? The Master said, "Not in accordance [with conventional logic]."
Once, while at Youshan, during a vegetarian feast, the Master himself beat the drum. The Teacher (Baizhang) entered the hall dancing while holding an alms bowl.
Youshan then threw down the drumstick and asked, "Which chorus is this? The Teacher replied, "This is the second chorus. Youshan asked, "What is the first chorus?
The Teacher went to the rice bucket, scooped up a ladleful of rice, and immediately left.
Li Ao, the Prefect of Dingzhou, had long admired the transformative power of Yaoshan. Although he repeatedly invited him, Yaoshan did not go. Li Ao then went in person to visit him.

Yaoshan held a scripture volume and paid him no attention. An attendant said, "The Governor is here. Li Ao, being of a narrow and impatient temperament, remarked, "A face is not as good as a reputation," and brushed his sleeves, departing at once.
Yaoshan said, "How can the Governor hold his ears so dear while disparaging his eyes? Upon hearing this, the Governor turned back.
He bowed in thanks and asked, "What is the Way? Shanshan pointed up and down and said, "Do you understand? Baoshou replied, "I do not understand.
Shanshan said, "Clouds in the blue sky; water in the pitcher. Baoshou was filled with joy and prostrated himself, reciting this verse:
"Refined is my physical form, like that of a crane; Beneath a thousand pines, two cases of scripture. I came to ask about the Way, and there was no further word."
"Clouds in the blue sky, water in the jar. Yongshou asked again, "What are precepts, concentration, and wisdom?
Shishuang said, "In my place, there are no such worldly furnishings. Yongshou could not fathom the fundamental meaning.
Shishuang said, "If you, Governor, wish to take charge of this matter, you must stand atop the highest mountain peak and walk upon the deepest ocean floor; [discard] all things of the inner chamber."
If one cannot relinquish [them], it becomes a leakage. An old master was sitting alone; a practitioner asked him, "While you sit upright in this hall, what is your primary concern?

The master replied, "The Dharma-body is still and silent; there is no going and no coming. (Fayan commented elsewhere: "What have you come here to do? Fandeng commented elsewhere: "This is not your realm.")

Compiled by the monk (Chao Yong), Abbot of Shenggan Chan Temple in the Capital.
Verified and presented by the Abbot of Kyoto’s Kokegwan-ji (Subject Monk) Chōkai:
The Three Generations Descending from Qingyuan.
When Chan Master Cuiwei Wuxue of Jingzhao Prefecture first visited Chan Master Danxia Yan, he asked, "What is the teacher of all Buddhas?
Danxia scolded him, saying, "Fortunately, you are already pitiable enough; why must you insist on taking up the towel and broom? The Master then stepped back three paces.

Xia said, "Wrong. The Master stepped forward. Xia said, "Wrong, wrong. The Master lifted one foot, turned his body once, and went out. Xia said, "You have attained it, indeed; yet you have brought shame upon all the Buddhas and Masters. From this, he understood the essential meaning. Later, while staying there, Touzi asked him, "I wonder, when the Second Patriarch first saw Bodhidharma, what did he obtain? The Master said, "When you see me now, what do you obtain? Touzi said, "I obtain nothing. The Master said, "The Second Patriarch also obtained nothing. Touzi said, "If so, why did he receive the transmission of the robe and bowl? The Master said, "It was because he had no other way. Touzi said, "If that is so, then the robe and bowl are not the true Dharma. The Master said, "How could they not be the true Dharma? If it were not for them, how could the Way have been transmitted from generation to generation? Touzi said, "If that is so, then the robe and bowl are the true Dharma. The Master said, "If that were so, then the robe and bowl would be like a worldly object. If they were like a worldly object, how could they be the true Dharma? Therefore, although the robe and bowl are the true Dharma, they are not the ultimate principle. Although the ultimate principle is the true Dharma, it is not the robe and bowl. It is only because the robe and bowl are the true Dharma that the ultimate principle is revealed. It is only because the ultimate principle is the true Dharma that the robe and bowl are transmitted. Thus, although the robe and bowl are the true Dharma, they are not the ultimate principle; and although the ultimate principle is the true Dharma, it is not the robe and bowl. This is why the Second Patriarch received the robe and bowl and also received the ultimate principle. Touzi said, "What is the ultimate principle? The Master remained silent. Touzi said, "Why do you remain silent? The Master said, "Because I am speaking. Touzi said, "If so, you are not speaking. The Master said, "If I were speaking, I would be deceiving you. Touzi said, "If you are not deceiving me, then you are speaking. The Master said, "If I were speaking, I would be deceiving you. Touzi said, "If you are not deceiving me, then you are not speaking. The Master said, "If I were not speaking, I would be deceiving you. Touzi said, "If you are not deceiving me, then you are both speaking and not speaking. The Master said, "If I were both speaking and not speaking, I would be deceiving you. Touzi said, "If you are not deceiving me, then you are neither speaking nor not speaking. The Master said, "If I were neither speaking nor not speaking, I would be deceiving you. Touzi said, "If you are not deceiving me, then you are both speaking and not speaking, and neither speaking nor not speaking. The Master said, "If I were both speaking and not speaking, and neither speaking nor not speaking, I would be deceiving you. Touzi said, "If you are not deceiving me, then you are neither deceiving nor not deceiving. The Master said, "If I were neither deceiving nor not deceiving, I would be deceiving you. Touzi said, "If you are not deceiving me, then you are both deceiving and not deceiving, and neither deceiving nor not deceiving. The Master said, "If I were both deceiving and not deceiving, and neither deceiving nor not deceiving, I would be deceiving you.
