What was attained? Touzi attained sudden enlightenment to the fundamental principle.

One day, while the Master was walking in the Dharma Hall, Touzi stepped forward to greet him with a bow and asked, "How does the Master show people the secret essence of the West? The Master paused for a short while.
Touzi said, "I beg the Master to grant me instruction. The Master replied, "Do you want another ladle of foul water? Touzi then prostrated himself.
"Thank you," [the Master] said. The Master added, "Do not be so clumsy. The monk said, "When the time comes, the roots and sprouts will grow of themselves.
The Master was making offerings to the Arhats. A monk asked, "Danxia burned the wooden Buddha; why does the Master make offerings to the Arhats?

The Master said, "Even if one were to burn them, they could not be burned. As for making offerings, let it be as you wish. The monk asked, "If one makes offerings to the Arhats, do the Arhats still come?"
"No. The Master said, "Do you eat rice every day? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "There are few who possess such spiritual acuity.
A monk from Xingkong Chan Master of Xiaoyi Temple in Jizhou came to visit. The Master extended his hand to show it to him. The monk stepped forward and then retreated.
The Master said, "Both your parents have passed away; why do you not show even a hint of grief on your face? The monk laughed heartily. The Master said:
After a short while, as the *ācārya* was raising a lament, a monk performed a somersault and left. The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven! The monk bowed and withdrew.

When the person had finished their attendance, the Master asked, "Going off like that—does it accord with the principles of the Buddha-dharma? The monk replied, "I am bound to be tongue-tied. The Master said, "And what about this old monk?

The monk replied, "I have never been a skilled hand. The Master said, [laughing]... (Note: The final sentence fragment "The Master" indicates the narrative continues, likely with the Master responding to the monk's admission of his lack of skill.)

The Master then straightened his body and joined his palms; the monk likewise joined his palms. The Master then struck downward three times with his palm. The monk brushed out his sleeves and departed. The Master said:
"The crow does not go before, the hare does not follow behind. How many people here run about in bewilderment? Only you, O Acharya, have realized the source;
your tongue is tied, for how could it ever cling to emptiness or existence?"
A monk from Mikkō arrived for an audience. He circumambulated the Master three times, struck the meditation seat, and said, "If I do not see the true host, I shall never descend from this assembly.
The Master asked, "Where have you been wandering in your conceptual consciousness? The monk replied, "Indeed, it is not there. The Master then struck him with a staff.
The monk said, "I nearly fell into conceptual consciousness. The Master said, "At the edge of the village grass, one encounters..."
"Ha! What words can there be for this?
Zen Master Yian of Mount Danxia was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "What is the venerable one?"
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then there is no distinction. The Master said, "Who told you that?
Chan Master Bentai once presented a portrait of himself to a monk. The Master said, "If this were me, to whom else would I present it?"
The monk said, "How could this be outside of one's allotted lot? The Master said, "If it is not outside of your allotted lot, then you take it back.

As the monk prepared to take it back, the Master struck him, saying, "This is precisely being overreaching and acting beyond your lot. The monk said, "If that is so, then I must present it to the Master. The Master said:
"Seize him! Seize him!
When a monk from Silla came to visit Master Xiantian of Changsha—a successor of Master Dachuo—he unfurled his sitting cloth and was about to prostrate when the Master seized him.
[The Master] said, "Before you left your own country, try to bring back a single phrase. The monk remained silent.
The Master then pushed him out, saying, "When he asked for one phrase, you spoke two. The monk bowed and spread his sitting mat.
The Master said, "If you understand it here, you will have wasted your entire life. The monk said, "If I do not understand it here, what then? The Master said, "Not here..."
"In what place do you understand? Where else could you possibly understand? He then struck him out. A monk came to attend upon the Master.
As soon as he spread out his sitting mat, the Master said, "There is no need for seasonal greetings; bring me back the principle of the time before patterns and traces had arisen.
The monk said, "I have a mouth; it would be idle to keep it mute. Why do you toil so hard to seek a fan for the month of December? The Master raised his staff, making a gesture to strike. The monk—
The Master seized him and said, "Return to me the principle that existed before I even raised the staff. The teacher replied, "Those who follow me go north or south;
those who do not follow me die staying in the east or west. [The monk] said, "Setting aside following and not following for a moment, I ask the Master to bring forth the east, west, south, and north.
The Master then struck him. Piyun arrived and, as soon as he entered the abbot’s quarters, the Master asked, "Before you have seen the East..."
When the old man had passed away, [the Master] asked, "How do you act for the sake of sentient beings? He replied, "I see only clouds arising over the azure peaks;
who knows the moon has fallen into the cold pond? The Master said, "Even this much is hard to find. He asked, "Is it not because you have not yet seen [it]? The Master then gave a shout.
Yunzhan spread his two hands. The Master said, "For one who falsely accuses others, what limit can there be? Yunzhan covered his ears and departed.
The Master said, "This fellow has died for the rest of his life. Luo Ping came to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? Ping said, "From Nanxi.
The Master said, "Have you brought news from Nanxi? Ping said, "The 'news' has already vanished; the 'message' has not yet ceased."
The Master said, "The most bitter thing is not yet having ceased. Zhizhenping asked, "Tell me, what is it that has not yet ceased?

The Master said, "Once you have seen my face, for a thousand years you will forget your name. Zhizhenping shook his sleeves and left. The Master said, "What limit is there to one who possesses the hand that handles a dead snake?
A monk came to pay his respects; as he was about to bow, the Master said, "Wild fox! What have you seen that you bow so readily? The monk said, "..."
"Old bald slave! Having seen what, do you ask such a question? The Master said, "Alas, alas! Today the Immortal Heaven has forgotten the past and lost the future.
[The monk] said, "Nevertheless, when one attains it, one ultimately does not compensate for what was lost. The Master said, "How could it not be so?"
[The monk] asked, "Who is it that finds this sweet? The Master laughed heartily and said, "Far, far indeed! The monk looked around in all directions and then departed.
While a monk was standing in attendance at Fuzhou Ciguang Chan Master’s [place], the Master opened his chest with his hand and asked, "Do you understand the old monk's business?
The monk replied, "There is still this one remaining. The Master then covered his chest and said, "It is not that it is too obvious. The monk asked, "What is there?"
"Where is there no place to avoid? The Master said, "There truly is no place to avoid. [The monk] asked, "What about right now? The Master then struck him.
Dadian Tong was a successor of Chan Master Sanping Yizhong of Zhangzhou.
He was the son of the Yang family of Fuzhou. Initially, he studied under Shigong, who was constantly drawing a bow...
With bow drawn and arrow fixed, ready for the opportune moment, Master Guǒ approached the Dharma seat. Guǒ said, "Behold the arrow!
The Master then pushed open his chest and said, "This is an arrow that kills people. What about an arrow that gives life? Guǒ snapped the bowstring three times, whereupon the Master bowed.
Guǒ said, "For thirty years I have drawn my bow and fixed my arrows, yet I have only managed to shoot half a saint. He then broke the bow in two.

[The Master] spoke of the bow and arrow. Later, he visited Dadian and brought up the previous conversation. Dadian said, "Since it is the arrow of a living person, why did you identify it by the bowstring?
Ping had no reply. Dadian said, "Thirty years from now, it will be difficult to find anyone who can bring up this story.
The Master asked Dadian, "Without pointing east or marking west, please give me a direct indication. Dadian said, "Youzhou."

At the river crossing stood a stone figure crouching. The Master said, "This is still like pointing east while marking west. Huangbo Duanji said, "If one were a phoenix chick, one would not seek it elsewhere. The Master prostrated.
Duanji said, "If you do not have the subsequent phrase, the preceding talk will be difficult to bring to completion.
Ascending the hall, [Duanji] said: "People nowadays who come forth all study running after things and creating fabrications, taking these as their own eyes."
What correspondence is there? Do you wish to study? There is no need for anything else; each of you has your own fundamental task. Why do you not realize it?
Merely having such a mind full of resentment and speech full of frustration—what benefit is there in that? I have explained it clearly to you:
if you seek the path of cultivation, as well as the gates of transformation established by the various sages, there are the texts of the Great Canon.
"In this matter of the School Gate (the Chan/Zen tradition), you must by no means apply your mind incorrectly.
A monk asked, "In the School Gate, is there still a path of study? The Master said, "There is one path as slippery as moss. The monk asked, "Can a student still grasp it?"
The Master said, "Do not conceive a thought; you look for yourself. A questioner asked, "What is it like when the black bean has not yet sprouted?
The Master said, "Even the Buddha does not know. A lecturer-monk asked, "I have no doubts regarding the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.
What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "An ox-tail whisk made of tortoise hair and a staff made of rabbit horns. Great Virtue, hide these away."
"Where is it? he asked. [The monk] replied, "Turtle hair and rabbit horns—how could they exist? The Master said, "The flesh weighs a thousand catties, yet the wisdom lacks a single grain.
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "If you people have never encountered a true teacher, that is not acceptable.
But if you have encountered a master of the Way, you ought to grasp some measure of his intent. Then, in mountain ravines, eating wood and wearing grass, you should act accordingly."
"Go! Only then will there be a slight degree of correspondence. If you rush about seeking to understand the meaning of words and phrases, you are already ten thousand *li* away from your hometown.
Take care! He asked the attendant, "What is your surname? The attendant replied, "It is the same as the Master's. The Master said:
"You say you know what Sanping’s surname is. The other said, "Where is the question? The Master said, "When did you ask me?
The other said, "Who is it that asks about the surname? The Master said, "Out of consideration for your beginner's mind, I grant you thirty blows.
The Master had a verse which says: "This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing; There is no further sound or form to present to you. If you understand this point completely,"

"No matter. As for essence and function, what does it matter whether they are divided or not? After the master had ascended the seat, a Daoist stepped forth from the assembly, moving from east to west, while a monk moved from west to east.
The Master said, "Just now, that Daoist actually possessed insight; you monks have not yet reached it.
The Daoist came forward and bowed, saying, "I thank the Master for his guidance. The Master struck him. The monk then came forward and bowed, saying, "I beg the Master..."
The Master also struck him. He then addressed the assembly, saying, "Regarding these two cases, how would you resolve them?
Is there anyone who can resolve them? He asked this three times, but the assembly remained silent. The Master said, "Since no one can resolve them, I shall resolve them myself.
Thereupon, he cast down his staff and returned to his quarters.
Chan Master Benkong of Majie Mountain ascended the hall and said: "In these very activities and movements, can you accord with your original patriarch?
If you can accord with it, then throughout the twelve periods of the day, there is no principle of empty waste. If you cannot accord with it," [he continued].
"Tea-drinking conversation" is often referred to as "tea-talk. A monk then asked, "How can one avoid it being considered tea-talk?
The Master said, "Do you even know what a mouth is? The monk asked, "What is the mouth? The Master said, "You do not even recognize two pieces of skin.
The monk asked, "What is the original patriarch? The Master said, "Do not drag this up in front of the assembly."
The Master said, "The father relies on the mother. He continued, "The assembly has departed with joy. The Master said, "Try to point out the nature of the assembly for me.
The monk bowed. The Master said, "He often says that one nature is all natures. As the monk was about to offer a word in reply, the Master said:
"I have brought my lifelong eye for traveling the path to naught; I ask you to set aside all present-day phrases and please, Master, point directly to the original nature.
The Master said, "Since you first became deluded about the source, how much time has passed? He replied, "I have now received the Master’s instruction."
The Master said: "If I were to point it out to you, you would immediately lose the source. [The student] asked: "How is it then? The Master presented this verse:

"The mind is the substance of nature; nature is the function of the mind. Mind and nature are one as such—who distinguishes them, who shares in them? To wander outside of reality is to lose the source; even this is difficult to penetrate.
From antiquity to the present, ordinary people and sages alike are like illusions, like dreams."
Cen Shenhui held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying: "If I hold it up, you immediately apply intellectual reasoning to the moment before it was held up;
if I do not hold it up, you immediately exercise mastery over the moment when it is held up. Now tell me:"
"Wherein does this old monk serve others? At that time, a monk came forward and said, "I dare not arbitrarily create complications.

The Master said, "I know you, Dharma-uncle, do not act beyond your station. The monk said, "In low places there is more than enough to level them; in high places one observes that they are insufficient.
The Master said, "To add complications upon complications. The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Covering one's nose while stealing a fragrance."
Vainly inviting guilt.
When Chan Master Shandao of Shishi in Tanzhou was a *śrāmaṇera*, Changzi sent him to receive the full precepts, saying to him:
He said, "On your day of return, you must go to Stonehead’s place to pay your respects. After the Master had received the precepts, he went to visit Stonehead.
One day, while following Stonehead on a mountain excursion, Stonehead said, "You and I shall cut down those trees in front of us so they do not obstruct me."
The Master said, "Do not bring the blade. Tou then drew his sword and held it out upside down. The Master said, "Why do you not come from that side? Tou said, "What would you do with that side?
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. He then returned to Changzi. Changzi asked, "Did you go to Shitou?
The Master replied, "I went, but I did not receive a name. Changzi asked, "From whom did you receive the precepts?"
The Master said, "Do not rely on others. Zhizang said, "If it is so there, how is it here with me?
The Master said, "Do not contradict it. Zhizang said, "You are being too talkative. The Master said, "Your tongue has never even touched it.
Zhizang shouted, "Novice, get out! The Master then went out. Zhizang said, "How could you have failed to meet the right person? The Master then... [continued].
During a period of monastic purging, he became a practitioner and lived in a stone grotto.
Whenever he saw a monk, he would raise his staff and say, "All Buddhas of the three periods of time arise entirely from this. Few who encountered him attained a profound resonance with his meaning.
When Changsha heard of this, he said, "If I were to see him, I would immediately have him put down his staff and convey another message. Sansheng then responded with these words.
This was recognized as the words of Changsha. Hearing that Sansheng had missed the mark, Xingshan went in person to Shishi.

Seeing that Master [Shishi] was accompanied by a crowd of monks from Xingshan, he hid himself and entered the rice-hulling shed to hull rice. Xingshan said, "It is not easy for an attendant to receive guests;
it is difficult for this poor monk to digest. The Master replied, "Serve it up in an open-hearted bowl; cover it with a lidless platter."
"Take it away! What do you mean by saying it is difficult to digest? Xing then desisted. Yangshan asked, "As for Buddha and the Way, how far apart are they?
The Master said, "The Way is like an open hand; the Buddha is like a clenched fist. Yangshan asked, "Ultimately, what is the definitive realization that can be trusted and relied upon?
The Master struck the air three times with his hand and said, "There is no such thing. There is no such thing. Yangshan said, "..."
"Must one still rely on examining the teachings? The Master said, "The Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings are matters external to one's own nature.
If you set yourself in opposition to them, this constitutes the duality of mind and objects, with both subject and object operating together;

this gives rise to all manner of views and is merely wild wisdom—it is not yet sufficient to be called the Way. If you do not set yourself in opposition to them, there is not even a single thing. Therefore, the Patriarch..."
"The Way has originally not a single thing. You do not see this. When an infant emerges from the womb, can one say, "I understand the teachings," or "I do not understand the teachings"?
At such a time, one does not yet know whether there is the principle of Buddha-nature or the absence of Buddha-nature.
By the time one grows up, various kinds of intellectual understanding emerge, and one then says, "I am capable" and "I understand. One does not realize that all of this—
These are adventitious afflictions (*āgantuka-kleśa*). Among the sixteen aspects of the noble truths, the conduct of an infant is supreme.

When one is "laughing and harmonious," it serves as a metaphor for the practitioner of the Path who has abandoned the mind of conceptual discrimination and grasping or rejecting; thus, the infant is praised as a fitting analogy to be adopted.
If one claims that an infant is the Way, people today have misunderstood. One night, the Master was gazing at the moon with Yangshan.
Yangshan asked, "When this moon is a crescent, where does the full circle go? When it is full, where does the crescent go? The Master said, "When it is a crescent, the full circle is hidden;
when it is full, the crescent remains. (Yunyan said: "When it is a crescent, the full circle remains; when it is full, there is no crescent.")
[The Master] said, "When it is pointed, it is not pointed; when it is round, it is not round. When Yangshan was taking his leave, the Master saw him out the door and called out, "Dharma brother!"
Shan assented. The Master said, "Do not go straight ahead; instead, turn back here. He asked, "Have you been to Mount Wutai?
The Master replied, "I have been there. He asked, "Did you see Mañjuśrī? The Master replied, "I saw him. He asked, "What did Mañjuśrī say to you, traveler?
The Master replied, "Mañjuśrī said, 'Your biological parents are in the deep grass.'"
Chan Master Qingzhu of Mount Shishuang in Tanzhou, a successor in the fourth generation under Daowu Zhi Chan Master of the Qingyuan lineage,
was a native of the Chen family of Xingan in Luling. He relied upon the Fourth [Patriarch] of Hongjing...

When Master Shanyuan was tonsured, he went to Luoyang to study the Vinaya teachings. Although he understood the rules of what was permitted and prohibited, he ultimately remained within the gradualist tradition.
Upon returning to Mount Gui, he served as the rice steward. One day, while sifting rice, Guishan said, "Do not scatter the donors' property."
The Master said, "I did not scatter it. Baizhang picked up a grain from the ground and asked, "You say you did not scatter it;
what is this? The Master had no reply. Baizhang said, "Do not underestimate this single grain. Hundreds of thousands of grains all arise from this one grain.
The Master said, "Hundreds of thousands of grains arise from this one grain, but I wonder from where this one grain arises?"
"From where does it arise? Baizhang laughed heartily and returned to his quarters. That evening, Baizhang ascended the hall and said, "The assembly, there are worms in the rice;
everyone, look well! Later, he visited Daowu and asked, "What is Bodhi as it meets the eye?
Daowu called out, "Attendant! The attendant responded, "Yes? Daowu said, "Fill the water pitcher. After a long while, he then asked the Master, "Just now..."
When [Nanyue] came to ask what it was, the Master was about to raise his hand when I suddenly rose and departed.
At this, the Master had an awakening. As I was about to pass away, I spoke these words: "In my heart there is something that has long been a source of affliction.

Who can remove it for me? The Master said, "Both the mind and the object are non-existent; to try to remove them only increases the affliction. I said, "Excellent! Excellent! Thereafter, the Master withdrew from the world and lived in obscurity.
He lived as a layman at Tiaojia Village in Liuyang, Changsha. He would travel there in the morning and reside there in the evening, yet no one was able to recognize him.

Later, a monk came from Dongshan, and the Master asked him, "What sayings or instructions did the Master give to his disciples? The monk replied, "Upon returning from the summer retreat, he ascended the hall and said:"
In early autumn, as the end of summer approached, the brothers were about to depart—one heading east and the other west.

[Zhaozhou] said, "You must go to a place ten thousand *li* away where there is not even an inch of grass. After a long silence, he asked, "As for that place ten thousand *li* away where there is not an inch of grass—how does one go there?

The monk asked, "Has anyone ever offered a response to this? [Zhaozhou] replied, "No. The monk asked, "Why not say, 'The moment you step out the door, it is already grass'? When the monk returned, he related this to Dongshan.
Shan said: "These are the words of a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) for fifteen hundred people. Because of this, the handle of the bag is finally revealed;
when the fruit ripens, its fragrance wafts abroad. At the request of the assembly to serve as abbot, he ascended the hall and said: "All of you, you each have your own fundamental task."
There is no need for frantic seeking. There is no place for you to judge right and wrong; there is no place for you to chew and gnaw upon.
The teachings of a single lifetime are intended to rectify the hands and feet of people of this age. Whatever has its origin invariably falls into the present moment.

Only when one reaches the Dharma-body, which is no-body, is this the ultimate limit of the teaching school. Yet we śramaṇas have no path of entry at all. To differentiate is to err; not to differentiate is to remain seated.
[The Master] was covered in mud and water. It was merely due to the deluded speech of the mind regarding what was seen and heard.

A monk asked, "What is the meaning of [the Master’s] coming from the West? The Master said, "A single stone in mid-air. The monk bowed. The Master asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand.

The Master said, "It is fortunate that you do not understand. If you had understood, I would have smashed your head. A monk asked, "What is the matter of the Master’s own fundamental division? The Master...
[The Master] said, "Does Shitou still break into a sweat? Question: "When one arrives at this point, why is it that one cannot speak?
The Master said, "To put a mouth on the soles of one's feet. Question: "Does the True Body appear in the world or not? The Master said, "It does not appear. Question: "What then of the True Body?
The Master said, "The opening of a glass bottle. Question: "What is the Master’s profound [teaching]? The Master said, "The opening of a glass bottle."
"In the deep place. The Master said: "The hairless chain rattles at both ends. While the Master was in the abbot’s quarters, a monk asked from outside the window:
"Within the span of a few feet, why do I not behold your countenance? The Master said: "It has never been hidden throughout the entire world."
The monk brought this up to Xuefeng, asking, "Regarding the statement, 'It is never hidden throughout the entire world,' what is its meaning?

Xuefeng said, "Where is it not Shishuang? When the Master (Dongshan) heard this, he said, "What kind of desperate urgency is this old fellow in? Upon hearing this, Xuefeng said, "I, the old monk, am at fault.

[Dongchan Qi said: "As for Xuefeng, did he understand Shishuang’s meaning or not? If he understood it, why did he say [the Master was] in a state of desperate urgency? If he did not understand it, how could Xuefeng have failed to understand? Nevertheless, the Dharma..."

Dongshan threw down his mattock and said, "Today I have not a single bit of strength. The Master said, "If you have no strength, how can you speak like this?
Dongshan said, "Do you suppose that one who possesses strength is the one [who speaks]? The Master desisted.
Lord Pei asked a monk, "When making offerings to the Buddha, does the Buddha eat? The monk said, "It is just as when you, Great Officer, perform sacrifices for your family."
The deity told the Great Master (Dafu), who related it to Yunyan. Yunyan said, "This monk has not yet left the household life. The Master asked, "What about you, Master?
Yunyan said, "There are several kinds of food; just bring them all down at once. Yunyan then asked the Master, "If they are brought down all at once, what then?
The Master said, "Close the bowl. Yunyan approved of this. A questioner asked: "When one ground is not seen..."

[The student] asked, "What is it like at the time of the second bhūmi? The Master said, "Are you not mistaken? What stage are you in? [The student] asked, "I beg the Master for a word regarding the matter of birth and death.
The Master said, "When did you die and come back? [The student] said, "I do not understand. I pray that the Master will explain."
The Master said, "If you do not understand, you must undergo a death before you can attain it. While the Master and Dongshan were walking, they suddenly saw a white rabbit leap out.
The Master said, "How magnificent! It is very much like a man in plain clothes being appointed as a high minister.
Dongshan said, "Old man, why do you speak such words? The Master asked, "What about you? Dongshan replied, "A family of generations of official rank, yet for a moment fallen into obscurity."
While the Master was threading a needle, Dongshan asked, "What are you doing? The Master replied, "Threading a needle. Dongshan said, "How is the matter of threading a needle?
The Master said, "Every stitch is like every other. Dongshan said, "We have been traveling together for twenty years, and this is the kind of talk you give.
The Master asked, "And what about you, Elder? Dongshan said, "It is like the great earth bursting into flames. The Master then questioned him further.
Dongshan said, "There is nothing that the reach of one's wisdom and knowledge does not traverse. At this point of direct cutting through, I beg the Master for a single word.

Dongshan replied, "How can you, my senior master, seek to claim merit? Thereupon, the Master was suddenly awakened; his subsequent utterances were extraordinary. Later, he [discussed this] with Dongshan.
They were crossing a single-plank bridge. Dongxian crossed it first. Picking up the wooden bridge, he said, "Come across! The Master called out, "Jia Acharya!
Thereupon, Dongxian lowered the bridge.
A monk asked Master Youxi: "When the great function manifests before one, and no rules or regulations remain—how is this?

The Master rose from his seat, walked once around the meditation platform, and sat back down. As the monk prepared to offer a word in response, the Master gave him a kick. The monk returned to his place and stood there.
The Master said, "You act thus, but I do not act thus; you do not act thus, yet I do act thus.
As the monk was about to offer further words, the Master gave him another kick and said, "Thirty years from now, my Way shall be widely practiced. A monk asked, "What is the Zen of the Patriarchs?
The Master said, "The clay ox steps forward at every pace. A monk asked, "When nowhere can it be encompassed," [how is it? The Master said, "The clay ox steps forward at every pace."
"What is it like at that time? The Master said, "At midnight, the stone man has no shadow; though he moves crosswise and lengthwise, his place of origin cannot be discerned.
Chan Master Shenzhou Cheng of Shipizhou was a successor of Chan Master Chanzi.
He was the son of the Liao family in Guangzhou. He left home at a young age and received the full precepts according to his years.

Observing the precepts, he studied the sutras and śāstras, becoming thoroughly proficient in the three trainings. He resided at Heilin Monastery in Runzhou. Prompted by the exhortations of Daowu, he went to visit Chuanzzi;

thus, the way of teacher and disciple was harmonized (the dialogue is found in the *Chuanzzi Zhang*). Respectfully following his final instructions, he withdrew from the world and set aside all artifice.

Soon thereafter, students gathered from all directions, their dwellings spreading out like stars as they sought his guidance morning and night. In the year Gengyin of the Xiantong era, the assembly...
Please open the Dharma-casket. Master Jia Shan ascended the hall and said: "Since the time of the Patriarchs, people have misunderstood; this has been handed down to the present day.
By taking the words and phrases of the Buddhas and Patriarchs as models for teaching others, they instead become madmen or those devoid of wisdom.
He merely points it out to you: that the absence of dharmas is itself the Way. The Way possesses not a single dharma; there is no Buddha to be accomplished and no Way to be attained."
It is attained. There is no dharma to be grasped; there is no dharma to be abandoned. Therefore, the old monk says: "Before one's eyes there is no dharma, yet the meaning lies before one's eyes.
This is not a dharma of the present moment. If you seek to learn from the Buddhas and patriarchs, such a person has not yet possessed the eye.

Why is this? Because they all depend upon their basis and lack autonomy. Fundamentally, they are merely lost within the vast expanse of birth and death; the nature of consciousness has no portion of freedom.
Even if one travels thousands of miles to seek a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), one must possess the correct eye to seek liberation from erroneous views.
One must definitively examine the birth and death before one’s eyes: do they truly exist, or do they truly not exist? If there is anyone who can definitively attain [this realization]...
I allow you to emerge from this. Those of superior capacity realize the Way upon hearing these words; those of middling or inferior capacity merely wander on like waves.
Why not settle the matter decisively within birth and death? Where else could you harbor doubts about the Buddhas or the Patriarchs? Let them take over your birth and death for you.
Wise people will laugh at you. If you do not understand, listen to another verse: Toiling to uphold the laws of birth and death, You seek only from the side of the Buddha.
Deluded before your very eyes regarding the true principle, You strike fire to search for bubbles.

A monk asked, "Regarding the meaning established by the patriarchs and the meaning of the teachings from of old, why does the Master, on the contrary, say there is none? The Master said, "If one does not eat for three years, there is nothing before one's eyes."
The hungry man said, "Since there is no such thing as a hungry person, why is it that I have not awakened? The Master replied, "It is precisely because awakening has deluded you, O Kalyāṇamitra.
He then showed him this verse: "Clearly, there is no dharma of awakening; The dharma of awakening, instead, deludes people.
Stretch out your two legs and sleep; There is neither falsehood nor truth. [He] asked about the twelve divisions of the teachings and the meaning of the Patriarchs' intent. The Master [responded]:...
"Why do you not allow others to ask? the Master said. "It is my sitting mat. The monk asked, "By what Dharma does the Master instruct people?

The Master said, "In empty space there is no path for a needle to hang upon; you, my son, labor in vain over the work of twisting thread. He asked again, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "The descendant of Golden Grain, the true body of Śāriputra, the profound mystery of the *wangxiang* (the non-apprehending)."
Talk. This is the den of the wild fox. Ascending the hall: Not knowing when dawn breaks; awakening does not depend on a teacher.

Leaping with scales at the Dragon Gate, one does not fall into the hands of the fisherman. It is simply that the mind does not lodge in private conditions, and the tongue does not cling to the original intent.

This is precisely where one may find a true知音 (zhīyīn—connoisseur). This is called the "innate talk" (*jùshēng huà*). If you harbor doubt regarding the original intent, you will ruin yourself, O *dàilǐ* (kalyāṇamitra)—like a weary fish.
The waters of the marsh have subsided; the dull-witted birds nest among the reeds. Clouds and water are not the *ācārya*; the *ācārya* is not clouds and water.
This old monk has attained mastery over clouds and water—how about you, *ācārya*? The Dharma Master from Xichuan, having finished his lectures, went on a pilgrimage to visit various teachers.
He went to Xiangzhou to visit Huayan and asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?

Huayan replied, "They are like the two wheels of a cart, or like the two wings of a bird. The Master said, "I had thought that the Chan gate possessed some special excellence; it turns out there is no difference at all."
He subsequently returned to Shu. Later, hearing that the Master’s Way had spread throughout all quarters, he sent a junior monk with this message to inquire after him.

The Master replied: "Carving sand lacks the discourse of engraving jade; weaving grasses contradicts the intention of a man of the Way. Upon hearing these words, the host performed a prostration from afar and said:

"I now realize that within the Chan school there is indeed a distinct excellence. [The Master] ascended the hall for instruction: "To hear and produce understanding is like applying colors beneath the ink; it is a mere painting upon the surface."
What was fresh before now becomes stale; long-accumulated things turn into illness. The green mountains and white clouds have never met since time immemorial.
When the shuttle-head is not caught by the warp-thread, the patterns may run wild, yet the meaning remains distinct. On the single path of auspiciousness, the wise know it to be sparse;
as for rootless auspicious grasses, the worthy do not prize them. Question: "What is the Way? The Master said: "The great sun overflows the eyes; ten thousand [things appear]."
"A village does not hang even a single cloud. [The student] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "In the clear, pure water, the swimming fish are dazzled.

[The student] asked, "What is the fundamental? The Master said, "Drinking water, one is not confused about its source. [The student] asked, "For what purpose did the ancients spread their hair to cover the mud?
The Master said, "The nine suns have been shot down, yet one speck of cloud still remains. When that single arrow falls to the ground, the whole world is plunged in darkness."
Hei asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "The wind blows through the lotus leaves, filling the pond with green;
ten li of traveler, one more stage. A monk asked, "When one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha, what then? The Master said, "You must brandish the sword.
If you do not brandish the sword, the fisherman will settle in his nest. Later, this monk asked Shishuang about "brushing away the dust and seeing the Buddha."
"How so? Shuang said, "He has no territory; where could one meet him? The monk returned and reported this to the Master.

After the Master had finished his discourse in the hall, he said, "In the establishment of the gate, I am not as good as Old Shuang; yet in the profound discourse that enters into principle, he is still a hundred paces behind me.
A monk asked, "What is it like when two mirrors reflect each other? The Master said, "The oyster reveals its priceless treasure; the dragon spits forth [the pearl]."
The Pearl Within the Belly. A monk asked, "What is the matter within silent stillness? The Master said, "The sleeping palace is empty.

After the Master had finished drinking tea, he personally brewed another bowl and passed it to his attendant. As the attendant was about to receive it, the Master withdrew his hand and said, "What is this?
The attendant was speechless. A lecturer asked, "If it were the meaning of the teachings, I would have no doubt. However, as for..."
"What is the matter within the Zen gate? The Master said, "This old monk only knows how to transform the raw into the cooked.
"Question: What is the principle of the ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*)? The Master said, "A stone grows a rootless tree;
the mountain contains unmoving clouds. "Question: What is a lion emerging from its cave? The Master said, "In the void there is no reflection; beneath one's feet wild clouds arise. The Master.
While serving as the head cook at Mount Gui, Guishan asked, "What vegetables are we eating today? The Master replied, "Two years under the same spring. Guishan said, "Attend well to your duties.
The Master replied, "The dragon dwells in the phoenix's nest. A monk asked, "How does one recognize the treasure within the house?
The Master replied, "In the midst of busyness, how can one become a person of leisure? A monk asked, "What is a 'concordant phrase'? The Master replied: [He remained silent].
He said, "The lotus leaf is round and round, as round as a mirror; the water chestnut horn is sharp and sharp, as sharp as an awl.
He asked again, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The wind blows the willow catkins like a ball;

the rain beats the pear blossoms and the butterflies fly. A monk asked, "What is 'one who is old and one who is not old'? The Master said, "The green mountains never move; the mountain stream flows forever."

Holding a *yeming* (night-illuminating) talisman in his hand, how many know when the sky breaks for dawn? Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "The golden crow and the jade hare vie with one another for brilliance.
When the sun is sat upon, the world is plunged into darkness. The upper lip and the lower lip have never known each other.
I tell you clearly: do not let your eyes look back at them. Why? Because the sun and moon are not sufficient to be called 'bright,' and the whole world is not sufficient..."
It is great. In the midst of emptiness, no adze is wielded; the skillful craftsman leaves no trace. Seeing one's nature, one does not retain the Buddha;
awakening to the Way, one does not preserve the teacher. As an ordinary old monk says: "To see Gautama with one's own eyes is like [viewing] yellow leaves.

The entire Great Canon of teachings is this old monk’s sitting mat; the original intent of the Patriarchs is a pair of worn-out straw sandals. It is better to go barefoot than to wear the finest shoes."
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "In this place, there is neither guest nor host. The monk asked, "With whom do you usually converse?
The Master said, "Mañjuśrī has already gone to fetch water; Samantabhadra has not yet returned with the flowers.
He ascended the hall and said, "I have lived on this mountain for twenty years, and I have never once raised the matters of the School of the Patriarchs (Zongmen). A monk asked, "I have heard..."
The Master said, "I have stayed on this mountain for twenty years, yet I have never once brought up a single matter concerning the School of the Lineage (Zongmen). Is this true or not?

The monk replied, "It is true. The monk then overturned the meditation seat, and the Master ceased speaking. On the following day, he requested that everyone be assembled for communal labor to dig a pit.
He ordered his attendant to invite the monks from the day before, saying, "For twenty years, this old monk has spoken meaningless words.
Today, I invite you, Venerable Ones, to beat this old monk to death and bury me in a pit! Invite him, invite him!

If you do not beat this old monk to death, then you, Venerable Ones, shall beat yourselves to death and bury yourselves in pits instead. When the monks returned to the hall, they packed their belongings and fled in secret.
He went up to the hall and said: "Apprehend the old monk at the tips of the hundred grasses; recognize the Son of Heaven in the midst of the bustling marketplace.
Touzi Heshang came to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Hunan. The Master asked, "Have you been to Shishuang?"
[The monk] said, "This is a main thoroughfare; everyone tries to pass through it, yet none can reach it. The Master asked, "I have heard that Shishuang has the 'Ball' (Qiuzi) koan. Is this true?
[The monk] said, "Even you, Master, must watch closely before you will succeed. The Master asked, "What is the Ball? [The monk] said, "It cannot be jumped out of.
The Master asked, "What is the Ball-stick? [The monk] said, "It has no hands or feet. The Master said, "Go for now, Old Monk."
The Master had not yet met with the *śrāmaṇera* when he ascended the seat the following day. The Master asked, "Was the one who arrived yesterday here?

The *śrāmaṇera* stepped forward and responded, "Yes. The Master said, "There is no dharma before the eyes; the intent lies before the eyes. It is not a dharma of the present moment; it is beyond the reach of ears and eyes.
The *śrāmaṇera* said, "Though you ask this today, it is nonetheless not so. The Master said, "A sliver of the moon is difficult to clarify; it is not—"
The Head said, "Don't stir up a boiling cauldron," and he made a gesture as if to overturn the meditation seat.
The Master said, "Wait, wait; in what way have you wronged this Senior? The Head raised his fist and said, "Can you endure this before your eyes?
The Master said, "A true practitioner, a true practitioner! The Head again made a gesture as if to overturn the meditation seat. The Master said, "Everyone, look! This one official..."
"Warrior General! If it comes to deploying forces at the gate, this mountain monk is not his equal; but as for discourse that accords with principle, he is still one rank below this mountain monk.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The eye does not hang upon the door; the mind does not dwell in the source.

Even when spiritual grass no longer grows, this is still but the station of the Five Heavens. The luster of the pearl and the essence of the moon are not yet the time of emergence. Here in this place..."
There is no old monk; at the head of the five paths there is no *ācārya*. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Jia Shan? The Master said, "A monkey carries its young back into the green peaks;
a bird carries a flower away before the azure cliffs. (Fayan said: "For twenty years I have understood this only as a discourse on the realm. Fushan Yuan said:

"Even if one does not understand it as a discourse on the realm, it is still not quite it. Why is that? 'The rhinoceros develops patterns on its horn from gazing at the moon; the elephant has flowers enter its tusks from being startled by thunder. The Master asked a monk, "What..."
"Where have you come from? he asked. "I have come from Dongshan," he replied. The Master said, "What words or phrases did Dongshan use to instruct his disciples?
"He usually teaches his students to train in three paths," he replied. "What are these three paths? the Master asked. "The Original Path, the Bird’s Path, and the Extended Hand," he replied.
The Master asked, "Do you truly have such words? "I truly do," he replied. The Master said, "A scholar carries his notes for a thousand miles; a man of the Way remains beneath the forest trees."
[The Master’s] Lament. On the seventh day of the eleventh month of the *xinchou* year of the Zhonghe era of the Tang Emperor Xizong, he summoned his attendants and said:
"I have discussed the Way with the assembly of monks for many years. The profound purport of the Buddha-dharma, each of you should know it yourselves.
My illusory body now reaches its end and shall depart. You must protect yourselves well, as you did when I was alive; do not act like the common worldlings, nor give way to despondency."
He sighed in regret. Having finished speaking, he suddenly passed away. He was enshrined in a stupa at his home mountain. His age was seventy-seven; his years since ordination were fifty-seven.
By imperial decree, he was posthumously titled Great Master Fuming, and his stupa was named Yongji.
Chan Master Lingzun of Anle Monastery on Mount Qingping in Ezhou was a successor of Chan Master Cuiwei. He was the son of the Wang family from Dongping.
When he first visited Cuiwei, he asked, "What is the true meaning of the coming from the West? Cuiwei replied, "Wait until there is no one else here, and I will tell you."
After a long silence, the Master said, "There is no one. He requested, "Please, Preceptor, speak. Xiangwei descended from his meditation seat and led the Master into a bamboo grove.
The Master spoke again, "There is no one. Please, Preceptor, speak. Xiangwei pointed to a bamboo stalk and said, "This stalk is so very long."
"How can that pole be so short? The Master understood the intent and went forth to reside at Dàtōng.

He ascended the hall and, citing the karmic conditions of his first meeting with Cuīwēi, said to the assembly: "The former master entered the mud and the water for my sake; it was I who failed to recognize what was good and what was bad.

From this point on, the Master extensively propagated the teachings and guided others. Subsequently, he moved to Qīngpíng. Ascending the hall, he addressed the assembly: "Venerable elders, as for going forth..."

Regarding the "Family" (Jiaren): you must first comprehend the Buddha’s intent before you can attain it. If you comprehend the Buddha’s intent, it does not depend on whether one is monastic or lay, male or female, noble or humble;
it simply requires that one find peace and ease according to the abundance or scarcity of one's household.

Venerable Elders, you have all long dwelt within the monasteries and have traveled extensively to study under venerable masters. So, how do you comprehend the Buddha’s intent? Come forth and let us deliberate together; do not merely harbor empty pride.
In the end, nothing will be accomplished and one's life will pass in vain. If you have not yet realized the Buddha’s intent,

then even if you were to emit water from your head and fire from your feet, burn your body and forge your arms, possess great wisdom and eloquence, gather a thousand or two thousand disciples, preach the Dharma like falling clouds and rain,
and cause heavenly flowers to shower down as you lecture— you would merely produce a heterodox teaching and engage in the contentious squabbling over right and wrong.
"You are still very far from the Buddha-dharma. Fortunately, you have encountered a time when the physical body [of the Buddha] is peaceful and healthy, and you have not met with various calamities;
why then do you not draw closer and apply some effort to realize the Buddha’s intent? Question: "What is the Great Vehicle (Mahāyāna)?
The Master said: "A well-rope. Question: "What is the Small Vehicle (Hīnayāna)? The Master said: "A string of coins. Question: "What is the 'Pure and Peaceful House'?"
Feng asked, "Master, [what is it like? The Master said, "A peck of flour makes three steamed cakes. He asked, "What is Chan?
The Master said, "A monkey climbing a tree, tail trailing behind. He asked, "What is 'with outflows' (sāsrava)? The Master said, "A bamboo strainer.
He asked, "What is 'without outflows' (anāsrava)? The Master said, "A wooden ladle. He asked, "When you present it face-to-face, what then? The Master said, "Handed over."

As the *dianzuo* (head cook), he employed various skillful means to guide sentient beings according to their capacities, never conforming to worldly sentiments. Whether acting in accordance with or contrary to circumstances, his teachings were expansive or concise as needed, transcending all conventional measures.
On the twenty-fifth day of the first month of the Bingyin year of the Tianyou era, he passed away at his native mountain. He was seventy-five years old.
By imperial decree, he was posthumously titled Chan Master Faxi, and his stupa was named Shanying.

Chan Master Datong of Touzi Mountain in Shu Prefecture was a native of the Liu family in Huaining County of that same province. In his youth, he followed Master Man of Baotang in Luoyang to receive the precepts.
Initially, he practiced the *ānāpāna* (breath-counting) meditation; subsequently, he studied the teachings of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, thereby illuminating the ocean of the nature (*dharmatā*).
He visited Cuiwei again and attained sudden enlightenment regarding the fundamental principle (the dialogue is found in the chapter on Cuiwei). Thereupon, he traveled freely throughout the land.
Later, returning to his native region, he took refuge on Mount Toutou, where he dwelt in a thatched hut. One day, Master Zhaozhou arrived at Tongcheng County.
The Master also came out from the mountains. Meeting him on the road, the Governor asked, "Are you not the Master of Touzi Mountain?
The Master said, "Give me some money for tea and salt. The Governor arrived at the hermitage first and sat down; the Master returned later, carrying an oil jar in his hand.
The Governor said, "I have long admired the Master of Touzi, but upon arriving, I see only an oil peddler. The Master said, "You..."
He recognized only the oil-seller, yet he did not recognize Touzi. The Governor asked, "What is Touzi?
The Master held up an oil jar and said, "Oil, oil. The Governor asked again, "When one who has died the great death comes back to life, what is it like? The Master said:

"Night travel is not permitted; you must arrive by the break of dawn. The Governor said, "I have already reported his whiteness; he has further reported his blackness. Ascending the hall, [the Master] said:
"All of you who come here intend to seek out fresh phrases and sentences, arranging four-six character couplets so that there is something worth saying in your mouths.
I, an old man, am somewhat lacking in strength; my lips and tongue are dull and slow, and I have no idle words to give."
"You! If you ask me anything, I shall answer you accordingly. There is nothing original or subtle that can reach you, nor do I teach you to rely on a fixed root.
I never speak of 'upward' or 'downward,' nor of Buddhas and Dharmas, nor of ordinary people and sages.
Nor do I maintain the bondage of sitting meditation. You all, manifesting a thousand transformations, are entirely carrying about your own self-arisen views."
In the future, you will receive the fruit of what you have done yourself. Here, I have nothing to give you; there is nothing, neither surface nor depth, to describe to you.
If anyone has a doubt, let them ask. A monk asked, "What is it like when neither the surface nor the depth can contain it?
The Master said, "You intend to plant your roots right here. He then descended from his seat. Another asked, "Within the Great Canon of the Teachings, is there anything extraordinary?"
The Master said: "To bring forth the Great Canon. Question: "What is the state when the eyes have not yet opened? The Master said:
"The eyes are pure, long, and wide like blue lotuses. Question: "All Buddhas and all Buddha-dharmas emerge from this sutra.
What is this sutra? The Master said: "By this name, you should uphold it. Question: "Withered wood..."
[The Master] said, "Is there also dragon-singing within? The Master said, "I say that within the skull there is the lion’s roar.
Question: "There is one Dharma that universally moistens all living beings. What is this one Dharma? The Master said, "It is raining. Question:
"When a single mote of dust contains the entire Dharma-realm, what then? The Master said, "That is already a multitude of motes. Question: "A student intends to... [The Master said: "Stop!"
When a practitioner wishes to cultivate the Way, how should they proceed? The Master said: "Empty space has never been subject to decay. The Chan guest Juyong came for an audience. The Master said:
"I, this old monk, have never uttered so much as a single word or half-sentence that could stick to the lips or teeth of those from all quarters.
Why do you insist on seeing me? Juyong said: "If I do not offer three prostrations upon arriving here, I simply will not feel at peace. The Master said: "You have left the household life."
The boy was so devoid of any record on a monument. Rong then circumambulated the meditation seat once and departed.
The Master said, "Having eyes but no ears, sitting by the fire in the sixth month. A monk asked, "Is it not the case that all sounds are the Buddha’s voice? The Master said, "Yes.
The monk said, "Master, do not let the sound of a boiling pot disturb you. The Master then struck him. A monk asked, "Regarding coarse words and subtle speech..."
"All return to the primary meaning; is this not so? The Master said, "It is. [The monk] asked, "Is it permissible to call the Master a 'head donkey'?
The Master then struck him. A monk asked, "What is the Tamer of the Ten Bodies? The Master descended from his meditation seat and stood there.
One day, the Master pointed to a stone in front of the hermitage and said to Xuefeng, "All Buddhas of the three periods of time are entirely contained within this. Xuefeng said, "..."
"You must know that there is something not contained within. The Master said, "An unpleasant lacquer bucket.

The Master and Xuefeng were traveling to Longmian, where there were two paths. Xuefeng asked, "Which one is the road to Longmian? The Master pointed at it with his staff. Xuefeng said, "Going east or going west?
The Master said, "An unpleasant lacquer bucket. Question: "What is it like when one is accomplished by a single blow? The Master said, "No."
This was a man of a fiery temperament. He asked, "When there is no need for even a single blow of the hammer, what then?
The Master said, "An unpleasant lacquer bucket. Feng asked, "Is there any ginseng here? The Master threw his hoe down in front of Feng. Feng said, "If that is so, then I shall dig right here.
The Master said, "An unpleasant lacquer bucket. As Feng took his leave, the Master saw him out the door and called after him.
[The Master] said, "What is the Way? Feng returned his head and responded, "Yes. The Master said, "Be well on your way. [The Master] asked, "The old year has passed and the new year has arrived;
is there anyone who does not fall into these two paths? The Master said, "There is. [The Master] asked, "Who is it that does not fall into these two paths?
The Master said, "The beginning of the New Year brings forth the mandate; all things are renewed. [The Master] asked, "It is somewhat like..."
[The moon] for half a month resembles three stars; neither heaven nor earth can contain it. In what place does the Master perceive it? The Master said, "What are you saying?

[The monk] said, "I suspect the Master has only the ripples of a still pond, but lacks waves that overflow the heavens. The Master said, "Idle talk. [The monk] asked, "When one comes from among the various categories of beings, how is it?
The Master said, "If you come from among the category of humans, you are of the human category; if you come from among the category of horses, you are of the horse category."
Question: "The patriarchs have transmitted it from one to another; what is it they transmit? The Master said: "I do not know how to speak falsely. Question:
"What is it to go out the door and not see the Buddha? The Master said: "There is nothing to be seen. Question: "What is it to enter the room and leave father and mother behind?
The Master said: "There is nothing born. Question: "What is it to hide one's body within the flames? The Master said: "It exists."
"What is a place of concealment? He asked. "How is it to hide one's body within a charcoal storehouse?
