"The Sage appeared in the world; he was merely a person who transmits words. Is this not the Master’s own words? The Master said, "It is.
[The student] asked, "Just as when the World-Honored One was born, pointing one finger to heaven and one finger to earth, he said: 'Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored.
Why is he called a person who transmits words? The Master said, "Because he pointed to heaven and pointed to earth."
"This is why he is called 'the man who transmits the words. The monk bowed and withdrew. A monk asked, "When there is no news from the ninefold gates, from where does the imperial pardon come?
The Master said, "Though the flowing light pervades all, it does not reach within the inner palace. The monk asked, "How far apart are the flowing light and the inner palace?
The Master said, "Green waters surge with waves; green mountains display their exquisite beauty. A monk asked, "Everyone says they request [instruction];"
Yi asked, "I do not yet understand how you, Master, will provide salvation. The Master said, "Tell me: has the great mountain ever lacked even a single inch of soil?
Yi said, "If that is so, then for what purpose did I travel across the four seas in search of the Way? The Master said, "Yanjiao lost his head and his mind went mad.
Yi asked, "Is there anyone who is not mad? The Master said, "There is. Yi asked, "Who is this one who is not mad? The Master—
[The monk] said, "Tou Xiao’s eyes were not open while on the road. He asked, "What is the student's own self? The Master said, "Ask anyone else.
[The monk] said, "If one accepts it as such right now, what then? The Master said, "Sumeru must further support Sumeru. He asked, "The patriarchs transmit to one another;
what exactly is being transmitted? The Master said, "Śākyamuni is stingy; Kāśyapa is wealthy. [The monk] said—
"What is Śākyamuni’s stinginess? The Master said, "He has nothing to give to others. "What is Kāśyapa’s wealth?
The Master said, "The Lord Mengchang within the borders of the state. "What is the ultimate matter that was transmitted?
The Master said, "An old man of a hundred years divides his night lamp. A monk asked, "The Buddhas are not my Way; what then is my Way? The Master said, "I am not."
[The monk] said, "If they are not the Buddhas, why do you nevertheless establish 'my Way'? The Master said, "Just now I briefly called them in;
now I am sending them out. [The monk] asked, "Why did you send them out? The Master said, "If I had not sent them out, dust would have formed in their eyes.
[The monk] asked, "If one cannot find [it] anywhere, is that not the Holy One? The Master said, "What is it?"
The student said, "When Niutou had not yet met the Fourth Patriarch, was he not a sage? The Master said, "He was a sage, but his traces of the sacred realm had not yet been forgotten.

The student asked, "How far apart are these two states of sagehood? The Master said, "Though there may be arts of invisibility within the dust, what can one do when the whole body has entered the Imperial Capital?
A questioner asked, "An ancient said, 'Because of the true, the false is established; from the false, the true is revealed. Is this so? The Master said, "It is."
[The student] said, "Is that so? [He asked,] "What is the true mind? The Master said, "That which is not mixed with food is it. [The student] asked, "What is the deluded mind?
The Master said, "Grasping at conditions and giving rise to inversion is it. [The student] asked, "Apart from these two paths, what is the fundamental essence?

The Master said, "The fundamental essence is not separate [from them]. [The student] asked, "Why is it not separate? The Master said, "If one does not revere the Goddess of Virtue (Guṇadevatā), who would despise the Woman of Darkness?"
Question: "The entirety of heaven and earth is, after all, a single eye. What is this 'heaven-and-earth eye'? The Master said: "Heaven and earth are within it. [The questioner] asked:
"Where is the heaven-and-earth eye? The Master said: "It is precisely the heaven-and-earth eye. [The questioner] asked: "Does it still illuminate? The Master said:
"It does not borrow the power of the three luminaries. [The questioner] asked: "If it does not borrow the power of the three luminaries, by what means is it called [the heaven-and-earth eye]?"
"Qiankun Eye. The Master said, "If it were not so, there would be countless people seeing ghosts before their own skulls. Question:
"Regarding 'a single stroke of painting,' why was it impossible to capture the true likeness of Master Zhigong? The Master said, "Xie Guiyao actually granted his permission to Zhigong."

[The student] said: "I have not yet understood what kind of person Wu Daoxuan obtained the certification of the ultimate meaning that led him to grant it to Zhizhong. The Master said: "A tortoise bows its head to the pillar of Mount Sumeru;
when asked about the movement of the countenance, one sinks into the ancient path. Only after the body has perished does one truly know. What is the meaning of this?

The Master said, "Steal money from the Buddha to buy incense for the Buddha. A student said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not understand, then burn incense as an offering to your own father and mother.
Later, the Master resided at Letan and passed away; he was posthumously titled Chan Master Dajue, and his stupa was named Yuanji.
Chan Master Jingxin of Yongquan in Taizhou was a native of Xianyou, Quanzhou. After receiving instruction from Shishuang, he resided at Yongquan.
There was a day when he did not wear his *kāṣāya* while eating his meal. A monk asked him, "Have you not become a layman? The Master replied, "Is one not a monk even now?
Two Zen practitioners, Qiang and De, saw the Master riding an ox along the road; they did not recognize him.
Suddenly [Dongshan] said, "The hooves and horns are very distinct; alas, how can the rider not discern them? The Master spurred the ox away.
Qiangde rested under a tree and brewed tea. When the Master returned, he dismounted from the ox and asked, "Two Chan guests, where have you recently come from?
Qiang said, "From over there. The Master asked, "What is the matter over there? Qiang lifted his tea bowl. The Master said:
“This is still a matter of ‘this side. As for the matter of ‘that side,’ how is it? [The monk] was unable to respond.
The Master said, “Do not say that the rider does not possess discernment. Ascending the hall, the Master said: “For forty-nine years I have been here, yet even now my eyes sometimes wander.
You people, do not open your mouths too wide. Those with intellectual understanding are many; those who possess both realization and practice are one in ten thousand.”
This one point—views and words—must all be thoroughly understood. If your realization is not complete, I dare say you will remain in the cycle of rebirth.
Why is this? It is because the outflows of consciousness have not yet been exhausted. You must simply exhaust the present moment before you can achieve establishment.
This is also called "achieving merit within the established"; shifting that merit toward him is also called "achieving merit within the approach. To personally approach him...
Therefore it is said: "The relative cannot cross over; the relative does not cross over the relative. If you do not even understand such a metaphor, you must take up the whole lump.
Just keep your mind from being distracted and stop wagging your tongue. Have you not seen Dongshan say: "Continuity is also very difficult"?
You must know that there is this matter. If you do not know it exists, there will be days of weeping ahead. Above.
The Hall. Blind and ignorant, one does not see the Buddha; opening one's eyes, one encounters a traveler on the road. When asked about matters of the journey, he has no body sixteen feet tall.
He did not come from the Five Indies, nor has he ever trodden upon Han soil. He was not born to the Zhang family; who says he is the son of the Li clan?
Three people leaning on a single staff, lying on a single bed—whether they resemble him or not, take them up and place them upon your shoulder. For...
He argued eighteen points of contention, but there was nothing that could be done about him.
When Chan Master Zhiyuan Yuanjing of Mount Yungai in Tanzhou was traveling abroad, he asked Yunju, "When Zhiyuan has no way to deal with him, what then?
Yunju replied, "It is simply because your efforts, Venerable Sir, have not reached him. The Master did not prostrate himself.
He went directly to Shishuang and asked the same question as before. Shishuang said, "Not only you, Master, but even I am at a loss.
The Master asked, "Why are you at a loss, Preceptor? Shishuang said, "If I were not at a loss, I would have taken away your being at a loss.
The Master then bowed. A monk asked Shishuang, "I do not ask about the ten thousand doors all being closed; [what about when] the ten thousand..."
When both were opened up at once, how was it? Shuang asked, "What about the matter within the hall? The monk had no reply.
After half a year, he finally offered this turning word: "No one can receive him. Shuang said, "To speak, you speak indeed;
yet you have spoken only eighty percent. The monk asked, "And what about you, Master? Shuang said, "No one recognizes him. The Master (Dongshan) understood.

He prostrated and requested that [Yunmen] lift him up, but Yunmen was unwilling. The Master then took Yunshuang by the arm and went to the abbot’s quarters, saying, "If the Abbot does not speak, I shall strike the Abbot!
Yunshuang said, "I dare you. The Master prostrated repeatedly. Yunshuang said, "No one recognizes him. At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "The Yellow-Faced One."

"What is it? [The monk] asked. The Master said, "It is within the storehouse. [The monk] asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "It is within the storehouse. [The monk] asked, "How is it when the Buddha of the Lamp has not yet appeared?
The Master said, "It cannot be obscured. [The monk] asked, "Why did the snake swallow the Master?

The Master said, "His entire body’s color was not the same as others. [The monk] asked, "What is a patch-robed monk? The Master said, "He travels about seeking and visiting the Way. Tangzhou Daozheng.

The Emperor heard that the Horse King requested a master for a debate on the Dharma. The King invited the Master, and they met upon the throne. After tea was finished, the Master asked the King for his sword.
Grasping the sword, the Master questioned him, saying: "In your own scriptures it is said: 'Vague and indistinct, yet within it there is something.
What thing is this? 'Profound and dark, yet within it there is an essence. What essence is this? If you cannot answer, I shall not spare your life."
"If you cannot explain it, I shall execute you. Daozheng was utterly bewildered; he immediately prostrated himself and repented. The Master asked the King, "Do you recognize this man?
The King replied, "I do. The Master asked, "Who is he? The King said, "Daozheng. The Master said, "It is not so.
If his Way were truly correct, he ought to have been able to respond to me, a monk. This is merely a solitary soul without a master. From this point on, the Daoist [was humbled].
Not confused. A monk asked Zen Master Cang of Gushan in Tanzhou: "The Dharma should even be relinquished, how much more so that which is not-Dharma.
What is 'the Dharma should even be relinquished'? The Master said: "Pouring clarified butter into the void. [The monk] asked: "What is 'that which is not-Dharma'? The Master said: "Songshan."
The Mountain Daoist feigned enlightenment; when asked, "What is it like when one is pressed out [of one's state]?
the Master said, "Has he ever squeezed you?
A monk asked Zen Master Zhongyungei of Tanzhou, "When a Master opens the hall for formal teaching, what should he do? The Master said, "For..."
“You donkey! [The monk] asked, “When the Buddhas appear in the world, for what purpose do they do so? The Master said, “To deal with you donkeys.

[The monk] asked, “How was it before the Patriarchs and Buddhas had appeared in the world? The Master said, “It cannot be represented. [The monk] asked, “How is it after they have appeared in the world?
The Master said, “Even you, O Ācārya, must turn your body aside before you can attain it. [The monk] asked, “What is the phrase that points directly upward? The Master said:
Wen-shu was left speechless. [The Master] asked, "What is the one phrase at the gate? The Master said, "A flower tucked in the hair.
He asked, "What is transcending the billions? The Master said, "Even a transcendent person cannot approve it."
A monk from the mountains on the southern bank of the river asked Master Yizhan, "I am fortunate to have gained your personal presence; I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master said, "If I were to give you instruction, it would be a humiliation for you. The monk asked, "How then should I, as a student, proceed? The Master said:
Be most careful not to fall into judgments of right and wrong. Question: What is the breath of a patch-robed monk?
The Master said: Has it ever perfumed you? Question: I do not ask about those of the same kind; what is it to be of a different kind? The Master said:
If you want your head, they will chop it off and take it away. Question: What is the Lord of the Dharma-body? The Master said: He does not come. [The questioner] asked: What is Vairocana?
The Master said, "It does not transcend. The Master passed away at Changqing; his posthumous title was Great Master Benjing, and his stupa was named Wuchen (Dustless).
Chan Master Huiyou of Qixian on Mount Lu was a native of Quanzhou. A monk asked, "What is the matter before the Five Elders Peak?
The Master said, "Ten thousand ages, a thousand autumns. The monk said, "If that is so, then the lineage will be cut off. The Master said, "Hesitate."
"Whom do you wish to give [this] to? he asked, as he approached from afar seeking the Master's teaching. "I pray the Master provide an exhortation. The Master said, "He does not rely on time.
The student said, "I pray the Master rely on time. The Master said, "I, too, do not exchange it. The student asked, "What is the Dharma such that every phenomenon is without difference?
The Master said, "Adding frost upon snow. Ascending the hall, the Master said: "If you understand this matter, there will be no place to set down your words."
A question was asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied: "The cold moon at the bottom of the well; the bright moon in the sky.
The Master passed away at Mount Lu and was posthumously titled Great Master Yuanguo; his stupa was named Chuan Deng (Transmitting the Lamp).
Chan Master Hongjian of Mount Fuchuan in Fuzhou was asked by a monk, "What is one's original face?
The Master closed his eyes and stuck out his tongue; then he opened his eyes and stuck out his tongue to show him. The monk said, "Is there really such a multitude of original faces?
The Master replied, "What did you see just now? The monk was speechless. Another asked, "What is the lion? The Master said, "It roars well."
"Hou! The monk clapped his hands and said, "A fine hand! A fine hand! The Master said, "Under the clear blue sky and bright sun, you have been bewitched by a ghost.
The monk made a gesture of overturning the meditation seat; the Master struck him and said, "The donkey’s business is not yet over, and the horse’s business has arrived.

The Master said, "Truly, you are a master. The monk shook out his sleeves and departed. The Master said, "To take a bowl and fill it with water, intending to compare it to the great ocean. [Question] (The monk asked: "..."
"What is the profound mystery? The Master said, "Before you have even heard it. Dao Wu asked, "I have long heard that the Master is proficient in Chan;
is this true? The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven! Dao Wu stepped forward and covered the Master’s mouth, saying, "Lower your voice, lower your voice!"
The Master gave me a slap on the face. I cried out, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master grabbed hold of me and said, "How can you be so impolite? I then gave him a slap in return.
The Master said, "I, this old monk, am at fault. I shook my sleeves and departed.

The Master laughed heartily and said, "Had I known it would be thus earlier, I would not have seen it as such. A monk came for an audience. As soon as he arrived, the Master made a gesture as if rising. The monk then left.

The Master said, "Come, Ācārya, let us exchange greetings. The monk turned back and made a gesture of drawing up his sitting mat. The Master then returned to his quarters. The monk cried out, "Heaven! Heaven!
The Master said, "A dragon's head and a snake's tail. The monk stepped forward and stood with his hands joined in *añjali*; the Master said:
The defeated general threw himself before the king; did he preserve his life? [The monk] asked: "When one with uncut jade presents it to a master, does the master accept it?
The Master struck the incense altar with his hand. The monk bowed. The Master said, "That you bow is not in doubt, but as for the matter within it, what is it?"

The monk struck the incense altar. The Master said, "The tongue does not leave the mouth. Three days before he was about to pass away, the Master ordered his attendant to summon the First Seat (the head monk).
The Master lay down and let out a single breath. The Seat called to the attendant, saying, "The Master is thirsty;
he wants some hot water to drink. The Master then lay facing the wall. At the moment of death, he ordered the assembly to gather and then extended both [hands].
He extended his tongue from his mouth and showed it to them. At that time, the third person in the assembly said, "Friends, the Master’s tongue-root has become stiff.
The Master said, "Alas, alas! It is truly as the third person in the assembly has said; my tongue-root has indeed gone stiff. Having finished speaking, he passed away into stillness.
He was posthumously titled Great Master Shaolong, and his stupa was named Guangji.
At Dingshou, Chan Master Cunde Hekong was asked by a monk, "What is the one phrase? The Master said, "Ask further.
The monk asked, "What is the Venerable’s *śātava*? The Master said, "Last night at the third watch, I saw the moon bright."
A monk asked Chan Master Chong’en of Jizhou, “Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said:
“Though there is a moon at Shaolin, it does not pierce the clouds over the Pamir Mountains. [The monk] asked, “What is the ‘kindred’? The Master said:
“The neighing is piercing by the奈何 bridge; one goes and returns within the forest of sword-trees.”
A monk asked Chan Master Shishuang Hui, "When the World-Honored One appeared in the world, he first delivered the five bhikṣus.
When you, Master, appear in the world, whom do you deliver first? The Master said, "I deliver no one at all. The monk asked, "Why do you deliver no one?
The Master said, "Because they are not the five bhikṣus."
A monk asked Zen Master Bajiao of Yingzhou, "How should one proclaim the ancestral vehicle? The Master said, "It has already been seen through by those with cold eyes.
The monk asked, "Without falling into any conditions, please, Master, point directly. The Master said, "There is a question; there is an answer.
The monk asked, "What is the single phrase by which you, the Master, benefit people? The Master said, "I only fear that you, O *jiaoli*, will not [understand]."
Question: "What is one who has gone forth? The Master said: "The young child of the Dong family weeps with every cry.
Question: "What is one who returns? The Master said: "A withered tree; a black dragon baring its claws and fangs."
A monk asked Chan Master Fojiao of Weitian in Tanzhou, "What is the matter prior to appearing in the world?
The Master said, "The pearl in the topknot has not yet been untied; the stone woman furrows her eyebrows. The monk asked, "How is it after appearing in the world?

The Master said, "The numinous tortoise presents the signs of the hexagrams; one loses sight of one's own body. Another asked, "What is the name of this place? The Master said, "Weitian (Fertile Field)."
[The monk] asked, "What should one plant? The Master struck him. The Master had a verse that said: To cultivate many fine phrases is a waste of effort;
Returning to the source is the height of folly. Ancestral Buddhas are not attained through cultivation or realization; Even if you travel the profound path, it remains rugged and treacherous.
A monk asked Chan Master Luhuan Hui of Tanzhou, "Without relying on any conditions, please, Master, speak. The Master struck the brazier and said, "Do you understand?
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Sleeping fool! Another asked, "How was it before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "Like the moon in the water. The monk asked, "And after he saw him? The Master said, "Like the water in the moon."
Question: "The patriarchs have transmitted it from one to another; I wonder, what exactly was transmitted? The Master said: "I ask you, and you ask me. The student said:
"If that is so, then there is no distinction between the black-robed and the white-robed. The Master said: "Where have you come from?"
A monk asked Master Yueliao of Tanzhou Bao’ai: “The jeweled canopy hangs high; what is the matter within it?

I beg the Master to issue a directive beneath his words—a single phrase that requires no elaboration. The Master said: “The jeweled canopy hangs in the void; there is a path, yet it has never been traversed.
If you seek a directive beneath my words, then east and west will immediately arise.”
A monk asked Zen Master Haiyan of Zhengmi Temple on Mount Yunmen in Yuezhou, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe?
The Master said, "It is like biting a hard stone. The monk asked, "What is the single incense burner in the ancient temple? The Master said:
"No one in successive generations has ever smelled it. [The monk] asked, "What is meant by 'smelling'? The Master said, "The six sense faculties do not reach it at all.
[The monk] asked, "I have long heard that you rescue those lost; why is it that upon my arrival, I do not see this rescue? The Master said, "You, O *jiaoli*, do not recognize the rescue."
A monk asked Master Wenshu of Hunan, "Why was it that Sengyou could not capture the true likeness of Master Zhigong?
The Master said, "It is not only Sengyou; even Zhigong himself could not capture his own likeness. The monk asked, "Why could Zhigong not capture his own likeness?"
The Master said, "I have not brought any colors. [The monk] asked, "Has the Master, then, been able to capture it? The Master said, "I, too, have not been able to capture it.
[The monk] asked, "Why has the Master not been able to capture it? The Master said, "It has no colors; how could I be instructed to capture it?
[The monk] asked, "What is the secret chamber? The Master said, "It is not entered through the gate. [The monk] asked, "What is the secret [essence]?"
A person in the room. The Master said: "He does not sit atop the ox of form.
When Chan Master Shizhu of Fengxiang Prefecture was traveling, he arrived at Dongshan. At that time, Master Qian uttered these words:
There are four kinds of people. One person excels in speech; even the Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot take a single step beyond them. Another person excels in practice;
even the Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot utter a single word beyond them. A third person is capable both of speaking and of practicing. A fourth person is incapable both of speaking and of practicing.

"Who, then, is that person? The Master stepped forward from the assembly and said: "The one who has surpassed the Buddhas and Patriarchs in speech yet cannot practice it—this is simply because he lacks a tongue, not permitted to walk.
The one who has surpassed the Buddhas and Patriarchs in practice yet cannot utter a single word of it—this is simply because he lacks feet, not permitted to speak.
The one who can both speak and practice—it is simply that the container and its lid match one another."
When someone says that one cannot speak and cannot act, it is like seeking life by cutting off one’s own breath; this is like a child born of a barren woman wearing a cangue and shackles.
Shanshan asked, “What about your own portion, Master? The Master said, “In my own portion, all things are encompassed and penetrated;
how could they not be clearly manifest? Shanshan asked, “As for Minggong Xiù on the sea, what about him? The Master said, “Two illusory people meeting.”
Clapping his hands, he laughed heartily.
Chan Master Cunsou of Daitong Monastery on Mount Qiyen in Hezhong Prefecture initially lectured on the sutras and śāstras;
later, in the presence of Shishuang, he forgot the trap (the means). After he took up residence there, a monk asked, "What is the place where you, Master, gained strength? The Master said, "No."
Occupying the position of Master, how could he be one merely sitting upon a white ox cart? A monk asked, "How is it before the lotus flower has emerged from the water?
The Master said, "Are you not asking about the lotus flower after it has emerged? The monk was speechless. The Master rarely spoke in his daily life, responding only when questioned.
He lived to the age of ninety-three and was posthumously titled Chan Master Zhenji.
Chan Master Xuantai of Nanyue was profound, tranquil, and spoke little. He never wore silk or fine fabrics; thus, his contemporaries called him "Tai the Coarse-Robed One" (Taibuna).
When he first met Deshan and later visited Shishuang, he was granted permission to enter the inner quarters. For twenty years, he served as the scribe, befriending Guanhui and Qiji.
Later, he resided at a hermitage called Jingangtai, where he did not establish formal disciples. Those who came from all directions seeking instruction...

Those who depend on him are all treated with the courtesy due to a friend. Once, because Mount Heng was frequently subjected to felling by mountain dwellers and slash-and-burn agriculture, he composed the "Ballad of the Slash-and-Burn Mountain":
"Children of the slash-and-burn mountain! Children of the slash-and-burn mountain! Knowing nothing at all, year after year you hack away the peaks of the green mountains.
Among them, the finest is the hue of Mount Heng; The pines and cypresses have their noble branches shattered by sharp axes. The numinous birds and wild cranes..."
Without cause or reliance, white clouds retreat as blue smoke flies. The path for monkeys and apes is cut off as crags and cliffs emerge;

the roots of medicinal herbs are lost, yet the weeds flourish. Year after year, once harvested, they are weeded again; though a thousand autumns pass, it is difficult to restore them to their original state.

It is further said that this year’s planting was not much, so next year one shall clear even more of the southern slopes. If the mountain ranges of the nation are already like this—how can it be otherwise?

How could this principle remain unknown? It was propagated far and wide and reached the imperial court. An edict was issued to prohibit [the practice], so that the monasteries within the mountains were no longer subjected to conflagration;
this was due to the Master’s efforts. When he was about to manifest his passing, he summoned the monks and ordered them to prepare firewood.
He spoke a verse, saying: "This year I am sixty-five; The four elements shall depart from their lord. The Way, from its very source, Is self-existent."

Within this, there are no Buddhas or patriarchs. There is no need for tonsure; there is no need for bathing. A single mass of fierce fire—ten thousand times sufficient, a hundred thousand times sufficient.
He passed away sitting upright with one foot pendant. His remains were cremated, the relics were collected, and a stupa was erected beside Yingyun Pavilion.
A monk asked Zen Master Yungai of Tanzhou, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master said, "A jade hare hidden within the moon. The monk asked, "And after he appeared?
The Master said, "A golden crow on its back in the sun. [Another monk] asked, "When it cannot be fathomed through ordinary sentiment, how is it?
The Master said, "The ingenuity of a tongueless child is exhausted. Fengxue went to visit [Yungai]. The Master asked him, "Stone..."
Jue, carrying his staff, emerged from the clouds onto the path. "What is your intention? asked Xue. Jue replied, "Red clouds enshroud the jade elephant; the peaks embrace the streams and sources.
The Master said, "I have come along with you. Xue said, "The Master must also lower his voice. The Master said, "Sit for a moment and drink some tea."
Chan Master Pumen of Longhu in Shaowu Commandery was the crown prince of Emperor Xizong of the Tang dynasty. From childhood, he abstained from meat;
as an adult, he had no interest in governing the world. Emperor Xizong doted on him, yet despite employing every means to mold and direct him, he could never change his mind.

At the beginning of the Zhonghe era, when Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, the Master cut off his hair and wandered away, with no one knowing his whereabouts. He traveled to Shishuang and asked: "The Patriarch..."
The Master asked about the matters of the separate transmission: "Would you be willing to entrust these to me? Baoshuang said, "Do not slander the Patriarchs.

The Master said, "The principles of the world are vast and magnificent; how could they be something fabricated? Baoshuang said, "Is this not a reality? The Master asked, "What is your own understanding of this?"
Fangshuang said, "When the mountain of the altar nods its head, I shall tell you. At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.

He took his leave and traveled until he reached the outskirts of Shaowu City. There he saw the mountains rising in deep, lush beauty; he pushed through the undergrowth to where smoke was rising and found an ascetic dwelling there.
Upon seeing the Master arrive, the ascetic said, "Master, you shall surely flourish here," and after bowing deeply, he departed. The Master...
After he had lived there for over ten years, one day an old man came to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Where do you reside? What do you seek by coming here?
The old man replied, "I dwell on this mountain; however, I am not a human, but a dragon. Because I have failed in my duty regarding the rain, the heavens have punished me and I am due to die.
I pray that you will grant me your protection. The Master said, "You have incurred the wrath of the Supreme Deity; what power do I have to exert on your behalf?"
Although he could easily change his form, the old man suddenly vanished from where he was. Looking beside him, [the Master] saw a small snake crawling into his sleeve.
At dusk, thunder and lightning shook the mountains as wind and rain broke out together; the Master sat upright and remained unmoved.
When dawn came and the sky cleared, the snake slipped out of his sleeve, fell to the ground, and departed. After a short while, the old man bowed and wept, saying: "Were it not for a Great..."
The Master was compassionate. He thought, "This mountain has been defiled by blood and filth; how may I repay this kindness?
He then hollowed out the base of a cliff to create a spring, saying, "May this spring serve as a provision for the many who will gather here in the future. It is now known as Longhu (Dragon Lake).

When the local people heard of these events, they contributed both wealth and labor to build a monastery together. Monks flocked there like clouds. The Master propagated his teachings for over thirty years.

As he approached the time of his passing, he struck the bell to assemble the congregation and spoke this verse: "I fled the world's hardships to leave the household life; The Master pointed out a place of rest for me.
I have dwelt on this mountain and gathered the assembly for thirty years; Ordinarily, I did not wish to bestow this lightly.
Today I shall explain it clearly to you; Listen all together when I close my eyes. He passed away peacefully, and his stupa was enshrined at the mountain monastery.
He was posthumously titled Chan Master Yuanjue.
The scholar Zhang Zhuo, having been directed by the Great Master Chan Yue, went to visit Shishuang. Shishuang asked, "Scholar, what is your surname?

He replied, "My surname is Zhang and my name is Zhuo. Shishuang said, "Even 'cleverness' (qiao) cannot be found; from where does 'clumsiness' (zhuo) come? At these words, the official suddenly attained realization.
He then presented this verse: "Brilliant light and silent illumination pervade the sands of the Ganges; Ordinary beings, sages, and all sentient creatures share my home.
When not a single thought arises, the whole body is fully revealed; As soon as the six sense organs stir, they are shrouded by clouds. To sever afflictions is to increase one's illness;
To pursue True Suchness is likewise a deviation. Accord with worldly conditions without hindrance; Nirvana and birth-and-death are equal to flowers in the sky."
Miaoxi said: "The donkey urinates where it finds damp ground.
Chan Master Yuan'an of Luofu Mountain in Lizhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Huijian of Jia Shan;
he was the son of the Tan family from Linyou in Fengxiang, and he left home to become a monk in his childhood.
He was fully endowed with the precepts and proficient in the sutras and śāstras. He sought the Way from Linji and served as his attendant.

Linji once praised him before the assembly, saying, "In the gate of Linji there is a single arrow; who dares to meet its point? Having received this seal of approval, the Master considered himself sufficient.
Later, one day while standing in attendance, a Dharma Master visited Linji. Linji asked, "Suppose there is a person regarding the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions [of the scriptures]..."
"Attaining clarity through the teachings. There was one person who did not attain clarity through the three vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.
Let us say: are these two people the same or different? The Master said, "If they have attained clarity, they are the same; if they have not attained clarity, they are different.
The Teacher said, "What place is this for speaking of 'same' or 'different'? Jie looked at the Teacher and asked, "And what about you, Master? The Teacher then—
"Hai! said Xuefeng. He escorted the Abbot back to his seat and asked the Master, "Was it not you who just now shouted at the old monk?
The Master replied, "It was. Xuefeng then struck him. Later, when the Master took his leave of Xuefeng, Xuefeng asked, "Where are you going? The Master replied, "To the South."
Ji took up his staff, drew a line, and said, "If you can pass through this, then go. The Master then gave a shout. Ji struck him.
The Master bowed and departed. The next day, Ji ascended the hall and said, "In the gate of Linji there is a red carp, shaking its head and wagging its tail, heading south.
I know not in whose house it will be drowned in a pickle jar."
After the Master had finished his travels, he went directly to Jia-shan to establish a hermitage. For a year he did not visit Jia-shan. Jia-shan then composed a letter and sent a monk to deliver it.
Upon receiving it, the Master sat down; when the monk extended his hands again to present the letter, the Master demanded it once more. The monk was speechless, so the Master struck him.
[The monk] said, "Go back and show it to the Abbot. When the monk returned and showed it to him, Mount [Shan] said, "If this monk opens the letter, he will surely arrive within three days;
if he does not open the letter, this man cannot be saved. The Master indeed arrived after three days.
Upon seeing Jia Shan, he did not prostrate himself, but instead stood facing him with his hands joined at his chest. Jia Shan said, "A rooster nesting in a phoenix's nest is not its proper place."
They were of the same lineage. [The guest] went out. The Master said, "You have come from afar to seek our style; I ask for a single reception. Guishan said, "Before my eyes there is no *śrāmaṇera*;
here there is no old monk. The Master then gave a shout. Guishan said, "Wait, wait! Do not be so hasty and careless.
The clouds and moon are the same, yet the streams and mountains differ. To cut off the tongues of all people in the world is certainly not beyond your ability, *śrāmaṇera*, but how..."

The Master instructed a tongueless man to understand speech. The Master stood there lost in thought; Shanshan struck him immediately. From this point on, he devoted himself to the teachings. (Xinghua spoke on his behalf: "He only knew how to become a Buddha.")
"Mochou asked Shanshan: "At a place where neither Buddha nor demons can reach, how does one realize it? Shanshan said: "The candle illuminates images for a thousand li;
yet in the dark room, the old monk remains lost. He was asked again: "When the morning sun has already risen and the night moon has not yet appeared, what then?
Shanshan said: "The dragon holds the pearl in its mouth; the swimming fish do not look back. As Shanshan was about to pass away, he left behind this final word: "The stone..."
"Look at this single branch; it will soon perish," said [Wuzu]. The Master said, "Not so. Foshan asked, "Why?
The Master said, "He has his own green mountains. Foshan said, "If it is thus, then our school shall not fall.
When Jia Shan passed away, the Master arrived at Cenyang and met an old friend. While discussing matters concerning Wuling, the friend asked, "In the blink of an eye, several..."

[The Master] said, “For many years. Where have you been fleeing from calamity? The Master replied, “I was right in the midst of the marketplace. [The other] asked, “Why did you not go to a place where there are no people?
The Master said, “What difficulty is there in a place where there are no people? [The other] asked, “How can one escape and hide within the marketplace?

The Master said, “Although I was in the midst of the marketplace, I sought to remain unrecognized by others; therefore, people could not fathom me. He then asked again, “Buddha after Buddha correspond with one another; Patriarch after Patriarch...”
The tradition relates: "When neither side condescends to bend, what is it like? The Master said, "Before the gate of a country elder, one does not discuss the affairs of the imperial court.
[The monk] asked, "What matters, then, should be discussed? The Master said, "As long as one has not met another, one will never open their fist.

[The monk] asked, "If there is someone who does not come from the imperial court, and they meet—would you still speak of this realization? The Master said, "The mechanism beyond measure is merely a labor for the eyes."
Ji Shu initially resided at Mount Luopu in Liyang. Later, he moved to Suxi in Langzhou. Disciples from all quarters flocked to him in great numbers. He ascended the hall and said:
"The final phrase is where one first arrives at the secure barrier; it locks off the vital passageway, allowing neither ordinary person nor sage to pass through.
I have always told everyone: 'Let the world rejoice as it pleases, yet I alone am unwilling.'"

Know that those who aspire to the higher stream do not take the words and teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and pin them upon their foreheads, like a tortoise carrying a map—this is a sign of self-destruction.
Even as a phoenix coils within a golden net, how can it hope to soar through the clouds and mists?
You must clarify the fundamental source beyond the literal meaning; do not seek patterns within words. Therefore, even a stone man whose mechanism resembles yours can sing the *ba* song.
If you were like a stone man, you would surely be able to harmonize with the "Snowy Melody. This single path toward the south is known by the wise. Question:
When one sees it in an instant of flash, what is it like? The Master said: "The morning star divides the dawn light;

how can it compare to the radiance of the sun? Question: When coming thus, there is no establishment; when going thus, there is no extinction—what is it like? The Master said: "The wood-seller carrying his firewood."
Noble! The Daoist Robed in Brocade says: "To offer sustenance to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas is not as good as offering sustenance to a single mindless Daoist.
I do not yet understand: what fault do the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have, and what virtue does the mindless Daoist possess?
The Master said: "A single sheet of white clouds spans the valley mouth; how many returning birds lose their nests? Question: "How is it when the sun has not yet risen? The Master said:
"The waters of the vast ocean are exhausted, yet the dragon remains hidden; the clouds rise into the azure heavens, yet the phoenix still soars.
Question: "What is this fundamental matter? The Master said: "A single grain lies in the wasteland; though the seedlings are not weeded, they flourish of their own accord."
[The monk] said: "If one does not weed them, will they not be buried by the grass? Or will they not exist at all? The Master said: "Flesh and bone differ from straw and weeds;

tares and barnyard grass can never truly hide them. [The monk] asked: "What is it like for one who does not harm the lives of living beings? The Master said: "The eyes grow dim, and the mountain shadows shift."
The deluded wander aimlessly; when asked, they do not speak of the present or the past—how can it be? The Master said: "The numinous tortoise has no omens in its lines;
the empty shell need not be drilled. He asked: "What then of this empty shell? The Master said: "When all is seen through, there is no place for artifice;
neither the heterodox nor the orthodox can be established. He asked: "In that case, there is no place of rest? The Master said: "The primal forms begin in the unmanifest."

[The Master said: "Form is empty toil; it is vexed by the adornment of colors. [The questioner asked: "Regarding the matter of the Dragon’s mechanism not emitting mist to moisten the canopy—how is this?
The Master said: "The Way is fundamentally nameless; it does not abide in light or darkness. [The questioner asked: "As for that matter of not being caught in light or darkness, how is it?"

The Master said: "Within words it is easy to raise [the matter], but beyond the mind it is difficult to bring forth. Question: "What is it like when one is neither born into the Tathāgata’s family nor seated upon the Flower King’s throne?

The Master said: "Tell me, how much does this brazier weigh? Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarchs, and what is the meaning of the Teachings? The Master said: "Tell me, how much does this brazier weigh?"
[The monk asked: "Are they the same or different? The Master said: "In the lion’s den there are no other beasts; where the elephant king walks, the tracks of foxes are cut off. [The monk] asked:

"When [the patriarchs] all came forth at once, how was it then? The Master said: "Presenting the raw jade without knowing the occasion; one merely exhausts oneself and invites having one's feet cut off.
He asked a monk: "Where have you recently come from? The monk said: "Jingnan. The Master said: "There is a person who goes in this manner; has he yet [reached his destination]?"
[The Master] asked, "Did you meet him? He replied, "I did not meet him. The Master said, "Why did you not meet him? He replied, "If I had met him, my head would have shattered into pieces.
The Master said, "Your three-inch tongue [your capacity for speech] is very tight. Later, when Yunmen saw this monk in Jiangxi, he asked, "Do you still have these words?
The monk replied, "Yes, Master. Yunmen said, "Luopu has retreated three thousand li! [Question: Regarding the practice of the inconceivable realm...

"What? the Master asked. [The monk] said, "The green mountains constantly lift their feet; the white sun does not shift its wheel. [The Master] asked, "Regarding the matter of standing alone in a withered and desolate field, what is it like?

The Master said, "A heron leaning against a snowy nest may still be distinguished; a crow alighting on black lacquer makes the matter difficult to discern. [The Master] asked, "What is the guest within the host?
The Master said, "One constantly asks the way when meeting people; beneath one's feet, one is perpetually lost."
[The student] asked, "What is it like when guest and host are both raised? The Master said, "A withered tree has no horizontal branches; a bird finds it difficult to set foot upon it.
[The student] asked, "How is it when one is perpetually dazed all day long? The Master said, "A jewel is cast into a mixture of sand; those who recognize it are naturally distinct from the rest.
[The student] said, "If that is so, then even when I extend my hand, I do not encounter the Master. The Master said, "Do not mistake the cry of a crane for the song of a warbler."
[The Master] wept. He asked, "Regarding the person of the three dots of the circle—everyone understands this; what is the 'house style' of Lu Pu like?
The Master said, "A single clap of thunder, and the sound of the cloth drum vanishes. He asked, "What is it like at the exact time of midday?
The Master said, "Midday still lacks half; only when the sun sinks does it become full. If you wish to understand the meaning within this, place a cow's head upon its tail. He asked.
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The rustling bamboo before the window does not grow cold of its own accord after the frost.
As the monk prepared to offer further words, the Master said, "I hear only the sound of the wind striking it; how many thousand stalks must there be?

He ascended the hall and said, "Sun Bin has closed his shop, yet there is still a diviner who comes forward. A monk said, "I request the Master to perform a divination for me. The Master said, "In your house..."
"The Patriarch has died. The monk had no reply. (Fayan, acting for him, clapped his hands three times. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?
The Master struck the meditation seat with his whisk and said, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "A sudden thunder from heaven startles the universe;
the toad at the bottom of the well does not raise its head. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Snow covers the solitary peak."

"Peak after peak is not white. Rain nourishes the stone shoots; the shoots must grow. [The student] asked, "Is it true that the Dharma-body is unconditioned and does not fall into any numerical categories?
The Master said, "It would be better to cherish your eyebrows. [The student] asked, "How can one avoid this fault?

The Master said, "A clay tortoise may live for a thousand years at your disposal, but it will never understand how to follow the clouds and cranes. [The student] said, "Even Sun Bin himself would suffer such a denunciation."
The Master said, "For a bull whose nostrils have not been pierced, what means of control is there? The monk then let out a bull's roar.
The Master said, "This beast! The monk then shouted. The Master said, "Tucking its tail and baring its teeth—it is still no good hand.
A monk asked, "When one lets go at the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom precipice, how can one avoid perishing the body? What is it like then? The Master said, "Mount Sumeru tied to a lotus root."
[The student] said, “What kind of realm is this? The Master said, “The heart of the upturned lotus atop the top of the *kṣa* pole.
[The student] said, “If that is so, then it is profoundly still and clear. The Master said, “Turning the body once more atop the peak of Mount Sumeru.

[The student] said, “If that is so, then it is filled with apprehension and urgency. The Master said, “Empty as he follows the decoy pigeon, he vainly loses his life in the net. [The student] asked, “How can one attain it?”
[The monk] did not follow him away. The Master said: "The neck of the ewer is small; intending to pass through, it looks toward the sky to fly. A monk asked:
"When the dew does not hang upon the multitude of trees, what then? The Master said: "Where there is a tiger, the crows must caw; where there is no person, the birds are not startled. A monk asked:
"If a person who can overturn heaven and earth comes, will you, Master, receive him? The Master held up his whisk. The monk said: "In that case, I have attained it."

[The monk] said, "I have met a wise ruler and am leaving. The Master said: "Vague and indistinct, like a tune just barely worth hearing; yet it is blown by the wind into another key. [The monk] asked:
"How can one discern the place where neither Buddha nor Mara reach? The Master said: "Yajnadatta did not lose his head;
it was his failure to recognize it in the mirror. [The monk] asked: "What is the means to rescue oneself from birth and death? The Master said: "Holding onto water to prolong a precarious life."

[The student] said, "I have not heard the wondrous music of the heavens; I ask from where the four great elements arise. The Master said, "In still water there are no waves; bubbles are stirred up by the wind.
[The student] asked, "When the bubble ceases and returns to the water, what is it like? The Master said, "Neither turbid nor muddy; fish and dragons leap as they please.
[The student] asked, "How can one transcend birth and death? The Master said, "In a single thought, forget all artifice; the vast void is without blemish."
Question: "What is the Way? The Master said: "To maintain a mental mechanism is still to be stuck in traces; to remove the stump, and the path is open. Question:
"What is that which cannot be contained within the Great Canon of Teachings? The Master said: "The rain nourishes the three types of grasses, making them flourish;
a single piece of jade shines by its very nature. Question: "When a single hair swallows up the vast ocean, what further words can there be therein? The Master said: "Home."
"There is the *Baize* (White Deer) Map; there will certainly be no such monsters. [Baofu says differently: "If one has no *Baize* Map at home, there are likewise no such monsters.
"What is it like when time is still and motionless? The Master said, "When the time comes, the thunder responds to the season, shaking the mountains and startling the hibernating insects.

[The monk asked: "How is it when all manner of movements are no different from this single moment of stillness? The Master said, "The spiritual crane soars beyond the void; the dull bird does not leave its perch."
Chao asked, "How is it? The Master said, "A white-haired old man bows to a youth; all the people of the world find this hard to believe.
A monk asked, "When the various sages come in such a manner, with what do you make offerings? The Master said, "Though the Earth-Dweller (Tu Su) holds a mendicant's staff, he is not a Brahmin.
A monk asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "The sun and moon shine together; whose house could have anything else?"

[The Master] said, "In that case, illumination and concealment follow different paths; matters are not uniform. The Master said, "As long as you do not lose your sheep yourself, why must you weep at the fork in the road?
A student asked, "When a student intends to return home, what then? The Master said, "The house is ruined and the people are gone;
where would you, my son, go to return? [The student] said, "If that is so, then I shall not return. The Master said, "The remaining snow in the courtyard is being melted by the sun."
The wheel has vanished. Who shall sweep away the drifting dust within the chamber? Thereupon, a verse was spoken: "Resolute in mind, I depart for my native land;

I board a boat to cross the Five Lakes. As I raise the oar, the stars and moon fade from view; When I halt the rudder, the sun’s orb stands solitary. Unmooring, I leave the shore of error; Setting sail, I emerge upon the path of truth.
Arriving home, all worldly attachments are swept away; Thus I am spared from being a fool within the house. Question: "Movement is the sprout of the Dharma King."
"Quiescence is the root of the Dharma King. As for the sprouts, I shall not ask. What is the Dharma King? The Master raised his whisk.
The monk said, "This is still but a sprout of the Dharma King. The Master said, "If the dragon does not emerge from its cave, who can do anything about it?
The attendant said to the Master, "Dharma Master Zhao has composed the *Four Treatises*, which are truly extraordinary. The Master said, "Master Zhao is indeed extraordinary."

"Essentially, one does not see the Patriarch. [To this] there was no reply. (Fadeng spoke on his behalf, saying: "Where, Master, is he? Yunju Xi said: "Where is he? Is it that the place where Master Zhao did not see the Patriarch contains so many words?
It is also said: "Master Zhao had many other words. [The Master] was asked: "What is the single path of the living mechanism?

The Master said: "Striking the void produces a sound; striking wood produces no sound. In the eighth month of the fifth year of the Guanghua era of Emperor Zhaozong of the Tang Dynasty (the Wuma year), [he] issued his final instructions.
The administrator said, "According to the dharma of leaving home, surplus possessions are not retained. At this time of sowing seeds, one must strictly practice economy.

All matters concerning construction and maintenance shall be suspended. Time flows swiftly, yet the Great Way is fundamentally profound; if one merely follows along with negligence, by what means could one realize it?
Although my exhortations have been earnest and sincere, the assembly treats them as routine and fails to heed them as a warning. When winter arrived, he manifested his passing.
He was ill, yet he did not weary of receiving visitors or requesting instruction. On the first day of the twelfth month, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"I shall either pass away tomorrow or the day after. Now I have a matter to ask you all: if you say this is so, it is like placing a head upon a head;
if you say it is not, it is like seeking life by cutting off one's own head. The First Seat replied: "The green mountains do not lift their feet; beneath the sun, no torch is carried."

[The Master] said, "Lamp. The Master asked, "What kind of talk is this for such a time? At that moment, the senior monk Yancong replied, "Apart from these two paths, I request that you, Reverend, do not question me further.
The Master said, "Not yet; speak on. Yancong said, "Yancong cannot exhaustively express it.
The Master said, "I do not care whether you can exhaust it or not. Yancong said, "Since Yancong has no attendant, I have responded directly to the Master."
"Furthermore," the Master then ceased speaking. When night fell, he ordered an attendant to summon Cong and asked him:
"Today, your response was most reasonable. You must have grasped the meaning of the former master. The former master said: 'Before one's eyes there is no dharma;
the meaning lies before one's eyes. It is not a dharma of the present moment; it is beyond the reach of ears and eyes. Now tell me: which phrase is the guest, and which phrase is the host?"
"This is the master. If he could discern this, the Master would have handed over the bowl bag to him.

[The monk] said, "Yancong does not understand. The Master said, "You ought to understand. [The monk] said, "Yancong truly does not understand. The Master shouted at him and drove him out, saying, "Suffering! Suffering! (Xuange said:

"Tell me, when the Master said 'the Senior truly does not understand,' was it because he feared seeing the bowl bag being held up before him? On the second day at noon, another monk raised the previous conversation and asked the Master about it. The Master said, "The Compassionate Boat does not..."
He rowed upon the clear waves; his efforts to release wooden swans at Jianxia were in vain. He then entered nirvana. His secular age was sixty-five, and his years as a monk were forty-six.
His stupa was erected in the northwest corner of the monastery.
A monk asked Chan Master Huizhong of Xiaoyao Mountain in Fuzhou, "Is there anyone who can utter a phrase that is not like anything else?
The Master said, "Either five days before the ritual feast, or five days after the ritual feast. Question: "The sword and mirror are sharp and clear; how could even a hair be deluded?
The Master said, "Amoghapāśa (The Unfailing Lasso). Question: "In the fierce flames of the great furnace, what is being forged? The Master said, "The Unfailing Lasso."

Wu asked, “The Master said, ‘I cook the Buddhas and cook the Patriarchs. How does one cook the Buddhas and Patriarchs? The Master said, “Karma is contained therein. Wu asked, “What do you call this karma?
The Master said, “Even the power of the Buddha is not equal [to it]. [Wu] asked, “For forty-nine years he did not speak a single word.
What is that word which was not spoken? The Master said, “A single shoe traveled west; the Wayman did not look back. Wu asked, “...”
"Is this not where the Master finds his rest? The Master said, "The horse is an official horse; there is no need for a seal.
[The monk] asked, "What is 'one old and one not old'? The Master said, "The three obediences and the six duties. [The monk] asked, "What is the wondrous phrase?

The Master said, "Sitting on the Buddha’s seat, chopping off the Buddha’s feet. [The monk] asked, "Between the Patriarch and the Buddha, which is the most [excellent]? The Master said, "The three obediences and the six duties."
The student said, "True gold is unwilling to be bartered; who would be willing to exchange it for a lump of clay?

The Master said, "If that is so, then you are unwilling to go. The student said, "You value it while I despise it. The Master said, "When the questioner is not a match for the army of demons, how can one realize the Way?

The Master said, "There is no need to dip a ladle into the waters of the sea. A student asked, "Dwelling nowhere among the clouded mountains, always abiding in a bottomless boat—how is this? The Master said, "Time is like..."
"What? the Master asked. "When fruit ripens, it naturally becomes fragrant. "Please speak further, Master," he said. "The true son of the Buddha stands before my gate," the Master replied.
"Why do I, as a student, not see him? he asked. "Wang Lao-shi is everywhere," the Master said.
Chan Master Kewen of Panlong Mountain in Yuanzhou was asked by a monk, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go?
The Master said, "The stone ox follows the ancient road; the night-bright lamp shines in broad daylight. He was asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "A foolish child abandons his father and flees."
Chan Master Yuelun of Huangshan in Fuzhou was the son of the Xu family of Fudang. Initially, he visited Sanfeng, but their karmic connection did not harmonize.
Subsequently, hearing that Jia Shan was flourishing in his teaching, he went there to seek him out. Jia Shan asked, "What is your name? The Master replied, "Yuelun."
Sansheng drew a circle and said, "How does this compare to that? The Master said, "If you speak in such a manner, Reverend, there will be many in all quarters who will not approve.
Sansheng asked, "What do you say, Dharma-heir? The Master replied, "Do you see the lunar disc?"
Mount [Shan] said, "If you speak in this manner, many people here will not approve of you; those in other quarters will certainly reject you.

Zun said, "A bright mirror stands upon its stand; I pray the Master will reflect upon it. The Master said, "I do not reflect. Zun asked, "Why do you not reflect?"
The Master said, "The water is shallow; there are no fish. It is but a labor to cast down the hook. Zhenzun had no reply, so the Master struck him.
A monk asked, "What is the mark of 'One Such'? The Master said, "The egret flies white through the Milky Way; the distant mountains are a deep, dark blue.

The disciples gathered together. Later, he established a Chan monastery at Hongjing, naming it after Shanglan. His transformative teachings flourished even more.
A questioner asked, "What is the fundamental matter of Shanglan? The Master said, "It is not borrowed from the thousand sages; how could it be sought among the myriad functions?
The questioner asked, "But what is it like when there is neither borrowing nor seeking? The Master said, "I cannot pick it up and place it before you."
"Can it be grasped in the hand? Question: "How does one discern [the truth] before the sharp edge? The Master said: "Before the sharp edge, no shadow is revealed;
do not seek it on the tip of the tongue. Question: "What is the singing of a tongueless person? The Master said: "Its resonance shakes the azure heavens."
[The Master] did not err in the tones of *gong* and *shang*. Question: "When the two dragons contend for the pearl, who is the one that obtains it?

The Master said: "The pearl covers the ground; even when seen with the eyes, it is like mud. Question: "After Sudhana saw Mañjuśrī, why did he nevertheless go south? The Master said: [He went south] because he had not yet finished his pilgrimage.]
Learning relies on entering the inner chamber; knowledge then penetrates all quarters. [A monk] asked, "Why did Maitreya instead send him to see Mañjuśrī?

The Master said, "The Way is vast and boundless; it is inexhaustible when encountered by people. At the beginning of the first month of the Great Shun gengxu year of the Tang Emperor Zhaozong, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"I originally intended to remain here for ten years. Now that my work of transformation is complete, I shall depart immediately."
When the fast was concluded, the bell was struck; he sat upright and passed away. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Yuanzhen, and his stupa was named "Original Emptiness" (Benkong).
A monk asked the Chan Master of Sizhan in Yanzhou: "The ancients said, 'If invited, they do not turn their backs. Now, if you invite the Master to enter a well, will he still go?
The Master said: "In the profound depths there is no other source; those who drink from it eliminate all afflictions. [The monk] asked: "How is it?"
"This is the family style of our Preceptor," the Master said. "One who understands this must know that the moonlight is cold. A monk asked, "How was it before all Buddhas had appeared in the world?
The Master said, "In the royal palace, all news was cut off. The monk asked, "And how was it after they appeared in the world? The Master said, "In the royal palace, all news was cut off."
The Master said, "Prosperity and decline are each different.
When Chan Master Hailu of Taiyuan was invited by someone to provide offerings for Tripitaka Master Guanding, and the seats had been spread out, the Master took his place on that very seat.
At that time, the Dharma Master Yunshe asked, "In what year did you, Reverend, begin your practice?"
The Master said, "Head Monk, come forward. Zhaozhe approached. The Master said, "As for Kātyāyana, in what year did he practice the Way?
Zhaozhe was at a loss. The Master shouted, "This bed-wetting ghost! [Zhaozhe] asked, "Why are there so few people in the Master’s monastery?
Why are there so many people in Dinghui Monastery? The Master said, "Where the grass is deep, wild deer abound; where the cliffs are high, rhinoceroses dwell."
Dih Xi asked, "What is it to answer without being asked? The Master said, "The resonance of pines is the sound of a lute.
Zen Master Baishui of Jiazhou was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "The four oceans have no dwelling place; a single drop moistens the universe.
He was asked, "Regarding the single path of Caoxi, what should be discussed there? The Master said, "The pine by the mountain stream."
A thousand-year-old crane comes to gather; in the moonlight, the fragrant cassia and the phoenix return. The questioner asked, "What is this sutra? The Master said:
"The shuttle-casting barren woman resounds through the vast void; the mud-ox at the bottom of the sea cries out frequently at night."
A monk asked Chan Master You of Mount Tiangai in Fengxiang Prefecture, “What is the water of Mount Tiangai?
The Master said, “The four seas overflow, yet not a single drop is transgressed. A monk asked, “When a student intends to study the scriptures, how should it be?
The Master said, “Since you are a great merchant, why seek small profits? A monk asked, “When one remains unmoved in the face of sensory objects, how is this? The Master said, “The frontier regions.”
"Though there is an order, it is not a year of Great Peace.
Regarding Chan Master Linggui of Sanjiao Mountain in Qizhou, who was a successor of Chan Master Qingping: when he first visited Qingping, Qingping asked, "Why have you come? The Master replied:
He came to pay his respects. Baizhang asked, "Whom do you usually pay respects to? The Master replied, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Abbot.
Baizhang scolded him, saying, "You dull-witted monk! The Master then bowed. Baizhang struck the Master on the neck once with his hand; from this, he attained the essential meaning.
Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Come tomorrow, and I will tell you. For now—"
It cannot be attained through words.

Regarding the question asked by a monk to Chan Master Touzi Ganwen, the Dharma successor of Chan Master Touzi Tong: "When the Master ascends the precious throne, whom do you instruct? The Master replied: "Like the moon."
He went to Qianxi. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then the whole earth is without deficiency. The Master said, "Do not speak thus. [The monk] asked, "The father did not surrender himself;
why then did he surrender to the son? The Master said, "Is this not the business within another's own house?

[The monk] asked, "Does the relationship between father and son belong to the realm of effort or not? The Master said, "It does not. [The monk] asked, "If it does not belong to the realm of effort, how is it? The Master said, "..."
The father and son each shed their skins. [The son] asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "You and I have met.
While the Master was traveling through the mountains, he saw a cicada’s molted shell. An attendant asked, "The shell is here; where has the cicada gone?
The Master picked up the shell and shook it three or five times by his ear, making the sound of a cicada. Thereupon, the attendant attained awakening.
Chan Master Weizhi of Niutou in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas of the three periods have not been able to employ even a single bit of artifice.
The teachers throughout the land have mouths like flat carrying-poles. How do you all fare? It is truly not easy to eliminate [delusion].
Unless one has a surplus of knowledge, one cannot know it. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master replied, "Coarse grain from the mountain fields."

[The Master] served rice, vegetables, and pale yellow pickled radish. [A monk] asked, "What if a distinguished guest were to arrive suddenly? How would you respond? The Master said, "If he eats, let him eat;
whether he eats or not, let him go as he pleases. [Another monk] asked, "Without asking for the pearl from the jaws of the black dragon, how can one recognize the treasure within the home?
The Master said, "In the midst of such bustle, how could one become a person at leisure?"
A monk asked Zen Master Dengzhao of Xichuan Qingcheng Xiangshan: "When the Buddhas encounter difficulty, they hide their bodies within the flames.
I wonder, when a patch-robed monk encounters difficulty, where does he hide his body? The Master said: "A Persian placed inside a crystal jar.
[The monk] asked: "What is the newly risen moon? The Master said: "Too many people do not see it."
A monk asked Chan Master Tianfu of Shanfu, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The Yellow River has not a drop of water;
Mount Hua and Mount Yue have all sunk away."
A monk asked Chan Master Zungu of Zhongliang Mountain in Xingyuan Prefecture, "In the empty kalpa there was no one able to ask about the Dharma;
now that there is someone asking about the Dharma, how can it be settled? The Master said, "The Bodhisattva of Great Compassion sits inside a jar.
[Another] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The Daoist carries a leaking cup."
A monk asked Chan Master Guyin of Xiangzhou, "What is the mechanism of the white clouds that is untouched? The Master said, "A crane wearing a crow’s face;
the floating world is not abandoned."
A monk asked the Zen Master of Mount Jiuzhong in Anzhou, "I have long heard of Mount Jiuzhong; yet now that I have arrived, I see only one peak.
The Master said, "You, Dharma brother, see only one peak and do not see the nine peaks. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the nine peaks?
The Master replied, "The water is swift and the waves are coarse."
A monk asked the Second Generation Chan Master of Mount Pan in Youzhou, “How can one escape the three realms? The Master said, “How long has it been since you have been inside them?
The monk asked, “How then can one escape them? The Master said, “Green mountains do not obstruct the flight of white clouds.”

Question: We have heard it said in the teachings that "a person created by transformation" (nirmāṇapuruṣa) is like [the speaker] and that "afflictions" (kleśa) are like the son of a barren woman. What is the meaning of this principle?
The Master said: "Ācārya, you yourself are just like the son of a barren woman."
A monk asked Zen Master Jiuzhong Jinghui, "How can one pass over the deep pit of liberation? The Master said, "Do not seek to pass.
The monk asked, "How then can one pass? The Master said, "Seeking to pass is also not it."
Chan Master Yantong of Kannon-in in Tokyo was the son of the Lin family from Xingtai. When he first attended the patriarchal seat, he traveled extensively through Hengshan, Mount Lu, Min, and Shu.
Once, while passing through a deep valley at Fenglin, he suddenly beheld precious treasures manifesting; his companions looked on at one another in astonishment.
He intended to take it, but the Master said, "The ancients treated gold as if it were mere rubble;
how could we possibly be attached to this? Having said this, he left it behind and departed. He went to visit Touzi, who asked, "Where did you stay last night?

The Master replied, "At the Immovable Site of Enlightenment (*acalabodhimanda*). Touzi said, "Since you say it is immovable, how did you come here? The Master replied, "Having arrived here, is that not movement? Touzi—
He said, "Originally, I had no fixed dwelling; I sought out Guanyin and have resided there ever since. The assembly has always numbered several hundred.

During the reigns of Emperors Gaozu and Shizong of the Zhou dynasty, whenever I ascended to the abbot’s quarters, they would invariably pay me their respects. Upon ascending the throne, [Shizong] specially bestowed upon me purple robes and appointed me as the Great Master of Pure Precepts.
In the spring of the Bingyin year of Emperor Taizu of Song’s Qiande era, he manifested his passing. Having finished bestowing his final instructions upon his disciples, he remained serene."
Yan joined his palms and passed away. He was eighty-five years old; he had been a monk for sixty-five years. His stupa was erected at Fengtai in the eastern suburbs.
When Chan Master Siming of Haozhou was among the assembly, a monk asked: "What is the conduct of a senior *śrāmaṇera*?"
The Master said, “Yes. [The monk] asked, “What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said, “A maggot in excrement, its head emerging and submerging.
A monk asked Zen Master Zhao Fu of Fengxiang Prefecture: “Both Dongya and Wuya have gone out on patrol; why does the Master [remain here]?”
Mo did not leave the assembly. The Master said, "The positions of abbot and attendant differ; why do you, O *ācārya*, find this strange?

"For a solitary wanderer, how can one find a way to turn back toward the source? The Master said:
[The student] said, "The paths for the assembly are blocked. The Master said, "If that is so, then there is no place for showing respect.
The Master continued, "I say this: when your alms bowl falls to the ground, you cannot pick it up. A monk asked, "What is it like when one gives a single push and it turns?
The Master said, "When the wild horse runs, the whip and reins are snapped; the stone man claps his hands and laughs heartily."
A monk asked Chan Master Longxing of Tanzhou, "What is it like when one turns [the wheel] with a single push? The Master said, "Your faculties are not sharp.
The monk asked, "What is it like when sitting upright and donning the robe? The Master said, "It is not dignified. The monk asked, "Why is it not dignified?
The Master said, "Because it is not attained through cultivation or realization. The monk asked, "What is it to be a person on the Way? The Master said, "All day long..."
Ji frowned and asked, "What is it like when the text has not yet been punctuated? The Master said, "A blind child does not go out the door.
He asked, "What is it like before guest and host have been distinguished? The Master said, "In the midst of the double-six game board, no one shouts 'cheer!
He asked, "And after they have been distinguished? The Master said, "The dice have not yet been cast."
