The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Do not call it the Feet Teaching? While at Heshan, the Master saw off a fellow practitioner.
As the Elder Ju was about to leave the gate, he took up his staff and thrust it forward once. Ju had no reply. The Master said, "A stone ox blocks the ancient road;
one horse gives birth to twin foals" (later, a monk cited this to Shushan, who said, "A stone ox blocks the ancient road; one horse gives birth to three tigers").
A monk took his leave of Baofu. Baofu asked, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "To pay my respects to Luoshan. Baofu said, "When you reach Luoshan, tell him this:"
In the autumn, Baofu went to the capital to have an audience with the Great King.

He prepared forty questions to pose to the Master, thinking that if even a single phrase did not accord with the truth, he would say, "Do not claim you did not say so. A monk related this to the Master, who laughed heartily and said:
"Master Chen, since entering Fujian, we have passed beneath the Hongtang Bridge; not a single village has we seen where a 'hair-tip star' appears.
You and I shall ask Congzhan about this. Master Chen had no such questions; he possessed only a single sword.
Beneath that one stroke, there must be the intent of dividing the body, and there must also be the path of manifesting one's own being. If not...
When Mingbian had to establish the "unmanifest" (avijñapti), the monk returned and reported this to Fufu. Fufu said, "At that time, I was merely joking with him.
Later, in the autumn, when the Master went to visit, he specifically prepared a tea ceremony to invite Fufu, but Fufu did not attend.
Instead, he told the monk, "I previously made some joking remarks; I fear the Master might ask about them. When the monk returned and reported this, the Master said to him, "Tell him..."
The tiger did not eat the prostrate meat. The monk left again, and Fú subsequently arrived.
The Venerable Wúzhěn asked, "Regarding Yàntóu’s statement, 'Dòngshān is a fine Buddha, he simply has no light,' I wonder what deficiency Dòngshān had that he was said to have no light?
The Master called to Zhěn; Zhěn responded. The Master said, "Truly, he is a fine Buddha; it is simply—"
Wuguang said, "Master, why did you dismiss Master Chen’s words? The Master replied, "Where did Old Teacher Chen ever dismiss your words?
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Wuzhen was speechless. The Master struck him thirty blows and drove him out.
Wuzhen reported this to Zhaoqing, who spent the entire summer reviling him. At the end of the summer, Zhaoqing came in person to ask about it, and the Master recounted the incident clearly.

Sishi Qingsi immediately performed a prostration and repented, saying, "I have mistakenly offended the Great Master. A monk quoted a poem by Hanshan and asked, "When the white crane carries the bitter peach, what then?
The Master said, "A chaste woman chanting within her chamber. [The monk asked,] "When traveling a thousand li in a single breath, what then?
The Master said, "Seeing off a guest outside the post station. [The monk asked,] "When wishing to go to Mount Penglai, what then? The Master said, "... (The text here ends).
The Master said, "Leaning on a pillow, one gazes at a macaque. [A monk] asked, "What if one were to take this as provisions? The Master said, "An ancient sword before a skull.
[Another] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s intent throughout the tips of the hundred grasses?

The Master said, "It pierces your eyes. [Another] asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Leaning against the wall. [Another] asked, "What is that which lies before one's ten-thousand-fathom height? The Master said, "Leaning against the wall."
"Hongya. After that, there were tigers, wolves, and lions. At such a time as this, what is to be done?
The Master said, "Who is the sovereign of the triple world? Ask freely. The Master said, "Do you still know how to eat? When he was about to pass away, he ascended the hall and gathered the assembly.

After a long silence, he extended his left hand. The administrators did not understand its meaning, so he ordered the monks on the eastern side to step back. Later, he again extended [his right hand].
He raised his right hand and then had the monks on the western side withdraw. He then said, "To repay the Buddha's kindness, nothing surpasses the circulation of the Great Teaching.
Go back! Go back! Take care! Having spoken thus, he passed away with a gentle smile.
Chan Master Congfan of Xiangxi in Fuzhou arrived for an audience. The Master asked, "Are you not a monk from Gushan? The monk replied, "I am.
The Master said, "Why does the pearl upon your forehead not appear? The monk had no reply. As the monk was taking his leave, the Master saw him off at the gate.
He called out, "Upādhyāya! The monk turned his head. The Master said, "Your belly is full of Chan. The monk asked, "What about you, Master?"
"What kind of mental activity is this? The Master merely laughed heartily. As the Master was putting on his patched robe (*kaṣāya*), he spoke a verse:
Kāśyapa’s upper robe: To put it on requires swift wit. As soon as the arrow that beckons is distinguished, The hidden tortoise is revealed without concealment.
While Chan Master Yan of Shengshou Monastery in Fuzhou was mending his robes, a monk came for an audience. The Master held up the robe to show him, saying:
"This mountain monk has a single robe; I spread it out for all to see. The two strips of cloud-patterned cloth are divided—do not let the needle and thread be exposed.
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The monk had no reply. The Master said: "For so long a time, what have you been doing?"
Chan Master Huizong of Lingyan in Jizhou was a native of the Chen family of Fuzhou. He received his monastic training at Guishan. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Lingyan?
The Master said, "Pines and cypresses stand in dense, thick rows. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm?
The Master said, "Every night there is the cry of a monkey. [Another] asked, "What is the student’s own original portion?"
[The Master said: "How can you cast away true gold to pick up rubble?
Chan Master Xuan Sha Shibei Zongyi of Fuzhou, a successor of Chan Master Xuefeng Chuan, was the son of the Xie family of Min. From his youth, he was fond of fishing. He would drift...

On a small boat on the Nantai River, he associated with fishermen. At the beginning of the Xiantong era of the Tang dynasty, when he was only thirty years old, he suddenly felt a longing to transcend the mundane world.
He abandoned his boat and went to Furuo to receive the tonsure, then traveled to Kaiyuan Temple in Yuzhang to receive full ordination.

Wearing a coarse cotton robe and straw sandals, he took only enough food to sustain his breath; he often sat in meditation all day long, which caused everyone to marvel at him. [He studied] with Xuefeng and Ben...
Among his Dharma brothers, he was as close as a teacher to his disciples. Because of his ascetic practices, Feng called him "Dhūta Bei.
One day, Feng asked, "Which one is Dhūta Bei? The Master replied, "I would never dare to deceive anyone.
On another day, Feng called out, "Dhūta Bei! Why do you not go forth to study under various masters? The Master said, "Bodhidharma did not come to this eastern land. II.

The Patriarch did not go to the Western Heaven; Feng agreed with this. When he ascended Mount Xianggu, he labored together with the Master to construct the monastery. Disciples gathered there in great numbers.
The Master entered the inner chamber to seek resolution, never flagging from morning until night. Furthermore, he studied the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and realized the mind-ground.
Feng’s responses to questions were swift and nimble, in perfect accord with the sūtras. Among the eminent scholars from all quarters, there was nothing they could not understand.

He made a definitive resolution and certainly followed through by requesting further instruction. When he reached the point of cross-examining Xuefeng, he did not yield, acting as one who takes responsibility for the task.
Xuefeng said, "Dhūta Bei is a man of the second coming. Xuefeng ascended the hall and said, "To understand this matter, it is like an ancient mirror set upon its stand:
when a barbarian comes, a barbarian appears; when a Han Chinese comes, a Han Chinese appears. A monk stepped forward from the assembly and asked, "What if a bright mirror were to come?"
"What? Feng said, "Both barbarian and Han are hidden. The Master said, "Old Monk, even your heels have not yet touched the ground.

Later, while presiding over the assembly in the Dharma hall, he said: "The Way of the Buddha is vast and open; there are no set paths. It is the gate of liberation that has no gate, the intent of the Way-man that has no intent.
Because it does not abide within the three periods of time, it cannot be ascended or descended. To establish it as something contrary to reality is not to belong to the realm of creation."

Transformation: movement gives rise to the root of birth and death; stillness leads to intoxication in the land of dullness. When both movement and stillness are extinguished, one falls into emptiness and oblivion;
when both movement and stillness are gathered together, one is deluded regarding Buddha-nature. One must face the dust and face the mirror like withered wood and cold ashes;
when applied according to the occasion, one does not lose what is appropriate. As a mirror reflects all forms without its radiance being disturbed, so too is the flight of birds.
In the midst of space, it is not mixed with the color of emptiness; therefore, throughout the ten directions there are no reflected images, and within the three realms there is no trace of movement.
It does not fall into the mechanism of coming and going, nor does it abide in the mind of the intermediate state. There is no sound of a drum within a bell, and no sound of a bell within a drum;
bell and drum do not intersect one another. In every phrase there is no before or after, like a strong man extending his arm—relying on no external force—as a lion roams.
Acting thus, how could one seek a companion? When the nine heavens are free from obscuration, what need is there for penetration?

This single segment of radiance has never been dimmed. If you arrive here, the essence is tranquil yet eternally lucid; like the blazing sun, its flames are boundless, manifesting perfect enlightenment.
Unmoving within the void, it devours and incinerates heaven and earth, shining forth in total detachment. Now, as for the Buddha’s appearance in the world, fundamentally there is no coming or going.
Therefore, it is said to be "without substance. The Way is fundamentally suchness; phenomena are naturally and truly so. It does not depend on cultivation or realization;

it simply requires emptiness and stillness, while remaining unclouded in its functioning and untouched by the mire of worldly dust. Within this state, even a hair’s breadth that cannot be expressed through the Way constitutes an affiliate of the Demon King.
The space before and after a phrase is where the student finds difficulty. Thus, when a single phrase accords with the Way, the eighty thousand gates are forever closed.

To sever birth and death: even if you attain a state like the moon’s reflection in an autumn pond or the sound of a bell in a still night—unimpaired by being struck and undispersed by touching the waves—it remains a matter belonging to the shore of birth and death. Where a man of the Way acts, it is like fire melting ice;
the ice will never become ice again. Once an arrow has left the bowstring, it has no power to return. Therefore, it cannot be caged.
Willingly abiding, they do not turn their heads when called. The ancient sages made no arrangements; to this day, there is no fixed location.

If you reach this point, you ascend to the ultimate with every step. It belongs neither to the heterodox nor the orthodox; consciousness cannot perceive it, and wisdom cannot know it. To stir is to lose the source;

to awaken is to become deluded regarding the essential meaning. The followers of the Two Vehicles tremble with fear, and those of the Ten Stages are struck with terror. The path of speech is cut off, and the sphere of mental activity—

Extinction. Directly, one attains that Śākyamuni closed his room in Magadha, Vimalakīrti sealed his mouth in Vaiśālī, Subhūti manifested the Way through non-speaking, and Śakra and Brahmā ceased their listening while flowers rained down. If you see it thus before you, what more is there to doubt?
There is no place to settle; it is beyond the past, present, and future; it cannot be delimited; the paths of mind and thought are cut off, not because of adornment.
Yan! Originally, it is truly pure. Whether in movement, speech, or laughter, it is clearly manifest in every situation, lacking nothing whatsoever.

People of the present age do not awaken to this underlying principle; they recklessly involve themselves in worldly affairs and sensory dust, becoming stained and attached everywhere, and bound by fetters at every turn.

Even if you attain some degree of awakening and perceive that sensory objects are manifold and that names and forms are unreal, you may then intend to settle the mind and withdraw thoughts, subsuming phenomena into emptiness.
You might close your eyes and hide your gaze, yet thoughts will inevitably arise; you will repeatedly attempt to eliminate them, suppressing every subtle thought as soon as it appears.
Such a view is precisely that of an externalist who has fallen into nihilism—a dead man whose soul has not yet dispersed. It is a state of darkness.
Dark and vast, without perception or cognition, one plugs the ears and steals the bell, merely deceiving oneself. To make distinctions here is not so;
it is neither this nor that. Peering through the door and by the window, every phrase is manifest before one. It cannot be deliberated upon, nor does it involve words or ink.
Fundamentally severed from the realm of dust, fundamentally devoid of rank or position, it is provisionally named "one who has left the home-life," yet in the end, there is no trace.
True Suchness, ordinary beings and sages, hell-dwellers and devas—these are merely expedient means for healing the madness of one’s own child.
Even empty space undergoes no change; how could the Great Way have rising or sinking? To awaken is to move freely in all directions without ever departing from the fundamental limit.

If you reach this point, there is no place for either ordinary beings or sages to stand. If you direct your intention toward words and phrases, you will be drowned and destroyed. If you gallop outward, you will stray further from the source.

Seeking further leads one to fall into the realm of Māra. When ascending toward Suchness (tathatā), there is nothing that can be contrived; it is like a polished mirror that harbors no mosquitoes or gnats.
This principle is fundamentally level and plain—what need is there for weeding, removing, stirring, or stilling, or even raising an eyebrow? This is the path of true liberation.
Do not forcibly apply mental constructs or establish views that deviate from the truth. If you reach this point, do not admit even a hair’s breadth [of conceptualization].
To point toward it with the intellect is already an error; even if a thousand sages were to appear, they could not place a single word there.
Long stay, take care. Ascending the hall, he said: "I now ask you all: what matter can you actually take up? In what world do you abide?"
To establish one's life upon the body—can you still discern this? If you cannot discern it, it is like pressing on the eyes and seeing flowers; your perception is already mistaken from the start.

Do you know that what you currently see before you—the mountains, rivers, and great earth, form and emptiness, light and darkness, and all these various things—are all but the phantom flowers of a weary, deluded mind?
To call them such is called inverted perception. Now, as for those who have left the household life, they must recognize the mind and attain realization.

This is the fundamental source; therefore, one is called a śramaṇa. Now that you have already shaved your hair and donned the robes, assuming the appearance of a śramaṇa, you possess the capacity to benefit both yourself and others.
Look at them now: they are entirely black and vast, resembling ink.
If you cannot even save yourself, how can you claim to have attained the Way? O Benevolent One, the matters of the Buddha-Dharma are of great significance; do not treat them with indifference.
Do not gather in crowds to engage in idle chatter and confused talk, wasting time for the sake of profit. Time is difficult to obtain and deeply precious.
You who are great men—why do you not reflect upon and examine for yourselves what this matter truly is? As for the ancestral lineage from of old...
This is the lineage of the crowns of all Buddhas. Since you are unable to assume this responsibility, I have used skillful means to urge you:
simply follow the gate of Kāśyapa and proceed directly upward in a single leap. This one gate transcends the causes and effects of ordinary beings and sages;

it transcends the wondrously adorned world-ocean of Vairocana; it transcends the expedient gates of Śākyamuni; and from this very moment, for all eternity, it does not allow for [gradual] instruction.
There is but one thing. I shall grant it to you so that you may see with your own eyes; why do you not investigate it with urgency yourself?
Do not merely say, "Wait until I have accumulated pure karma over three or two lifetimes. O worthy one, what is this matter of the *zongcheng* (the vehicle of the school)?
It cannot be attained by adorning yourself through diligent effort, nor can it be attained through the power of knowing others' minds or past lives. Do you understand? It is just like this:

Śākyamuni has emerged from his place and performed all these transformations, expounding the twelve divisions of the teachings like pouring water from a jar, creating a grand display of Buddhist ritual.
Yet, within this gate, not a single point can be used; not even a hair’s breadth of artifice will do.
Do you understand? It is like a dream, like a delirious utterance. A śramaṇa should not emerge from his place. Not.
Regarding the matter of the shared dream: can you recognize it? If you can recognize it, you are one who has attained great liberation and reached the ultimate realization.
Therefore, you transcend the ordinary and surpass the sages; you emerge from birth and depart from death; you leave behind cause and effect; you go beyond Vairocana and pass over Śākyamuni.
You shall not be deceived by the causes and effects of ordinary beings or sages; nowhere shall anyone be able to recognize you. Do you understand?
Do not remain forever entangled in the net of love for birth and death, for you will be seized and carried away by the karma of good and evil, leaving you with no freedom.

Even if you refine your body and mind until they become like empty space, and even if you reach a state of brilliant clarity and profound stillness, you have not yet transcended the *vijñāna-skandha* (the aggregate of consciousness).
The ancients called this "like a rushing torrent. Because the flow is so rapid, one is unaware of it and falsely deems it stillness.

Practicing in such a manner, one will never be able to transcend the bounds of saṃsāra; as before, one will continue to be carried away by the cycle of rebirth. Therefore it is said: "All conditioned phenomena are impermanent.
Even the fruits and merits of the Three Vehicles are thus to be feared. Without the eye of the Way, one will likewise not reach the ultimate end. Why?
It is as if an ordinary person of this world, without expending even a hair’s breadth of effort, were to suddenly transcend [to enlightenment].
Can you understand and save your mind and energy? Do you still aspire to this? I exhort you: I shall stand here now and wait for you to grasp it;
I will not further instruct you to apply effort or refine your practice. If you do not act thus now, when will you? Will you consent? Then he descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "All of you are like those sitting within the great ocean, submerged up to their heads and yet reaching out their hands to ask others for water to drink.
Those who study Prajñā must possess great capacity and great wisdom before they can succeed.
If one possesses wisdom, one may escape right now; but if one's faculties are dull, then directly—"
You must apply yourself with diligent effort and enduring resolve, forgetting fatigue day and night, losing sleep and food as if you had lost your parents.
If you are this urgent and persistent for the rest of your life, you will surely receive the support of others and be able to penetrate to the very bone and investigate the reality;
it will not be difficult to grasp. Furthermore, who nowadays is truly capable of receiving instruction? O worthy one, do not merely memorize!
Regarding what is called "giving an answer" (jìyǔ): it is somewhat like reciting a *dhāraṇī*. One steps forward with a swagger, making "tō tō hē hē" sounds in one's mouth.
When caught by someone and interrogated, having no way to escape, one immediately becomes angry and says, "The Master did not answer me;
practicing the Way like this is so bitter! Do you understand? There is a certain kind of monk sitting on a rope-bench who calls himself...
"Good spiritual friends," [he said], "when questioned, merely shake their bodies, move their hands, blink their eyes, stick out their tongues, and stare blankly.

Furthermore, there is another kind who speak of 'bright clarity' and 'spiritual awareness,' claiming that the nature of wisdom in the numinous mind can see and hear, acting as a sovereign within the field of the five aggregates.
To act as a spiritual friend in such a manner is to greatly deceive people. Do you know? I now ask you: if you were to recognize [it]..."
"Vivid and lucid—this is your true reality. Why is it that when you are drowsy, this vivid lucidity does not manifest?
If it were not present during drowsiness, why would there be times of vivid clarity? Do you understand? This is called 'mistaking a thief for one's own son';
it is the root of birth and death, the conditioning energy of deluded thought. If you wish to recognize its source,"
"Mā! I tell you: that which is luminous and aware exists only because of the dharmas of external objects, such as forms, sounds, and fragrances;
it is through these that discrimination arises, leading one to say, 'This is the luminous and aware. If those external objects were absent, this luminous and aware nature of yours [would not exist]."
It is like the hair of a tortoise or the horns of a rabbit. Where, O worthy one, does true reality reside?
If you now wish to attain mastery over the field of the five aggregates, you need only recognize your own secret vajra-body. An ancient said to you:
It is perfectly complete and all-pervading, encompassing the entire realm of sand-grains. I shall now provide a partial explanation for you, wise one, so that you may understand it through analogy.

Do you see the sun over Jambudvīpa to the south? Whatever worldly people undertake—whether for building projects, livelihood, sustenance, or their various mental activities and labors—all are established by receiving the light of the sun. As for the very substance of the sun itself:
Are there still many other types of mental activities? Is there anything that is not all-pervasive? If you wish to recognize the adamantine essence, you must likewise observe it in this way:
namely, as the mountains, rivers, and great earth; the lands of the ten directions; and form, emptiness, light, and darkness.
Even your own body and mind are entirely sustained by the manifestation of your perfected majestic radiance.

It is simply the karma performed by the various classes of beings, including devas and humans, which subsequently receives its retribution of birth. Whether sentient or insentient, there is nothing that does not sustain itself through your majestic radiance.
Even up to the point where all Buddhas attain the Way, realize the fruit, and engage with and benefit sentient beings—none of this occurs without entirely relying upon your majestic radiance.
As for this adamantine essence, does it contain ordinary beings and Buddhas? Does it possess the activity of your mind? One cannot say that it does not.
Then you will be able to depart. Do you understand? Since you possess such a marvelous capacity to manifest yourself in the midst of the present moment, why do you not clarify and seize the cause?
Why, instead, do you follow others and make your livelihood within the field of the five aggregates and the realm of ghosts, deceiving yourself right now?
Suddenly, when the demon of impermanence arrives, your eyes will roll back in terror and your body will fall into the view of self-existence.
I command you to see. At such a time, it is extremely difficult to sustain and bear; it is like the great agony of a living turtle shedding its shell.
O worthy one, do not mistake a state of drowsy understanding for the truth, for you have not yet been able to cover even a hair’s breadth of it.
Do you understand? There is no peace within the three realms; they are like a burning house. Furthermore, you are not yet a person who has attained peace and happiness. Only—
They form great crowds and roam here and there in the human world like wild deer flying or running about, seeking only food and clothing.
If you act in such a manner, how can you practice the Way of the King? Do you understand? Kings and great ministers do not bind or restrain you.
Your parents have permitted you to leave the household life; donors from the ten directions provide you with food and clothing;

and the local spirits and dragons protect you. You must possess a sense of shame and gratitude; only then can you succeed. Do not fail these people. On these long rows of beds, sitting in line upon the floor, you will gradually be transformed.
Do not say that this is true peace and happiness; it is all merely the nourishment of rice gruel and meals that has sustained you.
It is like a rotting winter melon being carried away and buried in the earth; the karmic consciousness is vast and boundless, with no foundation upon which to rely.
How can a śramaṇa come to such a state? As for all those wriggling creatures upon the great earth, I call them those dwelling in the kalpa of hell.
If you do not resolve this now, tomorrow or the day after, you will enter the womb of a donkey or the belly of a horse.
Dragging plows and pulling harrows; bitting iron and bearing saddles; being pounded by pestles and ground in mills;
being burned and boiled in water and fire—it is not easy at all to undergo these things. You must be truly fearful! This is your own doing; do you understand?

If you were to realize it, from this very moment down through eternal kalpas, I would never have let you have such news as this. If you do not realize it, this is the cause of affliction and evil karma.
"Conditions. It will not rest for one or two kalpas; it shall last as long as your own adamantine life. Do you understand?

While the Master was in the midst of his daily practice, he heard the sound of a swallow and said, "Profoundly expounding the true reality, skillfully preaching the essential Dharma. He then descended from his seat.
At that time, a monk requested further instruction, saying, "I do not understand. The Master replied, "Go! Who would believe you? Gushan arrived.
The Master drew a circle and showed it to him. Xiangshan said, "No one can get out of this.
The Master said, "I knew you would go about making your living in the belly of a donkey or a horse. Xiangshan asked, "And what about you, Preceptor? The Master said:
"No one can come forth with this," he said. Shanshan said, "The Master may say such things, but why can I not?
The Master replied, "I have it; you do not. One day, as the assembly gathered for the formal lecture, the Master took up his staff and drove them all away at once.
He then turned back toward the attendant and said, "Today I have reached a realization that nearly caused me to fall into hell!"
"Prison is like being struck by an arrow. A monk said, "I am joyful to have obtained, through the Master, a human body once again.

While the monk was standing in attendance, the Master pointed with his staff at a white spot on the ground before him and asked, "Do you see it? "I see it," he replied. When the Master asked this three times, the monk answered in the same way each time.
The Master said, "You see it, and I see it too. Why do you say you do not understand? The Master [then departed].
Once, he visited the Abbot of Sandou Hermitage. As soon as they met, the Abbot said, "Do not be offended that, having lived in the mountains for so long, I have no sitting mat.
The Master said, "Everyone has a hermitage; why do you have none? The Abbot said, "Sit down and drink some tea first. The Master said:
The Abbot had always been present [in the Way]. While attending Xuefeng, two monks passed by from below the steps.
Xuefeng said, "These two men are fit to be 'seed-grass' (disciples). The Master said, "I am not like this. Xuefeng asked, "How about you?"
The Master said, "He deserves thirty blows right now. Once, Xuefeng pointed to a fire and said, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time are turning the Great Dharma Wheel within this flame.
The Master said, "Lately, the royal decree has become quite strict. Xuefeng asked, "How so?"
The Master said, "I do not permit you to snatch away the market. Yunmen said, "The flames preach the Dharma for the Buddhas of the three periods;
the Buddhas of the three periods stand upon the ground and listen. Nanji went to Xuefeng. Xuefeng ordered him to visit the Master (Baizhang).
The Master asked, "An ancient said, 'In this matter, only I can know it. Elder, what about you? Nanji said, "One must know that which does not seek."
The Master said, "Zhizhe, why do you, a monk from the mountain peak, undergo such hardship?
Once, while Xuefeng was performing communal labor in the fields, he saw a snake. He lifted it up with his staff and called to the assembly, saying, "Look! Look! Then, with a knife, he cut it in two.
Zhizhe threw the staff behind him and did not look back. The assembly was stunned. Xuefeng said, "How magnificent!"
While attending Xuefeng as they were walking in the mountains, Xuefeng pointed to the ground before him and said, "On this patch of earth, one could build a seamless stupa.
The Master asked, "How high would it be? Xuefeng looked up and down. The Master said, "The merit and reward of humans and devas is not lacking;
however, as for the prediction received at Vulture Peak, you have not even dreamed of it. Xuefeng asked, "Then what do you say?"
Sheng said, "Seven feet or eight feet. Xuefeng said, "The world is one foot wide; the ancient mirror is one foot wide. The world is ten feet wide;
the ancient mirror is ten feet wide. The Master pointed to the brazier and asked, "How wide is this brazier?
Xuefeng replied, "It is as wide as the ancient mirror. The Master said, "Old monk, your heels have not yet touched the ground. The Master [said], "..."
He first resided at Puying Monastery and later moved to Xuansha. All the monastic communities throughout the land welcomed him as their guest upon hearing his reputation.
The regional governor of Min, Lord Wang, treated him with the etiquette due to a teacher. His disciples numbered over eight hundred, and the doors of his quarters were never closed.

After sitting in silence for a long while during an ascent to the hall, he said, "I have brought you to the point of utter exhaustion; do you understand? A monk asked, "When it is silent and wordless, how is it?"
"What? the Master asked. "Why are you talking in your sleep? The monk said, "I ask the Master to speak of the fundamental matter. The Master said, "Why are you dozing off?
The monk said, "The student is indeed dozing; how about the Master? The Master said, "How can you be so lacking in discernment?"

it is not that it is. What is the meaning of this? Baofu picked up his tea cup. The Master said, "Is that not being non-contradictory?"
Question: "What is the true human body? The Master said: "Right now, what is this body? Question: "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said:
"How could one ever reach such a state? Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "A single point of the golden crow;
ten thousand miles of cloudless sky. Ascending the hall, he said: "If you wish to know this matter, it is like a single-edged sword."
A monk asked, "The student is a corpse; what is the sword? The Master said, "Drag this corpse out!

The monk responded with an assent and immediately returned to the monks' hall, packed his things, and departed. When the Master heard of this in the evening, he remarked, "He deserves a blow from my staff.

(Dongchan Qi said: "If this monk had not been willing, what fault would there have been in Gushan? If he was willing, why did he depart so abruptly? Furthermore, Gushan’s staff both rewards and punishes him. Let those with discerning eyes try to deliberate upon this.")
He asked a monk, "Guishan had a saying: 'There is no sentence that does not cross the stone gate. How would you express this? The monk said, "I ask the Master to strike me immediately.
He asked, "What is the place where the ancients saved effort? The Master said, "Why do you exert effort in asking?
He asked, "It is said that one's words fill the world yet there is no fault in the mouth. What is 'no fault in the mouth'? The Master said, "What fault could there be?"

A question was asked: "What is this matter of the separate transmission outside the teachings? The Master said, "Go drink tea. The Master and the Military Governor of Min were gazing up at a Buddha image.
The Governor asked, "What kind of Buddha is this? The Master said, "I ask Your Majesty to examine it. The Governor said, "Examining is not the Buddha. The Master said, "Then what is it?
The Governor had no reply. (Changqing spoke on his behalf: "I have long heard that the Great Master dwells among the assembly; how can you act so precipitously?")
A question was asked: "How does one proclaim the supreme vehicle (zongsheng) from above? The Master struck him across the mouth with his whisk.
A question was asked: "What is the point of essential realization? The Master said, "Are you still ashamed? Addressing the assembly, he said:

"Now, for the sake of you gentlemen, I thrust my head into the transformative gate of the various sages, yet I cannot shake myself free. Therefore, I tell all people that the teachings cannot be set aside."
When he arrived, the Patriarch had not yet come from the West. Not even the Buddhas of the three periods could proclaim it; it cannot be contained within the twelve divisions of the teachings.

Neither ordinary beings nor sages can encompass it, and it cannot be transmitted through past or present. Yet, suddenly there was this man who, having not yet mastered a single message, spoke to him in such a manner.
When he was struck across the mouth by the other, can you blame him? Nevertheless, even so, it is not...
He received a beating. Gushan usually said, "There is yet another person who does not cross the Stone Gate;
there must be a phrase for not crossing the Stone Gate. "What is this phrase for not crossing the Stone Gate? Gushan remained silent for over thirty years.
Those who come from the five lakes and four seas go to the summit of the high mountain to gaze at the peaks and play by the waters;
yet not one person has been seen who has swiftly and penetratingly mastered this message. Is there anyone now who has mastered it? If one has mastered it, one is not deluded.
Brothers, if you have not, then disperse as you please. Be careful. The Master had a verse which said: "Even directly beneath..."

It is difficult to encounter. As soon as one seeks it through words, it becomes increasingly distant. If we discuss the Buddha and the Patriarchs, they are separated by a vast distance across the heavens.

The Master raised this point and asked a monk, "How do you understand this? The monk was speechless. The Master then said to his attendant, "I do not understand; please provide a turning word on my behalf.
The attendant said, "If the Master speaks in such a manner, you are still separated from them by a vast distance across the heavens. The monk reported this to the Master, and the Master—
He summoned an attendant and asked him, "Is it right for you to speak on behalf of this monk? The attendant replied, "Yes. The Master then struck him and expelled him from the monastery.
Chan Master Lingzhao Zhenjue of Longhua Temple in Hangzhou was a native of Goryeo. He traveled as a wanderer through Min and Yue, and subsequently ascended [to the abbacy].
The Hall of Xuefeng was in profound accord with the primordial intent. There lived a monk clad in a single robe who diligently attended to all communal duties;
the people of Min called him "Zhao the Cotton-Rag Monk. One night, pointing to the crescent moon, he asked the senior monk Pu, "Where has that other piece gone?
Pu replied, "Do not engage in false imaginings. The Master said, "One piece is lost. Although the assembly marveled at this, he remained serene and unassuming.
Zizhi. Initially residing at Mount Qiyun in Wuzhou, he ascended the hall. After a long silence, he suddenly extended his hand and looked at the assembly, saying, "Beg a little bit!
Beg a little bit! He spoke again, saying, "One person transmits what is false; ten thousand people transmit what is real. A monk asked: [Question omitted].
"The grass child can sing and dance. I do not know whether such a thing still exists today. The Master descended from his seat, performed a dance, and asked, "Does the śrāmaṇera understand?
The śrāmaṇera said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Even this mountain monk does not understand how to perform the *quzi* (ditty).

Later, he moved to Jingqing in Yuezhou. He ascended the hall and said, "Today, I have issued my command to its full extent. At that time, a monk came forward and said, "I ask the Master to state his command. The Master—
He then said: "Hūṃ hūṃ! Question: What is the fundamental matter of the student? The Master said: 'Jingqing does not spare his mouth. Question:
I ask the Master to polish it for me. The Master said: 'Eight parts complete. Question: Why is it not ten parts complete? The Master said:"
"Do you know how Jingqing attained realization? He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Wufeng.

The Master said, "What did you go there for? The monk said, "To pay my respects to the Master. The Master said, "Why do you not pay your respects yourself? The monk said, "I have already paid my respects.
The Master said, "The waters of Lake Jing are shallow. He was asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "Do not mistakenly employ names and words."
[The student] asked: "Is there not some skillful means? The Master said: "A crow's head raises a sparrow. [The student] asked:
"An ancient said, 'When you see form, you see the mind. This is form; which one is the mind? The Master said: "Asking such a question—do you not underestimate this mountain monk?
[The student] asked: "Before it was split open, please, Master, decide for me. The Master said: "Where does it fall? [The student] said: "I have let my mouth slip."

This was not permissible. The Master said, "This too is Hanshan escorting Shide. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Stop, stop! You have let your mouth run; I, the mountain monk, have let my mouth run.
[The monk] said, "A fierce tiger does not eat its own offspring. The Master said, "The donkey's head emerges; the horse's head turns back.
The Master suddenly asked a monk, "Do you remember? [The monk] said, "I remember. The Master said, "Say what? [The monk] said, "I say..."
"What is it? the Master asked. The monk replied, "A child from Huainan enters a temple. The Master said, "To ask 'What is this? is like a swift falcon; even a swift hawk cannot catch up.
The Master continued, "The *dārala* (monk) asks one way, and I, the mountain monk, answer another. The monk said, "I beg the Master to answer otherwise.
The Master said, "Travelers ten li away compare their journey to one more stage. [The monk] asked, "When it is said that 'though gold dust is precious, it cannot enter the eye,' what then?"
"What? the Master asked. "This very thing cannot be grasped; can it still be grasped? The monk bowed. The Master said, "The Shen of Deep Sands asks:
'Under the Bodhi tree, one delivers sentient beings. What is the Bodhi tree? The Master replied, "It is very much like the *kuliang* tree.
[The monk] asked, "Why is it like the *kuliang* tree? The Master said, "If you are not originally a fine horse, why trouble yourself with the shadow of the whip?"
The Master entered nirvana on the twenty-sixth day of the intercalary seventh month in the Dingwei year of the Tianfu era of the Later Han dynasty.
He was enshrined in a stupa at Mount Daci in Hangzhou. His age was seventy-eight.
Cuiyan Lingcan Yongming Chanshi of Mingzhou was a native of Anji Prefecture. A monk asked, "Without relying on the three inches [of the mouth], please let the Master speak.
The Master said, "He was cast out from the tea hall. [The monk] asked about the National Teacher’s three calls to his attendant.
"What is the meaning? The Master said, "Why do you press me so? He ascended the hall and said: "For an entire summer, I have been talking here and there with my brothers.

Chan Master Daofu Shunde of Jingqing Temple in Yue State was the son of the Chen family of Yongjia. From childhood, he abstained from meat and pungent roots.
His relatives strongly urged him to eat dried fish, which immediately caused him to retch. He subsequently sought ordination and received full precepts at Kaiyuan Temple in his home province.

[The monk] said, "Five peaks. The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows. [The monk] asked, "Where does the fault lie?

"How do you serve others? The Master said, "I have not yet drunk tea today. The monk asked, "Please grant me your instruction. The Master said, "You have already passed by.
A monk asked, "If I ask about the direct principle, I shall not ask; please point to it indirectly. The Master said, "Take the cat and go.

He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "Huaguang. The Master then pushed him out and closed the door; the monk was speechless. He asked another monk, "Where have you come from? [The monk replied,] "From the road. The Master said, "Go! The monk had no response.
When Feng met a man on the Way, he did not respond with either speech or silence. [Feng] asked, "I do not know what you would use to respond. The Master rebuked him, saying, "Get out! Ask the monks:
'What is the matter of face-to-face encounter? [Feng] said, "I ask the Master to examine it for me. The Master said, "If you speak in such a way, does that truly hit the mark?
[Feng] said, "It would be improper to do so intentionally. The Master said, "That is another approach entirely. [Someone] asked, "What is the numinous source?"

As he was traveling along the road, the Master asked, "How did you cross over? The Chief Administrator (Yuanzhu) of Xuefeng Monastery sent a letter inviting him, saying, "The Abbot at Mount Shantou is advanced in years;
why does the Elder not enter the mountain range once more? The Master replied in a letter:
"I shall enter the mountain range again only when the Abbot of Mount Shantou has attained a different realization. A monk asked, "What is the realization of Xuefeng?"
The Master said, "I am also startled.
Chan Master Xuantong of Dapushan in Fuzhou was a native of that same prefecture. A monk asked, "How can one obtain the pearl from beneath the chin of a black dragon?
The Master then clapped his hands and winked. [The monk] asked, "Regarding the previous matter before the application of skillful means, how is it? The Master then—
He sent the monk away. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "You bone-chewing fellow, get out!
A monk asked, "When one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha, what then? The Master said, "Take off your shackles and then we shall discuss it.
A monk asked, "I am seeking refuge in haste; I pray the Master will grant me refuge. The Master said, "Dull-witted fellow."
Chan Master Jiaoran of Changsheng Mountain in Fuzhou was a native of that same prefecture.
Having long relied upon Xuefeng, one day while he was cutting down trees with a monk, Xuefeng said, "When you reach the heartwood, stop. The Master said, "Cut it away!
Xuefeng said, "The ancients transmitted mind to mind; why do you say 'cut it away'? The Master threw down his axe and said, "Transmit it! Xuefeng struck him with his staff.
He took his staff and departed. A monk asked Xuefeng, "What is the first phrase? Xuefeng remained silent for a long while.
The monk reported this to the Master (Linji), who said, "This is the second phrase. Xuefeng then sent the same monk back to ask again, "What is the first phrase?
The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven! During a communal work session (*pǔqǐng*), Xuefeng asked, "The ancients said, 'Who knows the mat...'"
"Underneath that hat, he was originally a man of sorrow from the past. What was the meaning of the ancients' intent?
The Master tilted his straw rainhat sideways and said, "What kind of person speaks such words? Xuefeng asked the Master, "One who upholds the sutras is able to shoulder the Tathāgata.
Who is it that shoulders the Tathāgata? The Master then took hold of Xuefeng and placed him upon the meditation seat. During a communal work session (*pingsheng*), Xuefeng...
Feng was carrying a bundle of rattan when he encountered a monk on the road. He immediately threw it down.

As the monk reached out to pick it up, Feng tripped him over and went back, saying to the Master, "Today I have tripped this monk with great joy. The Master said, "It would be better if you, Master, were to take this monk’s place in the Nirvana Hall.
Feng then stopped. Xuefeng asked, "When both light and objects have vanished, what is it that remains?"
The Master said, "I let Jiaoran pass; tell me, where is the Way? Feng said, "How would you say it if I let you pass?
[Jiaoran] said, "I also let the Master pass. Feng said, "I grant you twenty blows! The Master then bowed. Later, when he resided [in his own monastery],...
A monk asked, "An ancient said, 'Ignorance is itself Buddha-nature; there is no need to eliminate afflictions.
What is meant by 'ignorance is itself Buddha-nature'? The Master’s expression turned fierce; raising his fist, he scolded him, saying, "I am going to beat this monk today!
The monk asked, "What is meant by 'there is no need to eliminate afflictions'? The Master seized the monk's head with his hand and said, "This monk has earned it."
Thus he inspired people’s karmic activity. A questioner asked: "When one meets a man who has attained the Way, if one does not respond with speech or silence, what then does one use to respond?
The Master said: "What can the ink on this paper be used for? The Military Governor of Min appointed him as the Zen Master Dashi;
his final whereabouts remain unknown.
Chan Master Zhifu of Ehu in Xinzhou was a native of Fuzhou. A monk asked, "The myriad dharmas return to the One; where does the One return?
The Master said, "It is not only you, Dharma brother, who are busy. Another asked, "If empty space were to preach the sutras, what would it take as its fundamental principle?"
The Master said, "Your Reverence is not right. He sent the assembly out and asked, "Does the son of one who has committed the five heinous crimes still receive his father’s legacy?
The Master said, "Though he may have the means to sever himself, he cannot avoid wounding himself. He asked, "What is it like to be a person above the Buddha?
The Master said, "I knew well that you, Your Reverence, would be at a loss. The questioner asked, "Why are you at a loss? The Master said, "Not yet."
"It must be that the petty man is able to see the noble one. [The monk] asked: "Please tell me, Master, what is meant by the phrase 'the question is before you'?
The Master said: "What are you searching for beneath your own heels? [The monk] said: "I am asking you right now. The Master said: "Look at the *ācārya* changing his form; he cannot be questioned.
"What was the meaning of Xuefeng throwing down his staff? The Master threw his incense-spoon to the ground. The monk said: "..."
"I do not understand; what is the meaning of this? The Master said, "This is no good seed. Get out! A monk asked, "What is the first phrase of Geohu?
The Master said, "Say something. The monk asked, "How is it so? The Master said, "It interferes with my sleep.

A monk asked, "When one does not answer when asked, 'Not asking,' how is it? The Master said, "Who would know among those who ask? A monk asked, "Regarding the lost son who has not yet [found his way]..."
"How is it when returning home? The Master said, "It is not on the road. "How is it after returning?
The Master said, "One is precisely in delusion. The monk asked, "What is the matter of the source? The Master said, "What are you seeking on the road?
A monk asked, "What is the one phrase? The Master said, "Do you understand? The monk said, "In that case, is this not it? The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven!"

Jingqing asked, "What is that which is right now? The Master said, "Why 'right now' again? Jingqing said, "I have nearly exhausted my efforts. The Master said, "The words are contrary, but the meaning is compliant. One day, the Master did not go to the hall. An attendant came to invite him to attend the hall. The Master said, "The words are contrary, but the meaning is compliant. The attendant said, "Master, why do you not go? The Master said, "If I go, it will be like adding frost to snow. The Master said, "Today I ate my fill of oil-cakes at the manor. The monk said, "The Master has never gone out of the monastery.

The Master said, "Just go and ask the manor owner. As the monk was about to leave the gate, he suddenly saw the manor owner returning to thank him, saying, "The Master came to the manor and ate oil-cakes."
Chan Master Wuzhen of Huadu Monastery in Xixing, Hangzhou, was a native of Quanzhou. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?
The Master raised his whisk. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Go drink tea. A monk asked, "What is one speck of dust?
The Master said, "The nine generations divided in a single kṣaṇa. The monk asked, "How can it contain the Dharma-realm? The Master said:
"Where does the Dharma-realm reside? [The Master asked: "The valleys and gorges each differ; what do you mean by 'clarifying oneness'?
[The student] said: "Why are you panting? [The student] asked: "I am a beginner; I beg the Master for instruction on the path of entry. The Master said: "What is it that you find strange about Huadu?
[The student] asked: "What is the mani-jewel that reflects colors? The Master said: "Blue, yellow, red, and white. [The student] said: [It is so.]
"What is the mani-jewel that does not follow form? The Master said, "Blue, yellow, and also white. Question: "What is the meaning of the coming from the West?
The Master said, "Is it coming from the East? Is it coming from the West? Question: "How was it before Niu-t'ou had seen the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "Birds and beasts were all lost in confusion. Question: "How was it after he saw him? The Master said, "The mountains are deep and the waters are cold."
Question: What was the subject of the conversation between Vimalakīrti and Mañjuśrī? The Master said: "There is only the Mirror Lake before the gate;
the clear breeze does not alter its waves of old."
Chan Master Longshou Shaoqing Xingfa was the son of the Chen family of Quanzhou.
While attending Xuefeng as they were walking in the mountains, he saw the leaves of a taro plant move. Xuefeng pointed to the moving leaf to show him. The Master said, "Shaoqing is very much afraid.
Xuefeng replied, "That is something inside your own house; why are you afraid? At these words, the Master attained realization. Subsequently, he resided at Longxi.
A monk asked, "An ancient said, 'The Maṇi Hall has four corners; one corner is always exposed. What is this corner that is always exposed? The Master raised his whisk.
Another asked, "If not a single grain of rice is stored, how can the hunger of ten thousand people be relieved? The Master raised his whisk.
The Master said, "It would be like snatching a sword from before a gallant; I see that you are no clever fellow.
A monk asked, "How is it at a place where the ears and eyes do not reach? The Master said, "You have no such activity. The monk said, "If that is so, then I hear.
The Master said, "Truly a deaf man!"
Chan Master Xingtao Renhui of Qianzong Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of the Wang family in Quanzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "I have studied under the same master as Śākyamuni.
Tell me, whom have you studied under? At that moment, a monk stepped forward, bowed, and prepared to ask a question.

The Master said, "Wrong! and immediately descended from his seat. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of [the Patriarch’s] coming from the West? The Master replied, "Mount Xiong'er has never hidden it."
A questioner asked for the Master’s expedient means regarding the matter of direct immediacy. The Master said, "Were it not for your question, I would not have spoken.
[The questioner] asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "In broad daylight, there are no idle people."
Chan Master Conggan Chaozheng of Lianhua Yongfu Monastery in Fuzhou was asked by a monk: "In the Confucian school, the Five Constant Virtues are taken as the ultimate standard.
I wonder, what does the School of the Patriarchs take as its ultimate standard? The Master remained silent for a long while. The monk said, "If that is so, then students would be acting with haste.
The Master said, "A staff is well suited for you. Another asked: "The scriptures say that there is only the One Vehicle."
[The student asked about] the Dharma. "What is the One Vehicle Dharma? The Master said, "Tell me, what am I doing here?
[The student] said, "In that case, I do not understand the meaning of the teaching. The Master said, "Even so, you have not failed me.
[Another student] asked, "Not receiving [the teaching] from the place of questioning—this is still the student’s way of questioning; how about the Master’s way? The Master said, "Go and drink tea."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Changqing says, 'When the Dharma is exhausted, there are no subjects.
Yongfu, however, does not agree with this. If the Dharma were not exhausted, how could one possibly have subjects? At that time, a monk said, "I ask the Master to exhaust the Dharma.

The Master said, "I do not want you to pay your taxes; I am not asking about anything else. Please grant me your compassion for this direct request. The Master said, "That will not do; prostrate three times!"

A great assembly had gathered, requesting the Master to preach the Dharma. The Master asked, “Do you hear? They replied, “If one were to hesitate further in thought, it would be difficult to reach [the truth].

The Master said, “In reality, it is attained. One day, as the Master was ascending the hall, he stood by his seat and addressed the assembly, saying, “Two Honored Ones do not manifest their transformations simultaneously,” and then he returned to his quarters.
Chan Master Guiben of Yun’gai Shuangquan Monastery in Xiangzhou was a native of Jingzhao.

When he first visited Xuefeng, after performing his prostrations, the Master sat astride the back of the meditation seat. At this, Guiben attained realization. Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "What is the Double Spring?
The Master said, "A pity for that pair of eyebrows. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Never [seen before]."
It would exhaust the strength of Yu; the matter of the turbulent currents remains unknown. [A monk] asked, "What is the true meaning of the coming from the West?

The Master then grabbed him by the collar. The monk’s face turned pale with alarm. The Master said, "In my place, there is nothing of this sort. The Master’s fingers were slender and long, exceptionally distinct from those of others;
he was thus titled the Great Master of Hand-Examination (Shouxiang Dashi).
A monk asked Master Linquan of Shaoshan, "What is one speck of dust? The Master said, "Unconsciously it becomes a mountain.
A monk asked Master Nanyuan of Luoyang, "What is the non-arising of all phenomena? The Master said, "It has already arisen."
There was a Confucian scholar who had extensively studied the past and present; he was commonly called Zhang Baihui (Zhang Hundred Meetings).

He went to visit the Master. The Master asked, "Are you not Zhang Baihui? He replied, "I dare not say so. The Master drew a line in the air with his hand and asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand."
The Master said, "If you have not understood even one, from where could you have obtained a hundred understandings?
Chan Master Keshou of Dongyan in Yuezhou was asked by a monk, "What is the true master of Dongyan? The Master said, "Open it.
He was asked, "What is the place where the Master intimately benefits people? The Master said, "The great ocean does not harbor the dead."
Shi asked, "What is the path that leads upward? The Master held up the collar of his robe and showed it to him.
A student asked, "I have traveled far to seek the teacher; please grant me a skillful means. The Master said, "The skillful means is already here."
A monk asked Zen Master Xingzhou of Fahai Monastery in Dingzhou, “What is it like when the wind is calm and the waves are still?
The Master said, “It blows down the southern wall. The monk asked, “What is the treasure within the Way? The Master said, “It does not reveal its radiance.
The monk said, “Is this not it? The Master said, “If it were, it would be revealed.”
A monk asked Chan Master Tong of Longjing in Hangzhou, "What is the dragon of Longjing? The Master said, "Its spirit and bearing are naturally distinct;
the divine artisan cannot paint it. The monk asked, "Why can it not be painted? The Master said, "It stands out from the crowd without horns;
it does not conform to its kind. The monk asked, "Does it know how to bring down rain? The Master said, "It universally moistens all without limit."

Everywhere there were grains forming. [The monk] asked, "Is there still the matter of the School Gate (the Zen school) or not? The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter of the School Gate?
The Master said, "From the beginning it has had no form or shape; responding to things, it has never been deficient."
Chan Master Zongjing of Longxing Monastery in Hangzhou was a native of Taizhou. He first visited Xuefeng, where he vowed to serve as the head cook for over ten years.
Once, while in the monks' hall, he bared one shoulder to hang a curtain.

Upon seeing this, Xuefeng remarked, "In the future, you shall dwell as an abbot, but among your thousand monks, there will not be a single true patch-robed practitioner. The Master repented his error and returned to Zhejiang to reside there.
At Liutong Yuan, the Qian Wang ordered him to reside at Longxing Temple. There were over a thousand followers, all of whom were disciples engaged in the study and recitation of the Three Studies.
This was exactly as Xuefeng had foretold. A monk asked, "What is the extraordinary proclamation of the Six Supernatural Powers?
The Master said, "It is being carried away by everyone in the world. The monk asked, "What is the house style of the Six Supernatural Powers? The Master said, "A single piece of plain cloth."
[The Master] said, "A bundle of patched robes, weighing more than one jin. A monk asked, "What is the one path for a student to advance?
The Master said, "Who would dare deceive you? The monk said, "Is there no expedient means? The Master said, "That would already be a state of oppression.
A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Morning congee; at noon, rice. The monk said, "Please tell me further, Master. The Master said, "Old man!"

Sengkun asked, "Ultimately, what is it? The Master simply laughed loudly. The King of Qian repeatedly invited him into the palace and appointed him as the Great Master of the Six Penetrations (Liutong Dashi).
Later, in the winter of the first year of the Xiande era of Emperor Shizong of the Later Zhou—the Jia-yin year—he entered nirvana at the age of eighty-four.
His stupa was erected at Mount Daci.
Chan Master Chiqian of Nanchan in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "As for famous phrases and wondrous sentences, everyone everywhere has already spoken of them.
Is there anyone here today among the assembly who can transcend the primary principle and bring forth a question? If there is, you shall not have brought shame upon others.
A monk asked, "What is the primary principle? The Master said, "Why do you not ask about the second?"

[The student] said, "This is the primary meaning. The Master said, "That has already fallen into the secondary meaning. [The student] asked, "I request the Master to harmonize with the melody of the ancient Buddhas.
The Master said, "I will not harmonize with you; you are all muddled and confused. [The student] said, "I do not understand why the Master does not harmonize.
The Master said, "Where have you come from?"

Shi Nai of Yuezhou, who had first gained a taste of the Dharma while studying under Chan Master Jianzhen of Xuefeng, later attended a vegetarian feast at Qingfeng Lou at the invitation of the King of Min.
After sitting for a long time, he suddenly caught sight of the sunlight and attained sudden, thorough enlightenment.
He then composed a verse, saying: "At Qingfeng Lou, attending the official feast, Today my lifelong eyes have opened wide. Only now do I truly believe..."

Regarding matters of long-standing and distant antiquity, [the Master] did not bring them from Mount Xi (Xīlǐng) but presented them upon his return to Xuefeng. Xuefeng approved of this. After he took up residence there, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha-body?
The Master said, "Which Buddha-body are you asking about? The monk replied, "The body of Śākyamuni Buddha. The Master said, "His tongue covers the three thousandfold world-system.
As the Master approached the end of his life, he presented this verse: "The eye-sense follows form; The mind-sense follows objects. When the two senses are extinguished, The true person is revealed."
All is exhausted. Ear-consciousness follows sound and vanishes; returning to the source has no other principle. Today and tomorrow—then he passed away while sitting in the lotus posture.
Chan Master Xuǎnè of Fúqīng Monastery in Quánzhōu was a native of Gāolì. When the Magistrate of Quánzhōu, Lord Wáng, asked him, "What is..."
Regarding a matter within the *zongcheng* (the core vehicle), the Master rebuked him. A monk asked, "What is bodhi as it meets the eye?
The Master said, "The *jueli* has lost his rice supply for half a year. The monk asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "It is simply because he is scheming for another's measure of rice.
[The monk] asked, "What is the pure *dharmakāya*? The Master said, "A crooked shrimp. [The monk] asked, "The teaching says..."
"The single, firm, and dense body manifests within every atom. What is this firm and dense body? The Master said, "Donkeys, horses, and cats.
[The student] said, "I beg the Master for further instruction. The Master said, "Even donkeys and horses do not understand.
[The student] asked, "How does one discern and clarify each and every thing? The Master extended one leg and showed it to him.
A monk asked Chan Master Ren of Nantai in Quzhou, “What is the realm of Nantai? The Master said, “I do not know its value.
The monk asked, “Ultimately, what is it? The Master said, “Where are you right now, Venerable?”
When Chan Master Dongchan of Quanzhou first opened the hall for teaching, a monk asked: "The King of Men has invited the Dharma King to appear in the world;
how should he proclaim the School of the Patriarchs so as not to err against the ancestral wind? The Master said: "Can you endure it? The monk said:
"If one does not go down into the water, how can one know there are fish? The Master said: "Do not speak idle words. [The monk] asked: "What is the Buddha-dharma?"

At the most intimate point, the Master said, "You have gone too far. A student asked, "I, a latecomer among students, request the Master’s very first phrase. The Master said, "From where have you come?
A student asked, "What is the matter that belongs to the student’s own portion? The Master said, "It is painful [to ask]. A student asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Fortunately, you are already pitiable enough; you need not insist on seeking it in a foreign land."

Chan Master Congxi of Dàqián Mountain in Hangzhou was a direct disciple of Xuefeng. Having received the seal of understanding from his own teacher, he thoroughly mastered the essentials of the School.
He often said, "I strike the drum of Guannan and sing the song of Xuefeng. Later, he traveled to Zhejiang to visit the King of Qián;
the King, deeply moved by his spiritual transformation, commanded him to reside on this mountain to propagate the Dharma. A monk asked: "It was not because of the King..."
[The monk] requested instruction. It was not a request made by a gathering of the assembly; the Master was asked directly for the meaning of that which comes from the West.
The Master said, "That monk over there has passed over here. [The monk] said, "I do not understand. I beg the Master to point it out again.
The Master said, "How can you be so ignorant of good and evil? Question: "Building a carriage inside the gate, fitting the tracks upon leaving the gate. What is "building a carriage inside the gate"?
The Master said, "I do not ask about the making of the carriage; what is the track? The student said, "I do not understand. I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master said, "When a skilled craftsman applies his handiwork, he leaves no trace of the axe or hammer."
A monk asked Chan Master Yongtai of Fuzhou, "I have heard that you, Master, see tigers—is this true? The Master made the sound of a tiger.
The monk made a gesture as if to strike him. The Master said, "You dead man! Another asked, "What is the Buddha of True Nature?
The Master clapped his hands and said, "I don't understand, I don't understand."
Chan Master Shoune Miaokong of Longshouchang Monastery in Chizhou was a native of the Lin family in Fuzhou. A monk asked, "Before reaching the Dragon Gate, how does one find a place to settle?
The Master said, "It is difficult to maintain one's life. A newly arrived monk came forward to pay his respects. The Master asked him:

"Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "I have not departed from the square inch [of my heart]. The Master said, "It is no easy matter to come here. The monk also said, "It is no easy matter to come here.
The Master gave him a slap. The monk asked, "What is the mind that is transmitted? The Master said, "I have instructed you repeatedly: do not speak of it to others.
The monk asked, "What is the ancestral vehicle (zongcheng)? The Master said, "Can it be placed within your mouth, O *jiaoli*?"
[Mao] asked, "I request the Master to grant me a direct introduction to the essential point. The Master said, "That is indeed essential.
A monk from Jianzhou Mengbi Chan Temple asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "I do not deceive you. The monk said, "Is that not it?
The Master said, "You are deceiving him. The King of Min invited the Master for a meal and asked, "Have you brought your brush with you?"
[The Master] said, "No. The Emperor asked, "Is it not the embroidered brush of Mount Xie? I am ashamed that it is not the rabbit-hair pen from within the moon.

Since Your Majesty has deigned to inquire, how could this mountain monk dare not present [an answer]? The Emperor asked again, "What is the Dharma King? The Master said, "It is not the literary style of the Dream-Pen."
A monk asked Zen Master Yuan Yan of Fuzhou Jile: "What is the家风 (family style) of Jile? The Master said: "It fills the eyes;
one cannot see enough. [Another] asked: "The myriad dharmas are fundamentally rootless. I wonder, what is it that you teach the student to take up?"
The Master said, "Do not speak in your sleep. [The student] asked, "I have long dwelt in a dark room and have not yet reached its source.

Today I have come here; I beg the Master for a single reception. The Master said, "Do not close your eyes and pretend it is night. [The student] said, "If that is so, then the udumbara flower has bent its stalk to accommodate the present age.
How do you instruct us regarding the supreme ancestral wind? The Master said, "Do you recognize it or not? [The student] said, "It is as such..."
"Ma" means that doubt has been stilled. The Master said, "Do not utter nonsense before the assembly. A question was asked: "I do not ask about Kāśyapa Mātanga entering the Han;
how was it when Bodhidharma came to Liang? The Master said, "Is it mistaken now?

[The questioner] said, "If so, then the principle has produced the Three Vehicles and the flowers have blossomed into five petals. The Master said, "Stop talking about the Three Vehicles and five petals; get out!"
A monk asked Chan Master Rutai of Mount Furong in Fuzhou, "What is the ancient melody? The Master remained silent for a long while and then asked, "Do you hear it?
The monk replied, "I do not hear it. The Master presented this verse: "The ancient melody emits a powerful sound; The rhythm of the present age is the same.
If one were to point with the first finger, Even the Buddhas and Patriarchs would lose their tracks."
At Qiehe Mountain in Luojing, a monk asked the Master, “What is Qiehe? The Master joined his two hands together and said, “Jubao, jubao.

The monk asked, “When a fine horse does not enter Western Qin, where does it go? The Master said, “Where would it go?”
A monk asked Master Qixian of Mount Gui in Tanzhou, "At this very moment, how does one draw near?
The Master said, "How do you intend to draw near? The monk said, "Is there no expedient means? The Master said, "The Kaiyuan and Longxing editions of the Great and Small Tripitaka.
[Another] asked, "What is swift supernatural power? The Master said, "New clothes become worn rags. [Another] asked, "As for suchness..."
"What is the Yellow Bridge? The Master said, "How many people has it deceived? A questioner asked, "Without resorting to much talk, what is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Do not make the sound of a jackal."
When Chan Master Yanzong of Chaoshan in Jizhou came to visit Zifu, the Master descended from his meditation seat to receive him.
Zifu asked, "Venerable Sir, how many years has it been since you have resided on this mountain? The Master replied, "A dull bird nests in the reeds; a weary fish rests in the marsh."
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then you are a true man of the Way. The Master said, "Sit for a moment and drink some tea.
A monk asked, "What is Chaoshan? The Master said, "It does not harbor corpses. The monk asked, "What is it like to be a person among the mountains?
The Master said, "Planting red lotuses upon rocks. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Above all, do not violate court protocol."

The Master said, "Nurturing its nature in the deep pool. The monk asked, "What is it like when it has emerged? The Master said, "As soon as it ascends to the celestial heights, the multitudes find it difficult to follow.

The monk asked, "What is it like after it has ascended? The Master said, "Hanging clouds cover all; its moisture reaches the great thousandfold world. The monk asked, "Is there still [anyone who does not...]"?
The Master said, "There is none who receives it. [The monk] asked, "How is it that there is no one who receives it? The Master said, "A wooden stump directly supports the great sun.

Xue went to listen to a lecture on the three causes of buddha-nature and the dharma-body of the three virtues. When the lecturer spoke extensively on the subtle principles of the dharma-body, the Chan practitioner could not help but laugh.
After the lecture concluded, the Master invited the Chan practitioner to drink tea and said to him, "My own aspirations have always been narrow and inferior."

"Explaining the meaning based on the literal text has just earned me your laughter; I hope you will instruct me. The Chan practitioner said, "I truly laugh at you, Master of Commentaries, for not knowing the Dharma-body (dharmakāya).
The Master said, "In such an explanation, where is it not correct? The practitioner said, "Please, Master, explain it once more.
The Master said, "The principle of the Dharma-body is like the great void: vertically it exhausts the three periods of time, and horizontally it spans the ten directions. It pervades...
It threads through the eight extremities and encompasses the two polarities; responding to conditions and meeting with stimuli, there is nowhere it does not pervade. [The interlocutor] said:

"It is not that the Master of the Seat is wrong in what he says, but he is merely speaking of the boundaries of the Dharma-body. In truth, he has not yet realized the Dharma-body itself. The Master said: [He has not yet realized it.]
"If that is so, Zen Master, you should explain this to me. He asked, "Dharma Master, do you believe it? The Master replied, "How could I dare not believe it?
He said, "If it is so, Dharma Master, suspend your lectures for ten days. Within your chamber, sit upright in quiet contemplation;
withdraw your mind and collect your thoughts, letting go of all conditions of good and evil at once. The Master followed these instructions exactly, from the first watch of the night until—
At the fifth watch, he heard the sound of drums and horns. Suddenly, he attained awakening and went to knock on the door. The practitioner asked, "Who is it? The Master replied, "It is I.
The practitioner rebuked him, saying, "I have instructed you to transmit and uphold the Great Teaching and to preach the Dharma in place of the Buddha.

Why, then, did you come home drunk last night and lie down in the street? The Master said, "O Virtuous Practitioner, I have been lecturing on the sutras all along; I have merely used the noses of my biological parents..."
Kong Niuzhu replied, "From this day forward, I shall never again dare to act in such a manner. The Chan master said, "Go for now;
we shall meet tomorrow. The teacher then ceased his lectures and traveled extensively throughout all quarters, his fame spreading across the land.
He once traveled through Zhejiang and attended a dharma assembly at Mount Jing. One day, before the Great Buddha Hall, a monk asked him, "Have you ever been to Mount Wutai?"
The Master said, "Have you been there? The monk replied, "Yes. The Master asked, "Did you see Mañjuśrī? The monk said, "I saw him.
The Master asked, "Where did you see him? The monk replied, "In front of the Buddha Hall at Mount Jing. Later, when the monk traveled to Minchuan, he related this to Xuefeng.
Xuefeng said, "Why did you not tell him to come over the mountain pass? Upon hearing this, the Master hurried to Xuefeng’s monastery to rest his staff; there, he gave some oranges to [the Master].
The monk Chōnggyeong asked, "Where did you bring it from? The Master said, "I brought it from beyond the ridges. Chōnggyeong said, "It was no easy matter to travel such a long distance;

The Master went up onto the Dharma Hall and looked around. Xuefeng immediately descended to look after him.

The Master recalled a previous conversation. He shook his fan but did not respond. Mount Shan (Shishuang Qingzhu) could not fathom this and struck the Master with a fist.

When Gushan (Dongshan Liangjie) went to attend a banquet invited by the Great King, Xuefeng saw him off at the gate. Upon returning to the Dharma Hall, Xuefeng said, "A single arrow of sainthood has shot straight into the innermost palace.
The Master said, "He is not yet there. Xuefeng said, "He is a man of ultimate penetration. The Master said, "..."
"If you do not believe me, wait until someone else has gone to investigate. He then pursued him to the middle of the road and asked, "Where is the Elder Brother going?
The Mountain said, "I am going to the Ninefold City. The Master said, "What if you suddenly encounter an encirclement by the three armies?
The Mountain said, "He has his own path that reaches through the heavens. The Master said, "In that case, you will leave the palace and lose the hall."
Yanshou said, "Where would he not be called Honored One? The Master shook his sleeves and turned back. Feng asked, "How was that?
The Master replied, "That fine arrow of a sage was broken mid-flight. He then recounted the previous conversation. Feng then said, "The fellow’s words remain."
The Master said, "This old, frozen lump still has a trace of hometown sentiment. The Master was standing in front of the storehouse when a monk asked, "What is Bodhi as it meets the eye?
The Master kicked a puppy, which ran off making a noise. The monk had no reply.
The Master said, "That little puppy didn't even require a single kick. While Baofu was picking melons, the Master arrived. Baofu said, "If you can say something, I will give you [some melon]."
[The Master] was eating melon. The Master said, "Hand it over. Fudu gave him a slice. The Master took it and departed.

The Master did not appear in the world [as a public teacher], so those in all quarters referred to him as "Venerable Fu of Taiyuan. Later, he returned to Weiyang, where Chancellor Chen kept him at his residence to provide for him.
One day, he said to the Chancellor, "Tomorrow, I shall lecture on the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* once, as an act of gratitude."
After the tea ceremony for the preparatory retreat (caizi) had concluded, the Master ascended the seat. After a long silence, he struck his staff once and said, "Thus have I heard.
He then called out, "Shangshu! Shangshu responded, "Yes? The Master said, "At one time the Buddha was... and then immediately descended from the seat.
Chan Master Baowen of Nanyue Banruo Weijin was a native of Fuzhou. He studied under Xuefeng and befriended Xuansha, penetrating deeply into the profound mysteries of the ultimate truth.
One day, he asked Upāsaka Jian, "I have heard that you have written a commentary on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*; is this true? Jian replied:
"I dare not," [the monk] replied. The Master asked, "How would you annotate the two Mañjuśrīs? He said, "I beg the Master to discern this. The Master then raised his sleeves and departed.
The Master once compiled the *Baolin Zhuan* (Record of the Baolin Temple) in four fascicles, recording the lineages and sources of the Chan school from after the Zhenyuan era.
He also separately authored the *Nanyue Gaoseng Zhuan* (Biographies of Eminent Monks of Nanyue), both of which circulate in the world.
