[The monk] asked, “What is the direct, single path? The Master said, “Cut off. [The monk] asked, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, “Suffering. [The monk] asked, “What is the Way? The Master said, “Pervasive. [The monk] asked, “What is...? The Master said, “... (The text ends here).

The Master said, "Not giving rise to views. He asked, "Who is the one within the Bodhimanda of Kāśyapa at the Piṇḍola Cave?

Chan Master Nan Yue Henglong, a successor in the seventh generation under Chan Master Ruiyan Yan of the Southern Peak (Nanyue), first resided at Jinlun. A monk asked: "What is the first phrase of Jinlun?"
The Master said, "Dull-witted fellow. [The student] asked, "What is the single arrow of the Golden Wheel? The Master said, "It has already passed. [The student] asked, "What is the Patriarch?
The Master said, "The eight winds blow, yet it is not extinguished. [The student] said, "In that case, then darkness does not arise?
The Master said, "In broad daylight, there are no idle people."
Chan Master Shenlu of Ruifeng Monastery in Wenzhou was a native of Fuzhou. Having long served as the attendant to [Master] Ruiyan, he later cleared the land and founded the monastery.
Disciples gathered around him. Addressing the assembly, he said: "Solitary and serene, dwelling alone with a contemplative mind, who would believe that the soundless lute emits wondrous tones?
All day long I sit in silence within the Dharma Hall; no one comes to inquire about the original mind. At that time, there was...
The Venerable Ponghyon asked, "What is the original mind? The Master called out, "Ponghyon! Ponghyon responded, "Yes. The Master said, "Go and serve tea to the old monk.
At this, Ponghyon attained faith and entry. He passed away in the winter of the Bingzi year of the Taiping Xingguo era of Emperor Taizong of the Song dynasty.
His worldly age was one hundred and five years.
Chan Master Huījī Chāohuì of Mount Hánglóng in Ézhōu was a successor of Chan Master Xuánquán Yàn. He was the son of the Zhāng family of Qīnghé.
Initially, he visited Yántóu and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Yántóu said, "Do you know how to make *jiǔcí* (rice cakes)? The Master replied, "I do."
Tou said, "For now, let us save the rice cakes. Later, he arrived at Xuánquán and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Xuánquán picked up a stalk of soapberry (*sòjiǎo*) and asked, "Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand. Xuánquán set down the soapberry and made a gesture of doing laundry.
The Master then prostrated himself and said, "I know for certain that the Buddha-dharma has no difference [from other teachings]. Xuánquán asked, "What did you see to say such a thing?"
Li asked, "Master, I once questioned Yantou. Yantou said, 'Do you know how to rescue sticky rice? Rescuing sticky rice is simply resolving adhesions.
When the Master held up the soapberry, that too was resolving adhesions; therefore it is said there is no difference. Quan laughed heartily, and the Master attained realization.
During the Tianyou era of Emperor Zhaozong of the Tang dynasty, he traveled to Ezhou, where the regional commander established [a monastery for him].

"Yes. The Master said, "Did you see Yangshan in your dream? Qing replied, "I do not want you, Upādhyāya, to provide the answer; I only wish to discuss it.
The Master said, "If you wish to discuss it, there is already the Great Teacher of fifteen hundred people at the Head Seat.
Later, when the Master arrived at Shuangyan, Shuangyan invited him for tea. During the session, he said, "I shall pose a question. If you can answer it, I will surrender [my position]."

The Master stayed with the *ācārya* in the monastery. When [the *ācārya*] said he could not explain it, the Master refused to leave the monastery. He then cited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, saying:
"All Buddhas and the *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* dharma of all Buddhas—all emerge from this sūtra.
"Tell me," he asked, "by whom was this sūtra spoken? The Master replied: "Whether it was spoken or not spoken, set that aside and put it over here."
"Master, you must certainly decide: what do you call this sutra? Yankong had no reply. The Master spoke again:
"If it is said that 'all worthies and sages are distinguished by means of the dharma of non-action,' then if the dharma of non-action is the ultimate, by what means could there be distinction?
As for this very distinction—is it an error or not an error? If it is an error, then all worthies..."
"The Sage is entirely beyond all faults. If he were not beyond fault, what could possibly be called his distinction?
Yankou remained silent. The Master said, "Alas! Xuefeng has spoken. Later, the Master visited Baoning; they met on the road, and the Master immediately asked:
The elder brother was among his fellow practitioners on the Way. He then pointed to his own nose and said, "This thing obstructs me; may you remove it for a moment?
Ning replied, "How long has it been since you, Master, first attained this? The Master said, "Alas!
You have caused me to wear out a pair of straw sandals," and he immediately turned back. Guotai spoke on his behalf, saying, "Not only I, but even all the Buddhas..."
"What can be done? The Master said, "Why do you compare yourself to others? The Master was at Zhizhe Temple in Wuzhou and served as the First Seat (*prathamāsanika*).
He habitually did not accept pure water. The administrator became angry and said, "The Senior Monk (*upādhyāya*) does not understand the distinction between the defiled and the pure."
"Why do you not accept this pure water? The Master leaped down from his seat, picked up the *śītapātra* (pure-water flask), and said, "Is this defiled or pure?
The monk was speechless. The Master then smashed the flask to pieces. From that time on, his reputation spread far and wide. The assembly requested him to reside at Mingzhao Mountain.
He ascended the hall to open the Dharma, meeting the challenge with total acumen; those who could truly recognize him were rare. To die together and live together—among ten thousand, one.

There is not a single one. To seek words and chase phrases, their number is like the sands of the Ganges. As for the path that points upward, even "cracking the eggshell" and "the hen pecking" are still at odds.

When Confucian scholars meet, they grasp their whips and turn their heads back; what the śramaṇas see is truly a bitter pity. They cast away the true gold to follow the crowd in gathering clods of earth.
I tell you, young children: do not wander aimlessly in vain waves. Even if you could understand his original source, it would still be no more than tiles and rubble. It is not as good as—
A single throw sends it soaring across the great void; who would dare approach this Spirit Peak? Let your arrows come as you will;
only then can one be called a man of stature. If you intend to swallow your voice in silence, it will not take more than a single snatch.

A monk asked, "How is it before the lion has emerged from its den? The Master said, "A swift hawk cannot overtake it. The monk asked, "How is it after it has emerged from the den? The Master said, "Ten thousand miles of turmoil."
Fen asked, "What is it like when one wishes to emerge but does not? The Master said, "Precipitous. Fen asked, "What about the matter of going forward? The Master said, "Zha.
Fen asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates beyond the Dharma-body? The Master said, "Turning the body after the Northern Dipper."
Question: "How should one proceed throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said: "Throw it onto the adamantine ground and ask:
'What was the subject of the dialogue between Mañjuśrī and Vimalakīrti? The Master said: "The hemp headband and the gauze cap have already been cast aside here.
Question: "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: "To bite into it successfully is to be a skilled hand."
Question: "When the crane is released from its cage and departs with the mist, what is it like? The Master said: "What can you do about that single dot upon its head?
Question: "Who is able to approach the fire that has no smoke? The Master said: "One who does not spare his eyebrows."
[The monk] asked, "Does the Master still manage to respond? The Master said, "Tell me, how many strands of eyebrows do I have?
When a newly arrived monk came forward to inquire, as soon as he ascended the Dharma Hall, the Master raised his whisk and then cast it down.

The monk said, "Take care," and departed. The Master said, "A true adept! A true adept! A monk asked, "What is it like when one is fully equipped with a sword? The Master said, "If you suddenly encounter..."
"At such a time as this, what then? The monk had no reply. One day, when it was cold, the Master ascended the hall.
As soon as the assembly had gathered, he said, "The wind at the peak is somewhat harsh; this is not the place for you to settle your body or establish your life.

Return first to a warm room to deliberate. He then returned to his quarters. The assembly followed him there and stood still. The Master spoke again: "As soon as you arrive in the warm room, you will see..."

[The Master] was dozing. He drove them all down at once with his staff. The Master asked Guotai, "An ancient said that Jushi merely recited the three-line incantation and was thus named 'One Who Surpasses All People.
How would you remove those three lines of incantation for him so that he might be named 'One Who Surpasses All People'?
Guotai held up one finger. The Master said, "Had it not been for today, how could this have been settled?"
"Recognizing the Guest from Guazhou. The Master had a junior teacher who was unwell at the monastery. He sent a letter by messenger asking:
"I am suffering from this great illness; right now I am experiencing intense pain, and there is nowhere to be found that can accommodate it."
"Is there anyone who can save them? The Master replied with a letter saying: "It struck the crown of his head; this adamantine arrow has passed through to the other side.
Later, a monk from the assembly went to live in a hermitage. After a year, he returned and paid his respects, saying:
An ancient said, "If you do not see someone for three days, do not look upon them as you did before.
The Master pried open his chest and said, "Tell me, how many hairs of gall-bladder do I have? The monk had no reply. The Master then asked, "When did you leave your hermitage?
The monk said, "This morning. The Master said, "When you came, to whom did you entrust your broken-legged cauldron? The monk again remained speechless. The Master—
He then shouted and said, "I have heard it said that you, Master, reside on the Peak of Mingzhao and propagate the mind of the ancient Buddhas.
What is the Peak of Mingzhao? The Master replied, "It changes your very eyes. He asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas?
The Master replied, "Are you out of breath yet? A student asked, "The student has come here from the clouds and waves; I ask the Master to spread out his bowl. The Master said:
"Pressing through and shattering the crown of your head," he said, "you must still go to Xiantuo. The Master then struck him and drove him out. The Master spoke a verse to the assembly, saying:
"A single clap from Mingzhao—few people understand it. This is the sublime and wondrous pivot of the True School.
Where does the flash of a spark vanish? Only a child born this morning should know. When he was about to pass away, he ascended the hall and addressed the assembly with his final instructions.
[The discourse] concluded. A monk asked, "After the Master passes away, where will you go? The Master raised one foot and said, "Look beneath my feet.
In the middle of the night, he asked his attendant, "In the past, at the assembly on Vulture Peak, Śākyamuni Tathāgata extended his two feet and emitted the light of a hundred jewels.
Now, how much do I emit? The attendant replied, "In the past, the World-Honored One..."
"Venerable One, this evening," [the master] said, "Master, brush aside your eyebrows with your hand and say: 'Do not let it be in vain! He then spoke a verse:
"Displaying full majesty amidst a thicket of blades; You all, guard and uphold this well. An iron ox gives birth to a calf within the flames."
"Who, standing at the parting of ways, understands how to engage my mechanism? Having finished this verse, he sat upright and passed away; his stupa and monastery remain there.
Chan Master Yinyue Jiaoji of Danning Monastery in Hongzhou was a native of the Yang family from Xingan, Yuzhang.

On the night of his birth, a brilliant light pierced through the room. At the age of seven, he relied upon Daojian of Shitou Monastery in his home district to leave the household life and receive full ordination. He subsequently...
He went to visit Master Luoshan. Luoshan guided him with the essential teaching on the lion in its den and emerging from its den, whereupon he attained awakening.
Later, returning to the region south of the Yangtze River, he met Ji Mengjun, the Magistrate of Longquan, who invited him to reside at the Shishandao Monastery.
He ascended the hall and said: "Is there anyone here who can soar through the air? Come forth! No one in the assembly stepped forward. The Master then said: "Soaring through the air is precisely..."
At that time, one must raise the eyebrows; from this, one departs from the mundane. Do not wait for the arrival of white-haired children.
A monk asked, "What is the Bridge of the Ten Virtues? The Master said, "Perilous. The monk asked, "How about those who cross it? The Master said, "Ruined.
A monk asked, "Venerable Zifu has passed away; where has he gone? The Master said, "His straw sandals are worn out. A monk asked, "What is the Yellow [River]? The Master said, "..."

[The monk] uttered a phrase regarding plum blossoms. The Master said, "How is it right now? [The monk] asked, "How does one transmit the message? The Master said, "The road to the Nine Rivers is cut off.
[The monk] asked, "For a beginner or a junior student, what is 'learning'? The Master said, "Head up toward heaven. [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, how is it?
The Master said, "Feet planted on the ground. [The monk] asked, "What is the Sword of the Dharma King? The Master said, "Exposed. It still kills."
[The monk] said, "There is no person. The Master said, "How so? [The monk] asked, "What is the Dragon Spring Sword? The Master said, "It does not leave the scabbard.
[The monk] said, "Please bring it out of the scabbard. The Master said, "The stars lose their positions. [The monk] asked, "The realm is at peace;
why does the pearl not appear? The Master said, "Where would it fall? Later, in the Xinhai year of the Guangshun era of the Later Zhou dynasty, Li of Jinling...

He requested to reside at Longguang Temple and was appointed as the Chan Master Jueji. In the eighth year of the Jianlong era of the Song dynasty (the Xinyou year), he followed the Li clan to dwell at Longjing Danning.
On the tenth month of that year, he manifested parinirvāṇa. He was seventy-six years of age and had fifty-six years of monastic seniority.
His posthumous title was Chan Master Xuanjì, and his stupa was named Changji.
A monk asked Zen Master Huaguangfan of Hengzhou, "The numinous platform is not established; is there still a place to emerge? The Master said, "There is.
The monk asked, "What is this place of emergence? The Master said, "To emerge. [Another] asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "The Way.
[Another] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "To verify. [Another] asked about Niu-tou. The Master said, "To emerge."
"Before you had seen the Fourth Patriarch, how was it? The Master said, "Free and at ease. [The monk] asked, "After seeing him, how was it?
The Master said, "Free and at ease. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter within the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Understood."
Chan Master Shaoshi of Luoshan in Fuzhou ascended the hall. Several monks came forward one after another to pose questions.
The Master said, "Just come out all at once and ask; wait while I, this old monk, answer you all at once. A monk then asked, "The students ask all at once;
we pray that the Master will answer us all at once. The Master said, "Granted. [Another] monk asked, "Students who have newly entered the monastery [seek] the Patriarch’s..."
[The student] said, "I seek the Master's meaning. Please point it out directly. The Master said, "Very well.
When Chan Master Dinghui of Xichuan first visited Luoshan, Luoshan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have traveled far from Xichu and have recently departed from Kaiyuan.
He then stepped forward and asked, "As for the matter at hand right now, what is it? Luoshan made a gesture of dismissal and said, "Eat!"
"Tea is served. As the Master hesitated, Mount [Shan] said, "The autumn air is somewhat warm; go.

The Master went out to the Dharma Hall and sighed, saying, "While at Mount Emei in Western Sichuan, I picked up a single arrow of thistle and mugwort from beneath my feet, intending to settle the chaos of the world."
Today at Dala Mountain Monastery, the bows have snapped and the arrows are exhausted. "Enough, enough! [said Master Shishuang], and he descended from his seat to join the assembly.
On the following day, when Master Shishuang ascended the hall, the Master stepped forward and asked, "Who is it that cuts through the door and windows and stands before the screen?

Shishuang gave a shout. The Master was speechless. Shishuang said, "Your feathers and wings are not yet complete; go for now. Thereupon, the Master tucked up his robes and departed. Having long since received his seal of approval, he later went to visit Master Tiantai.
At Shouguang Monastery, as the Abbot was seated, the Master entered directly by his side and stood with palms joined. Shouguang asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "I am still waiting for your answer," and then he departed. Shouguang picked up his whisk and pursued him to the front of the Sangha Hall;
seeing the Master there, he raised the whisk and said, "Ācārya, what do you call this? The Master replied, "Dare I breathe?"
Qi. Guang bowed his head and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Chan Master Lingyan of Baiyun in Jianzhou ascended the hall and said: "Who says that when sent to the gate of a master, one is facing the presiding mourner?"
Take care! A monk asked, "When one has not yet clarified the matter of one's own self, what serves as the proof? The Master said, "A wooden mirror reflects a plain face.

The monk asked, "What is it like after the proof? The Master said, "Not much different. [Another] asked, "The Three Ministers have issued an invitation; the fourfold assembly is present at the banquet."
Since you are situated where one must practice benevolence, I ask that the Master sing once. The Master said, "To sing it is not difficult. The other said, "Then please do so. The Master said:
"The night is still and the water cold; the fish do not bite. With empty boats, we return under the bright moon."
Chan Master Yizheng Changzhen of Tiantong in Qianzhou stayed at Luoshan for several years.

Later, when the Mountain [Master] fell ill, the Master asked, "After a hundred years have passed, if someone should ask the Abbot how you would instruct them, what would you do? The Mountain then threw himself flat on his back.
From this, the Master attained awakening. He immediately paid his respects and departed. After he took up residence elsewhere, a monk asked, "What is the great Dharma of the Buddha?"
The Master said, "Cold and heat press one another.
When Chan Master Weikang Zhenji of Qingping in Jizhou ascended the hall, he did not move his expression, yet there was already a sense of victory and defeat.
Was there anyone present? At that moment, a monk came forward and bowed. The Master said, "Not a true adept," and immediately returned to his quarters.
Zhàng asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "If you want the head, take it away.
He asked, "What is the sword that kills the living? The Master said, "Do you understand? He asked, "What is the blade that slays?
The Master rebuked him. He asked, "What is a lion cub? The Master said, "A single hair-tip arrays the universe."
A monk asked Chan Master Yizhao of Mount Jinzhu in Wuzhou, “What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, “Opening the door to conduct one’s livelihood. The monk asked, “If a thief should suddenly arrive, what then? The Master said, “Indeed! A newly arrived monk came to pay his respects.
As the Master lifted the curtain, he made a gesture with his hand as if removing a hat. The monk prepared to step forward; the Master said, “You have been deceived!”
A person, on account of this matter, spoke in verse: "A tiger’s head sprouting horns—how can one manage it? The spark of flint and the flash of lightning must be met with total readiness.
Even a true hero would find it difficult; How could one who is muddled know how to turn back?"
A monk asked Chan Master Gushan of Tanzhou, “I beg the Master for a word regarding the essential point. The Master immediately rose and departed.
The monk asked, “What is it like when a wild goat hangs from a horn? The Master said, “Where would you go to seek it? The monk asked, “What about after it has hung from the horn?
The Master said, “It runs away.”
When Chan Master Congsheng of Daowu in Hunan first resided at Longhui, a monk asked, "What is the matter of face-to-face encounter?
The Master said, "He has gone to the kingdom of Silla. The monk asked, "What is the house style of Longhui? The Master said, "Shooting straight across, both ways.
The monk asked, "A destitute son has come to you, Master; I beg you for ultimate salvation. The Master said, "Is it not that you are being made to feel humiliated?"
[The monk] said, "What can be done about this poverty? The Master said, "There are many who see it.
Chan Master Yinyuan of Luoshan in Fuzhou, while ascending the hall, remained silent for a long while and then said, "If you are a guest from under the gate of a true patriarch..."
"You will certainly not be surprised by Mount Luo. Take care. A monk asked, "I have heard it said of old:
'Since recognizing the road to Caoxi, one knows that birth and death are no longer relevant. I do not ask about the road to Caoxi; what is the road to Mount Luo? The Master spread out both hands.
The monk said, "If that is so, then one path is traversable, and all paths are likewise so. The Master said, "..."
"What are the various paths? A monk stepped forward and joined his palms. The Master said, "The spiritual crane soars beyond the misty heavens; the dull bird does not leave its nest.
A monk asked, "The scriptures state that when one accords with the Dharma-body, the myriad phenomena are all stilled; when one follows the function of wisdom, the myriad phenomena arise together."
"What is it like when all phenomena are simultaneously stilled? The Master said, "What is there [to see]? "What is it like when all phenomena arise together?
The Master said, "The cross-legged bench and its supports."

A monk asked Chan Master Lingyan of Guanzhou, “What is the treasure within the Way? The Master said, “The earth slants toward the southeast; the heavens tower above the northwest. The monk said, “I do not understand.
The Master said, “The setting sun reveals its wondrous function before one’s eyes. The Master composed a verse on Shigong receiving Sanping:
“He understood how to split the arrow aimed at his chest; why did he remain but half a person? It was because he followed the path of conceptual understanding.”
Therefore, he did not preserve his body.

Master Kuangshan of Mount Kuang in Jixian Prefecture addressed the assembly: "The Road of Mount Kuang! The Road of Mount Kuang! Its cliffs and precipices are so steep and perilous that people find it difficult to tread upon them.
If a traveler hesitates to deliberate, they are separated by a thousand mountains in a single phrase—a clarity that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs. *The Verse on the White Ox*
He said: "I have an ancient altar and a truly white ox, which my father and I have hidden away through many autumns. When going out, it heads straight for the peak of the solitary mountain;
when returning, it briefly crosses the head of Tiger Creek."
Chan Master Shengzhongman of Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Handed over face-to-face, it requires no written proclamation;
meeting the opportunity eye-to-eye is what is called a superior practitioner of the Yuan school. If one can act thus, the ancestral wind will not fall into decline. A monk asked:
"What is the phrase by which the ancestral style does not fall into decline? The Master said, "I, this old monk, cannot bear it. [The student] asked:

"In the assembly at Vulture Peak in the past, and now within the banquet of Xingsheng, how do you proclaim what the Master has personally transmitted? The Master said, "I am short of one question for you."
A monk asked Chan Master Qingjin of Baoying in Tanzhou, "What is the true mark? The Master said, "It is extinguished;

you have asked about the ultimate principle, which is beyond words. How can it be communicated? The Master said, "In a thousand differences and ten thousand distinctions. [The monk] said, "Where is the place where one gains strength?"
He requested the Master’s instruction. The Master said, “Sleeping man!
Chan Master Guichen of Luohan Monastery in Zhangzhou, a successor of Chan Master Xuansha Bei, was the son of Li of Changshan. When he was a young child, he would eat only once a day.
He maintained a vegetarian diet and his speech was extraordinary. After reaching adulthood, he entered the Wan-sui Temple of his native prefecture to take refuge under Master Wuxiang;

there he shaved his head, ascended the platform for ordination, and studied the *vinaya*. One day, after proclaiming the *prātimokṣa* sūtra and conducting the *poṣadha* ceremony for the assembly, he said:

"To uphold the precepts is merely to discipline the body; it is not true liberation. To interpret the texts according to their literal meaning—how could that awaken noble wisdom? Thereupon, he went in search of...
The Southern School. Initially, he visited Yunju and Xuefeng, where he served and inquired with diligent devotion; yet, he still had not attained any realization.
Later, he went to Xuansha, who gave him a single word of inspiration that cleared away all delusion. Xuansha asked, "The three realms are mind-only. How do you understand this?
The Master pointed to a chair and said, "What would you call this, Teacher? Xuansha replied, "A chair. The Master said, "Teacher..."
[The Master] still did not understand that the three realms are mind-only. [The Master] said, "I call this 'bamboo and wood. What do you call it?
The Teacher said, "Guichen also calls it 'bamboo and wood. [The Master] said, "Throughout the entire world, one cannot find a single person who understands the Buddha-dharma.
From then on, the Teacher redoubled his efforts to encourage himself. Whenever the Sand [Master] would exhort and instruct the students, he would command the Teacher to assist him.

Although Master Fa kept himself in obscurity while among the assembly, his reputation spread far and wide. At that time, the Duke Wang, the Governor of Zhangzhou, established a vihāra named Dizang and invited the Master to expound the Dharma.
Once, while the Master was planting rice in the fields, he saw a monk and asked him, "Where have you come from?"
[The Master] said, "Nanzhou. The teacher asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma there? He replied, "They deliberate upon it in a vast expanse.
The teacher said, "How can that compare to us here, where we till the fields to earn our food? He asked, "What then of the three realms? The teacher said, "What do you call 'the three realms'?
He questioned a monk, "Where have you come from? [The monk] replied, "From the South. The teacher said, "Regarding the teachers of knowledge in the South..."
"What phrase do you use to instruct your disciples? He replied, "That Middle Way. Although gold dust is precious, it cannot remain in the eye.
The Master said, "I say that Mount Sumeru is in your eye. One day, while accompanying Zhongta, they were attending on Xuansha.
Xuansha struck Zhongta with a staff and said, "Is this the name, or is it the essence? Zhongta did not respond. Xuansha then asked the Master, "How do you understand this?"
The Master said, "This monk deserves a blow; he does not know where it comes from. When the monk reported that Baofu had passed away, the Master said, "Baofu has passed away;
Dizang has entered the stupa. (A monk asked Falin, "What was the meaning of the ancients? Lin said, "Heaven! Heaven! Later, [the Master] moved to Lohan.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The fundamental mystery of the Zen school—is it simply this, or is there something else extraordinary?

If there is something else extraordinary, bring it forward for me to see. If there is not, you must not take these two characters and treat them as if they were the entirety of the School of the Patriarchs.
What are these two characters? They are 'the Patriarchal Vehicle' (Zongcheng) and 'the Teaching Vehicle' (Jiaocheng). As soon as you utter the words 'Patriarchal Vehicle'..."

This is the lineage of the school (zong-cheng). To speak of it as the vehicle of the teachings (jiao-cheng) is indeed the vehicle of the teachings. O virtue of Chan, the Buddha-dharma and the lineage of the school have always been within your own mouths;
to establish names for them and to take them up through speech—this is precisely it. At this very moment, turn toward this point.
They speak of the level and the real; they speak of the perfect and the eternal. Zen Master, what do you call "the level and the real"? What do you take to be "the perfect and the eternal"?
Having traveled among other teachers, you ought to have the ability to discern the truth; do not let yourself be buried by appearances.
You may have acquired some fragments of sound, form, names, and concepts, and stored them in your mind, saying, "I understand; I am skilled at making distinctions. But what exactly do you understand?
What is there to choose? That which is retained in memory is a name; that which is discerned is sound and form.
If it were not for sound and form, or name, how could you possibly retain them in memory or discern them? The wind blowing through the pine trees is also sound;
the croaking of a frog or the cawing of an old crow is also sound. Why do you not listen to and select [the truth] right there? If [you do not], then...
Within this there is a certain intention and appearance. As for the Master’s own words, how much intention could there possibly be?
Do not mistake this, Upādhyāya. Right now, as sounds and forms resound clearly, do they reach you or not?
If they do reach you, then your spiritual nature, the adamantine secret, must undergo destruction. Why is this so? Because...
Sound pierces through your ears; form penetrates your eyes. The causal conditions immediately block them up. Your illusory and deluded pursuit of the substance of sound and form kills you;
you must not tolerate this. If they do not reach you, from what place could sound and form come?
Do you understand? Try to discern whether they reach you or do not reach you. After a short while, he further said: "This is perfect, constant, and level."
"True. Who is it that speaks thus? This is not yet the understanding of a man from a village of barbarians who knows how to speak in such a way.

Those ancient sages were slightly eccentric; they acted in opposition [to convention] to assist in its manifestation. People of the present day do not recognize good from evil, and so they immediately settle upon "perfect reality," claiming, "I have a distinct lineage and a fundamental mystery.
Śākyamuni Buddha said, "Your tongue is not even equal to a tiny fragment of mine. Thus he spoke.
Mozhan said: "As for the offenses of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, though they are grave, they are still relatively light; there is still a time when they may cease.
But this slander of the Prajñāpāramitā blinds the eyes of sentient beings, leading them to swallow iron pellets in the Avīci Hell—do not treat this as a trivial matter."
Therefore, the ancients said: "The fault lies with the master who transforms others;
it does not concern you. Take care! Question: "What is the one phrase of an Arhat? The Master said: "If I were to tell you, it would immediately become two phrases. Question:
"When someone who does not understand comes, do you still receive them? The Master said: "Who is it that does not understand? [The questioner] said: "You have already said so just now."
The Master said, "Are you not being too self-effacing? A monk from Baofu arrived. The Master asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma there?
The monk replied, "Sometimes he addresses the assembly, saying: 'I block your eyes so that you cannot see; I block your ears so that you cannot hear;
I sit upon your minds so that you cannot discriminate. The Master said, "I ask you: what about when they are not blocked?"

[The monk] asked, "What is the right livelihood and food of a śramaṇa? The Master said, "Can you eat it? [The monk] said, "If I wish to eat this food, what expedient means should I employ?"

The Master said, “I will not tell you. [The monk] asked, “Why do you not say? The Master said, “That is my house style. [The monk] asked, “What is the body of the Dharma King?
The Master said, “What kind of body are you right now? [The monk] said, “If that is so, then there is no body. The Master said, “How painful!”
Shen was ascending the hall and had just taken his seat when two monks prostrated themselves at once. The Master said, "Both are wrong.
A monk asked, "What is the sentence that cannot be broken? The Master said, "Broken. A monk asked, "When one Buddha appears in the world, he does so for the sake of all sentient beings.

[The monk] committed an offense against the Master. The Master said, "Withdraw respectfully. [The monk] asked, "What is the original intent of all the sages? The Master said, "The four corners lie flat on the ground.
[The monk] asked, "When one is not yet willing to accept the Great Matter, what then?

The student replied, "When the Preceptor speaks thus, it is entirely lacking in compassion. While playing with the moon, he said, "The clouds move; it will rain. A monk asked, "..."
"It is not that the clouds move; it is that the wind moves. The Master said, "I say that neither the clouds move nor the wind moves.
The monk asked, "Just now, Master, you also said the clouds move. The Master said, "Who is at fault? The Master saw a monk raise his whisk and asked, "Do you understand?
The monk replied, "I thank the Master for his compassionate instruction to this student. The Master said, "You see me raising the whisk."
The Master then said to the student, "Every day you see mountains and see waters; do these not show themselves to you?
Furthermore, when you saw a monk approach and raised my whisk, that monk praised and prostrated to me. I asked him, 'You see me raise my whisk, so you immediately prostrate and praise me.
But when I sweep the ground here and raise my broom, why do you not praise me? He replied, 'I have received the teaching.'"
Someone said, "If one sees that all marks are no-marks, then one sees the Tathāgata.
What, then, is 'no-mark'? The Master said, "A lantern. A monk asked, "What is leaving home [to become a monk]? The Master said, "What would you call this a 'home-leaver'?

The monk said, "Parrots come from Longxi. The Master said, "That is not much of a difference. [He then] questioned another monk.
"From where have you come? he asked. The monk replied, "To repay my gratitude. The Master said, "Why do you not simply remain there? The monk said, "Monastics are not fixed in one place.
The Master said, "Since you are a monastic, why are you not fixed? The monk had no reply. (Xuánjué provided this substitute response: "I thank the Master for his inquiry.

[He] established a stupa in the western corner of the monastery and was posthumously titled Chan Master Zhenyi.

"What is the treasure within the Way? The Master said, "The clouds' descendant sheds tears as well. "Once all the sages have withdrawn their radiance and returned to the source, what then?
The Master said, "Three times the cries of the monkey are repeatedly cut off; ten thousand miles away, the traveler listens with sorrow. "I do not yet understand," he said.
"How can people of the present day reach the pivot of the ancients? The Master said, "I shall tell you for your own benefit: one must strictly avoid [clinging to] that which has not yet arisen."
At that time, Chan Master Tao of Guotai Monastery in Wuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Without departing from this very place, everything is the wondrously luminous true mind.
Therefore, Xuansha said: 'Few in the world know my final word. How does this compare to Guotai?"
The final phrase. A monk asked, "What is the final phrase regarding 'the nation being at peace'? The Master said, "Your question is far too late, Reverend.
He then returned to his quarters. A monk asked, "What is Vairocana? The Master said, "I am your disciple, elder brother.
A monk asked, "I do not ask about when Bodhidharma came; what is the matter of the future? The Master said, "I am your disciple, elder brother."
The Master said, "I personally met King Liang, who asked: 'What is it like when an ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master said: 'An ancient mirror. [The King] asked:
'What is it like after it has been polished? The Master said: 'An ancient mirror.'"

Chan Master Daohui of Bailong Monastery on Mount Sheng in Fuzhou was a native of that prefecture. He ascended the hall and said: "Without even lifting a foot—who is it whose majestic light shines? Do you understand?
If you say it is your own place of going, it has been so from the very beginning; yet, I am glad to say there is no connection. A monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?
The Master said: "From where have you come? A monk asked: "If [it is like this]... ...[text fragment]... The Master said: "From where have you come?"
"What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Prostrate three times immediately. The student asked, "I do not blame you for what has come before;
I ask that the Master speak directly. The Master said, "Attained. The student asked, "What is the true and correct Way? The Master said, "Riding a donkey while searching for a donkey.
The student asked, "I request the Master to answer the 'no guest and no host' dialogue. The Master said, "I remember it from years past. The student asked, "How is it right now?"
"What? the Master asked. "It is not only that his ears are deaf, but his eyes are also dim. A question was asked: "When emotion is forgotten and the body is merged [with reality], what is it like?

The Master said: "What else would you see in a dream? A question was asked: "I, a student, intend to pose a question; I beg the Master to provide a judgment. The Master said: "What do you wish to ask?"
The Master said, “I do not cut it. [The monk] asked, “Why do you not cut it? The Master said, “You must know that this is the work of a master hand.

A monk asked, “The great assembly has gathered; I request the Master to proclaim the Dharma. The Master said, “It is rare to find a listener. A monk asked, “Without involving the tip of the lips, I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master said, “Bring forth a question that does not involve the tip of the lips. [The monk] said, “In that case, all living beings will have their reliance. The Master said, “...The Master.”
[The monk] said, "Do not speak idly; I ask that you, Master, provide a reply based on the living pivot.
The Master said, "Bring paper and pen; I shall record it for you to take away. [The monk] asked, "What is the 'mouth of great thought'?
The Master said, "Come out and I will tell you. [The monk] said, "I have just now come out. The Master said, "How many people have you deceived so far?"
Chan Master Huiqiu Jizhao of Anguo Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of Putian, Quanzhou.
Among those who sought instruction within the quarters of Xuansha, he was foremost in his inquiries. Once, he asked, "What is the primary moon? Xuansha replied, "Why do you use this moon of yours?"

The Master attained awakening through this. Later, during the Wuchen year of the Kaiping era of the Later Liang, when Xuansha was about to pass away, Wang Shu, the military governor of Min, sent his son to inquire after his illness and requested that he secretly indicate who would succeed him in preaching the Dharma. Xuansha said, "Qiuzi shall obtain it."
The King silently took note of the deceased master’s final instructions and then inquired of Gushan, "Who is fit to hold the seat of the Dharma at Wolong?
Gushan named twelve venerable elders from the city who possessed the full eye of the Dharma; all were capable of appearing in the world as teachers. The King likewise kept this to himself.
On the day of the opening of the hall, the officials and the monks gathered together at the dharma assembly. The King suddenly asked the assembly, "Who is the Venerable Qiu?
Thereupon, the people pointed out the Master. The Wang family then invited him to ascend the seat. After a long silence, the Master said, "Do not resent the stillness; do not say it is inadequate.
Before the limits have been clearly discerned, how can one attempt to deliberate upon it? Therefore, he sought...
He often used their sounds, merely striking once or twice to assist them in triggering their own realization.

As for seeking a companion throughout the ten directions of the world, one cannot find anyone who could serve as such. A monk asked, "By what skillful means can one enter directly into the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Entering is itself the skillful means. The monk asked, "From which mountain does the cloud arise? From which ravine does the wind spring? The Master—

He said: "Exerting oneself in all actions, one does not depart from the Central Pagoda. Entering the hall, he said: "The circumstances of the rice gruel and meals here are for the sake of my brothers;

I raise them up for you to chant. Ultimately, this is not something constant. If you wish to attain what is essential and concise, it is rather the mountains, rivers, and the great earth that reveal it to you.
Since that Way is constant, it can also be brought to ultimate completion. If one enters through the gate of Mañjuśrī, there is nothing at all."
Earth, wood, tiles, and rubble assist you in triggering the mechanism [of awakening].

If you enter through the gate of Avalokiteśvara, all sounds—frogs, earthworms, and so forth—assist you in triggering the mechanism. If you enter through the gate of Samantabhadra, you arrive without moving a step.

I have shown you these three gates as skillful means, like taking a single broken chopstick and stirring the waters of the great ocean so that the fish and dragons therein may know water is their life.

Do you understand? If you lack the eye of wisdom to examine this with discernment, then no matter how many hundreds of clever and ingenious methods you employ, they will not lead to the ultimate realization.
Question: A student has recently entered the monastic groves but does not yet understand his own fundamental matter; I beg the Master for instruction.
Pointing with his staff, the Master said, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "My acting thus for you has instead resulted in suppressing you.

Do people still know this? From the standpoint of one's own nature, the matter that has been so from the beginning—whether one has just entered the monastic community or refers to the Buddhas of the past—is never lacking, just like the waters of the great ocean where all fish and dragons dwell."
"From birth until old age and death, the water one uses is entirely equal. Question: "Is this not the unerring true principle?

Please, Master, speak the truth. The Master said: "You yourself should speak for yourself. Question: "What about those who do not understand? The Master said: "Wait for those who do not understand to come.
Question: "Do the Buddhas have a teacher? The Master said: "They do. Question: "Who is it? The Master said: "Wait for them to come."
He was the teacher of all Buddhas. The Master said: "No one can recognize him. After sitting in the hall for a long time, a monk came forward and bowed.
The Master said: "Do not let your skull be crushed. A monk asked: "What is the matter of the ancestral vehicle (zongcheng) from of old?
The Master remained silent for a long while. The monk asked again, and the Master gave a shout and sent him out. A monk asked: "What is the matter at the top of Dayu Ridge? The Master—
The Master said, "I judge that you are unable to take this up. The monk asked, "How much weight does it have? The Master said, "For one such as this, even for kalpas one cannot do anything about it.
The Master then questioned the Hall Attendant: "As for what our late Master said—that the entirety of the ten directions of the world is the true human body—do you see the Sangha Hall?
The attendant said, "Master, do not let your eyes deceive you. The Master said, "Our late Master has passed away."

The flesh was still warm when he passed away. On the seventeenth day of the eighth month in the Guiyou year of the Qiandao era of the Liang dynasty, at the hour of the horse (noon), Master Cheng of Nantai on Mount Heng passed away without illness.
A monk asked, "Master, please expound upon the fundamental tenet of Xuansha. The Master said, "Very..."
"Where did you obtain this news? [The monk] asked, "What is meant by 'reaching down to receive'? The Master said, "When one meets the right person, one does not lose oneself.

[The monk] asked, "When the pond is clear and the moon appears, what kind of realm is that? The Master said, "It has nothing to do with you. [The monk] said, "If I am merely asking for information, why should it matter?"
The Master said, "One seeks the moon in the pool but cannot find it. [The monk] asked, "Why is there a fish-pattern at a distance of four fingers from the ground?
The Master said, "There is a sacred measure (ārya-mātrā) present. [The monk] asked, "For what kind of person is this measure intended? The Master said, "Not for a sage."
Chan Master Mingfa of Luofeng in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Every person is fully endowed with it; every person is its manifest realization.
How can one blame this mountain monk? Take care! A monk asked: "The quiescent nature of all phenomena cannot be proclaimed in words."

"What is the mark of quiescent extinction? The Master said, "Question and answer are both complete. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then in the *tathatā* dharma-realm there is neither self nor other.
The Master said, "This needlessly makes people sorrowful. [The monk] asked, "What was it like before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch?

The Master said, "His virtue was so profound that even ghosts and spirits revered him. [The monk] asked, "What was it like after he had seen him? The Master said, "His entire being was such that no one could surpass his sanctity."
Cè asked, "What is the single phrase of Luofeng? The Master said, "Suffering. He asked, "What is the person of original nature?
The Master said, "Forlorn; the realm of pine and vine is perilous."
A monk asked Zen Master Shuilongshan of Quanzhou, “What is bodhi as it meets the eye? The Master chased him away with his staff.
The monk then ran off. The Master said, “Stop, stop! Later, when you encounter a true adept, bring this up for them to examine.
He ascended the hall and, raising his staff, said, “I have lived on this mountain for thirty years and have gained its strength. At that time, a monk asked, “What did you gain from it, Master?”
"What strength do you have? The Master said, "Crossing streams and crossing ridges; leaning eastward and leaning westward.
When Chan Master Guangxu of Yunfeng on Mount Tiantai was ascending the hall, he said: "It is simply that sentient beings use it daily without knowing it.
For example, within the three thousand great thousandfold world-systems, one uses the stars and constellations daily, as well as the Yangtze, Yellow, Huai, and Ji Rivers, and all [other things]."
Sentient beings pass from one pore to another pore; the pores do not become smaller, nor do the worlds become larger.
The beings therein neither perceive nor know this. To make it easy to understand: even the daily activities of the Elder (the Master) are likewise unknown to them.
Once, a monk asked: "During the day, the monk carries the image; at night, the image carries the monk. I wonder, what is the meaning of this? The Master said:
"Preceptor, did you not come from the tea hall?
The hermit-master Qirú of Mount Dazháng in Fúzhōu is a native of this very province; he has long harbored solitary integrity and aspires to explore the Way of the Patriarchs."
Having entered the quarters of Xuansha, he attained an acute realization of the profound meaning. Xuansha remarked, "Your meditation has already reached a transcendent level;
in the future, you will have no need for even one person to stand by your side. From that time on, the Master did not strive to gather disciples nor maintain attendants.

He lived in seclusion at Xiaojie Mountain, carving out a small hovel from a large, decaying cypress tree that could accommodate only his body. Whenever traveling monks arrived, he would receive them there.
He responded according to what was asked, without fixed instruction. A monk asked, "When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them?
The Master said, "When the tally arrives, it is executed. The monk said, "In that case, one is taken away by birth and death. The Master said, "A-ye, a-ye.
[The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of holding the staff in India? The Master picked up his staff, struck the ground with it, and shook it. The monk said, [silently].
"I do not yet understand; what is the meaning of this? The Master said, "This is Zhang Family’s beating.
As the monk was about to offer a reply, the Master struck him with his staff. A monk asked, "Regarding Yuntai Qin, what is the true word for 'Qin'?
He replied, "Namo Buddhāya. The Master gave a different answer: "What? What? The two elders, Qinghuo and Chongxu, had long heard of the Master's reputation.
Once, when they visited together, Master Zhixu was gathering grain. Master Huo asked the visitor, "Where is the abbot?
The visitor replied, "From where have you come? Huo said, "From below the mountain. The visitor asked, "How did you get here? Huo said, "What place is this?
The visitor bowed and said, "Go and drink tea down there. Only then did the two men realize it was [the Abbot].
The Master then went to the hermitage. He found the lofty discourse deeply satisfying and sat beside him in conversation until, without his realizing it, night had fallen.
Suddenly, jackals and tigers rushed to the front of the hut and began to circle it naturally and submissively. Thereupon, Huo composed a poem: "My journey is no ordinary journey;

who knows the sentiments of going and staying? A single meal remains unsated; ten thousand households find no peace in life. Were it not for the Way, they would be difficult to subdue. [The text ends with "空" (empty/space).]
"Let no one contend with my fists. At the place where the dragon roars and clouds arise, he let out two or three leisurely cries.
The two masters sought him out at Dazhang Mountain and established a hermitage, inviting the Master to reside there. Sitting alone in both locations for fifty-two years, he passed away.
On the day Chan Master Yongxing Shenglü of Mount Lianhua in Fuzhou was invited by the Prince of Min to open the hall for formal teaching, before ascending the seat, he first stood before it and said:
"Great King and assembly, listen! There has already been a true and authentic proclamation.
This entire assembly has heard it; how could there be anyone who has not heard? If there were anyone who had not heard, we would be deceiving one another."
Only then did he ascend the seat. A monk asked, "The Great King has invited the Master to appear in the world; I do not understand why this assembly today is like that of Vulture Peak.
The Master said, "It penetrates the ancient and transmits to the present. The monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Within a single hair-tip, the sand-grains of the universe are revealed; the sun and moon appear therein."
When the Venerable Master Jing of Tiantai Guoqing Temple first met Xuansha, Xuansha addressed the assembly, saying:
"All of you, if you can for the rest of your lives act as if you had lost your parents, I guarantee that you will attain thorough penetration. The Master (Jing) followed up on these words and asked:
"Just as it is said in the teachings: 'One must not use the mind of what is known to fathom the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed knowledge and vision. Furthermore, how is this so?
Sandō said, "Tell me: even if you were to exhaustively master the mind of what is known to its very bottom, would you still be able to fathom it?"

The Master entered the path through faith from this point on. Later, he resided at Tiantai for more than twenty years, never descending from the mountain. He mastered the three studies (śikṣā) with comprehensive breadth; his conduct was solitary and peerless.

Beyond his practice of meditative stillness, he constantly perused the Dragon Canon (the Buddhist scriptures). He was held in high esteem by those both far and near, and was commonly referred to as "Dazheng the Elder.
Once, someone asked him: "When my disciple sits in meditation at night, my thoughts fly about in confusion. I do not yet understand how to restrain them."
"I prostrate myself before you and pray that you will grant me instruction on the method for subduing [the mind]. The Master said:

"If, while sitting peacefully at night, your thoughts fly about in confusion, take that very mind which is flying about and investigate the place from whence it flies. When you investigate and find no place, then where does the thought of flying about exist?
Turn back and investigate the investigating mind itself; then where is the mind that is capable of investigating? Furthermore, the wisdom that can illuminate is fundamentally empty."
The objects of perception are likewise quiescent. That which is quiescent yet not-quiescent is because there is no person who can bring about quiescence.
That which illuminates yet does not illuminate is because there is no object to be illuminated. When both object and wisdom are quiescent, the mind and its deliberations are at ease.

One does not seek out branches externally, nor does one dwell in meditative concentration internally. When these two paths are both obliterated, the single nature is serene. This is the essential method for returning to the source.
Regarding the Way: The Master, having observed the meaning of "illusion" within the teachings, composed a verse and asked the assembly of students:
"If all dharmas are like illusory existences, then one should incur no fault even by committing various transgressions and evils. Why, then, is the karma one has created not forgotten?"
Relying upon the Buddha’s compassion, he arose to provide guidance and conversion. At that time, there was an elder named Xiao Jing who replied:

"A phantom person manifests phantoms; the phantom wheel of existence is a phantom. Karma is able to summon phantoms, and because the object of treatment is not understood, phantoms give rise to various phantoms.
The perception of suffering is like a phantom; both phantoms and the unconditioned are thus. Both of these two elders passed away at their original mountain.

Chan Master Daokuang of Zhaoqing Monastery in Quanzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Changqing Leng. A native of Chaozhou, Daokuang entered the room to attend upon Changqing when the latter first resided at Zhaoqing.
He subsequently served as the head of the kitchen (tongtou) and frequently engaged in conversation with the assembly of monks. One day, Changqing saw him and said: "You..."
"What are you doing all day long, chattering away? the Master asked. Dongshan said, "If one does not work for a day, one does not eat for a day.
Yunyan Qing said, "In that case, you are sharpening your bow and honing your arrows. The Master said, "I am waiting specifically for Weichi to come. Qing said, "What happens after Weichi arrives?
The Master said, "I will make his sinews and bones cover the ground, and his eyes bulge out. Qing then went out.
When Qingsong was summoned, the Master succeeded him as abbot. Entering the hall for the formal address, he said: "If you realize it before the sound, you betray your lifelong study;
if you grasp the opportunity after the phrase, you utterly miss the essence of the Way. Why is this so? For an assembly such as this, tell me: how should one have acted from the very beginning?
Furthermore, did Qingzhao and all of you simultaneously express the point of ultimate resolution? At that time—
A monk stepped forward and said, "The assembly has all dispersed at once; does this accord with your Master’s intention?
The Master said, "I would give you twenty blows of the staff. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Though you have the intent of the blind turtle, you lack the progress of the bright moon.
The monk asked, "What is the progress of the bright moon? The Master said, "This is the intent of the blind turtle. [The monk] asked again: "How is it so?"
"What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said, "Neither practicing nor not practicing. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of coming from the West?
The Master said, "A mosquito on an iron ox. The monk asked, "What is the sword in its scabbard? The Master remained silent for a long time. The monk was at a loss.
The Master said, "You must also feel gratitude toward Zhaogqing before you may attain it. A monk asked, "What is the single phrase that upholds the essence?
The Master said, "Do not fail to recognize Zhaogqing. As the monk rose from his prostrations, the Master spoke again, "Do not fail to recognize Zhaogqing.
How would you entrust this to me? What is the single phrase that upholds the essence? The monk was speechless. A monk asked, "Regarding the sword beneath Mañjuśrī—"

15. At forty *laba* years [of age], Zen Master Shijin of Ruiyan in Taizhou, successor to Zen Master Longhua Zhao, was asked by a monk: "What is the realm of Ruiyan? The Master said: "Layer upon layer."

The Master said, "Ten thousand miles of white clouds pay homage to the Auspicious Peak; a light drizzle sprinkles before the curtain.

[The questioner] asked, "I do not yet understand how one may draw near to such a person. The Master said, "I thought you, O *jñātiputra*, had personally entered the inner chamber; it turns out you are still separated by ten thousand layers of gates."
A monk asked Chan Master Zhiqiu of Liutong Monastery in Taizhou, “What is it like when one wears a sword upon one’s entire body? The Master said, “It falls.
The monk asked, “And what of the one who encounters it? The Master said, “It steams the heavens and scorches the earth. [The monk] asked, “What is the realm of the six supernatural powers?”

The Master said, "The mountains and rivers fill the eyes; look as you please. [The student] asked, "What is it like to be a person within this realm? The Master said, "From antiquity to the present, they have come and gone of their own accord. [The student] asked, "Apart from these two paths, is there still a matter that transcends them? The Master said, "There is. [The student] asked, "What is this transcendent matter? The Master said, "Clouds and waters follow a thousand paths and ten thousand ways. [The student] asked Yongchui Yuantan: "Master, what is the ultimate meaning? Yuantan said, "It is right here before you. The student asked, "How can one enter this gate? Yuantan said, "If you wish to enter this gate, you must first abandon all seeking. The student asked, "If one abandons all seeking, how does one attain entry? Yuantan said, "If you do not seek, you will naturally find it. The student asked, "If one finds it naturally, what is its form? Yuantan said, "Formless and without shape. The student asked, "If it is formless and without shape, how can it be used? Yuantan said, "It is used everywhere, yet it never leaves its original place. The student asked, "If it never leaves its original place, why does it appear in various forms? Yuantan said, "Because it is not fixed, it appears in various forms. The student asked, "If it appears in various forms, is it not subject to change? Yuantan said, "Change is itself the unchanging. The student asked, "If change is itself the unchanging, then what is the unchanging? Yuantan said, "The unchanging is precisely this very change. The student asked, "If so, then how does one realize the Way? Yuantan said, "Realization is just like the clouds dispersing in the sky. The student asked, "If realization is like clouds dispersing, then what is the essence of the Way? Yuantan said, "The essence of the Way is like the empty sky. The student asked, "If the essence of the Way is like the empty sky, then how does one cultivate it? Yuantan said, "Cultivation is simply non-cultivation. The student asked, "If cultivation is non-cultivation, then what is the fruit of the Way? Yuantan said, "The fruit of the Way is like the harvest of the autumn fields. The student asked, "If the fruit of the Way is like the harvest of the autumn fields, then who is it that gathers it? Yuantan said, "It is gathered by those who have no self. The student asked, "If it is gathered by those with no self, then what is the benefit of the Way? Yuantan said, "The benefit of the Way is to liberate all sentient beings. The assembly replied, "On the fifteenth day of the second month, at the hour of Zi (11 p.m.–1 a.m.). The Master said, "I spoke these words earlier this very morning," and having finished speaking, he passed away. His lifespan was seventy years.
