At the beginning of the Dazhong era, following the general policy of re-admission through repentance, he received the full ordination at Qifeng Temple in Yanguan. Later, he went to visit Daci.
Kong said, "Why do you not travel extensively to seek instruction? The Master went directly to Huayan Temple on Mount Wutai. Upon arriving at the Vajra Cave, he paid his respects.
There he encountered an old man walking with an ox, who invited the Master into the temple. The old man called out, "Juntí! and a boy responded by coming out to welcome him.
The old man released the ox and led the Master up into the hall; the entire building was radiant with a golden light. The old man—
He sat upon the bed. [The Master] pointed to an embroidered cushion and bade him sit. The old man asked, "Where have you recently come from? The Master replied, "From the South.
The old man asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma maintained in the South? The Master said, "In the age of the final dharma, bhikṣus rarely uphold the precepts.
The old man asked, "How many followers do they have? The Master said, "Sometimes three hundred, sometimes five hundred. The Master then asked in turn, "How is the Buddha-dharma maintained here?"
[Zhaozhou] accepted it. The old man said, "Dragons and snakes are mixed together; ordinary people and sages dwell side by side. Zhaozhou asked, "How many people are there?
The old man replied, "Three times three before, three times three after. The old man called to his attendant boy to serve tea, along with offering *sukha* (butter) and *dadhi* (curd).
Zhaozhou partook of their flavors, and his mind was suddenly enlightened. The old man picked up a crystal cup and asked, "Is there such a thing as this in the South? Zhaozhou replied, "No."
The old man said, "What do you usually use to drink tea? The Master had no reply. Seeing that the sun was already late, the Master then asked the old man, "May I stay for one night?
The old man said, "You still have a mind of attachment; you may not stay. The Master said, "I have no mind of attachment.
The old man said, "Have you ever received the precepts? The Master said, "I have received them long ago. The old man said, "You..."
"If one has no grasping mind, what use is there for receiving the precepts? With these words, the Master took his leave. The old man ordered a youth to escort him.

The Master asked the youth, "What is the total of 'three times three' before and 'three times three' after? The youth called out, "Venerable Sir! The Master responded, "Yes? The youth said, "How much is that?
The Master asked again, "Where is this place? The youth replied, "This is the Prajñā Temple at Vajra Cave."
The Master was moved with sorrowful realization that the old man was none other than Mañjuśrī, and that he could not be seen again.
He immediately prostrated himself before the youth and requested a single word as a parting gift. The youth spoke this verse: "No anger on the face is the offering;
No anger in the mouth is the sublime fragrance; No anger in the heart is the precious jewel; Stainless and untainted, this is the true eternal. Having finished speaking, he departed.
Junti and the temple both vanished; only within five-colored clouds could one see Mañjuśrī riding a golden-maned lion, coming and going.
Suddenly, a white cloud emerged from the east and covered them, so they were no longer visible. At that time, monks such as Xiuzheng from Bodhi Monastery in Cangzhou arrived;
they still heard the sound of the mountain rocks trembling and roaring. Consequently, the Master remained at Wutai to reside. All [witnessed this].

After three years had passed, he went to Guanyin in Hongzhou and visited Yangshan, where his mind was suddenly awakened and his realization accorded with the Master's. Yangshan appointed him as the head cook (*diànzuò*).
Once, Mañjuśrī appeared atop the rice-pot; the Master took the stirring ladle and struck him, saying, "Mañjuśrī is Mañjuśrī, and I am I."
Wenxi was indeed Wenxi. Shu then spoke a verse, saying: "The bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip; the sweet melon is sweet from stem to end.
Having practiced for three great kalpas, I am instead resented by this old monk. One day, a strange monk came to seek alms-food.
The Master reduced his own portion and gave it to him. Yangshan, having foreknown this, asked: "Just now, a person of the fruit-stage arrived; did you give him food?"
"No," the Master said. Yang bowed his head and replied, "You have brought me great benefit. Later, he returned to Zhejiang, where the King of Qian invited him to preside over Longquan Monastery.
A monk asked, "What is the mark of nirvana? The Master said, "It is verified at the point where the incense smoke has vanished. [The monk] asked again.
"What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Call the monastery steward here; this monk suffers from madness. A monk asked, "What is one's own true self?
The Master remained silent. The monk was at a loss and asked again. The Master said, "The clear blue sky is shrouded in darkness."

"Not Flying Toward the Moon. During the *gengxu* year of the Dàshùn era of the Táng Emperor Xīzōng, the King of Qián memorialized the throne requesting that the master be granted purple robes and appointed as the Chan Master Wúzhù.
On the third day of the tenth month of the *gengshēn* year of the Guānghuà era, at midnight, the master addressed the assembly, saying:

"When the mind of the three realms is exhausted, this is precisely nirvāṇa. Having spoken these words, he sat in the full lotus posture and passed away. A white light illuminated the chamber, and the bamboo and trees were likewise suffused with it.
His physical appearance was [as described]. He lived to eighty years of age and had been a monk for sixteen years. His stupa was located in the western valley of Lingyin Mountain.

In the *Renxu* year of the Tianfu era, Tian Jun, the regional commander of Xuancheng, joined forces with the Hangzhou general Xu Si in rebellion. They unleashed their troops to plunder extensively and opened the master’s stupa.

Seeing that his flesh body remained undecayed, with his nails and hair having grown long, the King of Wusuku, Qian Liu, marveled at this and dispatched his subordinate general, Shao Zhi, to re-seal it with greater honor.
It was interred [there]. During the Gengchen year of the Jiading era of Emperor Ningzong of the Song dynasty, it was moved to the left of the stupa of Chan Master Zhijue Shou at Mount Jingci.
During the Gengyin year of the Shunzhi era of the Imperial Dynasty (the Qing), it was further moved to the right ridge of Mount Shengguo.
A monk asked Zen Master Sunji Ryōgo of Gwansan Mountain in the Kingdom of Silla, “What is the meaning of the West?
The Master held up his whisk. The monk said, “Is this not it? The Master lowered the whisk. Another monk asked, “It is not the character ‘yi’ (以), nor is it the character ‘pa’ (八).
What character is it? The Master drew a circle and showed it to him. There was another monk who... [text fragment]
Before the Master, he drew a five-petaled circular diagram. The Master broke it apart and drew a single circle.
A monk asked the Master Dongta of Yangshan in Yuanzhou, "What is the King’s Sword? The Master said, "The sail is lowered; no credit is claimed.

The monk asked, "How is it when it is used? The Master said, "It does not fall into human hands. [Another monk] asked, "What is the Dharma-King compared to the Ruler? The Master said, "He is the one who turns the wheel."
"How is it when the King meets him? The Master said, "Both palms are without partiality. [The monk] asked, "How is it after the meeting? The Master said, "In the midst, all images are severed.
This was the Dharma heir of Chan Master Xiangyan Huiyan.
A monk asked Master Zhiguan of Jizhou, “What is the Vairocana Teacher? The Master grabbed him by the chest and gave him a shove.
The monk asked, “What is suddenness? The Master said, “Neither Liang nor Chen.”
A monk asked Chan Master Shaozong of Shouzhou, “What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, “Good news does not leave the door;
bad news travels a thousand miles. A government official said to the Master, “I have heard it said that in Jiangxi they do not establish a school.”

The Master said, “When meeting conditions, one establishes [the teaching]. [The monk] asked, “What is it that you establish when meeting conditions? The Master said, “In Jiangxi, we do not establish a school.
Chan Master Wuran of Nanchan in Yizhou was asked by a monk, “Regarding the phrase that has no phrase, will you, Master, still provide an answer?
The Master said, “From the beginning, I have only clarified this very matter. [The monk] asked, “Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, “Go ahead and ask.”
A monk asked Master Pingshan of Yizhou, "What is it like at the point where even a blink of an eye cannot reach?
The Master said, "I do not have the leisure even to blink my eyes. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch? The Master said, "Coming from India, going to Tang."
A monk asked Chan Master Chengfu Yanjiao of Yizhou, "What is the speech of vast emptiness? The Master said, "Attaining the Way without a mouth.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the [Master’s] coming from the West? The Master said, "Today and tomorrow."
A monk asked Chan Master Qinggan of Dajian Mountain in Anzhou, "How did all the sages of the past realize enlightenment?
The Master merely scratched his forehead. Another asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "A goat-headed cart pushes the bright moon."
A monk asked the Abbot of Fengde Temple on Mount Zhongnan, “What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, “I am wall-eyed regarding all matters. The monk asked, “What is the matter of original nature? The Master said, “I certainly will not ask others again.”
A monk asked Zen Master Foyan Hui of Mount Wudang in Junzhou, "I have been ill for many years and have also been poisoned;
I beg the Master to act as my physician. The Master said, "One bowl of medicinal soup, suitable for both conditions. The monk asked, "What is the matter beyond the Buddha?
The Master said, "A conch-shell topknot. The monk asked, "What is the matter below the Buddha? The Master said, "A lotus throne."
A monk asked the Chan practitioner Tando of the Double Creek on Mount Lu in Jiangzhou, “What is the mechanism of the simultaneous pecking and hatching?
The Master made the gesture of pecking with his hand. The monk asked, “What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, “From where have you obtained this question?”
Master Hongzhou Miling, a successor of Chan Master Yìn of Jìngshān, often said: "Nothing surpasses this. A monk asked, "I do not yet understand what it is that nothing surpasses.
The Master said, "It does not go beyond this. Later, the monk asked Chángqìng, "Why does it not go beyond this?"
Qing said, "What do you intend to call it?
Master Shuangfeng was a Dharma heir of the Chan Master Gu of Shuangfeng in Fuzhou;
his original vocation was lecturing on the sutras, but he subsequently studied under the former Master Shuangfeng. Shuangfeng asked him, "Virtuous One..."
"Where do you reside? he asked. "In the city," [the monk] replied. Feng said, "Do you ever think of me, the old monk?
He replied, "I constantly think of the Master, but have no way to pay my respects. Feng said, "This very act of thinking is you, the virtuous one. From this, the master attained his realization.
He immediately ceased his lectures and attended [as a servant] for several years. Later, he went to Shishuang, where he merely followed the assembly without further seeking instruction.
The community remarked, "The former attendant once received the seal of approval from Shuangfeng; this has often been heard regarding him at Shishuang.
Shishuang wished to interrogate him regarding his realization but had not yet found the opportunity. When the Master took his leave, Shishuang took his whisk and escorted him out the gate.
Xuefeng turned his head. Xiangshuang called out, "Attendant! The Master turned his head back. Xiangshuang said, "To conceptualize it is already a deviation; to affirm it as 'this' is to go astray.
Do not conceptualize it as 'not this,' nor should you form any understanding of it at all. Unless one knows that there is [the Way], no one can know it. Go, go!"
The Master responded, "Yes, yes," and immediately set forth. Shortly thereafter, Shuangfeng entered nirvana, and the Master continued as the abbot.
A monk asked, "When you took your leave of Shishuang at that time, what was the meaning behind Shishuang’s words? The Master said:
He simply taught that the mind should not cling to right or wrong (Xuánjué said: "Now tell me, did he understand Shīshuāng’s meaning or not?").
He was a successor of Chan Master Xītǎ Mù of the sixth generation under Nányuè.
A monk asked Chan Master Ruyao of Zifu in Jizhou, “What is the phrase that responds to the occasion? The Master remained silent. The monk asked, “What is the original intent?
The Master said, “Close the door for me. The monk asked, “What is the meaning of Lu Zu’s wall-gazing?
The Master said, “There is no connection. The monk asked, “What is the true eye of the ancestors from of old? The Master remained silent.
The Master beat his breast and said, "Heaven! Heaven! [The monk] asked, "May I ask what is the hindrance? The Master said, "I am weary.
[The monk] asked, "Does this [state] admit of further study? The Master said, "I have never yet dug into the earth to plant empty space.

[The monk] asked, "What is the most urgent matter for a patch-robed monk? The Master said, "It does not go beyond this question. [The monk] said, "Before the student has even asked, please let the Master [speak]."
[The student] asked, “How is it that a single mote of dust enters right concentration? The Master made the gesture of entering meditative absorption.
[The student] asked, “How is it that all motes of dust arise from samādhi? The Master said, “To whom are you asking? [The student] asked, “What is the one path to the gate of nirvāṇa?
The Master snapped his fingers once and then opened both hands wide. [The student] asked, “How should I understand this? The Master—
He said, "It is not the brightness of the autumn moon; you yourself are wandering aimlessly. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master?

The Master said, "Three bowls of tea after the meal. One day, the Master picked up his meditation cushion (*pūtāna*), showed it to the assembly, and said, "All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and sages who have entered into principle all emerge from here.
He then threw it down, opened wide his chest, and said, "Do [it]!"

"How is it? The assembly had no reply. The Master asked, "I, a student, have entered this monastery myself; now that the end of the summer retreat is approaching, I have not yet received instruction from the Master.
I pray you will deign to provide me with guidance. The Master spread his hands and said, "Since I have been the abbot, I have never blinded a single person's eyes.
On another occasion, the Master sat for a long time, then looked around left and right and asked, "Do you understand? The assembly said [nothing].

"No," the Master said. "If you do not understand, I shall deceive you. One day, the Master placed a meditation cushion upon his head and said, "At such a time as this, it is difficult to converse with you all.
The assembly had no reply. He then sat down and said, "It is still somewhat better than that."
Chan Master Huiqing of Bajiao Mountain in Yingzhou was a successor of Chan Master Nanta Yong. He was a native of Silla. Once, he ascended the hall, held up his staff, and said:
"If you have a staff, I will give you a staff; if you have no staff, I will take it away from you."
[The Master] leaned on his staff, descended from the seat, and said: A monk asked, "What is the water of the banana tree?
The Master said, "Warm in winter and cool in summer. A monk asked, "What is the 'blow-off-hair sword'? The Master said, "Step forward three paces.
The monk asked, "How about one who uses it? The Master said, "Step back three paces. A monk asked, "What is the single phrase by which the Master benefits others? The Master said:
"I only fear that you, Ācārya, will not ask. "Does the assembly understand? "Those who fully comprehend it are few. Take care!
A monk asked, "When there is no speech, how is it when there is a question? The Master said, "Before leaving the three gates, it is a thousand li's journey.
A monk asked, "What is one's own self? The Master said, "Look toward the south for the Big Dipper. A monk asked, "When both light and objects have vanished, what is it? The Master said—
He asked, "What do you know? The Master said, "Jiulao of Jianzhou. Ascending the hall, he said:
"It is like a person walking along who suddenly encounters a ten-thousand-fathom deep pit ahead, while a wild fire pursues from behind, with thorny thickets on both banks.
If he moves forward, he will fall into the pit; if he retreats, the wild fire will burn his body. If..."
As he turned over, he was obstructed by a thorn forest. At such a time, how can one avoid it?
If you can avoid it, you must possess a way to emerge; if you cannot avoid it, you are a man who has fallen into death.
Question: "What is the school of Deva? The Master said: "The red banner is on the left. He asked a monk: "Where have you recently come from? The monk said: "Please [tell me]."
The Master tested him, saying, "Tell me, what do you say? The monk said, "I took you for a merchant on a ship; it turns out you are just a petty local client. [The Master] asked, "Do you ask or not?
Do you ask about the two heads and three peaks? [The monk] requested, "Please, Master, point directly to my original face.
The Master sat silently and upright. [Another monk] asked, "When a thief comes, one must strike; when a guest comes, one must look. But what if both guest and thief arrive at once?"
The Master said, "Inside the house there is a pair of worn-out straw sandals. [A monk] asked, "As for those worn-out straw sandals, are they still fit for use?
The Master said, "If you take them away, it will be ominous in front and inauspicious behind. [Another monk] asked, "What is the meaning of 'the Northern Dipper hiding its body'?
The Master said, "Nine times nine is eighty-one. He then asked, "Do you understand? [The monk] said, "No. The Master said, "One."
2, 3, 4, 5. The Master said to the assembly: "When I was twenty-eight years old, I went to Yangshan to visit Nanta.
Seeing him ascend the hall, he said: 'All you people here—if you are a true man, as soon as you emerge from your mother’s womb, you should let out a lion’s roar;
do you agree? At these words, my body and mind came to rest, and I stayed there for five years. He asked.
“How was it before the ancient Buddhas had appeared? The Master said, “The root of a thousand-year-old eggplant.
“How was it after they had appeared? The Master said, “Vajrapāṇi opens his eyes. He ascended the hall and, after a long silence, said, “How deeply you have humiliated me!
Be careful! Someone asked, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, “Which Patriarch’s meaning are you asking about? The man replied, “Bodhidharma’s.”
[Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "Alone and weary, he crossed the river in the dark. [Question:
"When Niu-t'ou had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch, what was it like? The Master said: "He knew. [Question: "After he had seen him, what was it like?
The Master said: "He knew. [Question: "What thing has no two ends? What thing has no front or back? The Master said: "My body has no two ends; my speech has no front or back."
The questioner asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, "First, you must not ask; second, you must not rest.
The questioner said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Come for a third time, and I shall meet with you."
Chan Master Quanfu of Qinghua in Yuezhou was a native of Kunshan in Wu Commandery. He first visited Nanta, who asked him, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "From Ezhou. Nanta asked, "What is the name of the Magistrate of Ezhou?
The Master said, "I do not dare to offend him while under his jurisdiction. Nanta said, "In this way, you do not fear him. The Master said, "Why must a great man [behave] thus?"
The Master laughed heartily and, having thus granted his seal of approval, the Magistrate of Anfu County in Luling established Yingguo Chan Garden and invited the Master to gather disciples there.
When the local authorities heard of this, they were moved and bestowed upon it the name Qinghua Monastery.

A monk asked, "What is the Master’s urgent means of benefiting others? The Master said, "In the morning look to the southeast; in the evening look to the northwest. The monk said, "I do not understand."
The Master said, "You have traveled in vain to seek a guest from the East; you do not recognize the treasure of the West.

A monk asked, "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master said, "I, for one, do not know. The monk asked, "Why does the Master not know? The Master said, "It would be improper to wet the bed under a clear blue sky and bright daylight.
Later, when the Master returned to his native country, the Prince Wenmu of the Qian family treated him with exceptional courtesy and honor.
In the *dingyou* year of the Tianfu era of the Jin dynasty, a garrison commander of the Qian family cleared away Yunfeng Mountain to establish a monastery, also naming it Qinghua.
He invited the Master to open the hall. A monk asked, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said:

“A wooden crane flies from atop the pillar of a *huabiao*. The monk asked: “When meeting a person who has attained the Way, one does not respond with speech or silence. I wonder, what then will you use?”
[The monk] said, "What is it? The Master said, "The pupil in the eye is a whistle. [The monk] asked, "How old are you, Preceptor? The Master said, "I first saw last year’s September ninth;
now I see again the autumn leaves turning yellow. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then you have no fixed number [of years].
The Master said, "Ask the yellow leaves. [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, what is the matter? The Master said, "Six dice rolled full."
Pénghóng asked about the passing away of a deceased monk: "Where has he gone? The Master said: "The long river flows without interruption; gathered foam drifts at the mercy of the wind.
[The monk] asked: "Does he still receive offerings? The Master said: "Offerings are not lacking. [The monk] asked: "How are they offered? The Master said:
"Fishermen sing as they raise their oars; the sound is heard within the valley. Zhōngxiàn Wáng bestowed upon him the purple robe.
The King offered him a square-cut robe (*fāngpáo*), but the Master would not accept it. The King then changed it to a patched robe (*nièyī*) and continued to style him as Chan Master Chunyi.

The Master said, "It is not that I am feigning modesty; I fear that later generations might imitate me and give rein to their desires. In the autumn of the Dingwei year of the Kaiyun era of the Later Jin, the Master manifested his passing.
At that time, a great wind blew, toppling and shattering bamboo and trees. He was sixty-six years old and had forty-five years of ordination seniority.
A monk asked Chan Master Yichu Mingwei of Mount Huanglian in Shaoyang, "I do not ask about the Three Vehicles or the twelve divisions of the teachings;
I request that the Master open his mouth without answering my question. The Master said, "Upon the jeweled flower pedestal, past and present are settled.

The monk asked, "What is it like to settle past and present upon the jeweled flower pedestal? The Master said, "A single dot of ink; the cycle turns without shifting. The monk asked, "... [The text ends here].
The student said, "I do not understand at all; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "Though spiritual awareness revolves, the flowers in the sky do not fall.
[The student] asked, "The ancient path leaves no trace; how does one advance upon it? The Master said, "The golden bird circles Mount Sumeru; its essence is simultaneous with the kalpa.
[The student] said, "If that is so, then one attains the other shore. The Master said, "The Yellow River overflows once every three thousand years."
Duching’s patron was Lady Liu. Having long admired the Master’s spiritual transformation, she invited him into her residence to preach the Dharma.

A monk asked, "When the Human King and the Dharma King meet, what is it like? The Master said, "Two mirrors reflect one another; the myriad phenomena are clearly manifest. The monk asked, "Regarding the essential heart of the Dharma King:
when Bodhidharma came from the West, the Fifth Patriarch transmitted it to Caoxi. From that time on, the robe and bowl were no longer passed down."
"I do not understand. Before the emerald steps, what was entrusted to him? The Master said, "A stone ram walks upon the water; a wooden horse at night rolls over its foal.
[The questioner] said, "If that is so, then the King has a resonance, and the ten thousand nations return to court. The Master said, "All people of this age sing the song of Great Peace.
Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "On his chest is inscribed the *svastika*; on his back he bears a halo. [The questioner] said: [How is it?]
"What is the Way? The Master extended both hands and showed them to him. The monk asked, "How far apart are Buddha and the Way?
The Master replied, "Like water and its waves."
A monk asked Zen Master Hongji Miaoji of Huilin in Shaoyang Prefecture, “The sages of the past have always traveled this path;
what is this path? The Master said, “Indeed, you do not see it. A monk asked, “What is the meaning of Luzu’s wall-facing?
The Master said, “What snow-cleansing place is there? A monk asked, “What is the urgent matter? The Master said, “A dull-witted fellow. A monk asked, [“... The Master said, “A dull-witted fellow.”

"What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "The general rule in all quarters. "Regarding the study of concentration and wisdom as being equal, and the clear realization of Buddha-nature—how is this principle?
The Master said, "A newly constructed Buddhist temple."
The Dharma Heir of National Teacher Baofu of the Seventh Generation under Nanyue,
Chan Master Zengsui of Zifú in Jizhou, was asked by a monk: "Upon seeing the ancients, what realization did you, the Master, attain?"
"Rest. The Master showed him this [fish-shaped] symbol (○). Question: "What is the song of the ancients?
The Master showed him this ○ symbol. Question: "What is the very first phrase? The Master said: "Before the world was formed."
The *ācārya* was also present there. [A monk] asked, "What is the meaning of Baizhang’s gesture of rolling up his mat? The Master remained silent for a long time.

[Another monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the ancient saying, 'Three before and three after'? The Master said, "What is your name? [The monk] replied, "I am so-and-so. The Master said, "Go and drink tea.
[Once], while ascending the hall, he saw the flagpole of Zifu Temple across the river and immediately turned back on his feet.
Follow him down. He deserves thirty blows. Furthermore, when he first came over the river, as soon as a monk stepped out, the Master said, "Not fit for conversation.
Question: "What is the mind of the ancient Buddha? The Master said: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth."
A monk asked Master Fushou of Jizhou, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
The Master extended his hand and asked, "Mañjuśrī rides a lion; Samantabhadra rides an elephant king. I wonder what Śākyamuni rides?
The Master raised his hand and said, "Ya! Ya!"
A monk asked Master Lùyuàn of Tánzhōu, "When one attains Buddhahood in other lands, is there still a distinct name?
The Master drew a circle (○) and showed it to him without a teacher’s mediation. The monk asked, "What is the single path of Lùyuàn? The Master said, "Bring forth the tongue of a Jìlǎo.
The monk asked, "What is 'building a cart while the door is shut'? The Master said, "The Stone Bridge at Nányuè. The monk said, "Just so."
"What is it that, when one leaves the gate, the tracks coincide? The Master said, "The head of the staff; the shoes on one's feet.

Ascending the hall, he spread his two hands and said, "The life-roots of all the old monks and all you venerable ones are entirely here. A monk came forward and asked, "Is there anything to be gathered up?
The Master said, "Beside the Stone Bridge at Tiantai. The monk said, "I do not think so. The Master said, "I humbly hope you will remain well."
Xiang asked, "What is the meaning of 'The World-Honored One speaks that which is not spoken'? The Master said, "Mount Sumeru falls.
Xiang asked, "What is the meaning of 'Kāśyapa hears that which is not heard'? The Master said, "The great ocean dries up."
Zen Master Jiche of Bajiao Mountain in Yingzhou was a successor of Zen Master Bazhao Qing. When he first visited Fengxue, Fengxue asked him, "What is the True Dharma Eye?
The Master replied, "A clay pellet. Fengxue marveled at this. He then went to visit the former master Bazhao, arriving just as the master was ascending the hall to give a discourse, citing Yangshan.

"The Way has two mouths and no tongue; this is my school’s fundamental principle. Upon hearing this, the Master attained a sudden realization. After he took up residence there, a monk asked, "What is the realm of Línxī?
The Master said, "There are mountains and there are waters. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm?
The Master said, "In front of the main gate, behind the Buddha hall. A monk asked, "What is the place of profound depth? The Master said, "The stone man opens [his mouth]."

Finally, he arrived at Linchuan and visited Fayan. Upon seeing him, Fayan immediately regarded him with deep esteem. The Master, having traversed the monastic forests extensively, was also weary of it.
As for his formal inquiries, he merely followed along with the assembly. One day, when Fayan was ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is one drop of water from the Cao source?
Fayan replied, "It is one drop of water from the Cao source. The monk withdrew, feeling bewildered. The Master [Xuedou] was seated nearby.
He attained sudden enlightenment; all the stagnations of his life were dissolved like ice melting away. He then reported what he had realized to Fayan.
Fayan said, "In the future, you shall be a teacher to kings, causing the ancestral Way to shine with great brilliance; I am not your equal."
From this point on, he resolved the various divergent doctrines of the different regions and the fundamental keys of the ancient and modern teachings, leaving not the slightest trace behind.
He soon returned to his original path and traveled to Mount Tiantai, where he beheld the remains of the Venerable Zhizhe Yi; they appeared as if they were his former dwelling.
Since the Master shared the same surname as Zhizhe, he was at that time regarded as his reincarnation. When he first resided at Baisa, King Zhongyi was still a prince.

At that time, [the Prince] was stationed in Taizhou and, having heard of the Master’s reputation, invited him to inquire about the Way. The Master said to him, “In the future you shall become a hegemon;

do not forget the Buddha’s kindness. In the fifth year of the Gānyòu era of the Hàn dynasty (Wùshēn), when the Prince succeeded to the throne, he dispatched an envoy to welcome the Master and performed the rites due to a disciple.
There was one named Xì Jí, who transmitted the teachings of Zhìzhě of Tiāntái (he was Luóxī); he repeatedly spoke to the Master concerning Zhì...
As for this teaching, as the years have passed, there is much concern that it will become scattered and lost. Now, the kingdom of Silla possesses its original texts in their entirety.
Were it not for the compassionate power of the Upādhyāya, who else could have brought them here?

The Master then informed the King, who dispatched an envoy bearing the Master’s letter to that country. They returned with a complete transcription of the texts, which has flourished in the world until the present day.
Ascending the hall after his stay: The skillful means of the ancient sages are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. The Patriarch said, "It is not the wind or the banner that moves;
it is the mind of the noble one that moves. This is the Dharma-gate of the Unsurpassed Mind-Seal. We are disciples under the lineage of the Patriarchs.
How do you understand the meaning of the Patriarch? Do not say that the wind and the banner are unmoving while it is your own mind that is falsely moving.
Do not say that you do not strike at the wind and the banner, but rather seek understanding through them. Do not ask, "What is it when the wind and the banner move? Someone said:
To clarify the mind by means of external objects is not to recognize the object itself. Some say, "Form is emptiness," while others say, "It is neither the wind nor the banner that moves.
One must understand this with subtle insight. But if one understands it in such a way, how does it relate to the intent of the Patriarchs?
Since such an understanding is not permitted, you venerable seniors should surely know this. If you were to attain thorough enlightenment right here, what dharma would there be?

Though you have entered the gate, you do not yet see clearly. Once the skillful means of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are simultaneously and thoroughly understood, what further doubt could there be?
Therefore, the ancients said: "When one thing is understood, a thousand things become clear; when one thing is deluded, ten thousand things are confused.

Does it mean that you realized this today, but will not understand it again tomorrow? Is it perhaps because there is a portion of the "transcendent matter" (shangxiang shi) that is difficult to comprehend? No.

A certain class of inferior ordinary people will not understand this view. Even if they were to spend aeons as numerous as motes of dust, they would only exhaust their own spirits and weary their thoughts;
it is impossible for them to attain it. A monk asked, "The mark of the extinction of all dharmas cannot be expressed in words.
How do you, Reverend Father, guide others? The Master said, "When you reach other places, ask once more. The monk said, "If that is so, then it is cut off."
[The questioner] departed from the words. The Master said: "Awake within a dream. Question: "When both oars and rudders have been set aside, how can one reach the other shore?
The Master said: "I congratulate you on your life thus far. Question: "What are the three kinds of sick people? The Master said: [He remained silent].
Someone asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddha? The Master said, "This question is not weak. Someone asked, "What are the six characteristics?
The Master said, "It is you yourself. Someone asked, "What is skillful means? The Master said, "This question is most appropriate.
Someone asked, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? The Master said, "I certainly will not tell you."
[The student] asked, "Why do you not speak to me? The Master said, "I fear you would not understand. [The student] asked, "A single flower opens into five petals;
the fruit is naturally formed. What is 'a single flower opening into five petals'? The Master said, "The sun rises and the moon is bright.
[The student] asked, "What is 'the fruit being naturally formed'? The Master said, "Heaven and earth are luminously clear. [The student] asked, "As for... (The text here ends).
"What is the Buddha Without Sorrow? The Master said, "It kills people with grief. "From what do all mountains, rivers, and the great earth arise?
The Master said, "From where does this question come? "What is the mind that repeatedly arises? The Master said, "How can you avoid it?
"What is the eye of the śramaṇa? The Master said, "Black as lacquer. "How is it when there is nothing more to cut off? The Master said, "It is like a man who has lost his way."
"How is it when news is received? The Master said, "Thank you for pointing this out. The questioner asked, "What is it to transform objects so as to be identical with the Tathāgata?
The Master said, "What do you call 'objects'? He replied, "In that case, one is identical with the Tathāgata. The Master said, "Do not let out the howl of a jackal.
A questioner asked, "When Prince Nanda dismembered his flesh to return it to his mother and his bones to return them to his father, after which..."
[The Master] was preaching the Dharma to his parents upon a lotus flower. [A monk] asked, "I do not yet understand: what is the Prince’s body?
The Master said, "Everyone sees; ask the Elder. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then the great trichiliocosm is of one true nature.
The Master said, "It is vaguely like a melody just fit to hear, yet it is blown by the wind into another tune. [Another monk] asked, "When the six sense-faculties have all ceased, why..."

[The monk asked: "In that case, principle and phenomena are not clearly understood. The Master said, "Where are they not clear? [The monk] said, "If so, then principle and phenomena are both as they are.
The Master said, "Where was my previous statement? Ascending the hall, he said: "Generally speaking, words and phrases must be free from leakage before they can be considered correct."
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the phrase that is free from leakage? The Master said, "Your mouth is like your nostrils.
The monk asked, "What is not realizing a single dharma? The Master said, "Wait for my words. The monk asked, "What is realizing all dharmas?
The Master said, "Why are you drunk? He then said, "Just as when I respond to you in this way, what do you all, venerable seniors, do?"
Is it that you have realized the essence? Is it that this is the true mark? Is it that at this very moment there is not a single dharma to be realized?
Is it that you recognize its place of origin? Is it that the whole body is fully manifest? Do not misunderstand!
Such a view is called "clinging to grass and attaching to wood"; it is worlds apart from the Buddha-dharma.

Even if one’s answers and discernments were as fluent as a cascading river, they would merely result in a perverted understanding. If one prizes only the ability to answer questions and discern with discrimination, what difficulty is there?
Yet I fear it will be of no benefit to others and will instead lead them astray. As for the Venerable One mentioned above...
Regarding what you have studied—discriminating through questions and answers, memorizing and explaining principles—you have done so in great abundance. Why, then, does your doubt not cease?
When you hear the skillful means of the ancient sages, you fail to understand them specifically because there is too much emptiness and too little substance.
Elder, it would be better for you to look directly from beneath your heels all at once and see: what principle is this? How many Dharma-gates are there to compare with this?

As he sat in doubt seeking resolution, he finally realized that all the matters he had previously studied were merely the root-source of birth and death, the livelihood within the realm of the five aggregates (*skandhas*).
Therefore, the ancients said: "If seeing and hearing are not yet liberated, they are like the moon in the water. Be at ease; take care! The Master had a verse which says:
At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, it is not of this human world. Outside the mind there is no dharma; it fills the eyes.
When Seigen (Qing Shan) heard this, he said, "This very verse can revive my school. Later, when the Master was expounding the Dharma at Hannya-ji (Prajñā Temple), he ascended the hall and said:
"A hair swallows the vast ocean, yet the nature of the ocean remains unimpaired; a tiny speck of dust enters the sharp point of a blade, yet the sharpness of the blade remains unmoved.
Whether one sees or does not see, whether one realizes or does not realize—it is known only by me. He then offered this verse: "Having briefly descended from the high..."
The Peak has already proclaimed it: Prajñā is perfectly pervasive throughout the ten directions; among humans and devas, all are vast and without distinction;
throughout the Dharma-realm, in every vertical and horizontal direction, it is manifest everywhere. Be careful! [He] ascended the hall. A monk asked: "I have heard an ancient saying:
'If a person sees Prajñā, they are bound by Prajñā; if a person does not see Prajñā, they are also bound by Prajñā. Since one has already seen Prajñā..."
“If so, why then are you bound? The Master said, “Tell me, what does Prajñā see? He replied, “Prajñā sees nothing.
The Master asked, “Why then are you also bound? He replied, “Tell me, where does Prajñā not see? Thereupon, the Master said:
If one perceives Prajñā, it is not called Prajñā; if one does not perceive Prajñā, it is likewise not called Prajñā.

For how can one speak of perceiving or not perceiving? Therefore, the ancients said: "If there is a lack of even a single dharma, the Dharmakāya is not realized. If there is an excess of even a single dharma, the Dharmakāya is not realized.
If there is even a single dharma, the Dharmakāya is not realized. If there is not even a single dharma, the Dharmakāya is not realized."
The Dharmakāya—this is the true essence of Prajñā. A monk asked, "Having just left the master’s chamber at Mount Ningfeng, you now sit within the Prajñā Maṇḍala.
Regarding today’s house style, I ask the Master for a single phrase. The Master said, "In what way have you been deficient?
The monk said, "If it is so, then the thunderous sound shakes the realm of heaven and earth; there is not one person who does not receive its grace. The Master said, "Fortunately..."
"But you have not yet met [the truth]. For now, do not poke your head out. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Poking your head out is not appropriate.

May all you venerable elders together bear witness so that the Dharma may endure for a long time, the land remain peaceful, and all be well. Take care. Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "I have heard it said in the teachings:
'The source of returning has no duality, yet there are many gates. What is the source of returning? The Master—

[The student] said, "You ask and I shall answer. [The student] asked, "What is the gate of skillful means? The Master said, "You answer and I shall ask. [The student] asked, "How does one proceed toward it?
The Master said, "Why do you act so perversely? [The student] asked, "One body is immeasurable bodies; immeasurable bodies are one body.
What is the immeasurable body? The Master said, "One body. [The student] said, "If that is so, then at the former Vulture Peak..."

"I have witnessed this with my own eyes today. The Master said, "The principle dictates that you should act immediately. He then said, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time all bear witness to you, Venerable One, at this very moment.
How do you understand this? If you understand it, there shall be no shifting of time; not even a hair’s breadth can be moved or altered. Why is this?
Because the past, future, and present—these three temporal limits—are you, Venerable One. And yet, you, Venerable One, are not [those three]."
The three periods of time are like rain falling upon the great ocean; every drop fills it completely. Within the emptiness of a single speck of dust, the entire Dharma-realm is fully contained.
Be careful. [The Master] ascends the hall. A monk asks: "The fourfold assembly has gathered like clouds; devas and humans pay respectful homage. With our own eyes we behold Your Honored Countenance;

we pray that You will proclaim the Prajñā. The Master says: "Take this clearly to heart. The monk says: "As the Master proclaims the wondrous Dharma, may the King live ten thousand years, and may the people enjoy peace and happiness."
The Master said, "Who told you that? [The monk] said, "It is naturally so. The Master said, "You are indeed quick-witted.

[The monk] asked, "The Buddhas of the three periods do not know it exists; the 'cat' and the 'white ox' (the lay devotees) do know it exists. Since they are the Buddhas of the three periods, why do they not know it exists?
The Master said, "In fact, it is you who know it exists. [The monk] asked, "Why [do] the cat and the white ox..."
[The monk] said, "I know there is [one who knows]. The Master asked, "Where do you see the Buddhas of the three periods?

The monk asked, "The teachings state that 'the eye does not see form-objects and the mind does not know dharmas. What is meant by 'the eye does not see form-objects'? The Master said, "It is actually the ear that sees.
The monk asked, "What is meant by 'the mind does not know dharmas'? The Master said, "It is the eye that knows. The monk said, "If that is so..."

Where seeing and hearing are cut off, yet sounds and forms are clamorous. The Master said, "Who told you that? He then replied, "As for all questions and answers, they are like the meeting of needle points;
there is not the slightest discrepancy. There is no matter that is not penetrated and no principle that is not complete.
This is truly because all speech, all samādhis—whether horizontal or vertical, deep or shallow, hidden or manifest, coming or going—are the Buddhas."
The Gate of True Reality. Simply verify it right now, at this very moment. Be careful! [Ascending the hall: An ancient said, "What is Chan?
The three realms are continuous. What is the Way? The ten directions are vast. Why does he say the three realms are continuous?
Where is the principle that the ten directions are vast? Do you wish to understand? Block your eyes; block your ears.
Stop the ears; block the tongue, body, and mind. There is no place for vacancy, and no place for movement. Elder, how do you understand this?
It cannot be grasped horizontally, nor can it be grasped vertically; it cannot be extended, nor can it be seized.

There is no place for the application of the mind, nor is there any place for contrivance. If you can understand it in this way, only then will you understand that the Dharma-gate is utterly free from discrimination. All things—
"Language is cut off from leakage. Once, a monk asked, "What is the language that is cut off from leakage?
He replied to him, "The mouth is like the nostrils. This is excellent. If you, Venerable One, understand it in this way, you will naturally not let the wind through.
If you recognize that the entirety of the ten directions of the world is the adamantine eye, there is nothing more to do; take care. [He] ascended the hall. A monk asked:
"The world is at peace. May Your Majesty live long. "How is it that you are the King? the Master asked. "The sun rises and the moon is bright," [the Emperor] replied.
"How do you understand this? the Master asked. "Who is the student? the Master said. Then he said, "The world is at peace. May Your Majesty live long.
The land is abundant and joyful, free from all calamities and hardships. These are the words of the Buddha; they have not changed in antiquity nor shifted in the present. One word is sufficient."
"By establishing the past, one establishes the present; this is how to harmonize and grasp what is excellent, O Venerable Elders. Furthermore, a monk asked, "I have heard it said in the past:

'There is a thing prior to heaven and earth; formless, it is fundamentally silent and desolate. How is it that there is a thing prior to heaven and earth? The Master said, "Neither identical nor joined.
The monk asked, "How is it that it is formless and fundamentally silent and desolate? The Master said, "Who asks about what is prior to heaven and earth? The monk said, "In that case..."
[The monk said: "In that case, one goes alone to wander through the quiet forests. The Master said, "Why do you speak so recklessly? He then said, "The Buddha-dharma is not a matter such as this.
Do you wish to understand? When words are uttered, they are no sound; before form, there is no object. Only then will you understand:
'All under heaven is at peace; may the Great King live long. [He stood for a long time; take care of yourself. Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddha-dharma is already accomplished."
Everything is fully complete. Have you not seen it? The Way is as perfect as the great void; there is nothing lacking and nothing in excess.
If this is so, then who is lacking and who has a surplus? Who is right and who is wrong? Who is one who understands and who is one who does not understand?
Therefore it is said: "Going east is also the Seat-Holder; going west is also the Seat-Holder; going south is also the Seat-Holder; going north is also the Seat-Holder."
This is also the Elder. For what reason does he become east, west, south, and north?

If you can understand this spontaneously, the paths of seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are cut off, and all dharmas manifest before you. Why is this so? Because the Dharmakāya is formless, yet forms appear before every eye;
Prajñā is without cognition, yet it reflects in response to conditions. You must grasp this thoroughly and all at once. All Elders—
"Seated. How should one who has left the household life act? This is the principle inherent from the beginning; it is not something extraordinary.
To recognize the mind and reach the source is why one is called a śramaṇa. If you recognize the mind as luminously clear, there is truly not a hair’s breadth of obstruction."
"Please stand for a long time; take care. [The Master] ascends the hall. A monk asks, "One who wishes to enter the ocean of non-action must first board the Prajñā boat.
What is the Prajñā boat? The Master says, "Always dwelling nowhere. [The monk] asks, "What is the ocean of non-action? The Master says:
Furthermore, he boarded the Prajñā boat and questioned the ancient masters: "Ascending to heaven without borrowing a ladder; throughout the earth there is no path to walk upon.
What is 'ascending to heaven without borrowing a ladder'? The Master said, "Not leaving behind even a thread or a hair’s breadth.
He asked, "What is 'throughout the earth there is no path to walk upon'? The Master said, "What did I just tell you? Then he said: "The hundreds of thousands of gates of samādhi..."
The thousand gates of spiritual powers and the hundred-thousand gates of wondrous functions do not, in their entirety, transcend the ocean of *prajñā*. Why is this?
Because all phenomena are established upon the ground of non-abiding. Thus it is said: "Arising and ceasing, coming and going, the heterodox and the orthodox, movement and stillness."
A thousand transformations and myriad changes—this is the great samādhi gate of all Buddhas; nothing surpasses it.

May all you venerable elders investigate this thoroughly, thereby increasing the life-span of the Buddha-dharma. Take care! [Ascending the hall: A monk asked, "The World-Honored One, with the Eye of the True Dharma..."
[The Master] entrusted [the Dharma] to Mahākāśyapa. As for Kāśyapa, while he was in the Piṇḍola Cave, it is not yet known to whom he entrusted it.
The Teacher said, "Who would I have taught to speak it? [The other] said, "If that is so, then the entrustment at Vulture Peak is no different from today."

The Master said, "Where did you see Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa? [The monk] asked, "Regarding the 'Precious Seal' (Bao Yin) personally transmitted by Master Fayan—unfortunately, I do not know who it shall be entrusted to today.
The Master said, "The drum beats *dong dong*; struck at one end, it resonates at both ends.

[The monk] said, "If that is so, then the thousand sages are of one kindred, and past and present are no different. The Master said, "The waves of the Chan-river are calm; seeking the water, one loses the source. The monk [departed].
Qingyu asked, "The Emperor has requested your life; you have come to fulfill the King’s grace. Within this Prajñā assembly, we request that you preach. The Master said, "Take this clearly to heart.
Qingyu said, "If it is so, then the jeweled nets of the Cloud Terrace shall together proclaim the wondrous sound.
The Master said, "Where is Qingyu? Qingyu said, "The Dharma of the Dharma King is thus. The Master said, "Who will bear witness? He then said, "At Vulture Peak, [the teaching] was entrusted..."
The entrustment is clear. Let all the senior elders examine it at once. If you can verify it, there is no other principle;
it is simply as it is now. It is like the great void: when the sun is bright and the clouds dark, the mountains, rivers, the great earth, and all conditioned worlds appear clearly;
even the unconditioned is likewise so. The World-Honored One’s entrustment has continued down to the present day, and remains entirely...
There is not the slightest difference. To whom else could it be entrusted? Therefore, the Patriarch said: "The mind is the original mind;
the original mind is not a dharma. If there were dharmas, there would be an original mind; but since it is neither mind nor dharma, it is the fundamental Dharma.
This is the model for the entrustment at Vulture Peak. All you venerable seniors, understand this thoroughly! Do not let your time pass in vain. O King, your kindness is difficult to repay.
The kindness of the Buddhas is difficult to repay; the kindness of parents and teachers is difficult to repay; the kindness of donors throughout the ten directions is difficult to repay.
How much more so is this establishment of the successive stages through which the Buddha-Dharma flourishes! Were it not for the power and grace of the king, how could such a thing have been achieved?

If you wish to repay his kindness, you must clarify the eye of the Way and enter the ocean-nature of Prajñā; only then will it be attained. [This concludes] the "Precious Admonition for Long-Stationed [Students].
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "An ancient worthy said, 'The person is empty and dharmas are also empty; these two aspects are fundamentally the same. What do you say to this? The Master said:
"Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. The monk said: "I do not understand. I beg the Master for an expedient means. The Master said: "Where would it not be?"

This is a skillful means. [The student] asks about the provisional nature of names and the provisional nature of phenomena, the emptiness of persons and the emptiness of dharmas, and turning away from all conditions, requests that the Master point directly.
The Master says, "Thank you for this question. [The student] says, "If one does not behold the majesty of the royal palace, how can one know the dignity of the Son of Heaven?
The Master says, "In greedily gazing at the moon in the sky, you have lost the oar in your hand. [The student] asks, "The teaching says: 'Because the mind is pure, the dharma-realm is pure.'"
[Pu'an asked: "Regarding purity, what is the pure mind? The Master said: "The kalaviṅka bird and the saṃjīvaka bird. [He] asked: "Are they one with the dharma-realm, or are they two?
The Master said: "You should ask this of others yourself. Then [the Master] said: "The Great Way is vast and open;
how could it be confined by past or present? It is nameless and formless. As for 'dharma' and 'cultivation,' it is simply because the dharma-realm is boundless and the mind is likewise limitless."
There is no matter that is not manifest; there is no word that is not revealed. To realize it in this way is called the manifestation of *prajñā*.

Its principle is identical to the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*): all mountains, rivers, and the great earth, the myriad phenomena of the forest and the heavens, walls, tiles, and pebbles—none of these possess even a hair’s breadth of deficiency or lack.
Having stood for a long time without cause, take care. [Ascending the hall: A monk asked, "I have heard the Master say, 'Nine..."
The Celestial One holds the Jade Seal; it is the precursor to the minds of the Seven Buddhas. "What is this seal? the master said, "It reveals no characters.
"What is this mind? the master said, "Your name is An-si. He then continued: "The nature-sea of the Dharma-realm is like a box and its lid, like a hook and its chain, like gold meeting gold.
In every position they are perfectly equal, without the slightest discrepancy, never becoming confused or intermingled."
Neither one nor different; neither the same nor distinct. If one returns to the ground of reality, every dharma reaches its ultimate limit.
This is not a matter of asking "how" or "what" as has been done above; it is precisely when there is no questioning, and it is not being upon the long bedsteads [of the monastic hall].
"It exists when sitting; it does not exist when not sitting. Yet, the teachings of the venerable masters throughout all quarters remain in the world like the sands of the Ganges River;
every scroll of the Tathāgata’s Great Canon expounds the Buddha-principle, and every sentence speaks of the Buddha-mind.

Why is it that you still do not understand? If you merely weave together these teachings and seek understanding through the conscious intellect, even if you were to do so for a hundred thousand eons...
Even if an Elder (Sthavira) were to spend kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, he still could not reach its bottom. This is called inverted knowledge and view;
it is the calculating mind of consciousness, which has no place where it can find strength. This is because the foundation of one's roots is not clear.

If one thoroughly investigates the source of all Buddhas' Dharma, the great treasuries as numerous as the sands of the Ganges will all appear before one at once—neither lacking even a hair’s breadth, nor exceeding it by even a hair’s breadth. All Buddhas...
At all times, throughout the world and beyond the world, he has constantly preached the Dharma to deliver sentient beings without ever ceasing.

Even down to the cries of monkeys and the calls of birds, the grasses, trees, and forests always assist the Elder in triggering his realization; there has not been a single moment when they did not do so for him.
The Elder possesses such extraordinary qualities—how truly precious he is! May all you Elders investigate this thoroughly, so that the Dharma may long abide in the world.
May the lifespans of humans and devas increase; may the kings of nations enjoy peace and happiness; may all be free from calamity—farewell.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] cited the ancients who said: "I have a single word. Throughout the world and among humanity, if people do not understand it, there are only green waters and blue mountains.
But how is this? What is the principle of this "single word"? The words of the ancients must be understood with penetrating insight before they can be grasped. If one merely takes these words...
Yet regarding names, there is no place of understanding within words. It is only by thoroughly investigating the very root of all phenomena that one begins to understand;
a single word is not merely a single word or half-sentence. To attempt to understand through calculation and intellectual interpretation is what is called "a single word.

If you understand that the path of speech is cut off and the sphere of mental activity ceases, only then do you reach the realm of the ancients. Furthermore, this is not like closing one's eyes and hiding one's sight in the dark.
To call that which is without anything seen "the severance of the path of words" is, for now, a deceptive understanding. The Buddha-dharma is not this principle.
Do you wish to understand? Even if one were to speak for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, not even half a phrase would ever reach you, venerable elders.
Yet, even if one did not speak for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, not even half a phrase would ever be lacking. You must understand it thoroughly to the very bottom.
Only then can it be attained. If one deliberates upon names and words in this manner, it will merely exhaust one’s mind and strength to no avail.

Let this be mutually verified with all the senior monks; those of later generations and beginners must quickly investigate and grasp this. I shall remain standing for a long time; take care. [Ascending the hall.]
A monk asked, "The skull constantly dries the world; the nostrils touch the family style. What is 'the skull constantly drying the world'?
The Master said, "Wait until I have answered your question. [The monk] asked, "What is 'the nostrils touching the family style'?"
The Master said, "I shall raise this question once more. He asked one person: "One man holds a torch and burns his own body; another man embraces an ice block and lies across a corpse on the road.
Of these two people, which one has realized the Way? The Master said, "He who does not abandon [the path]. [The student] said, "I do not understand. I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master said, "Your name is Jingxin (Venerable New). [The student] said, "I wonder, is there anyone else who can bear witness to this? The Master said, "There is."
[The student] said, "Who can testify to this? The Master said, "Jingxin. [The student] asked, "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?

The Master said, "A wondrous landscape and a sacred trace; all who behold them are filled with admiration. [The student] asked, "And what was it like after he saw him? The Master said, "What did I just tell you? [The student] asked, "An ancient said:
'Striking the void, the *gǔgǔ* resounds. The stone man and the wooden... [The Master continued: "...the wooden man... (The text here is incomplete).
The assembly responded in unison. "In the sixth month, snow falls in profusion. This is the Tathāgata’s Great Perfect Enlightenment.
What is it that strikes at empty space? The Master said: "A slave from Mount Kunlun, wearing iron trousers; with every stroke of the staff, he takes a step."

Someone asked, "What do you mean by the emptiness of phenomena (*dharmasūnyatā*)? The Master replied, "It is not empty. He then showed the assembly with this verse: Autumn river, misty islands, clear skies; Gulls and egrets stand in rows.
If one does not call upon Avalokiteśvara, How can one know the entry through the Universal Gate?
Chan Master Shoune of Shanglan Monastery in Hongzhou ascended the hall. He fully took up the essential principles: "No one sweeps the ground;

let the brothers of the monastic community together provide witness. Those among the later generations who have doubts, please ask your questions. A monk asked, "I pray you open the gate of ambrosia and contemplate the primary truth.
Without falling into the extremes of existence or non-existence, I beg the Master to grant us instruction. The Master said, "Great..."
The assembly requested proof. [A monk] said, "If that is so, then do not humiliate us. The Master said, "Idle talk.
[Another] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Ask someone else."
A monk asked Master Fuchuan of Fuzhou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "I do not know.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Do not slander the Patriarch."
At Fǎngxiān Monastery in Hángzhōu, Zen Master Pǔzhào Fǎguī and Fǎmíng were asked by a monk:

"When Śākyamuni appeared in the world, the heavens rained four kinds of flowers and the earth shook in six ways. I wonder, what auspicious signs are there today? The Master said: "The entire assembly sees them. The monk said:
"The Dharma-King’s Dharma is thus. The Master said: "The Human-King is present now. [Question: Regarding the Precious Seal of the Fǎyǎn lineage... and so forth.
"Shangqin’s oral transmission—this assembly today—should be entrusted to whom? The Master said, "Who would not have their share?
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then the thunderous sound will universally shake infinite lands. The Master said, "You must listen well."
Chan Master Huilang of Huacheng Temple on Mount Lu was invited by Song Qichu, the Chancellor of Jiangnan, to ascend the Dharma seat.

The Master ascended the seat and said: "Today, the Lord Chancellor has requested this mountain monk to serve the assembly. Is this not to uphold the Buddha’s entrustment and never forget the Buddha’s kindness?
If there is anyone among you who wishes to pose a question, please come forward to create karmic affinity for the Lord Chancellor. A monk asked: "The Lord Chancellor personally..."
[The Master] descended. The great assembly gathered like clouds. They requested the Master to proclaim the ancestral vehicle of the patriarchs.

The Master said, "Is this not to be a betrayal of the Duke? A monk asked, "The Master constantly rebukes us with bitter words; why is it that we students do not clarify our own fundamental matter? The Master said, "Where, Ācārya, is it not clear?
The monk said, "I pray the Master provide a definitive judgment regarding the point where it is not clear. The Master said, "Just now, I told you."
“What do you say? [The monk] said, “In that case, it is entirely due to today. The Master said, “Step back and pay three prostrations.
Chan Master Daohong Tongbian of Huiriji Yongming Temple in Hangzhou ascended the hall.

A monk asked, “Having traveled far from the realm of Tiantai, I have come to ascend the peak of Huiriji. I have long heard of the lion’s roar; today I ask the Master to explain it. The Master said, “I hear.”
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then Chongshou of the past is Yongming of today. The Master said, "Fortunately, you are naturally quick-witted; why must you speak so confusedly? He then said:
"The Great Way is vast and open, eternally as it has been from antiquity to the present. The true mind is all-pervasive, and the wisdom that accords with reality is brilliantly clear.
The myriad phenomena and the ten thousand forms are all truly real aspects; encompassing heaven and containing earth, they extend through all eternity."
“Will the great assembly return? Will they be able to provide a clear explanation? A monk asked, “The King has issued a gracious command, and a noble official presides over this assembly.
May I ask what matter is to be addressed today? The Master said, “Find out for yourself. The monk asked, “What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, “Where have you come from? The monk said, “If that is so, then it would be a hasty conclusion. The Master said, “Stop speaking nonsense.”
A monk asked Zen Master Lingjian of Goryeo, “What is a pure monastery? The Master said, “The cowshed and the stable.
The monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Drag out that madman!”

A monk asked Master Shangquan of Jingmen, "When two dragons contend for the pearl, who is the one that obtains it? The Master said, "I obtain it. The monk asked, "From afar I have come to seek you, Master;
how do you receive me? The Master leaned his staff against him and gazed at him; the monk bowed, and the Master then gave a shout.
A monk asked, "What is it like when a foot-long jade disc is flawless? The Master said, "I do not value it. The monk asked, "After it is no longer valued..."
"How is it? The Master said, "A cricket flies up into the sky amidst the flames.
When Chan Master Dun, a monk of Dailin Temple on Mount Lu, was first residing at Yuan Tong, a monk cited this: A monk asked Xuansha—

"Regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school (*zōngchéng*), how can one discuss it here? Xuansha said, "Few people listen. [The monk] asked, "I do not yet understand the meaning of Xuansha’s intent.
The Master said, "Wait until you have moved Stone Ear Peak, and I shall speak to you. (Niu Ruozong of Guizong said, "Speak in a low voice.")
A monk asked Zen Master Yuansheng of Renwang Monastery in Chizhou, “When farmers are beating the *rang* (earthen clods), what is it like?

The Master said, “The monastic community has its own fundamental duty. The monk said, “I am not asking about the monastic community’s fundamental duty; when farmers are beating the *rang*, what is it like?
The Master said, “Where is the pivot of the question?”
