The Chan Master Huiji Yongming Yanshou Zhijue of Hangzhou,
a descendant of the tenth generation under Nanyue and a successor of National Teacher Tiantai Shaokang, was a native of the Wang family of Yuhang. From his early childhood...

In his youth, he turned his heart toward the Buddha Vehicle. Once he had reached the age of majority, he abstained from meat and took but one meal per day. He upheld the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, reciting seven lines at once;

in barely sixty days, he was able to recite it entirely. He moved the hearts of flocks of sheep, who knelt to listen to him. At the age of twenty-eight, he served as the military commander of Huating.
It happened that Chan Master Ciyun Shouzhen was residing at Longce Temple, where he was extensively propagating the profound transformation of the Dharma. At that time, the King of Wuyue...

King Mu, recognizing that his teacher yearned for the Way, granted him his wish. He subsequently received Cuiyan as his master and attended to the community with diligent labor, completely forgetting his royal status.
His garments were not of silk or flossed cotton, and his food lacked rich flavors; he sustained himself morning and evening with wild vegetables and coarse cloth tunics.

He then traveled to Tiantai Mountain, to the Peak of the Celestial Pillar, where he practiced meditative concentration for ninety days. There was a bird, similar to a quail, that nested within the folds of his robes.

Later, upon meeting National Teacher Yao, he was deeply esteemed by him at first sight; the Master secretly transmitted to him the fundamental principle. Furthermore, the National Teacher said to him, "You have a karmic affinity with the Yuan-shuai;
in the future, you shall greatly propagate the Buddhist teachings. He first resided at Xuedou. Entering the hall, he ascended the seat and said: "Xue..."
At this place, Xuedou, a torrential waterfall plunges a thousand fathoms without pausing for even a grain of dust; wondrous cliffs rise ten thousand cubits with no place to set foot.
You people of the assembly—where do you take your next step? A monk asked, "How does one tread upon the single path of Xuedou? The Master said, "Step by step, frosty flowers form;
word by word, the very depths are ice. The Master had a verse that says: "A lone monkey cries out, causing the moon to fall..."
The moon over the central crags; a rustic guest chants by the dying lamp at midnight. Who finds the true meaning in this scene and at this moment?
A monk sitting in meditation deep within the white clouds. King Zhongyi invited [Zhili] to open the new Lingyin Monastery.

The following year, he moved to the Yongming Doctrinal Center, where the assembly numbered more than two thousand. A monk asked, "What is the wondrous principle of Yongming? The Master said, "Add more incense."
The monk bowed. The Master said, "I am glad there is no connection. The monk prostrated. The Master said, "Listen to this verse:
'If you wish to know the meaning of Yongming, there is a lake before the gate. When the sun shines, radiance arises; when the wind comes, waves stir.
[The monk] asked, "A student has long been at Yongming; why is it that he does not understand the house style of Yongming? The Master—
[The student] said, "I understand at the point where there is no understanding. [The Master] asked, "How do you understand at the point where there is no understanding?
The Master said, "An elephant calf born from the womb of an ox; red dust rising from the azure sea. [The student] asked, "One cannot escape even becoming a Buddha or an Ancestor;
one cannot escape the saṃsāra of the six realms. I wonder, from what place can one not escape? The Master said, "One cannot escape from the very place of your question."
Question: Regarding the teaching on the Middle Way, it is said that all Buddhas and all Buddha-dharmas emerge from this sutra.
What is this sutra? The Master said: "It revolves continuously for a long time; it is neither meaning nor sound. Question: How should one receive and uphold it? The Master said:
"If you wish to receive and uphold it, you must listen with eyes wide open. Question: What is the Great Perfect Mirror? The Master said: [The text here ends abruptly.]
It is said: "Breaking the Sand Pot. The Master resided at Yongming for fifteen years, ordaining one thousand seven hundred disciples.
In the *jiashu* year of the Kaibao era of Emperor Taizu of the Song dynasty, he entered Mount Tiantai, where he conferred the precepts upon approximately ten thousand people.

He constantly bestowed the Bodhisattva precepts upon the seven assemblies. At night, he offered food to ghosts and spirits; in the morning, he released various living creatures—beyond all calculation. (6)
At that time, he scattered flowers along his path. With his remaining strength, he recited the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* approximately thirteen thousand times.
He composed the *Zongjing lu* (Record of the Mirror of the Source) in one hundred fascicles. His poems, verses, and rhapsodies totaled several million words, which were disseminated beyond the seas.

Upon reading the Master’s teachings, the King of Goryeo dispatched an envoy bearing a letter to express the etiquette of a disciple and presented him with a robe woven from gold thread and purple silk.

There were crystal beads, a golden water-pitcher, and other items. Thirty-six monks from that country, all bearing his seal of authorization, returned to their own land in succession, each transforming the people of their respective regions.
On the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month of the year Yihai of the Kai-bao era, he manifested illness.
Two days later, he burned incense, addressed the assembly, sat in the full lotus posture, and passed away peacefully. He was seventy-two years of age and forty-two years since his ordination.
His stupa was enshrined at Mount Daci. In the *Gengxu* year of the Ming Wanli era, it was moved to the rear of the Zongjing Hall on Mount Nanping.
Chan Master Pengyan Guangfa of Changshou Monastery in Suzhou was the son of the Qin family of Yongjia.
A monk asked, "What is the primordial principle? The Master said, "The four corners are pressed flat to the ground. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma that is beyond even a hair's breadth?
The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. The monk said, "In that case, one perceives phenomena while being without phenomena. The Master said, "That too is madness."
[The Master] said: "Question: What is direct speech? The Master said: "A thousand detours and ten thousand windings. [The student] said: "In that case, then nothing is not total?
The Master said: "What kind of words are those? [The student] asked: "What is the Way? The Master said: "The journey is not easy.
In the *Xinyou* year of the Jianlong era of Emperor Taizu of the Song dynasty, he entrusted the abbacy to his disciple Faqi. (4)
On the sixth day of the month, he demonstrated the extinction of his life; his lifespan was forty-nine years, and his dharma age was thirty-five.
A monk asked Chan Master Kehong of Daining Monastery in Wenzhou, "What is the single path of true reality? The Master said:

[The student] said, "Seven topsy-turvy, eight upside-down. [The Master] said, "If that is so, then there would be no distinction among the Dharma gates. The Master said, "I know you have misunderstood.
[The student] asked, "When it is bright and clear without a single thread of hair, what then? The Master said, "The head of the talk has already fallen."

[The monk] said, "I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "What was just now was not established in vain. [The monk] asked, "Regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school, I request the Master to proclaim it.
The Master said, "Your question is far too late. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then I shall not go as a *śrāmaṇera* [novice].
The Master said, "I know well that you will go in such a manner."
Chan Master Zhifeng of Huayan Monastery on Wuyun Mountain in Hangzhou was a native of Yuhang. From birth, he loathed meat and blood; his skin and body were fragrant and pure.
In his youth, he left the household life at Langzhan Monastery on East Mountain in Lin’an and received full ordination according to the prescribed age.

He mastered the three studies and thoroughly comprehended both the nature (xìng) and characteristics (xiàng) of reality. Once, he dreamed of ascending Mount Sumeru, where he beheld three Buddhas seated in a row. At first, he...
Kāśyapa and Maitreya both prostrated at his feet, but he did not recognize the third honored one, merely gazing upward at him.
Śākyamuni Buddha said to him, "This is the one who will succeed you as Maitreya; he is the Buddha Siṃhacandra. Only then did the Master prostrate himself.
Later, while perusing the Tripitaka, he found that it accorded with his dream. Subsequently, during the Tianfu era of the Jin dynasty, he traveled abroad and arrived at Tiantai Yunmen.
He resided there and served as National Preceptor. Through the karmic conditions of the master-disciple relationship, profound mysteries were suddenly awakened.

One day, he entered the Hall of Samantabhadra to sit in meditative repose. Suddenly, a divine being appeared, kneeling before him. The Master asked, "Who are you? He replied, "I am a deity who protects the precepts.
The Master said, "I have a burden of past transgressions that I have not yet extinguished; do you know of this? He replied, "What sins does the Master have? Only..."
"It was merely a minor transgression," he said. The Master asked, "Why? He replied, "In general, even the water used for rinsing a bowl is the property of a donor.
It is not appropriate for you, Master, to habitually pour it away. Having finished speaking, he vanished. From that time on, the Master drank all the water used for washing his bowl.

After a long period, this caused him to develop a spleen ailment, which only healed after ten years. (Whenever one discards food, drink, saliva, mucus, or excrement, one should snap the fingers, silently recite a mantra, and cultivate a mind of giving before pouring it away.)

The King of Wu-Yue, admiring the Master’s spiritual influence, summoned him to bestow upon him purple robes and appointed him as Chan Master Pujue, commanding him to reside at Gongchen Monastery in Lin’an.

Ascending the hall, he addressed the assembly: "Distinguished elders, you all abandon one teacher to seek another, following entirely the example of Sudhana’s journey to the south. But let me ask you, elders: when Sudhana took his leave of Mañjuśrī..."
I intended to ascend Mount Miaofeng to pay my respects to the Bhikṣu Dechen. Yet, upon arriving at that place, why was it that Dechen met me on a separate peak?

The intent of the Teachings and the intent of the Patriarchs are one and the same expedient means; ultimately, there is no separate principle. If he had understood this clearly, [he would not have acted thus].
This is also perfectly clear. All you elders, you who are now gathered around this old monk—do you see me or not?
Is this place Mount Miaofeng or another peak? If you can depart from here with this understanding, you may be said not to have disappointed this old monk;
you will constantly see the Bhikṣu Deyun, never for a single moment separated from him. Do you believe this yet?
A monk asked, "The monastic communities raise their voices to provide for the needs of the present age. What is the true intent of the meritorious official? The Master said, "Do you see?
The monk said, "If that is so, then the entire assembly rejoices. The Master said, "I take it you are a lion cub.
A monk asked, "Buddha after Buddha hands over the hand; patriarch after patriarch transmits the mind. I wonder, Master, what is it that you transmit? The Master said, "You have received it."
"Can one attain it? He replied, "I, this student, cannot take it upon myself. [The Master asked,] "Is there anyone else who can take it upon themselves?
The Master said, "The assembly will laugh at you. A monk asked, "What is the Tathāgatagarbha? The Master said, "You have just asked.
A monk asked, "What is the pivot of all Buddhas? The Master said, "Can you say it? He ascended the hall. After a long silence, he said, "The assembly, look!"
"Look! he said, and then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, the Master said: "The ancient worthies traveled on foot for the sake of the Dharma, undaunted by toil and hardship.
Take Xuefeng, for instance: he went to Touzi three times and visited Dongshan nine times; though he lingered and traveled back and forth, he still could not find a way of entry.
Look at you people who study these days: as soon as you step through the gate, you demand that this old monk lead you in and point out the Way, telling you to speak of Zen."
Furthermore, you who wish to cultivate the Way of the Ultimate Source—how could this be treated as something casual?

Moreover, this matter has its own proper timing; how can it be attained through restless seeking? Do you wish to know when the moment of awakening arrives? For now, each of you should go down and sit in stillness within the hall.
Wait until Mount Yangjia nods its head, and the old monk will then explain it for you. At that time, a monk stepped forward and said, "Mount Yang..."
Jiafeng nodded his head and said, "I also ask the Master to explain. The Master said, "Tell me, everyone: does this monk understand my words, or does he not? The monk bowed.
The Master said, "Today, by chance, I have failed in discernment.

He asked, "Why is it that for one who is unconditioned and without affairs, there is still the 'difficulty of the golden lock'? The monk had no reply. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "It is precisely because of non-existence."
To eliminate all affairs, he asked about the Middle Way of the Teachings. Suddenly, Mañjuśrī gave rise to the view of a Buddha and the view of the Dharma;
seized by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, he was led toward the two Iron Ring Mountains. What is the underlying meaning? The Master said: "Where are the two Iron Ring Mountains?"
The monk remained silent. The Master said, "Do you understand? If anyone today were to give rise to a view regarding the Buddha-dharma, I would brew two cups of tea for them.
Now tell me: is this a reward or a punishment? Is it in accord with the intent of the teaching or not?
In the *Xinwei* year of the Kaibao era of Emperor Taizu of Song, the general Ling Chao founded a monastery on Mount Wuyun and invited the Master to spend his final years there.
The Master would often carry a large fan while begging for money to buy meat to feed the tigers; the tigers would always come to meet him and carry him back to the mountain.
He passed away in the Yixi year of Emperor Taizong’s reign (985). His stupa was erected at the monastery; he was seventy-seven years of age and fifty-eight years since his ordination.
The stupa was named "Ever-Shining Jewel Peak" (Bǎofēng Chángzhào).

Chan Master Fadu Huiyue of Ba’en Temple in Hangzhou ascended the hall and said: "For several nights past, I have engaged in various conversations with you venerable seniors, yet we have not yet exhausted the source.
Today, for the sake of you venerable seniors, I shall employ great skillful means to explain it all at once.
Will you take pleasure in this? Please remain standing for a long while; I bid you farewell. A monk asked: "As a student, I have come here in this manner; I request—"
The Master reached out to receive him. The Master said, "I do not receive you. The monk asked, "Why do you not receive me? The Master replied, "Because you are too clever and sharp.
Chan Master Shaoyuan Tongbian Mingda of Ba’en Temple in Hangzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The assembly is listening intently."
"Please do not be sparing with your instruction," [the student] requested. The Master said, "How strange! [The student] said, "If that is so, then today I have met the Master.
The Master said, "What words are these? He then said, "One phrase returns to the truth; it remains indestructible for ten thousand kalpas. Today, for the sake of you all, I shall utter one phrase.
After a long silence, he said, "Take this clearly to heart," and then descended from his seat. [On another occasion,] he ascended the hall and said, "Fortunately, there is a tower."
The platform encircles the earth. Constantly upholding the ancestral seal, it is not beyond the reach of the various elders to investigate and take it up.
Standing for a long time, I bid you all adieu with care. A monk asked, "What is the master’s house style? The Master said, "It is already accomplished everywhere.
The monk said, "In that case, it spans from antiquity to the present. The Master said, "Do not engage in idle talk."

Chan Master Shouwei Zongyi of Guangping Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of that province. Having attended upon the National Teacher (Guishan Lingyou) and attained his realization, he was subsequently entrusted with the robe and the Dharma.
At that time, a monk asked: "At the head of Dayu Ridge, it could not be lifted; how is it that today you entrust it to the Master?
The Master lifted it up and said, "Is there anyone who dares say that Tiantai obtained it? He ascended the hall [to preach]. "The Great Master Bodhidharma..."
[The Master] said: "My Dharma shall not shift by so much as a hair’s breadth three thousand years hence. Today, this mountain monk likewise does not shift a hair’s breadth from Bodhidharma.
Those who have already attained shall together provide mutual verification; those who have not yet attained shall likewise not shift a hair’s breadth. A monk asked:

"The resonance of the great bell has ceased, and the assembly is gathered before you. The Patriarchal intent has come from the West—please, Master, proclaim it for us. The Master said: "The resonance of the great bell..."
[The Master] cut him off. As the assembly was seated at the table, someone asked: "An ancient said, 'Let a thousand sages see you;
I have the Buddha of True Nature. What is the Buddha of True Nature? The Master said, "A thousand sages. [Another] asked, "What is the family style of Guangping?"
The Master said: "Who does not enjoy [this]? Ascending the hall, he said: "There is no need to open the sutras or chant the Sanskrit;

there is no need to spread out the commentaries or arrange the sections. Is there any place for theoretical reasoning? Even if there were a place for theoretical reasoning, it would still be merely expedient talk.
As for the matter of the School of the Patriarchs (Zongcheng), how should one act? A monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said: "No one has ever [attained it]."
[The student] replied, "I have attained it. [The Master] said, "Please request a skillful means from the Teacher. The Master asked, "Why do you not ask further?
Chan Master Yong’an of Bào’ēn Temple in Hángzhōu was the son of the Wēng family of Wēnzhōu. In his youth, he relied upon Huìzhēng of his home prefecture to leave the household life.
During the Tiānchéng era of the Later Táng dynasty, he followed his preceptor into the kingdom. Emperor Zhōngyì appointed Zhēng as the Sangha Rectifier (Sēngzhèng). As for the Master...

He particularly took no pleasure in worldly affairs and intended to travel secretly to Minchuan to seek out a Zen assembly; however, as the roads were difficult and obstructed, he returned to Mount Tiantai to build a thatched hut.
There he soon encountered the National Teacher, who gave him instruction, leading to his sudden awakening to his original mind. He then took his leave and departed the mountains.

The Emperor was informed of this, and the Emperor commanded him to reside at Qingtai Monastery in Yuezhou. Subsequently, he summoned him to dwell at Shangsi Monastery and appointed him as Chan Master Zhengjue Konghui.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas of the ten directions have gathered like clouds all at once, together with all you venerable elders, to bear witness."
"The various elders have simultaneously witnessed this with the Buddha. Do you still believe it? You must strictly avoid intellectual speculation.

"At Longhua, here, it is merely a matter of gathering firewood and selecting vegetables; coming and going, a single gruel in the morning and a single meal at noon; drinking tea after sleep. Simply this."
"Investigate in this manner. Take care. A student asked, "I have not yet clarified my own self. How can I distinguish between shallow and deep?
The Master said, "Recognize the eye of your own self. The student asked, "What is the eye of one's own self? The Master said, "What did I say to you?"
Chan Master Yu Zhen of Qiyun Mountain in Wuzhou was the son of the Yang family of Yue Province.
A monk asked, "What is the seamless stupa? The Master said, "Five or six feet. The monk bowed; the Master said, "The stupa has collapsed.

A monk asked, "Regarding 'perfectly clear awareness,' why does it not depend on mental thought? The Master said, "Perfectly clear awareness. The monk asked, "How is this different from mental thought?"
The Master said: "What do you call 'mental activity'? While sitting idly on an autumn evening, he composed a verse:

"The autumn courtyard is solemn, the wind whistles; Cold stars are arrayed in the sky, the moon’s orb is high. Resting my chin, I sit in stillness, my spirit unwearied; From the bird's nest, without cause, feathers are blown forth.
He passed away at Dashiensi Temple while in the midst of his ultimate realization.
Chan Master Benchuan of Rui鹿 Temple in Wenzhou was the son of the Zheng family of that same prefecture.

He visited Tiantai, where he was guided by the words, "It is not the wind or the banner that moves; it is the mind of the wise man that moves. At that moment, the Master attained awakening and understanding. Later, while presiding over the assembly, he said:

"When I first studied the Dharma-gate of Tiantai, I realized it immediately upon hearing the words. Nevertheless, for a thousand days thereafter, throughout my four modes of conduct, I remained like an object."

There was something obstructing his chest, as if he were harboring a grievance against someone occupying the same space. After a thousand days, within a single day, that obstruction vanished from his chest;

the grievance was no longer shared with another, and he experienced immediate peace and joy. He suddenly realized his former faults and composed three verses. The first, titled "It Is Not the Wind or the Banner That Move, But the Mind of the Wise Man Moves," states:
"It is not the wind or the banner that move, But only the mind that moves. This has been transmitted from antiquity down to the present. Now...
Later, when the "water-and-cloud" man was about to dawn [to understanding], the Patriarch truly was a connoisseur of sound. Second, regarding "seeing form is seeing mind," it is said:

"If seeing form were seeing mind, when someone came to question you, you would find it difficult to answer; you would further seek out various principles and explanations, thereby betraying the three matters of your lifelong practice as a monk.
Third, regarding "knowing oneself," it is said: "Throughout vast kalpas, it has always been just like this."
Thus he was one with heaven and one with earth. Being one with earth and one with heaven, what form could there be? What differentiated forms were not [manifested] within him?
From that time on, the Master’s feet never trod upon city gates, his hands never handled wealth or goods. He did not provide bedding or furnishings, nor did he wear silk or flossed silk.
He ate but a single meal a day and remained in meditative seclusion throughout the entire day. From dawn until dusk, he exhorted and guided others for over thirty years; such was his resolve.
Mili ascended the hall and said: "Do you all see the bamboo groves, the hermitage, the mountains, the waters, the monastic quarters, and the assembly?
If you say you see them, then there are phenomena outside the mind.

If you say you do not see them, how can it be that the bamboo groves, the hermitage, the mountains, the waters, the monastic quarters, and the assembly are all vividly present right here? Do you understand? If you understand, you will be remarkably sharp."

"Do not stand idly by. [The Master] ascends the hall. Generally speaking, regarding the study of the Way: it is not necessarily the case that studying "talking about the matter" (*huà*) constitutes the study of the Way;

it is not necessarily the case that studying "discriminating the matter" constitutes the study of the Way; it is not necessarily the case that studying "substituting words" constitutes the study of the Way;

it is not necessarily the case that studying "alternative words" constitutes the study of the Way; it is not necessarily the case that studying the "extraordinary phrases" found within the sutras and treatises constitutes the study of the Way. It is not necessarily...
To pick apart and tear asunder the extraordinary words of the Patriarchs is the way of study.

If you engage in such study, no matter how thoroughly you may master the seven penetrations and eight accomplishments, if you lack a point of realization within the Buddha-dharma, you are called a follower of dry wisdom (*śuṣka-prajñā*).
Have you not heard the ancient masters say: "Cleverness cannot withstand birth and death; those of dry wisdom cannot escape the wheel of suffering"? If you people...
Regarding study: one must engage in authentic study before it can be attained. When walking, take up the inquiry while walking; when standing, take up the inquiry while standing;
when sitting, take up the inquiry while sitting; when sleeping, take up the inquiry while sleeping; and when speaking, take up the inquiry while speaking.
When silent, take it up in silence. When engaged in all manner of tasks, take it up during all those tasks. Since you are taking it up at such times as these, tell me:
whom are you taking up? What phrase are you taking up? At this point, you must reach a state of personal clarity;
if you do not, you are merely called a person of hasty and superficial practice, and that will not do.
The Essential Meaning of Thorough Investigation. [Ascending the hall: "In the secluded forest, birds cry out; in the azure stream, fish leap. Clouds unfurl like scrolls;
waterfalls murmur with plaintive sounds. Do you all recognize such manifold scenes? Shall I show you an entrance?"
If you can understand this, it will not hinder your practice; you should take it up for study. Entering the hall, [the Master said]:
"In the teachings of Tiantai, the three gates of Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, and Samantabhadra are explained. The gate of Mañjuśrī is all forms; the gate of Avalokiteśvara is all sounds;
the gate of Samantabhadra is to arrive without moving a step. I say that the gate of Mañjuśrī is not all forms."
As for the "gate of sound," it is not all sounds. As for the "gate of Samantabhadra," what is this? Do not say you have set aside the teachings of the Tiantai school;
there is nothing to do, so please withdraw. [The Master] ascended the hall and said: A monk asked Changsha, "Where has Nanquan gone after his passing?
Changsha replied, "He became a donkey at East House and a horse at West House. The monk said, "What about me, your student?"
"No. Sha said, "If you wish to ride, you ride; if you wish to dismount, you dismount.

The Master said, "If it were someone seeking to transcend the three realms and practice the Way who heard these words, they would surely be filled with doubt and surely be struck with alarm. When Nanquan passed away, where did he go?
He became a donkey for the eastern neighbor and a horse for the western neighbor. Someone else offered this interpretation: "A thousand transformations, ten thousand changes..."

Transformation does not depart from the true and eternal. Some have explained it by saying: "One must realize the practice within the midst of different species before one can truly understand these words.
Others have explained it by saying: "The eastern neighbor is Nanquan; the western neighbor is Nanquan. Still others have explained it by saying: [and so forth].
"The gentleman of the eastern house; the gentleman of the western house. Some understand this by saying, "What is the eastern house? What is the western house?
Others understand it by braying like a donkey and neighing like a horse. Still others understand it thus: [and they remain silent].
"What do you call the donkey of the eastern house? What do you call the horse of the western house? Some understood this by saying:
"Since he asked about passing away, the answer lies in the question itself. Some understood it by saying: "He has gone to where the pillar stands exposed. Others understood it by saying: [silence].
"The house to the east becomes a donkey; the house to the west becomes a horse. Where does Nanquan suffer any loss?

Thus do these various houses understand; they all find a place of peace within the Buddha-dharma. When Nanquan passed away, where did he go? The house to the east becomes a donkey; the house to the west becomes a horse.
Students do not understand this: if you wish to ride, you ride; if you wish to dismount, you dismount. This talk requires no further elaboration."
One attains realization through many principles. If you see the nature of the Dharma-realm, even going about your affairs will be free from multiplicity. Take care! [Ascending the hall:
The form and shadow within a mirror depend solely upon the light of the mirror to manifest. So it is with all the deeds you people perform.
Now tell me: by what means alone does it manifest? Do you know? If you do know, then within your study of the Way, you will have all that is needed, a thousandfold and ten-thousandfold;
there is nothing more to do. Do not stand idly by. [Ascending the hall: You people here, when you sleep soundly at night...
They do not know anything. Since they do not know anything, let me ask you all: at that time, was there an original nature, or was there no original nature?
If you say there was an original nature at that time, yet they still do not know anything, then it is no different from death.
"If you say that at the time of sleep there is no original nature, yet when one suddenly awakens from sleep, the awareness is just as it was before—do you understand?
To not know this is no different from being dead. When one suddenly awakens from sleep, the awareness is just as it was before. At such times as these, what is it?
If you do not understand, each of you must investigate this for yourselves. Do not stand idly by when there is nothing to do. [Ascending the hall: "All dharmas..."
All that is produced is but a manifestation of the mind. Such words provide an excellent gateway for entry. Now, let me ask you all:

when the eyes see all forms, the ears hear all sounds, the nose smells all fragrances, the tongue discerns all tastes, the body touches all textures—whether soft or smooth—and the mind discriminates all phenomena—just as it is with the eyes, ears, and nose...
As for the objects encountered by the tongue, body, and mind: are they merely your own minds, or are they not your own minds?
If you say they are merely your own minds, why do they not merge with your bodies into a single mass and come to an end?
Why is it that the objects encountered by the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind are, in fact, outside of you?

If you say that the objects encountered by the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind are not your own mind, then what can you do about the fact that all phenomena arise as mere manifestations of the mind?
Why do these words remain in the world without anyone ever bringing them forth? You!
"Understand this teaching? If you do not yet understand, let us all deliberate with care so that you may be instructed.
May you find joy within it; do not grow weary of study. For now, I shall withdraw as there is nothing further to discuss.

In the second month of the Wushen year of the Dazhong Xiangfu era during the Song dynasty (988 CE), the Master said to his senior disciple Ruzhou: "You should construct a stone niche. On the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month," he said.

"I shall follow the transformation. At noon, he received his final instructions and passed away. When the appointed time arrived, scholars and commoners from near and far rushed to pay their respects and gaze upon him.
On that day, he conducted his inquiries as usual; at noon, he sat in the abbot’s quarters, formed the *ratnamudrā* with his hands, and said to Zhòu: "The ancients said..."
"Riding the tiger’s head, one strikes the tiger’s tail. As for the matter of the center, what is it? Zhao said, "It is also just like Zhao. The Master said, "You ask me.
Zhao then asked, "Riding the tiger’s head, one strikes the tiger’s tail; as for the matter of the center, how about you, Master? The Master said, "I too cannot bring myself to play with this.
Having finished speaking, he suddenly passed away, opening one eye and gazing faintly before his life ended. His age was...
[He was] sixty-seven [years old]. He had been a monk for forty-two years. His work, the *Zhulin ji* (Bamboo Grove Collection) in ten fascicles, circulated in the world.
During a communal labor session with National Teacher Hongshou, Master Xingjiao of Hangzhou heard a piece of firewood fall and attained realization.
He composed a verse, saying: "Where it falls is not some other thing; In its horizontal and vertical spread, it is no mere dust. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth— All fully reveal the Dharma."
The King’s Own Body.
A monk asked Chan Master Daoyuan of Chengtian Yong’an in Suzhou, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Shame on you, you outcaste!
The monk said, “I am a beginner; I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, “What are you asking? The monk said, “I ask...”
The Buddha. The Master said: "Tsk! You outcaste!

Chan Master Daoci of Yunju in Hongzhou, a successor of Chan Master Qingliang Qin, was the son of the Jin family of that same province. He traveled extensively through various Chan assemblies, yet his mind of study remained unsettled.

Later, while serving as the Librarian of the Jingzang at Shanglan Monastery, Fadeng one day asked the Master, "If someone asks me about the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, I answer them, 'Neither East nor West.
How do you understand this? The Master replied, "Neither East nor West.
Fadeng said, "Even if you understand it thus, how can that suffice? The Master said, "Daoqi simply understands it in this way; I do not know what you, Master, think."
"Master Shangzun, what do you think? Dēng said, "His family naturally has its own descendants. Thereupon, the Master suddenly understood his meaning and composed a verse:
"Receiving beings and benefiting life—how exquisite! Yet an outsider will ultimately be unworthy. His family naturally has its own descendants;
When brought forth in the future, they will be used most appropriately. Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "You..."
[The student] asked: "Who is this? [Dongshan] said: "In the midst of thorny thickets, there is no way out. I beg the Master to use his skillful means to open it for me.
The Master said: "Where do you intend to go? [The student] said: "I have almost never been here. The Master said: "Idle words. [The student] asked:
"If one cannot avoid saṃsāra, what is it like when one does not seek liberation? The Master said: "Have you ever questioned Jian Mountain? [The student] said: "I have studied [with him]."
The man could not do so. He requested the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, "Let go! Let go! Thirty blows! He asked, "What are the Three Jewels?

The Master said, "What jewel are you? He replied, "I do not know. The Master said, "Earth, wood, tiles, and pebbles. The Master composed the *Zuyu Yao* (Essential Phrases with Commentary), which includes the *Soyuan*, *Niangong*, *Dibie*, and other works;
these were widely circulated in the monastic communities. This was during the Dingyou year of the Zhi Dao era of Emperor Taizong of the Song dynasty.
In the ninth month, he manifested illness. He struck the bell to assemble the congregation and said, "This old monk has served as abbot in three places for over thirty years.
Throughout this time, you brothers from the ten directions have gathered to discuss the Way, and the administrative officers and heads of departments have assisted with diligent hearts.
Today, the fires and winds press upon me; I have come specifically to meet you all. Do you see me now? If you see me today, it is..."
This is the final expedient. Where do you all see it? Do you see it within the four elements and five aggregates? Or do you see it within the six entrances and twelve bases?
If you see it here, it can be said that for twenty years at Yunju Mountain, the later students have had their reliance.
After I depart, I entrust the mountain gate and the great assembly to Qi Gui; he shall open the hall and serve as abbot. In all matters, be diligent.
Practice accordingly. Each of you must exert yourselves. Farewell. As soon as the assembly had dispersed, the Master returned to his quarters in the western wing and passed away.
He was enshrined in a stupa at his home mountain. He was sixty-nine years of age and forty-eight years since his ordination.
A monk asked Chan Master Daoci of Gongchen Monastery in Hangzhou, successor to Chan Master Lingyin Song: "The Master has ascended the precious seat and the great assembly has all gathered;

we pray that you will proclaim the teachings of our school. The Master said, "The great assembly bears witness. The monk said, "If so, then it is thus from the beginningless past to the endless future."
The Master said, "You must also grasp the meaning of the words.
Chan Master Yuanzhao of Luohan Temple in Xiuzhou was a native of Qiantang. He ascended the hall and said: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are true spiritual friends;
they constantly preach the Dharma and perpetually deliver sentient beings. This does not hinder you, venerable monks, from investigating them for yourselves. A monk asked:
"The style of the Arhat family. Please, Master, give us one phrase. The Master said, "The grain rejoices as the ears form; the fragrance is transmitted to the upper realm.
The monk asked, "This is still the style of the Grain-Rejoicing family. What is the style of the Arhat family? The Master said, "If you travel to various places, explain it clearly there.
Later, while residing at Xiangyan Temple in Hangzhou, a monk asked, "Not establishing even a speck of dust—please, Master, speak directly."
The Master said, "Everyone laughs at you. The monk asked, "How do you understand this? The Master said, "Give me back the head of the story.
A monk asked Chan Master Shizhi of Ba’en Monastery in Chuzhou, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Who does not see it? A monk asked, "What is the samādhi of one mark? The Master said, "Blue, yellow, red, and white. The monk asked again.
"Where is this single mark? The Master said, "You are indeed quick-witted. The questioner asked, "The patriarchs have transmitted the patriarchal seal from one to another;
whom do you now take as your Dharma heir? The Master said, "Before the Vulture Peak, the lunar disc is bright and clear."
A monk asked Master Xian of Huning in Quzhou, "What is the house style of Huning? The Master said, "Thank you for pointing it out.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "Why do you find the old monk strange?
The monk said, "I do not understand; I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, "Was this not, just now, your question regarding the meaning of the Westward Journey?"
A monk asked Chan Master Daoduan of Guangxiao Monastery in Hangzhou, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Ask with a loud voice.
The monk said, “Is it not this very thing? The Master said, “There is no connection. Later, while residing at Lingyin Monastery, he passed away.
When Chan Master Nying of Baiching Monastery on Mount Xi in Hangzhou ascended the seat for the opening of the hall, two monks prostrated simultaneously.
The Master said, "Both have erred. As the monks prepared to offer a word in response, the Master immediately descended from the seat.
Chan Master Zhitui Yongxi Bianlong of Funing Prefecture was a native of Mingzhou. He ascended the hall and said:
"The majestic true reality (dharmatā) fills the void; its adamantine essence is indestructible. Does the great assembly see it or not?
If you say you see it, yet the essence of true reality is fundamentally neither blue, yellow, red, nor white, neither long, short, square, nor round—it is also not something seen."
Regarding the dharmas of hearing, awakening, and knowing—how can one speak of the principle of seeing?
If you say you do not see, yet it is also said that the sublime reality (*dharmatā*) fills all of empty space; why then do you not see it? A monk asked, "What is the path that leads upward?
The Master said, "That which is beneath your feet. The monk said, "In that case, I am constantly treading upon it. The Master said, "Do not."
[The student] mistakenly asks: "What is the firm and dense body? The Master says: "Nakedly exposed. [The student] says:
"If that is so, then it is not dense. The Master says: "What do you see?"
A monk asked Zen Master Xiyuan of Ruelong Temple in Hangzhou, “What is the master’s house style?
The Master said, “I thank you, Kalyāṇamitra, for asking. The monk said, “There is no doubt that you have been asked; what then is the house style? The Master said, “Sleeping beauty!”
A monk asked Zen Master Xinglin Zuyin of Nan’gang County, successor to Chan Master Ruozongrou: “When heaven pours down sweet dew and the earth wells up the seven treasures, whose affair is this?
The Master said, “Thank you for informing me. The monk said, “If that is so, then [it is] a Buddha-son’s...”
"Abiding in this ground is precisely the Buddha’s enjoyment of going. The Master said, "You must still examine this with great care.
He ascended the hall. Just as he sat down, a cat suddenly leaped onto his body. The Master picked it up and showed it to the assembly, saying:
"In the past, Nanquan personally slew it; today, Yashas shows it to his original disciples. Now I am selling it to all you Zen guests—here is the clear deed of sale."
[The Master] said, "There is none. After a long silence, he threw down the cat and descended from his seat.
A monk asked Zen Master Xīn of Tiāntóng in Míngzhōu, "What is the secret function? The Master said, "When has it ever been secret?"
Question: "When the path of the mind has not yet been opened through, how is it? The Master said: "What thing obstructs you? Question:
"When one seeks it but cannot find it, how is it? The Master said: "Why seek it? [The student] asked: "How is it then? The Master said: "When was it ever lost? Question:
"What is the realm of Tiantong? The Master said: "The clouds grow without anyone to plant them; how could their birth have an end? The water..."
"Who taught you to go and not return?
A monk asked Zen Master Jueke Xinyin of Gōngshēn Monastery in Hángzhōu, "The Patriarch is not on either the East or West Mountain;
where, then, does he dwell? The Master said, "Go find out. [Another] asked, "What is the True Buddha of Heaven? The Master said, "Why [do you ask]?"
I venture to provide this brief account.
Chan Master Qingjian of Tiantong in Mingzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Qiantang. The Master was solitary and pure in his conduct;
at the time, he was called "Jian" (Simple) by the travelers of Zhejiang. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "I do not wish to speak to you."
[The student] said, "Please, Master, speak. The Master replied, "Bodhidharma cannot come again. Later in life, the Master resided at Xuedou and passed away there;
his stupa was erected in the eastern corner of the monastery.
Chan Master Chengzhi of Xiqian on Mount Lu was a dharma successor of Chan Master Heng of Baizhang.
He was a native of Jianning. A monk asked: "At Zhaozhou’s Stone Bridge, donkeys and horses are both ferried across;
at the Stone Bridge of the Three Gorges, who should be ferried across? The Master said: "Shrimp and earthworms. The monk said: "If that is so, then all things..."
All things were thoroughly moistened by his grace. The Master said, "If you do not step upon it. A questioner asked, "Yesterday at Xian Dong, you finished the chanting;
today at Qixian, we request you to proclaim it. The Master said, "What will you do tomorrow? The questioner said, "I do not yet understand. How should I comprehend this?"
The Master said, "The arrow has passed to Silla. [Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Zhang San and Li Si. [Question: "What was the intent behind the ancients' slaying of the snake?
The Master said, "They still do not know pain or itching. [Question: "This is the field for selecting Buddhas;

one returns home having attained the 'Pass with Distinction' through the emptiness of mind. How may a student attain such a distinction and return? The Master said, "I am but a man of no talent, acting with caution."
Retreat. Evening *zanchan* (general assembly). The Master said, "In the morning I did not meet with you all; tonight it would be improper to remain silent.
He then descended from his seat. Question: When the Seer Viśvāmitra took Sudhana by the hand, he saw as many Buddhas as there are atoms in the universe.
“Just as when you had not yet grasped hands, what did you see? The Master said, “What do you see now?

Ascending the hall, he remained silent for a long while and then said, “It is fortunate that there is this dish of rice; it need not be seasoned with pepper and ginger. Nevertheless, try to taste it. He then descended from his seat.
The Master’s character was lofty and simple. He disciplined himself with rigorous strictness; his every movement conformed to the laws and measures of propriety.

In his later years, he completed three full recitations of the Tripitaka; considering reading while seated to be a lack of reverence, he would instead recite while standing or carry the scrolls while walking.
When Huanglong Nan first traveled to study under him, he followed him for many years; thus, much of what Nan did throughout his life was modeled after his master’s example.
Chan Master Wanshou Dexing of Suzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The assembly gazes upon him all at once.
The monk asked, "What is the one phrase by which you, the Master, benefit others? The Master said, "You should first benefit yourself."
He then said: "Question and answer are both complete; who among you has grasped the meaning? If you seek it from another, you merely end up acting in a peculiar, artificial manner.
For a long time I have dwelt in the deep mountains to hide my ineptitude; I never expected that today I would enter the gate of Wanshou, where it can truly be said that I cannot hide it.
Since it cannot be hidden, it is clearly revealed. I wonder, which of you perceives it first?"
As if there were a place for him to be seen, he came forth before the assembly and disclosed his message. After a long silence, he said, "I have stood here for a long time; take care.
Zen Master Yongxi Yong of Yunmen in Yuezhou was asked by a monk, "What is it like when the lion has not yet emerged from its den?
The Master said, "Do not roar for now. The monk asked, "What is it like after it has emerged from the den? The Master said, "Step back. [The monk] asked, "How about..."
"This is the path of the ancient Buddhas. The Master said, "Who does not tread upon it? Question: "What is the place where the student lets the mind rest and the will cease?
The Master said, "Have you even managed to break the staff yet? Question: "What is it like when the Mind-King issues an imperial edict?
The Master said, "Read it aloud once more and see. Question: "What is the definitive meaning? The Master said, "It cannot be [grasped]."
Attachment. Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "This meaning is no small matter.

Chan Master Kuangsheng of Qianguangwang Temple in Hangzhou, a successor of Chan Master Yongming Quan, was the son of Zheng [surname] from Wenzhou. He left home to become a monk at a young age and was diligent in his practice.

He thoroughly investigated the Vinaya section and settled his mind in the perfect and sudden *śamatha-vipaśyanā*. Later, while reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he found its literary principles so vast and profound that he could not yet penetrate them.
One night, as he leaned over his desk, he fell into a light sleep and dreamed that a solar disc descended from the sky; he opened his mouth and swallowed it.
From this point on, he attained awakening, and the various gates of doctrinal meaning became clear to him without obstruction. Later, he visited Yongming, who...
[The Master] first gave his seal of approval. There was no separate finger-pointing analogy; rather, he bestowed the patched robe left behind by King Zhongyi as a token of faith.
After [the assembly] had settled, he ascended the hall and said: "Venerable Elders, the Buddha-dharma is not otherwise. The sun and moon of the past are the sun and moon of the present.
The wind and rain of the past are the wind and rain of the present. The elders of the past are the elders of the present. Having raised this point, he concluded: "To speak of it is also finished."

All was perfectly realized; all manifested as auspicious. Adieu! In the seventh month of the *Ren-shen* year of the Kaibao era of Emperor Taizu of Song, a precious tree and bathing pool suddenly appeared before him.
The Master said, "All phenomena that possess marks are entirely illusory. Three days later, he manifested illness.
He gathered the assembly to bid them farewell, sat upright, and passed away. His remains were cremated, and his relics (*śarīra*) were collected to build a stupa. He was sixty-seven years old.

In the *Qingzhou Zhenjingzhi*, a monk asked Master Cheng: "What is the sword that settles heaven and earth? The Master said: "It does not let even a hair's breadth slip through. The monk asked: "How is it used? The Master said: "One does not know. Later, while they were engaged in communal labor (*pùqǐng*), a monk asked [the same question]. The Master said: "One does not know. The monk asked: "Why is this so? The Master said: "Because you do not know. The monk asked: "Who is it that does not know? The Master said: "Even I do not know. The monk asked: "If even you do not know, who is it that knows? The Master said: "I do not say that I know; I simply do not know. The monk asked: "Does one not know by means of this very non-knowing? The Master said: "I do not say that I know by means of this non-knowing; I simply do not know. The monk asked: "Is there no way to understand this? The Master said: "There is no way to understand it. The monk asked: "If there is no way to understand it, how can one attain liberation? The Master said: "Liberation is precisely this lack of understanding. [The monk] said, "In that case, there would be no transgression. The Master said, "Cause and effect are clearly manifest. Later, he moved to Baoyun Temple on Mount Xi in Hangzhou;
the Emperor bestowed upon him purple robes and appointed him as the Great Master Jixian.
Chan Master Chenxiang of Chongfu Monastery in Mingzhou ascended the hall and said: "Virtuous Chan practitioners, the nature of seeing is all-pervasive; the nature of hearing is likewise so.
It penetrates the ten directions, being neither internal nor external. Therefore, the ancients said: 'Acting in accordance with conditions without fabrication, movement and stillness are ever true.
Such conduct is entirely the functioning of true wisdom. A monk asked: "What is the person of original nature? The Master [replied].
[The monk] said, "Tall and imposing, six feet in height—how very distinct! [The Master] asked, "As for this person of original nature (*puruṣa*), does he still rely upon such physical appearance?
The Master said, "What do you call 'the person of original nature'? [The monk] said, "I beg the Master for a skillful means (*upāya*. The Master said, "To whom would I provide a skillful means?"
Chan Master Daocheng Tongfa of Baoming Monastery in Fuzhou, successor to Chan Master Ba’en Ming, ascended the hall and said: "As it is for one person, so it is for many. Take care.
A monk asked: "The perfect sound vibrates universally, and the three grades hear it equally. We pray that the Master will reveal the mind of the Seer from the land of Zhuyi."
[The Master] remained silent for a long while. The monk said, "If that is so, then the wild horse of the mind has become a precious steed, and the ox of the heart has suddenly turned into a white ox.
The Master said, "Seven tops and eight bottoms. [The monk] said, "If that is the case, you will surely be laughed at by many.
The Master said, "After prostrating, withdraw. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Master’s coming from the West? The Master said, "I have never [spoken of it]."
Upon arriving in the Western Heaven (India), he asked, "What is the meaning of the student's coming from the West? The Master replied, "How long have you been in the Eastern Land?
Baoci said that [this was] the Dharma heir of the Master.
Chan Master Yining of Yunju in Nankang Army ascended the hall and said: "There is no need to come up here.
Let the Elder Kauṇḍinya in the hall act as the senior elder for all the elders and turn the Dharma-wheel of the primary truth (*paramārtha*). Can you do it?

If you have sufficient faith, each of you should return to your quarters and investigate for yourselves. After descending from the seat, he asked a monk: "Just as I instructed the elders a moment ago..."
The Master took his seat and addressed the assembly: "The Holy Monk—what does he say in return? A monk asked, "I specifically thank the Master;
please raise the question again: what is the Buddha? The Master said, "The very mind is the Buddha. The monk said, "I do not understand; I beg the Master for an expedient means.
The Master said, "The expedient means is to call it 'Buddha. Turn the light back upon yourself and reflect: what thing are body and mind?"
Chan Master Lingcen of Mount Yuntai in Quanzhou was a successor of Chan Master Chou of Chongshou. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Mount Yuntai?
The Master said, "The mountain in front and the mountain behind. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "A sleepyhead."
The Abbot of Ziguō, Seng Yuánjìn, asked: "What is the meaning of Danxia burning the wooden Buddha?

The Master said: "Inviting the cause while carrying the fruit. He asked: "What is the meaning of 'the cypress tree in front of the hall'? The Master said: "The blue-eyed barbarian monk smiles and nods his head. He asked:
"An ancient said, 'At the eastern house he becomes a donkey; at the western house he becomes a horse. What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "..."
"How is it? The Master said, "His acquaintances fill the world.
Regarding Chan Master Daojian of Qixian on Mount Lu, a successor of Chan Master Ba'en: An official asked, "I have gathered my troops at Jinling and am ready to engage in battle."
"A person has no fixed number. Does he still have offenses or not? The Master said, "I, this old monk, simply keep watching. Question:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The Yanglan and Zuoli rivers: waves rise even without wind."
Chan Master Huicheng of Guizong on Mount Lu was the son of the Cui family of Yangzhou. On the day he ascended the hall, he stood before the Dharma Hall and addressed the assembly, saying:
"When devas and humans attain the Way, they take this as proof. Having said this, he dismissed them immediately; even so, it was already too much elaboration.
As they did not yet understand, he repeated his explanation. He then ascended the seat. A monk asked, "The Prefect is present at this assembly;
we request the Master to expound the Dharma. The Master said, "I am not as good as you. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "How could it not be so?
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "I do not know. Then he said, "Let your questioning cease for a moment. Even if you were to ask—"
Reaching the end of kalpas—no matter what you ask, it does not hit the mark; reaching the end of kalpas—no matter how you answer, it falls short. Why is this?
It is simply because each person has their own fundamental task, which is perfectly complete throughout the ten directions and spans from antiquity to the present;
even the Buddhas dare not err regarding it. People then call this the "Summit Lineage," yet it merely serves to assist and inspire the Elder. Therefore it is said:
All sentient beings throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm realize the fruit of the Sugata in every thought-moment. Since they are great men, so am I;
how can I disparage myself and succumb to despondency? O Venerable Elders, do not be despondent. Believe and accept this, and let it suffice.
When the Patriarch came from the West, he spoke only of seeing one's nature to achieve Buddhahood; all other teachings do not equal this teaching. Furthermore, there is another...
This is a marvelous expedient. He presents it to all people and, after a long silence, says: "Take this clearly to heart. When you travel to other regions, do not misrepresent it.
I have stood here for a long time; take care. A monk asked: "How can one pass through where there is no passage for the wind? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
“From where have you come? The monk cited Nanquan’s question to Deng Yinfeng: “The copper pitcher is the object.
There is water in the pitcher; do not touch it. Bring the water to me, O Elder. Yinfeng then picked up the pitcher and poured out the water.
“I do not understand—what was the meaning of this? The Master said, “Deng Yinfeng was indeed extraordinary, yet he poured it out in a chaotic manner.”

The Master held the abbotship for fourteen years, with a constant assembly of five hundred. On the eighteenth day of the third month in the Dingwei year of the Jingde era of the Song dynasty’s Zhenzong reign, he ascended the hall to bid farewell to the assembly and passed away in peace.
He was sixty-seven years of age and fifty-two years since his ordination. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at his home mountain.
Chan Master Bianshi of Chang’an Monastery in Luzhou, successor to Chan Master Chang’an Gui, was asked by a monk: “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said: “Dwelling on the Spirit Peak of Shaoshi, amidst the nine heavens.”
Chan Master Yongqing of Yungai in Tanzhou was the son of the Zhao family of Hezhou.
A monk asked, "If there is a person at the bottom of a ten-thousand-fathom well, how can they get out? The Master said, "Fortunately, we have met.

The monk said, "In that case, he has pierced the clouds and penetrated the moon. The Master said, "What about the affairs of the thirty-three heavens? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "Deceiving me!"
"What are you saying? [The Master asked. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Yungai? The Master said, "Three spring wells outside the gate. [The monk] asked, "Who is the person within the realm?
The Master said, "The novice serving as a son. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The secret instruction for sealing the mouth at Yungai:
if you hesitate, your brains will split. Clapping hands, chasing the void; clouds reveal the moon over the western mountains. A monk asked, "What is the seal?"
The oral instruction: The Master said, "Pervading heaven and pervading earth. [A monk] asked, "If that is so, then the stone man nods his head and the pillar claps its hands.
The Master said, "A single flask of pure water and a single incense burner. [The monk] said, "This is still but a shrimp at the bottom of a well.
The Master said, "It troubles the assembly. The Master always regulated his food and drink. He partook with the community during the two meal periods, merely unfolding his alms bowl.

Sometimes he would remain for months or years without practicing disciplined training or taking medicinal elixirs, yet this did not hinder his daily activities. Whenever invited, he would certainly attend;

he would then eat his fill without any sense of restraint or attachment. On the second day of the fourth month in the year of Bingshen (976) during the Zhizhao era of Emperor Taizong of the Song dynasty, he manifested parinirvāṇa.
A stupa was erected on the mountain where he resided.
A monk asked Chan Master Congjin of Puzhao at Tiantai Bayan, a successor of Chan Master Yunju Xi: "What is it like when the cold spring flows in the ancient ravine?
The Master said, "Above all, do not drink from it. The monk asked, "And if one drinks? The Master said, "You will lose your very life."
A monk asked Chan Master Zhichao of Qinghua in Yuezhou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Who are you?
The monk replied, "Are you not he yourself? The Master said, "If it were so, there would be no connection."
Chan Master Fachi of Changshou in Suzhou, a descendant of the eleventh generation under Nanyue and a dharma heir of Chan Master Changshou Yan,
was the son of the Ding family of Wuzhou. Initially, he lectured on the *Mingmen* and *Yinming* treatises.
The Commentary: Having traveled abroad for some time, he received the Mind-Seal (Cittamudrā) from Guangfa.

When the Imperial Commissioner Qian Ren respectfully invited him to succeed Guangfa as the abbot, on the day of his opening address to the assembly, the Master of the Hundred Dharmas (Bai-fa-zhuzhu) questioned him. At the command of the Duke, the fourfold assembly gathered like clouds.

[The student] asked, “Ultimately, what is it? The Master said, “All dharmas are without self. [The student] asked about the old woman east of the city who was born at the same time as the Buddha:
why did she not see the Buddha? The Master said, “If you do not see him, then speak! [The student] said, “In that case, then I see him. The Master said, “... (The Master remained silent).

The Elder Lady of the Eastern City was born at the same time as the Buddha. She manifested her passing on the eleventh day of the twelfth month of the Gengzi year of the Xianping era of Emperor Zhenzong of the Song dynasty.
Her age was eighty-nine, and her years since ordination were seventy-two.

instead, one carries it home in a bottomless basket. I wonder, does the Master accept it or not? The Master said, “Where did you get that? The monk replied: [silence].
"If that is so, then it is not bestowed in vain. The Master said, "For now, take it with you. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "Beyond the reach of praise. The monk said, "Is this very thing it? The Master said, "It does not cause people to praise."
A monk asked Zen Master Wensheng Ciji of Lingyin Temple in Hangzhou, “What is it like when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished?

The Master said, “The ancient mirror. The monk asked, “What is it like after it has been polished? The Master said, “The ancient mirror. The monk asked, “I do not know: are they divided or not? The Master said, “The ancient mirror.”
[The Master] looked at him again and asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Do not be surprised by its rusticity.
[The monk] asked, "What do you do when a guest suddenly arrives? The Master said, "Go drink tea."

Chan Master Zhiquan of Guanghui in Mingzhou was the son of the Wei family of Hangzhou. He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the fundamental matter of a patch-robed monk?
The Master said, "Do not embarrass me. The monk bowed. The Master said, "In fact, it is the assembly that is embarrassing you," and he descended from his seat.
A monk asked, "How is it when a thief does not strike the house of a poor man? The Master said—

The monk said, "The person I spoke to did not believe me. The Master said, "In that case, you should prostrate and withdraw. The monk asked, "What have you gained? Chan Master Juxu of Damei Baofu in Mingzhou was asked by a monk, "What was the intent behind the ancients' 'wall-facing'? The Master said, "I do not know. The monk asked, "Why do you say you do not know? The Master said, "Because I do not know. The monk said, "If you do not know, why do you say you do not know? The Master said, "If I were to tell you, you would not believe it. The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall prostrate and withdraw. The Master said, "What have you gained? The monk said, "I have gained nothing. The Master said, "If you have gained nothing, why do you say you have gained nothing? The monk said, "If I were to say I had gained something, I would not be speaking the truth. The Master said, "If you are not speaking the truth, why do you say you are not speaking the truth? it is what is called the 'Inexhaustible Treasury of Creation. The first month of the Jichou year of the Renzong era of the Song dynasty.
On the eighth day of summer, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Movement arises in response to stillness; there has never been a limit to this.
I have moved for sixty-four years; now I am still. Yet, fundamentally, what existence can there be for movement or stillness? Thereupon, he passed away in profound tranquility.

The Dharma heir of National Teacher Lingyin Sheng of the twelfth generation under Nanyue was Chan Master Yan Shan Huiming of Lingyin, Hangzhou. A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The Way is far."
"How profound it is! [A monk] asked, "What is the single path of true correctness? The Master said, "Not even a hair's breadth can pass through.

The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall follow it and practice accordingly. The Master said, "Do not wander about recklessly. He ascended the hall and said, "I offer you, the elder, a single thread of the Way.
But how do you maintain and discuss the Buddha-dharma? If it is as impenetrable as water being unable to leak through, then I will leave you, the elder, with no place to rest your body."
At the moment of establishing one’s destiny, the Patriarch and Buddha emerge from within. To say there are "twenty blows" for such a statement—does the mountain monk have any fault here?
Have you not seen that when the World-Honored One was born, he took seven steps, gazed in the four directions, pointed one finger at heaven and one finger at the earth, and said:
"In the heavens above and on the earth below, I alone am the Honored One"? Clouds...
The Gatekeeper said: "If I had seen him at the very beginning, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to the dogs.
Why do you act thus? You seek nothing more than peace throughout the world. Now tell me: when Yunmen speaks in this manner, does he possess the principles of the Buddha-dharma or not?
Even so, Yunmen possesses only a single eye. I shall now take my leave; farewell.
A monk asked Chan Master Guize of Jianfu Monastery in Changzhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The sound of the bell ringing by my ear."
A monk asked Zen Master Luyin Yuncong of Hangzhou, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "It is present when you call for it.
The monk said, "I do not understand; what is there? The Master said, "The *zhilu* staff of Tiantai. [Another] asked, "How is it when the ancient path is being restored?
The Master said, "Leveling the high and following the low."
A monk asked the ancient Chan Master Nanqing of Hangzhou, "The Western Patriarch transmitted [the Dharma]; I ask the Master to convey its message.
The Master said, "What did you say? The monk replied, "If that is so, then it cannot be conveyed. The Master said, "You are quite clever."
A monk asked Chan Master Zong of Jiangning Baoning, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Why ask further?
The monk said, "Is it not simply this very thing? The Master said, "Do not be full of empty pretense."
A monk asked Chan Master Youbang of Shaoxing Stone Buddha Temple, "The patriarchs have transmitted one to another, passing down the seal of the patriarchate;
whom do you, Master, now take as your Dharma heir? The Master said, "The man who spread his hair to cover the mud was entirely overlooked by all.
The monk said, "In that case, this branch of Lingyin is uniquely prominent at Nanming. The Master said, "Guessing with a ladle while listening to empty sounds."
A monk asked Zen Master Neiju of Qingliang Cihua in Jiangning: "Since the one dharma is fundamentally non-existent, how can the myriad dharmas exist?
I wonder, what does the Master speak of? The Master said, "You remember it very clearly.
The monk said, "If that is so, then everything has vanished. The Master said, "I do not believe you either."
A monk asked Chan Master Siyuan of Cuiyan in Mingzhou, a successor of Chan Master Haewon of Suiryam, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said:
[The Master] said, "I buy and sell with cash; I never accept credit. [The monk] asked, "Is there anything further above this? The Master said, "It is well that you do not trust people's honesty.
Chan Master Wenhui of Damei in Siming was asked by a monk: "The patriarchs have transmitted one to another, passing down the Patriarchal Command. You, Master, have now attained it."
"Who is your Dharma heir? The Master said, "Few are fit for it. [The monk] said, "I have already informed the legitimate successor.
The Master said, "What did I just tell you? [The monk] asked, "What is the realm of Damei? The Master said, "Look.
[The monk] asked, "What is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Go drink tea."
A monk asked Chan Master Sishu Ru of Jinhua Zhizhe Temple, a successor of Chan Master Damei Xu, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Appointing to office according to one’s talent.
The monk asked, “What is it like after being appointed? The Master said, “The staff of Tiantai. [The monk] asked, “What is true reality?”

[The monk] asked, "What is the essential substance? The Master said, "Today is a cold day. [The monk] asked, "What is the underlying meaning? The Master said, "A thousand mountains and ten thousand peaks are covered in snow.
Chan Master Shoujian Fayan of Wanshou Monastery in Suzhou, successor to Chan Master Zhangjiang Yuan, was asked by a monk, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Who does not [know it]?"
[The Master] stepped forward and asked, "What is it like to be one who walks the Way? The Master said, "Coming in thousands, going in tens of thousands.

Chan Master Longhua Cheng, a successor of Chan Master Wenxuan Mi of Lingyan in Wenzhou, was asked by a monk: "The *udumbara* flower has withered, and all people know it; the Patriarch’s command is personally [manifested]."
"How should one conduct oneself? The Master said, "One who knows the Dharma is apprehensive. [The student] said, "In that case, my actions will have a basis.
The Master said, "A small person with a large heart."
The thirteenth generation descendant of Nanyue, Chan Master Zhiren, Dharma heir of Chan Master Chengtian Chengyue of Jinhua.
A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The setting sun lingers in the deep recesses."

[The Master] said: "Grass. He was asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master replied, "This year firewood and rice are expensive. When he was about to pass away, he spoke a verse:
"Where does one go when departing? Where does one dwell when staying? Whether going or staying, from where do they arise? Transcendent and peerless.
At this parting, to whom can I utter a single word? The Milky Way is white at night as the solitary moon emerges. Having finished speaking, he sat in the lotus posture and passed away.
A monk asked Zen Master Xuwai of Jinhua Huazang, "I know that you have long harbored a treasure within your bag;
today at this assembly, I wish to borrow it and look upon it. The Master said, "Lift your eyebrows! The monk asked, "What is it like after seeing it? The Master said, "How very clear!"
Chan Master Ke-song of Jin-hua Jing-tu had a verse on leaving the world that said: "The numinous tree has no root; the Big Dipper has a handle.
The waves of the great ocean are my life-span. Eight feet or sixteen feet—whom do we call ordinary, whom do we call sage?
If you ask about going or staying, it is like spring following the ordinances of autumn. Take care, O worthy ones; when the form is upright, the outward expression is correct."

Chan Master Linji Yixuan of Zhenzhou,
a successor in the fourth generation under Nanyue and a dharma heir of Chan Master Huangbo Xiyun,
was a native of the Xing clan from Nanhua in Caizhou. From his youth, he bore the aspiration to transcend the mundane world.
As for Zhì: after he had shaved his head and received full ordination, he devoted himself to the Chan school. Initially, while at the assembly of Huangbo, his practice was pure and singular.
At that time, Muzhou served as the First Seat (the head monk). He asked, "How long have you been here, Senior Monk?
The Master replied, "Three years. Muzhou said, "Have you ever asked for instruction? The Master said, "I do not know how to ask for instruction; I do not even know what to ask about. Muzhou said:
"Why do you not ask the Abbot, 'What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?'? The Master then went to ask him.
Before his voice had even ceased, Baizhang struck him. The Master came down [from the hall], and Mazu asked, "How did your inquiry go?
The Master said, "Before I had finished asking, the Master struck me; I do not understand. Mazu said, "Just go and ask again. The Master went once more.

[The Master] asked. Huangbo struck him again. Thus he asked three times and was struck three times. The Master said to Prefect Zhou, "I have long received your encouragement in inquiring about the Dharma, and I have repeatedly received the Master’s blows.
I regret that due to my karmic obstacles, I did not grasp the profound meaning. I shall now take my leave.
Prefect Zhou said, "If you are going, you must first bid farewell to the Master before you leave. The Master bowed and withdrew. Prefect Zhou went ahead to Huangbo.
Huangbo said, "The questioner, the *upāsaka*, though a junior, is truly extraordinary. If he comes to take his leave, you must skillfully receive him;
in the future, he will become a great tree that provides shade for all people under heaven. The next day, the Master took his leave of Huangbo.
Huangbo said, "There is no need for him to go elsewhere. Go directly to Daoyi at Tancheng in Gaoyang; he will certainly [awaken] you."
[The Master] said: "The Master went to Dayu. Dayu asked, 'Where have you come from? The Master replied, 'From Huangbo. Dayu asked, 'What words did Huangbo say?
The Master replied, 'Three times I asked him about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, and three times I was struck.'"
"I do not know whether this person has committed an offense or not. Yunju said, "Huangbo was so earnest in his compassionate concern that he exhausted himself for your sake;
yet you come here again to ask whether there is an offense or not. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and said:
"Originally, Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is not much. Yuyou grabbed him and said, "You bed-wetting little devil!
Just now you asked whether there was a transgression or not; now you say, 'Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is not much.
What principle have you seen? Speak quickly, speak quickly! The Master struck Yuyou three times under the ribs. Yuyou pushed him away and said:
"Your teacher Huangbo has nothing to do with my affairs. The Master took his leave of Dayu and returned to Huangbo.
Upon seeing him, Huangbo asked, "This fellow comes and goes; when will he ever have an end to it? The Master said, "It is only because of your grandmotherly concern.

Having finished his formal greetings, he stood in attendance. Huangbo asked, "Where have you been? The Master replied, "Yesterday, I received the Compassionate Command of the Abbot, ordering me to practice *chán* (meditation)."
When Daoyuan returned from his visit to Dayu, Huangbo asked, "What words did Dayu say? Daoyuan recounted the previous conversation. Huangbo said, "That old fellow Dayu is too talkative;
wait until he returns, and I will give him a thorough beating. Daoyuan said, "What is the need to wait for him to return? I shall strike him right now!"
He then slapped him. Huangbo said, "This madman has come here to pull at a tiger’s whiskers.

The Master (Linji) then gave a shout. Huangbo called to his attendant, saying, "Take this madman to the meditation hall. (Miaoyan raised this question to Yangshan: "At that time, did Linji obtain the power of Dayu or the power of Huangbo? Yangshan replied:
"Not only could he ride on the tiger's head, he also knew how to grasp the tiger's tail. One day, while Huangbo was out on a work assignment, the Master followed behind him. Huangbo...
Turning his head, he saw that the Master was empty-handed, so he asked, "Where is the mattock? The Master said, "A man has taken it away.
Baizhang said, "Come closer; let us deliberate on a matter together. The Master then approached him.
Baizhang held up the mattock and said, "This very thing—no one in the world can lift it. The Master snatched it from his hand, held it up, and said, "As for this—"
"What is it? [Huangbo] replied, "It is right here in my hands. Huangbo said, "Today there is someone else;

let us go back together for the communal labor" (Later, when Yangshan was attending Muzhou, Muzhou brought up this story before finishing it.
