While the Master was working the land during the communal labor, he saw Huangbo approaching and stood with his hoe resting against him. Huangbo said, "Is this fellow exhausted?"
The Master said, "The mattock has not even been lifted; what is there to be exhausted? Baizhang struck him immediately.

The Master caught the staff and sent it flying so that it fell. Baizhang called out, "Venerable One, help me up! When the Venerable One helped him up, he said, "How can you tolerate this madman’s impertinence?
As soon as Baizhang rose, he struck the Venerable One. The Master was hoeing the ground and said, "In other places, they perform cremations."

"I am being buried alive here" (When Guishan asked Yangshan, "What was the meaning of Huangbo’s beating the *karmadāna*? Yangshan said, "The real thief has run away, and the one who caught the red herring is eating the stick.
One day, while the Master was sleeping in the Sangha Hall, Huangbo entered the hall and saw him. He struck the head of the wooden board with his staff once.
The Master raised his head; seeing it was Huangbo, he went back to sleep. Huangbo struck the head of the board again, then went up to the upper section. Seeing [the Master there]...
The Head Seat was sitting in meditation when he said, "The junior monks in the lower quarters are actually sitting in meditation;
what are you doing here, pretending to meditate? The Seat replied, "What are you doing, you old fellow? Huangbo struck the head of the meditation board once more and then went out.

(Miaoshan raised this to ask Yangshan, "As for Huangbo’s intention, what do you make of it? Yangshan said, "Two colors, one match. While the Master was planting pine trees, Huangbo said, "Planting trees in the deep mountains..."
"What does Mazu do with so many pine trees? The Master said, "First, to provide a scenic setting for the mountain gate;
second, to serve as a signpost for future generations. Having finished speaking, he struck the ground three times with his mattock.
Huangbo said, "Even so, you have already received thirty blows from me. The Master struck the ground three times again and let out a long sigh. Huangbo said, "My lineage has reached..."

"You shall bring great prosperity to the world" (Miaoshan raised this question to Yangshan regarding Huangbo. At that time, he had only entrusted it to Linji alone; yet there was another person. Yangshan said: "There is one, but because the era has been so remote, I am reluctant to mention him to you, Master.

Miaoshan said: "Even so, I still wish to know who it is. Just name him. Yangshan said: "One person points the way south; his commands are carried out throughout Wu and Yue, yet they cease when they encounter a great wind.
Huangbo once entered the kitchen and asked the head cook, "What are you doing? The cook replied, "I am sorting the rice for the assembly's meal. Huangbo said, "One..."

"How much did you eat all at once? Baizhang asked. "Two *shí* and five [dǒng]," the head cook replied. "Is that not too much? Baizhang said. "I am still afraid it was too little," the head cook replied.
Baizhang then struck him. The head cook reported this to the Master (Huangbo). The Master said, "I shall test this old fellow for you.

As soon as he arrived and stood in attendance, Baizhang recounted the previous conversation. The Master said, "The head cook does not understand. Please, Preceptor, provide a substitute phrase for him. Baizhang said:
“Just bring it,” the Master said. Baizhang replied, “Is that not too much? The Master said, “I will eat another meal tomorrow. Baizhang said, “What do you mean by ‘tomorrow’?
Eat right now! He then gave him a slap on the face. Baizhang said, “This madman has come here again to pull at the tiger’s whiskers.
The Master let out a shout and went out. (Miaoyan cited this and asked Yangshan, “What was the meaning of these two venerable elders? Yangshan—)

Yangshan asked, "What about you, Master? Guishan said, "Only by raising a son does one come to know a father's compassion. Yangshan said, "Not so. Guishan asked, "And what about you, my son? Yangshan said, "It is very much like inviting a thief to ruin the house.
Later, during the summer retreat, the Master went up to Huangbo and saw Huangbo reading a sutra. The Master said, "I thought he was a man of realization;

it turns out he is just an old monk who hides black beans. He stayed for several days and then took his leave. Huangbo said, "You arrived after the summer retreat has already begun; why did you come?"
He did not leave at the end of the summer retreat. The Master said, "I have come for a moment to pay my respects to the Abbot. Baizhang then struck him and drove him away.

After traveling several li, the Master felt doubt about this matter and returned to stay for the remainder of the summer. Later, he took his leave of Baizhang again. Baizhang asked, "Where are you going?"
The Master said, "If it were not Henan, it would be Hebei. Baizhang then struck him. The Master grabbed him and gave him a slap.
Baizhang laughed loudly and called to his attendant, "Bring the meditation board and desk of our late master Baizhang here. The Master said, "Attendant, bring fire.
Baizhang said, "Not so. You simply take them away; in the future, you shall cut off the tongues of all people under heaven."
When the Master arrived at the head of the Shishuang Damo Pagoda, the keeper of the pagoda asked, "Do you pay homage first to the Buddha, or do you pay homage first to the Patriarch?

The Master said, "I pay homage to neither the Patriarch nor the Buddha. The keeper said, "What grievance could there possibly be between the Patriarch, the Buddha, and you, Elder? The Master shook his sleeves and departed.
While the Master was serving as abbot at Huangbo, he sent a letter to Mount Wei. During a conversation with Yangshan, Yangshan said, "My elder brother..."
"If you go northward from here, there is a place where you may dwell. The Master said, "How could such a thing be? Nanquan said, "Once you have gone there, someone will assist you;
this person will simply have a head but no tail, a beginning but no end. (This was a prediction regarding Puhua.
Later, the Master resided at Linji in Zhenzhou, where disciples gathered like clouds. One day, he spoke to Puhua and Ke Fu.
The two senior monks said, "I wish to establish the school of Huangbo here; you should first refute me.
With these words, the two of them respectfully descended. Three days later, Puhua came up and asked, "What were you saying three days ago, Master?
The Master struck him. Three days later, Ke Fu came up and asked, "Master, why did you strike Puhua the other day?"
"What are you doing? The Master struck him as well. Later that evening, during a small assembly (xiaocan), he said: "Sometimes one takes away the person but not the environment;
sometimes one takes away the environment but not the person; sometimes both person and environment are taken away; and sometimes neither person nor environment is taken away.
Kefu asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not the environment'? The Master said: "The warm sun brings forth life, spreading a carpet of brocade across the earth. [He continued: "An infant..."
The boy’s hair hung down, white as silk. He asked, “What is ‘seizing the realm but not seizing the person’? The Master said, “The Imperial decree has already been issued throughout the world;
the General beyond the frontier has cut off all smoke and dust. He asked, “What is ‘seizing both the person and the realm’?
The Master said, “News is cut off between Bing and Fen; one dwells alone in a single region. He asked, “What is ‘neither seizing the person nor seizing the realm’? The Master said:
The King ascends the precious throne; the village elders sing songs of joy. A monk asked, "What are the true Buddha, the true Dharma, and the true Way?
I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "As for the Buddha, it is the purity of mind. As for the Dharma, it is the luminosity of mind. As for the Way, it is..."
The Pure Light that is unimpeded everywhere is such that three are one; all are merely empty names and lack substantial existence.
Just as a true practitioner of the Way maintains a state of mind that is uninterrupted from moment to moment, so it was with the Great Master Bodhidharma when he came from the Western Land:
he sought only a person who would not be deluded by others. Later, upon meeting the Second Patriarch, he attained realization in a single word, and only then did he know [the truth].
"Your previous efforts were in vain. My realization today is no different from that of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.

If you can realize it within the first phrase, you are fit to be a teacher of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. If you can realize it within the second phrase, you are fit to be a teacher of gods and humans.
If you can realize it within the third phrase, you will not even be able to save yourself. A monk then asked, "What is the first phrase?"
[The student] asked: "One phrase. The Master said: "The seal of the three essentials opens; the vermilion dot is narrow. There is no room for hesitation;

host and guest are distinguished. [The student] asked: "What is the second phrase? The Master said: "How could the subtle understanding allow for Wuzhuo’s question? How could the *upāya* fail to match the mechanism that cuts the current?
[The student] asked: "What is the third phrase? The Master said: "Just look at the puppeteers at the head of the stage; their pulling and tugging is entirely [dependent on others]."
The person inside the screen said, "In general, when chanting the teachings of the *zong* (the fundamental school), one phrase must contain the three gates;
each gate must contain the three essentials. There is the provisional and the real; there is illumination and function. How do you all understand this?
The Master said to the monk, "At times, a single shout is like the Vajra-King’s precious sword; at other times..."
One shout is like a lion crouching on the ground; sometimes one shout is like a probing pole and its shadow-grass;
sometimes one shout is not used as a shout. How do you understand this? When a monk hesitated, the Master shouted. Addressing the assembly:
Those who study the Way must be extremely careful. It is like the meeting of host and guest, where there is an exchange of words and discourse, or perhaps a response.

The object manifests its form: sometimes as a total embodiment of activity, sometimes wielding power and displaying joy or anger, sometimes appearing as half a body, or riding a lion, or riding an elephant king.
If there is a true student of the Way, they will immediately shout; first, they produce a lacquer basin.
The good teacher (the opponent) fails to discern it as a trap and enters that realm, adopting various postures and gestures, whereupon he is caught.
The student shouts again, yet the former person refuses to let go; this is a terminal illness that cannot be cured.

This is called "the guest looking at the host. Alternatively, if a true teacher (a *kalyāṇamitra*) does not bring forth an object, but simply seizes [the student] according to the point of their inquiry, and the student, having been seized, stubbornly refuses to let go even unto death—this is "the host looking at the guest. Or there may be a student...
One should present a single pure object before a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*).

When the spiritual friend discerns this object and seizes it to throw it into a pit, the student says, "Excellent, spiritual friend! The spiritual friend then says, "Alas! You do not distinguish between good and evil. The student then prostrates;
this is called "the host looking at the host. Alternatively, there may be a student who is still wearing the cangue and shackles.
When he stepped before the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), the friend further placed another layer of shackles upon him.

The student rejoiced; neither could discern it for themselves, yet they called it "viewing the guest" (*bīn kàn bīn*). "Virtuous One," the mountain monk says: all that I have raised is to distinguish demons, to select the extraordinary, and to know the false from the true.
The Master asked Luopu: "From the beginning until now, one person practices the staff, while another practices the shout. Which is it?"
“Which one is intimate? [The monk] said, “Neither is intimate. The Master asked, “What is intimacy? Pu then gave a shout. The Master then struck him and ascended the hall.
“There is one person who, for kalpas, remains on the road yet never leaves home; there is another person who leaves home and is no longer on the road.
Which of these two deserves to receive the offerings of devas and humans? The Master asked the temple steward, “Where have you been?”
The man went away and returned, saying, "I have come from selling yellow millet in the prefecture. The Master asked, "Have you sold it all? The man replied, "I have sold it all.

When the kitchen steward arrived, the Master brought up the previous conversation. The steward said, "The head of the monastery does not understand the Master’s meaning. The Master asked, "And what do you say?

An old master came to consult him and asked, "Is it right to prostrate, or is it right not to prostrate? The Master gave a shout. The old master then prostrated.
The Master said, "What a fine bandit! The old master said, "Thief! Thief! and then went out. The Master said, "Do not say it was 'no affair' (wu-shi). At that time...

[The Seat] said, "Both have transgressions. The Master asked, "Where does the transgression lie? The Seat then departed.
The Master said, "Do not say it is good to have nothing to do. (When Nanquan heard this, he remarked: "Official horses trampling one another. The Master went to the capital to beg for alms.
Arriving at the door of a certain house, he said, "Add to your family’s provisions; fill my bowl. A woman said, "You are truly insatiable!
The Master replied, "I have not even received any rice yet; why do you say I am insatiable? The woman then shut the door. The Master ascended the hall. A monk stepped forward, and the Master—
[The Master] shouted. The monk also shouted. [The Master] bowed again, and the Master struck him. When Zhaozhou arrived at the monastery during his travels, he was washing his feet in the rear hall.
The Master asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou replied, "I happen to be washing my feet.
The Master stepped forward and made a gesture as if listening. Zhaozhou said, "If you understand, then you understand; why do you keep picking at it?"
The Master then returned to his quarters. The Governor said, "After thirty years of traveling as a mendicant, today you have erred by providing a commentary for others.
He then questioned a monk: "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Dingzhou. The Master raised his staff; the monk hesitated, and the Master struck him. The monk did not accept this.
The Master said, "In the future, you will surely encounter those with clear eyes. Later, that monk went to visit Sansheng; as soon as he brought up the previous incident...
[The Master] spoke. Sansheng then struck him. As the monk hesitated, Sansheng struck him again. The Master frequently used the shout (*he*) in response to the occasion.
The disciples under his guidance also learned the Master’s shout. The Master said: "If you all simply imitate my shouting, I shall now ask you this:
suppose one person comes out from the East Hall and another comes out from the West Hall, and both shout at the same time—how do you distinguish them here?"
“Have you attained the status of host and guest? For now, how will you distinguish them? If you cannot distinguish them, you must not imitate this old monk’s shouting hereafter.

Addressing the assembly, he said: “Sometimes I first manifest illumination and then function; sometimes I first function and then manifest illumination; sometimes illumination and function occur simultaneously;
and sometimes illumination and function are not simultaneous. When there is one who exists before illumination and after function, that is the former case.”
Later, there was the illumination of existing phenomena; the illumination and its function were simultaneous. It drove the plowman’s ox and snatched the food from the hungry man;

it struck the bone to extract the marrow and applied the needle and awl with piercing pain. When illumination and function are not simultaneous, there is questioning and answering, and the roles of guest and host are established.
Mixing water with mud, he meets beings according to their capacities. If one is a person of superior capacity, they should "spring up and go" even before the staff is raised;

this would still be a slight advantage. When the Master arrived at Longguang, he encountered the abbot ascending the hall. The Master stepped forward and asked, "Without deploying any sharp edge or blade, how does one achieve victory?
Longguang sat firmly in his seat. The Master said, "Great Good Knowledge, do you have no expedient means? Longguang stared at him.
Muzhou said, "Ha! The Master pointed his finger and said, "This old fellow has been defeated today. Next, he arrived at Sanfeng Ping’s place.
Ping asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Huangbo. Ping asked, "What words did Huangbo have for you?

The wind blows through the jade flute; who among them is a connoisseur? The Master said, "It penetrates straight through the ten-thousand-li pass;

The Master asked, "Where has he gone? The woman then walked away. The Master called out to her; she turned her head back, and the Master simply continued on his way. Upon arriving at Fenglin, he said, "He is here."
"May I ask about the characteristics of phenomena? The Master said, "Why do you gouge out flesh to create a wound?

Lin said, "The ocean moon is clear and without shadow; the swimming fish alone is deluded. The Master said, "Since the ocean moon has no shadow, how can the swimming fish be deluded? Lin said: [He remained silent.]
"Observing the wind, one knows the waves arise; gazing at the water, the wild sail drifts. The Master said, "The solitary moon shines alone as the rivers and mountains fall silent;
with one long啸 (shout), heaven and earth turn autumnal. Lin said, "If you will freely wield your three-inch tongue to cast over heaven and earth, try saying a single phrase on the spot.
The Master said, "When meeting a swordsman on the road, one must present a sword; if one is not a poet, one does not offer a poem. Lin then—
"Stop. The Master then uttered this verse: "The Great Way is beyond sameness; it extends freely to the west or east.

The spark of flint cannot catch up; the flash of lightning finds no passage. (Maoshan asked Yangshan: "The spark of flint cannot catch up; the flash of lightning finds no passage. By what means do the sages of antiquity define a person? Yangshan said: "What is your own intention, Preceptor? Maoshan said: "As soon as there is verbal expression, there is no real meaning.

Yangshan said: "Not so. Maoshan said: "And how about you, my son? Yangshan said: "In public, not even a needle is admitted; in private, carts and horses pass through. Magu asked: "The Twelve-Faced Avalokiteśvara..."
Yin asked, "Which one is the front? The Master descended from his meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Where has the Twelve-Faced Avalokiteśvara gone?
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Gu turned around and prepared to sit down; the Master struck him immediately. Gu caught the staff and grappled with him.
Returning to the abbot’s quarters, the Master asked a nun, “Welcome, or unwelcome? The nun gave a shout. The Master raised his staff and said, “Speak further!
Speak further! The nun shouted again. The Master struck her. One day, the Master held up a steamed bun and showed it to Luopu, saying:
The myriad kinds and thousand variations do not depart from this very thing; their principle is non-dual. Baofu asked, “What is this principle of non-duality?
The Master again picked up a cake and showed it to him. Baofu said, “If that is so, then there are still myriad kinds and thousand variations. The Master said, “...[is precisely] non-duality.”
Regarding the "excrement" interpretation, Pu said: "Master Luo gazes into a mirror. When a monk approached, the Master raised his whisk;
the monk bowed, and the Master struck him. Another monk came, and the Master again raised his whisk; the monk paid no heed, and the Master likewise struck him.

(Yunmen spoke on his behalf, saying, "It is only fitting for this old fellow. Dajue said, "He has attained it, yet he still has not seen the pivot of Linji. Magu asked, "Of the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion, which one is the True Eye?

"Quick! Quick! Guze drew the master down from the meditation seat and sat back down. The master asked him a greeting, saying, "How have you been?
Guze was about to deliberate on his response when the master gave a shout. He drew Guze down from the seat again, and Guze immediately left.

Ascending the hall for a discourse, a monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The master held up his whisk. The monk gave a shout, and the master struck him. Another monk asked: "As for..."
"What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master also held up his whisk. The monk then gave a shout. The Master also shouted. The monk hesitated.
The Master struck him and said, "O Great Assembly! One who seeks the Dharma does not shrink from losing body or life.
At the place of my late teacher Huangbo, I asked three times about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, and three times I was struck as if by a bundle of mugwort."

[This was] similar to [the story of] Wufu. Now, thinking of another session, [the Master asked], "Who will take the first stroke? At that time, a monk came forward and said, "I will take the first stroke.
The Master handed him his staff; as the monk reached out to receive it, the Master struck him immediately.

[This was] the same as with Puhua. While attending a donor’s vegetarian feast, the Master asked: "A hair swallows the vast ocean, and a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. Is this the wondrous function of spiritual powers, or..."
Furthermore, this was in accordance with the natural order of things. Huayan kicked over the rice table. The Master said, "You are too crude.

Huayan replied, "What kind of place is this, that you speak of coarse or fine? The next day they went to a meal together again. The Master asked once more, "How does today's offering compare to yesterday's?
Huayan again kicked over the rice table. The Master said, "It is well done, indeed; yet you are still too crude. Huayan [remained silent].
Huangbo said, "Blind fellow! What 'coarse' or 'subtle' is there to speak of regarding the Buddha-dharma?
The Master then stuck out his tongue. The Master and Wang, the Attendant, went to the Sangha Hall. Wang asked, "Do the monks in this hall study the sutras?

"What are you doing? The Master said, "I am teaching them all to become Buddhas and Patriarchs. [The monk] said, "Though gold dust is precious, if it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract.
The Master said, "I took you for a common man. Later, while the Master was ascending the hall, the two head monks of the two halls met and simultaneously let out a shout.
A monk asked, "Does the Master have a guest or a host? The Master said, "Guest."
The Master was clear and decisive. He summoned the assembly and said, "If you wish to understand the Linji phrase of guest and host, go ask the two head seats in the hall.

Later, while residing in the East Hall of Xinghua Temple in Daming Prefecture, on the tenth day of the fourth month of the eighth year of the Xiantong era of Emperor Yizong of the Tang dynasty (the Dinghai year), as he was about to pass away, he spoke this verse of the transmission of the Dharma:

[Zhaozhou] said, "I have nothing to do with whether you succeed or fail. The Master said, "Venerable One, you only know how to pounce on a dead sparrow on the ground;
you do not know how to cover it over with a turning phrase. Zhaozhou asked, "And what about you? The Master said:
"Please act as a new arrival for the Abbot. Jie then said, "A newly ordained monk does not understand.
The Master said, "In fact, this is my own fault. Jie said, "Your words conceal the sharp point. As the Master hesitated, Jie struck him. That evening, Jie spoke again:
"Today when I questioned the new arrival, it was like taking a dying sparrow and flicking it on the ground, or striking it right within its nest. And now, when you came out..."
He obtained the words. Again he shouted, rose up, and struck toward the blue clouds. The Master said, "The grass-thief is utterly defeated. Ji then struck him.
While serving as the head seat (shouzuo) in Sanxing’s assembly, he would often say, "I traveled on foot throughout the South;
wherever my staff’s tip reached, I could not find a single person who understood or could point toward the Dharma. When Sanxing heard this, he asked, "Do you possess..."
"What eye is this? he asked, speaking thus. The Master then gave a shout. Sheng said, "It must be you who can do so.

Later, when Da-jue heard this being cited, he remarked, "How could it have come to blow into the gate of Da-jue? Subsequently, the Master went to Da-jue and served as the head of the monastery (Yuan-zhu).
One day, Da-jue called out, "Head of the monastery! I heard you say that you were traveling southward on pilgrimage."
"Since I first encountered the tip of the staff, I have never once struck anyone who truly understands the Buddha-dharma.
On what basis do you speak in such a manner? The Master then shouted; Jue struck him. The Master shouted again; Jue struck him again.
The next day, as the Master was passing by the Dharma Hall, Jue called out to the Hall Attendant: "I have been harboring doubts about those two shouts you made yesterday. The Master then...
"Ho! Jue struck again. The Master shouted once more, and Jue struck again.

The Master said, "I learned a 'phrase of guest and host' from my elder brother San-sheng, but I have been completely defeated by you, elder brother. I pray you grant me a Dharma-gate of peace and bliss.
Jue said, "You blind fellow! You come here to admit defeat. Take off your patched robe; I shall beat you soundly!"
In a single moment, under these words, the Master realized the principle of how his late teacher Linji had received the blows from Huangbo.
Later, on the day he opened the hall, he offered incense and said: "This one stick of incense was originally intended for my elder brother Sansheng;
yet Sansheng was too close to me. It was originally intended for my elder brother Dajue; yet Dajue was too distant from me. It is better that I offer it..."
While serving his late master Linji, a monk asked, "Before the Many-Sons Stupa, what did you two discuss?

The Master said, "One person transmits the empty; ten thousand people transmit the real. On another occasion, the Master called to a monk. When the monk responded, the Master said, "The point is reached, but it does not arrive.
He then called to another monk. When that monk responded, the Master said, "It arrives, but the point is not reached. A question was asked: "Regarding the four directions and the eight points..."
"How is it when one comes? The Master said, "Strike the one in the middle. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "Yesterday I went to a village feast.
On the way, I encountered a sudden storm of wind and rain, so I took shelter inside an old temple and managed to get through."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the place of Cui Chan.
The Master said, "Did you bring back Cui Chan’s shout? The monk said, "I did not bring it back. The Master said, "In that case, you have not come from the place of Cui Chan.
The monk then shouted. The Master then struck him. Addressing the assembly, the Master said: "I hear that they shout in the front corridor and they shout in the back quarters. My sons, you..."

Do not shout recklessly or shout in disorder. Even if you were to shout until Xinghua were driven into the void and then dashed down so that he had not a single breath left, and once I had recovered and risen, were I to say to you, "It is not yet," why would that be?
It is because I have never yet scattered real pearls from within the purple silk curtain for you all. Why do you shout so recklessly and in disorder?
When Yunju was residing at Sanfeng Hermitage, the Master asked him, "Suppose I borrow a question for you as a mere pretext;
what would you say? Yunju had no reply. The Master said, "I suspect you cannot answer this question, Master. It would be better to bow and withdraw."
Twenty years later, Yung-chü said, "If I were to reflect on it now, it would not even be worth mentioning; one might as well ask, 'Why bother?
Later, a visiting master came to the teacher’s place. The teacher asked, "When you were staying at San-feng Hermitage, I asked you a question and you could not answer it.
Have you been able to answer it by now? The master recounted the previous conversation, and the teacher said, "For twenty years at Yun-chü, you have done nothing but..."
"If you can say it, why bother? Xinghua said, "It is not so. How could it compare to saying, 'There is no need'?
The Master said to Vinaya Master Kebin, "Before long, you shall become a master of the liturgy. Kebin said, "I will not enter this protective community.
The Master asked, "Do you enter it after understanding, or do you enter it without understanding? Kebin said, "In neither way. The Master then struck him and said, "Kebin!"
"Venerable Vinaya Master, you were defeated in the Dharma-battle; you shall be fined five strings of cash and must provide a single meal of steamed rice.

The next day, the Master himself struck the wooden gavel and said, "Vinaya Master Keko, having been defeated in the Dharma-battle, you shall not eat this meal," and immediately expelled him from the monastery.
He then asked National Teacher Huizhao, "What is the meaning of calling for an attendant? The Master replied, "One blind man leading a crowd of blind men. The Master saw [the point].

A fellow practitioner came. As soon as he entered the Dharma Hall, the Master gave a shout. The monk also shouted. The Master shouted again; the monk also shouted. The Master stepped forward and raised his staff.
The monk shouted once more. The Master said, "Look at this blind fellow! He still thinks he is the master. The monk hesitated, and the Master struck him directly.
As they descended from the Dharma Hall, an attendant asked, "What did that monk do to offend you? The Master replied, "He was trying to steal my thunder."
Furthermore, the Master said: "When he came here before, there was both the provisional and the real; there was both illumination and function.
But when I held my hand out horizontally before him, crossing it twice—having reached this point, he could not proceed. It is just like this."
Blind fellow, I do not strike you. When else would I wait? The attendant bowed and asked: "I know that you have long hidden the precious sword;
today, on this very stage, I beg to borrow it for a moment. The Master said: "I will not lend it. The attendant asked: "Why will you not lend it? The Master said: [Silence].
"It is not Zhang Hua’s eye; it is merely peering at the light of the shooting star. The monk asked, "What about one who employs it?

The Master said, "Lying across the body to face the universe—who is the person who puts their head out? The monk then made a gesture of stretching his neck forward. The Master said, "Ha! The monk said, "Yes," and immediately returned to the assembly.
Emperor Zhuangzong of the Tang dynasty traveled by imperial carriage to Hebei. Upon returning to Weifu, he summoned the Master and asked him, "I, the Emperor..."
Having conquered the Central Plains, he obtained a treasure for which no one had ever offered a price.

The Master said, "I beg Your Majesty to examine this treasure. The Emperor extended the ends of his *baku-to* (head-wrap) with both hands. The Master said, "As for the treasure of a sovereign, who would dare offer a price?

[Master Xuanjue’s inquiry: "Tell me, did Xinghua approve [the Emperor's gesture], or did Zhuangzong refuse? If Zhuangzong had approved, where was Xinghua’s eye? If he refused, where lay the fault? The Emperor was greatly pleased and conferred a title upon the Master.

The Master would not accept it, yet they sent the horse anyway. While riding it, the horse bolted in alarm; the Master fell and injured his foot. (In the *Wenyuan Yinghua*, there is a stele inscription for the Xinghua Pagoda composed by Gong Chengyi.

It states that the Master passed away on the twelfth day of the seventh month in the first year of the Wende era of Emperor Xizong of the Tang. The Wende era, marked by the *wushen* cyclical sign, was thirty-six years prior to the *guiwei* year of the Tongguang era of Zhuangzong of the Later Tang. Thus, it is clear this was not Zhuangzong.

Examining the period now, the one wearing the *shu* head-wrap with long tails was likely Prince Li Kuyong, yet he was erroneously identified as his son, Zhuangzong Cunchu. According to the first year of Guangming of Emperor Xizong, the *gengzi* year, Huang Chao entered Chang’an and the Emperor fled to Xing...)

Formerly, Huang Chao usurped the throne for two years. In the second year, the *renyin* year, Li Kuei-yung led the Shatuo troops toward Hezhong. In the third year, the *guiyou* year, in the fifth month, Li Kuei-yung defeated Huang Chao and recovered Chang’an. By imperial decree, Li Kuei-yung was appointed as the Regional Inspector (Jiedushi) of Hedong. In the fourth year, the *jiachen* year, in the fifth month, Huang Chao advanced toward Bianzhou;

Li Kuei-yung pursued and utterly defeated him. In the seventh month of autumn, Shi Pu presented Huang Chao’s head. In the eighth month, Li Kuei-yung was promoted to the title of Prince of Longxi. This is what the *Chuan Deng Lu* refers to as "recovering the Great Liang and obtaining a priceless jewel.

As for the use of such titles as "I" (*zhen*), this is a corruption resulting from the time of Emperor Zhuangzong. Furthermore, the inscription states: "In the eighth month of the first year of Longji, the Great Virtuous One fulfilled the final instructions of his former master."

On the twenty-second day, he burned his own physical body within this monastery; by employing the contemplation of dharmas, he manifested parinirvāṇa. The following year was the Jǐyǒu year, the first year of Emperor Zhāozōng’s reign. This is now verified according to the stupa inscription and the national history, which serve as reliable records. One day, the Master summoned the monastery director and said, "Make me a wooden crutch. When the director had finished it and brought it to him, the Master took it and walked around the monastery. He asked the monks, "Do you recognize this old monk? They replied, "How could we not recognize our teacher? The Master said, "I am already leaving. He then leaned on the crutch and passed away. He was seventy-one years old. His dharma heirs numbered over one hundred. The Master’s secular surname was Lǐ; he was a native of Yángzhōu. His father served as the Prefect of Wúxīng. At the age of twelve, he left home to study under National Teacher Huìzhào at Mount Tiantai. Later, he traveled to the capital and studied under National Teacher Huìzhēn at Mount Wǎngzǔ. At that time, the National Teacher was already advanced in years; he transmitted the Dharma to the Master and appointed him as his successor. The Master then returned to Mount Tiantai to propagate the teachings. He received an imperial decree from Emperor Wénzǔ to reside at Mount Guāngshān. During the Dàtóng era, he was invited to reside at Mount Tiantai. He later moved to Mount Tàizhōng, where he resided for many years. He was summoned by Emperor Mùzōng to reside at Mount Guāngshān. 19. On the twenty-second day of the eighth month of the Jihyou year, the first year of the Longji era of Emperor Zhaozong (the forty-first year of the Xila period), he was cremated.

Chan Master Baoshou Zhao of Zhenzhou (the First Patriarch). A monk asked, “What is it like when the myriad objects of perception come to invade?
The Master said, “Do not concern yourself with them. The monk bowed. The Master said, “Do not touch them; if you touch them, I shall break your waist.

While the Master was sitting in the abbot’s quarters, a monk came to pay his respects. As the monk was inquiring after him, the Master said, “The hundreds of thousands of sages are all entirely contained within this.”
Inside the abbot’s quarters, [a monk] asked, “As for what the ancients said: ‘The great trichiliocosm is but a bubble on the sea’—I wonder where this abbot’s quarters is placed?
The Master said, “A thousand sages are present. The monk asked, “Who can testify to this? The Master then threw down his whisk.
The monk moved from west to east and stood there; the Master struck him. The monk said, “Had you not been a long-time practitioner, how could you have known this?”
"Exactly so. The Master said, "Thirty years from now, these words will spread widely. When Zhaozhou arrived, the Master was sitting on his meditation seat with his back turned.
Zhaozhou unfolded his sitting cloth and prostrated. The Master rose and entered the abbot’s quarters; Zhaozhou gathered up his sitting cloth and departed.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From the Western Mountain. The Master said, "Did you see the monkeys? He replied, "I saw them."
The Master said, "What kind of trickery are you performing? [Hu Dingjiao] replied, "Seeing you, Master, I cannot perform even a single trick.
The Master then struck him. Hu Dingjiao came for an audience. The Master asked, "Are you not Hu Dingjiao? He replied, "I dare not say so.
The Master said, "Can you still nail the void? He replied, "Please, Master, break it open for me. The Master then struck Hu. [Hu] said, "Master..."
"Do not strike me by mistake," [Huai-han] said. The Master replied, "In the future you will have many mouths; I shall break them open for you.
Later, Huai-han went to Zhaozhou and recounted the previous conversation. Zhaozhou asked, "Why were you struck by him? Huai-han said, "I do not know where my fault lay.
Zhaozhou said, "Even this single seam you still cannot manage. At these words, Huai-han attained realization.
Zhaozhou said, "For now, nail down this seam. [Someone] asked, "What is it like when there are no clouds ten thousand miles away?
The Master said, "Even the blue sky must receive a blow of the staff. [The questioner] said, "I do not understand. What fault does the blue sky have? The Master then struck him.
[Someone] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "A dark face and white eyes. [Someone] came from Xiyuan to inquire.
[The monk] asked, "When one has already trampled through the 'transformed city' (the provisional stage), how is it at that moment? The Master said, "I do not spare a man who deserves death.

The monk said, "Kill him! The Master struck him. The monk repeated, "Kill! Kill! and the Master struck him again with each word. The Master then returned to the abbot’s quarters and said, "Just now, this monk..."
To offer raw red meat in exchange for a dry stick—what such urgency could there be?
After receiving the seal of transmission from Linji, Chan Master Huiran of Sansheng Monastery in Zhenzhou traveled extensively through the monastic communities until he reached Yangshan.
Yangshan asked, "What is your name? The Master replied, "Huiji. Yangshan said, "Huiji is my name. The Master...
Yangshan said, "My name is Huiran. The mountain [master] laughed loudly and that was all. Later, when an official came to visit Yangshan, the master asked, "What office do you hold?
The official replied, "I am a *tui-guan* (Investigating Official). Yangshan held up his whisk and asked, "Can you investigate this? The official had no reply.
Yangshan ordered the assembly to offer their own comments, but none were in accord with the truth. At that time, the Master was unwell and was staying in the Nirvana Hall.
Inside, he was resting. Master Shanshan ordered an attendant to go and request a response from the Master. The Master said, "Just say that the Abbot has business today.
Shanshan again ordered the attendant to ask, "I wonder what kind of business it is? The Master said, "He will not tolerate a second offense;
go to Xiangyan. Xiangyan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "From Linji. Xiangyan said, "Have you brought Linji’s shout with you?"
"Ma! The Master struck him across the mouth with his sitting mat. Upon arriving at Deshan, as soon as he spread out his sitting mat, Deshan said, "Do not spread out your cooking cloth;
there is no left-over gruel or stale rice here. The Master said, "Even if there were, there would be no place for it. Deshan then struck him.
The Master caught the staff and pushed it onto the meditation platform. Mountan laughed loudly; the Master wailed, "Heaven! and then went down to attend the hall.
The Head Seat in the hall, nicknamed "Kick-the-Sky Tai," asked, "A high-ranking traveler must possess a certificate of passage from this region.
What is your certificate of passage? The Master said, "What do you mean? The Head Seat asked again, and the Master struck him with his sitting cloth.

[The Master] said: "This lacquer bucket has offended how many worthy and virtuous men from beginning to end! He intends to pay his respects. The Master then proceeded to the second seat to pay his respects.
Upon arriving at Daowu’s [monastery], Daowu knew this in advance; he wore a red head-wrap and stood at the gate holding a divine staff.
The Master said, "Be careful and wait upon me. Daowu responded with an assent. After the Master had finished visiting the hall, he went up again to pay his respects. Daowu...
He assumed the proper dignified demeanor and sat within the abbot’s quarters. As soon as the Master approached him, he said, "May I ask you something?
The Master replied, "That was just now the wild fox spirit," and immediately departed. Later, while presiding over the assembly, he ascended the hall and said, "Whenever I meet someone, I come forth;

but when I come forth, I do not act for others. He then descended from the seat. (Xinghua said: "Whenever I meet someone, I do not come forth; but when I come forth, I act for others. [Question: As for this...
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "A stench draws flies. He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from?
The monk gave a shout. The Master also shouted. The monk shouted again. The Master shouted again. The monk said, "If you strike me with a staff, I will go blind," and he shouted once more.
The Master raised his staff. The monk turned around and made the gesture of receiving the blow. The Master said, "Not running down the slope—such a swift opportunity is hard to encounter.
He then struck him. The monk said, "You thief! and departed. The Master then cast down his staff.
Later, another monk asked, "Just now, why did you allow that monk to get away? The Master said, "It was because he saw the former Master coming."
Dajue Wufu visited Linji. As soon as Linji saw him, he held up his whisk; the Master spread out his sitting cloth. Linji threw down the whisk;
the Master withdrew his sitting cloth and said, "I am going to attend the hall. At that time, the assembly of monks said, "Is this monk perhaps a relative or a personal acquaintance of the Master?
He does not prostrate, nor does he receive a blow of the staff. When Linji heard this, he ordered an attendant to summon the one who had just arrived.
A newly arrived monk came forward. The Master followed the attendant to the Abbot’s quarters.

Jie said, “The assembly says that you have come to visit the Elder, yet you neither prostrate nor accept a blow of the staff; could it be that you are an acquaintance of the Elder? The Master then said, “I take my leave,” and went down.
After the Master had taken up residence there, a monk asked, “What is the original body? The Master replied, “The head rests upon Mount Heng, and the feet [rest upon Mount Heng].”
While traveling to Mount Beiyue, he asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "A fine horse does not wait for the whip; it tilts its ear and knows the master's intent.
He asked, "What is the National Treasure? The Master said, "Pierced ears—unsellable.
He asked, "How is it before the fragrant herb has grown? The Master said, "If you smell it, your brain will split. He asked, "And after it has grown? The Master said—
[The monk] said, "My brain is splitting! [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "At the crossroads.
[The monk] asked, "How is it when one looks toward the sky and offers a prayer? The Master said, "An evil thought. [The monk] said, "This is utterly perverse! The Master then struck him.
[The monk] asked, "What is it like when suddenly coming and suddenly going? The Master said, "The wind blows the willow catkins as they roll away. [The monk] said, "No."
"How is it when there is neither coming nor going? The Master said, "The three peaks of Mount Hua point toward heaven.
"How is it when one has eaten their fill and forgotten a hundred hungers? The Master said, "Even if you encounter food at the crossroads, accept just what is available.
At the time of his passing, he said to the assembly, "I have an arrow that I wish to hand over to someone. At that moment, a monk stepped forward and said, "Please [give it to me]."
"The Master’s arrow. The teacher asked, "What do you call this 'arrow'? The monk shouted. The teacher struck him several times and then returned to his quarters.
He called the monk back in and asked, "Did you understand just now? The monk said, "I did not understand.
The teacher struck him several more times, threw down his staff, and said, "In the future, when you meet someone with clear eyes, explain it clearly to them. Thereupon, he passed away.
Ji. Chan Master Changsha Guankui Zhixian was the son of the Shi family of Guntao in Weifu. In his youth, he followed Boyan to receive the tonsure and the full precepts.
Later, he visited Linji; Linji suddenly grabbed him by the chest, and the Master said, "Understood, understood. Linji let him go and said:
"For now, I let you off with one blow. After the Master left Linji, he went to Mount Mo (the dialogue appears in the "Chapter on Mount Mo").

Following his arrival there, he ascended the hall and said: "At my grandfather Linji’s place, I received half a ladle; at my grandmother Mount Mo’s place, I received half a ladle. Together they make one full ladle.
Having called it 'reaching all the way,' I have been satiated and am not hungry even until now. A monk asked: "I ask the Master for that which is not borrowed."
The Master said, "One cannot say it even with a full mouth. The Master further said, "At the head of Dayu Ridge, the Buddha does not understand;
on the road to Huangmei, there are no sentient beings. A monk in the Master’s assembly went to visit Shishuang. Shishuang asked, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Guankxi.
Shishuang said, "My South Mountain is not as good as his North Mountain. The monk had no reply. Upon returning, the monk related this to the Master.
The Master said, "Why do you not say: 'Guanxi has finished repairing the Nirvana Hall'? [The monk] asked, "I have long heard of Guanxi;
having come here, I see only the hemp-soaking pond. The Master said, "You see only the hemp-soaking pond, but you do not yet see Guanxi."

[The monk] asked, "What is Guankui? The Master said, "As swift as a split arrow. (Later, someone recounted this to Xuansha, who said, "Even after thirty more years of study, you would still not have understood Chan.
[The monk] asked, "What are the bones of the ancients? The Master said, "They cannot be placed. [The monk] asked, "Why can they not be placed?
The Master said, "How could the golden crow be made to descend from the azure sky? [The monk] asked, "After the golden lock is broken, what then? The Master said:
This is precisely the Dharma for you. [A monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Rice is served in the bowl; soup is served in the ladle. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "When hungry, eat; when full, rest. He ascended the hall and said:
"The ten directions have no walls; the four sides have no gates. It is bare and naked, clear and open, with nothing to grasp."
He then descended from his seat and asked, "What is 'one color'? The Master said, "Not following [anything] is 'one color. He asked further, "What comes after that?
The Master said, "Is there a part for you, O *ācārya*, to take up, or not? Another asked, "In this assembly today, whom do we face as our opponent?"
The Master said, "Neither ordinary nor holy. [The questioner] asked, "How is it with one phrase? The Master said, "It does not fall within the reach of the thousand sages.
[The questioner] asked, "What is the water in the cave? The Master said, "It does not wash people.

On the twenty-ninth day of the fifth month in the year of Yimao (875) during the Qianning era of Emperor Zhaozong of the Tang dynasty, the Master asked his attendant, "Who dies while sitting? The attendant replied, "Śākyamuni. The Master said, "Standing [death]."
"Who has died? He replied, "Senghui. The Master then took seven steps, extended his hands, and passed away.
Chan Master Zhiyi Kefu of Zhuozhou initially asked about Linji’s Four Kinds of Critical Examination. Under the Master's words, he attained realization of the essential meaning.
Later, he composed a verse which said: "To take away the person but not the environment— The conditions themselves carry the confusion. If one intends to seek the profound..."
The Essential Meaning. Do you ponder and instead reproach [yourself]? The pearl of the black dragon shines brilliantly; the shadow of the moon on the cassia tree wavers.

Face-to-face, there is no discrepancy; yet one still remains caught in the net. Not taking away the environment, but not taking away the person—searching for the truth in words, where is the reality? To ask about Chan is for Chan to be a delusion; to investigate principle is for the principle to be distant.
The sun shines upon the cold light, which is serene; the mountain sways with fresh verdant hues. Even if you were to directly comprehend the source...

To attain it is but dust in the eyes; when both person and environment are simultaneously stripped away, the authentic command has been exercised from the beginning, regardless of Buddha or Patriarch.

How could one speak of the sentiments of sages or ordinary people? To even attempt to violate it is like encountering a "blind man in the woods" before a hair-cutting sword. To step forward seeking a subtle meeting is to needlessly sever one's own spirit.
When neither person nor environment is stripped away, the intent of contemplation is not biased; in the dialogue between host and guest, words are few.
Different. Question and answer, principle and form, both complete. Treading through the moon in the clear pool; piercing open the sky in the azure void.

Unable to clarify the wondrous function, one sinks and drowns in the absence of conditions. A monk asked, "What is the guest within the guest? The Master said, "Leaning on the gate, hanging by the door;
like one drunk, speaking out, breathing forth without shame. The monk asked, "What is the host within the guest? The Master said:
Murmuring Amitābha’s name with two staffs held in both hands, his eyes are blind and his pupils do not emerge from their sockets.

[The student] asks: "What is the guest within the host? The Master says: "Holding high the ancestral seal, employing it to benefit all beings; you should know that these words carry a tone of compassion.

[The student] asks: "What is the host within the host? The Master says: "Horizontally grasping the Mohe sword, he maintains the full authority of the true command; throughout the peaceful realm, he executes the foolish and the stubborn."

[The questioner] said, "Since this is already a realm of Great Peace, why then do you execute the foolish and obstinate? The Master said, "One is not permitted to travel at night without holding a torch;
one must certainly show oneself to others on the road."
Chan Master Shanshui Cui of Dingzhou was invited by the regional governor, Wang Linggong, to preach the Dharma at his official residence.

The master ascended the seat, took up his staff, and said: "I will strike you if you come forward; I will strike you if you do not come forward. A monk stepped forth and asked, "What about Chan Master Cui?
The master threw down his staff and said, "I have stood here for a long time, Excellency Wang. I pray you, take care. A monk asked: "If [a person] is like this..."
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The ceramic ware of Dingzhou sounds like a bell. The student said, "I do not understand;
what is the intent? The Master said, "Every word is clear and distinct, without any slant or crookedness."
A monk asked Master Wanshou of Zhenzhou, “What is the Kāśyapa robe of supreme practice? The Master said, “A crane flies through a thousand points of snow;
clouds lock ten thousand layers of mountains. The monk asked, “What is the sixteen-foot golden body? The Master said, “Cutting the collar from the sleeves;
scooping the lapel from beneath the armpits. The monk said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “If you do not understand, ask someone else to tailor it for you.”
The Master visited Baoshou. As Baoshou sat without rising, the Master spread out his sitting mat. Baoshou descended from his meditation seat, and the Master sat back down.

Baoshou hurriedly entered the abbot’s quarters and shut the door behind him. When the administrative officials saw that the Master remained seated and did not rise, they said, "We invite the Abbot to come to the storehouse for tea.
The Master then returned to the monastery. The following day, Baoshou came again to pay his respects. The Master sat firmly upon the meditation seat, and Baoshou spread out his sitting mat.
[The Master] was present. The Master also descended from his meditation seat. Shou returned to his seat. The Master went back to his quarters and closed the door.
Shou entered the attendant’s hall, took some ash, circled the Master’s quarters, and then departed. The Master then opened the door and said, "I did not do it that way; he did it that way."
Master Kōng of Tán in Yōuzhōu had a paternal aunt who was a nun. She traveled on pilgrimage and, upon returning, wished to open a hall to teach others.
The Magistrate of Zhēnzhōu ordered the Master to examine her. The Master asked, "I have heard it said that you wish to open a hall to teach others;
is this true? The nun replied, "It is. The Master said, "A nun possesses a body subject to the five obstacles. How will you teach others? The nun replied, "The Dragon Girl."
"At the age of eight, he attained perfect enlightenment in the Southern World of No Defilement. [The monk] asked, "And what about that?
The Master said, "The Dragon Girl has eighteen transformations; try performing one yourself. The nun said, "Even if she were able to transform, she would still be nothing but a wild fox spirit.
The Master then struck her. Upon hearing this, Muzhou said, "If the Master’s staff had broken, it would have been well! A monk asked Deshan:
[A monk] strikes with his staff. Linji shouts. "I wonder which of these is most intimate? The Master said, "Previously, while among the assembly, I too have discussed this.
The monk then shouted. The Master said, "It is you who understand. The monk said, "Wrong! The Master then struck him. He ascended the hall for the discourse.
When the assembly had gathered, a monk stepped forward and said, "What is it like when one intends to ask but does not ask? The Master said, "Aha! The monk then...
"Ho! The Master said. The monk shouted again. The Master raised his staff. The monk said, "Blind man! The Master threw down the staff and said, "Today I have lost.

The monk said, "The grass-thief is utterly defeated," and then returned to the assembly. The Master pointed a single dot toward the sky with his hand and said, "Great assembly, is there anyone who can discern this?
If there is one who can discern it, come forth and speak before the assembly."
"Look," the Master said after a long silence. "The eye upon the crown of the head cannot even be pierced. He then descended from his seat.
Baoshou asked, "When someone comes who lacks both the middle and superior faculties, Elder Brother, what will you do?
The Master said, "You have just now made a mistake in your phrasing. Baoshou said, "Elder Brother, you too cannot be without fault. The Master said, "Then you must act as my teacher."
Brother Shou (Shouxian) slapped his palm and said, "This old thief!
A monk from Lichun Monastery in Xiangzhou asked, "What is it like to attain liberation by observing sounds?
The Master struck a piece of firewood with a poker and said, "Do you hear that? The monk replied, "I hear it. The Master said, "Who, then, is not liberated? [The Master] passed away.
While boiling tea, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master held up the tea scoop.
The monk said, "Is this all there is to it? The Master threw it into the fire.
The Monk Micang of Cangzhou was invited by the provincial governor, along with Baoshou, to enter the hall for a formal offering.
The governor sent a messenger with a message, requesting that the two elders engage in a discussion on the Buddha-dharma. Baoshou said, "I request that you, Elder Brother, provide the response.

The Master (Micang) then gave a shout. Baoshou said, "I have not even asked a question; why do you shout? The Master replied, "You still think this is too little. Baoshou then gave him one [shout] in return.
"Ho! One day, the Master of Mount Jiri in the kingdom of Silla addressed the assembly, saying: "Winter is not cold until after the twelfth lunar month.
He then descended from his seat.
A monk asked Chan Master Chè of Shànquán Mountain in Chángzhōu, “Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
The Master said, “Winter is cold; summer is hot. The monk asked, “What does this mean? The Master said, “On a scorching day, it is fitting to disrobe; after winter, one should hide away even deeper.”
A monk asked Master Jinsha, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Listen.
The monk said, "In that case, the assembly is listening intently. The Master said, "One hundred and eight thousand [miles]."
A monk asked Zen Master Qi Song, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “I do not know at all.

The monk then asked, “What is the Way (*dharma*)? The Master said, “Coming and going without obstruction. He added, “If you suddenly encounter the great ocean, what will you do?”
A fault arose. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him.
When a monk came from the Western Capital to visit Master Yunshan, the Master asked, "Have you brought a letter from the host in the Western Capital?
He replied, "I dare not falsely convey any news. The Master said, "An adept master-monk has a natural presence. The monk said, [yes].
"Who will eat this leftover gruel and stale rice? The Master said, "Only you, Venerable, dare not eat it. The monk then made a gesture of vomiting.
The Master called to his attendant, saying, "Escort this sick monk out. The monk then departed. When the Master saw the monk coming back, he made a gesture of rising;
the monk then departed again. The Master said, "How remarkably quick-witted! The monk then shouted, "Ha!"
To possess such an eye and yet succeed Linji—how utterly a pity! The Master said, "I merely hope that you, Reverend, will transmit this well.
The monk turned his head; the Master shouted, "To possess such an eye and yet misjudge the terminology of all quarters!
He then struck him.
A monk asked the Master of Huxi Hermitage, "How many years have you been here, Master? The Master replied, "I have only seen the withering in winter and the growth in summer;
I do not remember the years at all. The monk said, "Excellent, that you do not remember. The Master said, "What do you say? How many years have I been here?
The monk said, "Withering in winter and growing in summer? The Master said, "A tiger in the midst of a bustling market."
A monk came to visit him. The Master did not look at him. The monk said, "I know that the Hermitage Master possesses such a sharp wit.
The Master snapped his fingers once. The monk asked, "What is your fundamental teaching? The Master struck him. The monk said, "I know that today I have fallen into your trap.
The Master said, "You still want to eat another blow of my staff! Another monk had just entered the gate when the Master shouted. The monk remained silent.
The Master struck him. The monk, in turn, shouted. The Master said, "What a fine petty thief! A monk approached and said, "How do you do, Hermitage Master?
The Master said, "Who is it? The monk then shouted. The Master said, "To act so without guest and host.
The monk said, "I still want a second shout. The Master then shouted. A monk asked, "Where are you from, Preceptor? The Master—
The monk said, "I am from Longxi. The Master asked, "I have heard that Longxi produces parrots—is this true?
The monk replied, "It is. The Master said, "Are you not perhaps a parrot yourself? The Master then made the sound of a parrot. The monk said, "What a fine parrot! The Master then struck him.
The Abbot of Fupo asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "I have come down from Mount Fupo. The Master said, "Did you see the abbot?
The monk gave a shout; the Master struck him. The monk said, "Why did you do that? The Master leaned his staff against the wall. The monk hesitated.
The Master struck him again. One day, a monk came weeping up from the foot of the mountain. The Master shut the door;
the monk drew a circle on the door and stood outside. The Master emerged from behind the hermitage and went back down the mountain weeping.
The monk shouted, "You are still acting as if you were going toward this very thing. The Master then slapped his chest with his hand and said, "What a pity!
My late teacher has been utterly buried by this. The monk said, "Alas! Alas! The Master replied, "The abbot of the hermitage has been deceived."
The Abbot of Tōfū-an asked a monk, "If you suddenly encounter a tiger here, what will you do?
The Master then let out a tiger’s roar. The monk made a gesture of fear. The Master laughed loudly. The monk said, "This old thief! The Master replied, "What can you do about this old monk?
A monk arrived before the hermitage and immediately departed. The Master called out, "Disciple! The monk turned his head back. The Master gave a shout. The Master [laughed].
After a long silence, the monk said, "This old fellow is dead! The Master struck him, and the monk was left speechless. The Master laughed heartily.
Another monk entered the hermitage and seized the Master. The Master cried out, "Help! Help! The monk pushed him away and asked, "Why are you crying out?
The Master said, "Who? The monk then gave a shout, and the Master struck him. As the monk went outside, he looked back and said, "Wait a moment—"
"Wait, wait. The Master laughed heartily. An old man entered the mountain to visit him. The Master asked, "Where do you dwell? The old man did not speak.
The Master said, "You are well able to respond to the occasion. The old man picked up a blade of grass from the ground and showed it to the Master.
The Master then gave a shout. The old man bowed. The Master then returned to his hermitage. The old man said, "In such a way, you leave everyone in doubt."
While at Sōyō-an, a monk arrived to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Who is it? The monk replied, "The abbot of Sōyō-an.
The Master said, "It is I. The monk then gave a shout. The Master made a sighing sound. The monk said, "I still want to eat some blows. The Master then struck him. The monk departed.
The monk asked, "What principle did you realize, Abbot, that led you to dwell on this mountain? The Master said, "I wished to explain my origins, yet I feared being scrutinized by others.
The monk said, "How could you avoid it anyway? The Master gave a shout. The monk said, "Exactly! The Master struck him.
The monk laughed loudly and departed. The Master said, "Today I have been thoroughly defeated."
When the Venerable Ding first visited Linji, he asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?

As he spoke, Linji descended from his meditation seat, seized him, and as the Master hesitated, Linji struck him with a blow. The Master stood there lost in thought. A monk standing nearby said, "Venerable Ding, why do you not prostrate yourself?
Only then did the Master perform a prostration, whereupon he suddenly attained great enlightenment. Later, while traveling south, he encountered Yantou and Xuefeng Qin on the road.
There were three men from Mount [Shishuang]. Yantou asked, "Where have you come from, Senior? The Master replied, "From Linji. Yantou said, "The Master is in full health.
The Master said, "The Master has already passed away. Yantou said, "We three men went specifically to pay our respects."
"Lacking merit, we have not encountered [him]. We do not know what words or phrases the Master spoke during his lifetime;
I request you, Senior, to cite one or two instances. The Master then cited Linji’s ascent to the hall, where he said:

"Upon this lump of red flesh, there is a true person of no rank who constantly enters and exits through the gates of your faces. Those who have not yet attained realization, look! Look! At that time, a monk asked: "As for..."

"What is this 'person of no station'? Linji descended from his meditation seat, grabbed the monk, and said, "Speak! Speak! As the monk hesitated, Linji pushed him away and said, "What is this person of no station?
A dried-up shit-stick! Yantou involuntarily stuck out his tongue. Xuefeng said, "Linji is much like a thief who steals in broad daylight.
Qingshan said, "Why not say that upon the bare flesh-ball there is nothing that is not [the Way]?"

"Regarding the 'true person of no station' (wuwei zhenren): Master [Linji] then seized him and said, 'The true person of no station and that which is not the true person of no station—how much do they differ?
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Qianshan, having been seized, was left with a pale, sallow face and could find no words."
Yantou and Xuefeng said, "This new novice does not know good from evil; he has offended the Senior Monk. We pray you will show him compassion.
The Master said, "Had it not been for these two old fellows, I would have beaten this bed-wetting ghost to death!
While the Master was at a vegetarian feast in Zhenfu, he returned and sat upon a bridge. He encountered three *Zuozhu* (Presidents of the Monastery), one of whom asked, "What is Chan?"
"In the deep part of a river, one must exhaustively reach the bottom. The Master seized him, intending to throw him under the bridge.
The two presiding masters (zuozhu) stepped forward and pleaded, "Please do not take offense at our interruption; we pray you show us compassion.
The Master said, "Had it not been for these two presiding masters, I would have driven him right to the bottom."
When the Venerable Huaihai left Linji to visit Deshan, as soon as Deshan saw him, he descended from his meditation seat and made a gesture of picking up his sitting mat.
The Master said, "Setting this aside for a moment, suppose a person whose mind and environment are one-in-the-same were to come;
what would you say to them so as to avoid being censured by those of all quarters? Deshan said, "I am still three steps ahead of my former self; let me act as your host."
When Huichong arrived, the Master (Nanquan) gave a shout. Huishan remained silent. The Master said, "This has blocked the throat of this old fellow," and he shook his sleeves and departed.

When Guishan heard this being recounted, he said, "Although Upāsaka Huichong gained the advantage, what can he do? It is like covering one's ears while stealing a bell. Upon arriving at Baizhang, after the tea was finished, Baizhang said:

"I have a matter I wish to ask about," [the monk] said. The Master replied, "Fortunately, it is not something that needs words; why do you need this cup of tea? The monk said, "In that case, I am permitted to ask.
The Master said, "Having secured Annam, you still worry about the north of the pass. The Master then opened wide his chest and said:
"Is it thus? Or is it not thus? Zhao said, "In any case, it is difficult to grasp; in any case, it is difficult to grasp. The Master said, "If you know, you will attain it;

if you know, you will attain it. (Yangshan said: "If there were someone who could understand where these two men have fallen, it would be truly extraordinary. If one cannot discern this, it is very much like losing one's way at midday.")
Chan Master Huiyong of Nanyuan (also known as Baoying) of Ruizhou,
a successor in the sixth generation under Chan Master Xinghua Jiang of Nan Yue, ascended the hall and said: "The various quarters possess only the 'simultaneity of the peck and the hatch.'"
The Eye does not possess the function of "the simultaneous act of pecking and hatching. A monk asked, "What is the simultaneous act of pecking and hatching?
The Master said, "A master does not peck; at the moment of pecking and hatching, it is lost. The monk said, "That is still the place where a student asks. The Master said:
"What is it that you ask? The monk said, "The Master has been lost," and Nanquan struck him. The monk did not accept this;
later, he went to Yunmen’s assembly and recounted the previous incident, expressing his dissatisfaction. At that time, a bystander said, "At that moment, Nanquan’s staff must have broken!
Upon hearing these words, the monk attained great enlightenment at once, finally seeing the point of Nanquan’s response. The monk then returned to Nanquan.
He went to Ruzhou to pay his respects at the ancestral hall, but finding that Nan’uan had already passed away, he went instead to Fengxue to pay his respects.
Recognizing him immediately, Fengxue asked, “Is the Venerable the one who previously questioned Nan’uan about the saying, ‘The hen and the chick peck at the same moment’?
The monk replied, “I am. Fengxue said, “Do you understand it yet? The monk said, “I understand. Fengxue asked, “How was it then? The monk said, “At that time...”
"It is like walking within the shadow of a lamp. Xue said, "You understand. Question: "What is it like when the Great Function does not encounter anyone?
The Master said: "Cocks and geese dance upon the Way; they lead one into a thousand peaks. Question: "What is it like when the ten directions are thoroughly open? The Master said:
"Calamity extends from the eight extremities to the very gate. Question: "What is it like when the dragon leaps forth from the rivers and streams? The Master said: [Silence].
Suddenly showing anger, suddenly showing joy, he asked: "What is it like when the hills and rivers are overturned? The Master said: "An old crow has no beak. [The monk] asked:
"Do you see the point where the ancients of old failed to exhaust it? The Master said: "One who grasps his hair and spits out his food is not looked upon;
the whole court says only that Zhou Gong was good. The monk struck him on the mouth. The Master said: "This practitioner is great!"
“Blind! Blind! [The Master] said. “Is there such a blind old man who speaks like that? The Master then struck him.
A monk asked, “Where have all the sages of the past gone? The Master said, “Not to heaven, but straight into hell. The monk asked, “What about you, Master?
The Master said, “Do you know where the Old Man Baoying has ended up? As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him.
He gave a strike with his whisk and said, "Do you know who it is that eats the whisk? The monk said, "I do not understand.

The Master said, "The true command is actually being carried out by you," and he struck him again with the whisk. A monk asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "Try saying it yourself. The monk then shouted.
The Master clapped his hands and said, "The assembly, what a fine shout! The monk shouted again, and the Master struck him.
Question: "What is it like when circling through the air? The Master said: "Striking continuously from all four sides. Question: "What is it like when the dragon and the beast entwine?
The Master said: "At the crest of Dog Ridge Slope. Question: "What is it like when walking alone across the crimson sky? The Master said: [Silence].
The student asked: "Running five hundred li a day—how does one's name appear upon the golden list? The Master said: "Dragging one’s feet beneath the sun. The student asked:
"A great thunderclap and a rainbow—please, Master, provide a verification. The Master said: "Three *ke* (fifteen minutes) beneath the sun.

The student asked: "After Huang Chao has passed by, where can one find refuge? The Master said: "Beneath the six-pronged military banner. The student asked: "What if you are suddenly caught? The Master said: [Silence].

The Master said, "When a white dog faces execution, do not resent Heaven. "Question: When a person encounters the emerald..."
"How is it when the eye is active? The Master said, "Ghosts quarrel over a lacquer bucket. "Question: How is it when walking alone across the azure sky?

The Master said, "Having struck, he drags out the resonance. "Question: The Phoenix perches..."
"Before one has even arrived, what then? The Master said, "Suddenly hearing an old owl being struck down in the courtyard.
"Question: What is the state where the principle and phenomena of Guizong are cut off? The Master said, "A mistake at the place of Na Ru. "Question: What is it like when the sun is exactly at noon?
The Master said, "Principle and phenomena are very clear," and he struck him. "Question: What is it like to walk alone through the four quarters? The Master said, [and struck him].
At the mountain peak, the Master said: "Walking on the bottom of the deep sea. [Question: "What is it like to be as free and easy as a lion?
[Master: "A golden hammer restrains his throat; with a white staff, he is led forth. Ascending the hall, he said:
"All of you have traveled back and forth among all quarters. It is not that you do not know or see; do you know that I here have a taboo name?"
A monk then asked, "Please tell me your honor’s name. The Master said, "Calculating and resolving doubts. The monk asked, "What is the *campaka* grove? The Master said, "The demon-averting arrow.
The monk asked, "What is the Immovable Honored One (*Akṣobhya*)? The Master said, "Running straight into Yazu Prefecture.
The monk asked, "When one intends to cross the vital ford, what then? The Master said, "A heap of ashes and dung. The monk asked, "When all is finished and everything is done..."
“What was it like at that time? The Master said, “Not yet a master hand. “Regarding the struggle for power during the Great Meaning (Dà-yì), how should one respond?
The Master said, “The light lacquer meets the community. “How will you present your offering? The Master said, “I offer fresh grass; the only thing suitable is donkey dung.

“The figures are depicted on the Stele of the Virtuous (Lín-gé); I beg the Master to show compassion. The Master said, “A silk sash brushes against the dust on his face. [Question: ... The Master said, “... [The text here appears to be truncated.]
"What is the beverage of liberation? The Master said, "The reeds are soaked in blood; the contents of the ritual vessels are not many.
A monk asked, "What is the indestructible diamond body? The Master said, "I am beneath your feet. The monk then shouted. The Master said, "Not yet.
The monk shouted again, and the Master struck him. A monk asked, "What is it like when the sun rises over Mount Fūsang? The Master said, "Jambudvīpa."
[The Master] was passing beneath a tree. [A monk] asked, "How is it when ordinary people and sages dwell together? The Master said, "Two kittens, one ferocious.
[A monk] asked, "What is it like when the sandalwood is dense and thick? The Master said, "Sitting alone beneath a willow tree.
[A monk] asked, "What is it like when one cannot draw near? The Master said, "An enemy difficult to escape. [A monk] asked, "Today at the Dragon Gate ten thousand fathoms high..."

*Shao Wei*: Question: "When one moves one's feet but does not know the path, what is it like? The Master said: "The Bird-path; the blind man meeting [the way].
Upon entering the hall, those from all quarters are all grasping at the head of a snake seeking rest; they ultimately do not dare to answer the guest’s question from the second head.
If you are a monk of true substance, then do not speak with them. What is a monk of true substance?
After a long silence, he said, "There is winning and there is losing. A Defense Commissioner asked, "Venerable sir, do you still possess seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing?

The Master gave him a kick, knocking him over. He then asked the garden keeper, "Has the gourd flowered yet? The keeper replied, "It has been flowering for some time.
