The Master gave him a kick, knocking him down. He then asked the garden keeper, "Has the gourd flowered yet? [The keeper] said, "It has been flowering for a long time. The Master said, "Has it set fruit yet? [The keeper] said, "Yesterday it was hit by frost. The Master said:
"What will the great assembly eat? A monk hesitated, and the Master struck him. He asked Fengxue, "Regarding the single blow in the South, how do you deliberate upon it?
Fengxue said, "I deliberate upon it as something extraordinary. Fengxue then asked the Master, "How do you deliberate upon the single blow here?
The Master took up his staff and said, "Under the blow is the patience of non-arising; at the moment of action, there is no yielding."
On one occasion, seeing a group of monks coming for an audience, the Master seized the head monk and asked, "What is this?
The monk was speechless. The Master said, "For thirty years I have been riding a horse; today I have been thrown by a donkey. He then said to himself, "O assembly, do not say these are idle words.
He questioned another monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Xiangzhou. The Master asked, "What thing comes in such a manner? The monk replied:
"Try saying something, Master," the monk said. The Teacher replied, "The one who just prostrated himself. The monk said, "Wrong. The Teacher asked, "In what way is it wrong?
The monk said, "A second offense will not be tolerated. The Teacher said, "After thirty years of riding horses, today you have been thrown by a donkey.
You blind fellow, go to the meditation hall!"
Attendant Shoukuo asked Deshan, "Where have all the sages of the past gone? Deshan said, "What? What?
The Master said, "The imperial decree summons the flying dragon horse, yet the lame turtle sticks its head out. Deshan then ceased speaking.
The next day, after Deshan had finished his bath, the Master passed him tea. Deshan patted him on the back once and said, "Yesterday’s case."
"How is it? The Master said, "This old fellow has only just begun to see clearly today. Then Shanshan also withdrew.
Later, the Master traveled on pilgrimage to the assembly of National Teacher Huayan in Xiangzhou.
One day, Huayan ascended the hall and said, "If you people here today were the descendants of Linji, Deshan, Gaoteng, Dayu, Niaoke, or Chuanzi, there would be no need for this. What then?"

"How so? [Huayan] replied. "Then I shall request you to enter directly with a single blade; Huayan will provide you with evidence. The Master stepped forward to prostrate. As he rose, he let out a shout.
Huayan also shouted. The Master shouted again. Huayan also shouted. The Master rose from his prostration and said, "Great assembly, look at this old fellow’s total defeat!
He let out another shout, clapped his hands, and returned to the assembly. Huayan descended from his seat and retired to the abbot's quarters. At that time—
Fengxue served as the *karmadāna* (rector). When he went up to inquire after [Master Yan’s] well-being, Yan said, "Karmadāna, it is intolerable that you have come here.
Just now, Shoukuo was twisting and squeezing me; I am going to assemble the community and give him a beating to drive him out.
Fengxue said, "It would be too late to drive him out. It is simply that you, Master, have spoken too harshly. He is a descendant of Linji; his fundamental nature is such."
Moyan said, "Yanguan, cease your anger and come down from the niche. He then recounted the incident to the Master. The Master said, "For what reason did you try to dissuade this fellow?

Chan Master Siming of West Court in Ruzhou, successor to Chan Master Baoshou Zhao, was asked by a monk: "What is the monastery? The Master said: "A thicket of brambles. The monk asked:
"Who are the people within the monastery? The Master said: "Badgers and raccoon dogs. [The monk] asked: "What is..."
[The Master asked about] "the unchanging substance. The Master said, "Strike the stone with the silk cloth. [The monk] asked, "What is Linji’s one shout?
The Master said, "A crossbow of a thousand *jin* does not fire its trigger for a field mouse. [The monk] asked, "Wherein lies the compassion of the Monk? The Master then struck him.
Congyi had been at the Dharma seat for ten days when he constantly said to himself, "Let alone those who claim to understand the Buddha-dharma; even to seek [it]..."
"There is not even a single person who can raise this story. When the Master heard this, he remained silent. On another day, while they were ascending the Dharma Hall, the Master called out, "Congyi!
Congyi looked up. The Master said, "Wrong! Congyi took two or three steps forward. The Master said again, "Wrong! Congyi approached him.
The Master said, "Those two 'wrongs' just now—was it the Venerable Upadhyaya who was wrong, or was it the old fellow Ximing? He replied, "It was [the old fellow]."
Yi made a mistake. The Master said, "A mistake, a mistake. Yi then said, "Venerable Sir, please stay here for the summer retreat; we shall deliberate together on these two mistakes.
Yi was unwilling and departed. Later, while residing at Tianping Mountain in Xiangzhou, he would frequently cite this previous conversation, saying:
"When I was traveling on foot, I was driven by a fierce wind and arrived at Ruizhou. There was an elder of the West Court who examined me and found two consecutive errors.
He then asked me to stay for the summer retreat, saying he wished to deliberate with me. I did not say that I was mistaken at that time;
rather, I knew I was mistaken as soon as I set out toward the south. (Shoushan Nian said: "According to Tianping’s understanding, he has not even dreamed of the West [Court].")
[The Master asked: "What is the reason for being in this monastery?

[Baoshou] was the second-generation abbot at Baoshou Temple. At that time, the Master served as the *kōmyōshu* (officiant for offerings). Baoshou asked, "Before your parents were born, bring me back your original face.
The Master stood there until deep into the night, but his response did not accord with the kōan. The following day, he took his leave.
He departed. Baoshou asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "Yesterday I received the Master’s questions, but I did not find them resonant.
I am going south to visit spiritual teachers. Baoshou said, "In the south, they prohibit the summer retreat but not the winter;

here in my place, we prohibit the winter but not the summer. For now, you should spend the summer as a wandering mendicant. As for the Buddha-dharma, it is vast and expansive even amidst the bustling marketplace."
In the midst of the red dust of the world, he constantly preached the True Dharma, and his disciples did not dare to disobey him.

One day, seeing two people quarreling on the street, he struck out a single fist and said, "How can you be so shameless? At that moment, the Master attained great enlightenment. He hurried to see Baoshou;
before he could utter a word, Baoshou said, "You have understood it; there is no need to speak. The Master then prostrated himself. This was when Baoshou was about to pass away.
At that time, San-sheng was commissioned to request the Master to open the hall for formal teaching. On the day the Master opened the hall, San-sheng pushed forward a monk;
the Master struck him immediately. San-sheng said, "To act as a teacher in such a manner will not only blind this monk’s eyes, but will also blind the people of the entire city of Zhenzhou.
(Fayan asked: "Where is it that he blinds the people's eyes? The Master threw down his staff and returned to his quarters.
A monk asked, "Without occupying the threshold, I ask that you do not slander me. The Master said, "Do not.
[The monk asked,] "When various adornments are offered with great sincerity, what then? The Master said, "Do not defile my field of mind.

As the Master was about to pass into *parinirvāṇa*, he said to his disciples, "Do you know where I have been walking? They replied, "We know, O Monk; you sit constantly and do not lie down. The Master said, [“That is so.”]
Again, he summoned a monk to come forward. As the monk approached, the Master said, "Depart; you are not of my kin. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
Zen Master Sansheng Ruan was a dharma successor of Venerable Dabe of Zhenzhou.
A monk asked, "Setting aside 'above' and 'below,' please, Master, speak otherwise. The Master said, "Open your mouth."
The monk immediately made a mistake. [The Master] said, "Truly, you are a teacher of students. The Master said, "Today you died at the hands of this disciple.
[The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s secret function? The Master raised his staff. The monk turned his body and received the blow.
The Master threw down the staff and said, "I will not strike this dead man. [The monk] asked, "What are words of ultimate truth? The Master said, "The tongue pressed against the palate."
[The Master] struck the upper palate. [The monk] asked, "Why is it thus? The Master then struck him. A monk asked, "What is the realm of great compassion?
The Master said, "When a thousand eyes come together, they are all gathered in one. [The monk] asked, "What is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Hands flustered and feet in disarray.
A monk asked, "Without falling into the categories of saint or ordinary, I request the Master to provide an answer. The Master said, "A fine monk! As the monk hesitated, the Master gave a shout.
A monk asked the Waterland (Shuilu) Worthy of Zizhou, “What is the place where a student applies the mind? The Master said, “To apply the mind is an error.
The monk asked, “What is it like when not a single thought arises? The Master said, “You useless fellow! Another asked, “How does one maintain this matter?
The Master said, “By all means avoid it! Another asked, “What is the very first phrase? The Master then gave a shout.
The monks prostrated. The Master pointed with his whisk and said, "Let this pass for now. He asked, "What is it like when meeting on a narrow path?
The Master then thrust his chest forward, pushing him away.

A monk asked the Abbot Dajue of Luzhou, a successor of the Abbot Dajue of Weifeng: "When Niutou had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch, why did birds and beasts bring him flowers? When he went to serve as a Daoist priest, he did not succeed at his first attempt and subsequently left the household life. He took refuge with Master Zhigong at Kaiyuan Temple in his native province, where he shaved his head and received full ordination.
There, he studied the *Tiantai* system of *śamatha-vipaśyanā*. At the age of twenty-five, he visited Jingqing, who asked him, "Where have you recently departed from?"
The Master said, "Since leaving the East, [I have come]. Qing asked, "Did you cross the Xiao River?

The Master said, "Even the vast ocean fears the power of the *meng-lun* warship; with sails flying toward the Milky Way, one crosses the Five Lakes. Qing stood upright.

Lotus Eyes looked toward the assembly and said, "At this very moment, tell me, what is being said?
If you say that it is 'speaking without speaking,' that would be to obscure the former sages. So, tell me, what is being said? The Master then shook his sleeves and went down;
Xue threw down his staff and returned to the abbot’s quarters. A attendant followed him to request further instruction, saying, "Nianfa..."
Fahua did not respond to the Master. Xue said, "I am mindful of the Dharma Flower Assembly.
The following day, while the Master and Zhen the garden supervisor were together paying their respects, Xue asked Zhen, "What is the meaning of 'The World-Honored One’s non-speaking speech'?"
Zhenshu said, "The sparrow cries atop the tree. Xue said, "Why do you perform so much foolish merit?
Why do you not investigate the meaning of these words? He then asked the Master, "How about you? The Master said, "Moving the countenance to reveal the ancient road;
not falling into the silent mechanism. Xue said to Zhenshu, "Why do you not look at the sub-commentary on the *Lotus Sūtra*? The Master received [the transmission from] Fengxue.
After receiving this seal of approval, he obliterated his traces and concealed his brilliance; no one knew the reason why.

When Baimiao Chu arrived at Xuanhua in Ruizhou, Fengxue ordered the Master to go there and deliver a message. As soon as they met, [the Master] raised his sitting cloth and asked, "If you unfold it, that is one thing;
if you do not unfold it, what then? Chu said, "Look for yourself. The Master then gave a shout. Chu said, "I have personally experienced this..."
A close acquaintance arrived. [Zhao] had never before dared to act so hastily. The Master said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated.
Zhao said, "If I see Fengxue tomorrow, I shall report this to him in detail. The Master said, "Do as you wish; do not forget it.
The Master then returned first and reported the matter to Fengxue. Fengxue said, "Today, you have once again captured another officer for me."
"Cowardly thief," the Master said. "A true master does not flaunt his name. On the following day, as soon as Chu arrived to meet him, he brought up the previous conversation.
Xue said, "Not only yesterday; today I have caught you red-handed with the evidence. Thereupon, the Master's fame resounded throughout the four quarters, and students bowed before his reputation.
He established the Dharma at Shou Shan, serving as its first patriarch. Upon entering the monastery and ascending the hall, he spoke of the Buddha-dharma.
He entrusted [the Dharma] to kings, ministers, and powerful patrons, causing the Buddha-Dharma not to be severed, with lamp after lamp continuing until the present day.
The assembly, tell me: what was it that continued? After a long silence, he said:
"It must have been Elder Kāśyapa. At that time, a monk asked: "What was different about this assembly on Vulture Peak compared to today? The Master said: "Falling into a pit."
[The Master] fell into the moat. [The monk] asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "Blind. [The monk] asked, "Whose song do you sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed?
The Master said, "It was personally handed down before the cliff of Shaoshi. [The monk] said, "I request you to harmonize one note with a grand voice."
The Master said, "Even now, I wish for everyone to know. Question: "What is the direct path?
The Master said, "Sometimes in the mountains; sometimes under a tree. Question: "What is the point of intimacy for the student? The Master said:
"Five nines end the day, yet spring meets again. [The student] asked, "Ultimately, what is the matter? The Master said, "When winter arrives, it is one hundred and five days until Cold Food Festival.
[The student] asked, "What is the patriarchal style of the Master's house? The Master said, "A single word cuts off the mouths of a thousand rivers."
"Only at the foot of the Ten-Thousand-Fathom Peak do you first attain the Origin. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Shoushan? The Master said, "Let everyone look as they please.
The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Have you finished eating the staff yet? The monk bowed.
The Master said, "As for eating the staff, wait for another time. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The wind."
Chui Rizhi asked, "Where do all the sages of antiquity practice? The Master said, "Plowing with the plow and pulling the handle.
He asked, "What was the meaning of the ancients striking the mallet and raising the whisk? The Master said, "The solitary peak has no overnight guests."
[The student] said, "I do not yet understand the meaning of this. The Master said, "One who merely waits by the stump [will not find the hare].

[The student] asked, "What is the path to Bodhi? The Master said, "It is five li from here to Xiang County. [The student] asked, "How is it regarding the matter that transcends [this level]? The Master said, "Coming and going are no easy matters.
[The student] asked, "Please, Master, proclaim that which has not been reached by the various sages. The Master said, "The divine light extends ten thousand miles."
A single universal illumination. Who dares to rival the sun? Question: Regarding Linji’s shout and Deshan’s staff, what matter do they clarify?
The Master said: "Try saying something yourself. The monk then shouted. The Master said: "Blind! The monk shouted again.
The Master said, "You blind fellow, why do you shout so recklessly? The monk bowed, and the Master struck him.
A monk asked, "The Master is a great *kalyāṇamitra*; why then do you guard the mountain? The Master said, "I do not sit atop the solitary peak; I always keep company with the idle white clouds.
A monk asked, "When the fourfold assembly surrounds you, what Dharma do you preach? The Master said, "Striking the grass, the snake is startled. [The monk] said, "Not yet."
"Examine it thoroughly: how do you apply yourself? The Master said, "Just now, how nearly you lost your life! Question: "When two dragons contend for the pearl, who is the one that obtains it?
The Master said, "The one who obtains it loses. Question: "What about the one who does not obtain it? The Master said: [He too loses.]
"Where is the pearl? [The student] asked, "All Buddhas emerge from this sutra.
What is this sutra? The Master said, "Lower your voice, lower your voice. [The student] asked, "How should it be upheld? The Master said, "One must not let it be defiled.
[The student] asked, "After the World-Honored One’s parinirvāṇa, to whom was the Dharma entrusted? The Master said, "A fine question; no one can answer it. [The student] said, "..."
"What is the World-Honored One’s 'not-speaking speech'? The Master said, "Let the vast ocean change as it may;
I shall never explain it for you. "What is Kāśyapa’s 'hearing what is unheard'? The Master said, "The deaf man merely tilts his ears in vain.

A questioner asked, "An ancient said, 'When seeing form, one sees the mind. Since all dharmas are formless, with what is there anything to see? The Master said, "There is trouble within the household."

The masters of the hundred schools were busy. [A monk] said, "I, this student, do not understand. I beg the Master to point it out again. The Master said, "Look after three days. [The monk asked: "What is it like when a Bodhisattva has not yet attained Buddhahood? The Master said, "Sentient beings. [The monk asked: "What is it like after attaining Buddhahood? The Master said, "Sentient beings, sentient beings. [The monk asked: "When meeting a person who has reached the Way, one does not respond with speech or silence. I wonder, what should one use instead? The Master said, "Do not speak. The monk said, "If I do not speak, am I not still responding? The Master said, "That is precisely why I told you not to speak. The monk said, "If I do not speak, I have no fault. The Master said, "If you do not speak, you will surely fall into hell. The monk said, "Even if I fall into hell, I would rather be there than speak. The Master said, "You are truly a person who has reached the Way. The monk bowed. The Master said, "You have just now met a person who has reached the Way. The monk said, "I have already met him. The Master said, "Where did you meet him? The monk said, "I met him right here. The Master said, "If so, why did you ask me about it? The monk said, "I was just testing the Master. The Master said, "You have been testing me for a long time; I have been testing you for a long time as well. The monk said, "Who is the one testing? The Master said, "You yourself are the one being tested. The monk said, "If that is so, then who is the one testing the Master? The Master said, "I do not know. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be a person who has reached the Way? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am a person who has reached the Way. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you teach others? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I can teach others. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you save sentient beings? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I can save sentient beings. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you attain Buddhahood? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I can attain Buddhahood. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you enter Nirvana? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I can enter Nirvana. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be called a Buddha? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am called a Buddha. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you preach the Dharma? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I can preach the Dharma. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you transform beings? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I can transform beings. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be a teacher of men? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am a teacher of men. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be a guide to the world? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am a guide to the world. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be a refuge for all beings? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am a refuge for all beings. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the ultimate truth? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the ultimate truth. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the source of all dharmas? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the source of all dharmas. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the root of all Buddhas? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the root of all Buddhas. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the foundation of all phenomena? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the foundation of all phenomena. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the treasury of the eye of the true Dharma? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the treasury of the eye of the true Dharma. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great sun of wisdom? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great sun of wisdom. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great moon of compassion? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great moon of compassion. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great wind of liberation? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great wind of liberation. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great earth of endurance? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great earth of endurance. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great ocean of samādhi? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great ocean of samādhi. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great mountain of dhyāna? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great mountain of dhyāna. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great fire of prajñā? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great fire of prajñā. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great water of purity? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great water of purity. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great space of emptiness? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great space of emptiness. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great mirror of the mind? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great mirror of the mind. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great sword of wisdom? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great sword of wisdom. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great bow of skillful means? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great bow of skillful means. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great arrow of the Dharma? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great arrow of the Dharma. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great chariot of the Path? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great chariot of the Path. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great horse of non-attachment? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great horse of non-attachment. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great elephant of patience? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great elephant of patience. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great lion of fearlessness? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great lion of fearlessness. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great dragon of transformation? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great dragon of transformation. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great phoenix of enlightenment? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great phoenix of enlightenment. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great jewel of the Dharma? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great jewel of the Dharma. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great medicine of liberation? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great medicine of liberation. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great vessel of the Way? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great vessel of the Way. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great lamp of wisdom? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great lamp of wisdom. The monk said, "If you do not know, how can you be the great bridge of the Path? The Master said, "Because I do not know, I am the great bridge of the Path. The monk said
"What is the correspondence? The Master said, "In a mere flash, the three thousand worlds. [The student] said, "If it is so, then even looking with one's eyes is unnecessary.
The Master said, "The imperial grace has not yet been encountered; once regret arises, it is difficult to pursue. Ascending the hall, he said:

"If you realize the first phrase, you are fit to be a teacher to the Buddhas and Patriarchs. If you realize the second phrase, you are fit to be a teacher to humans and devas. If you realize the third phrase, you yourself—"
[He] could not save him. At that time, a monk asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "The Great Function does not raise an eyebrow;
under the staff, blood must be seen. [The monk] asked, "Where is the compassion? The Master said, "Send him out through the three gates. [The monk] asked, "What is the second phrase?
The Master said, "I would not strike such a donkey-like fellow. [The monk] asked, "Whom do you intend to receive? The Master said, "Like..."
"How can this dispute be resolved? [The monk] asked. "What is the third phrase? The Master said, "There is no one to answer though you ask.
[The monk] asked, "Who is it that is responding right now? The Master said, "Do not let outsiders know. [The monk] asked, "To which phrase does the Master’s realization belong?
The Master said, "The moon sets at the third watch as he passes through the marketplace. He then asked about Vimalakīrti’s silence and Mañjuśrī’s praise of its excellence.
"I do not understand the meaning of this; how is it so? The Master said, "The audience at that time certainly was not like this.
[The monk] asked, "If it was not like this, then what about Vimalakīrti’s silence? How was that? The Master said, "Those who recognize kindness are few; those who betray kindness are many.
He then said, "As for this matter, in truth, it does not even touch upon a single character of the word 'origin' (yuan). Thereupon, he descended from his seat. [A monk] asked, "How is it?"
“This is the mind of the ancient Buddhas. The Master said, “The radish from Zhenzhou weighs three jin. A monk asked, “What is the center of the mystery?
The Master said, “If there are words, you must speak them. The monk asked, “What is the meaning of this? The Master said, “Without words, even a ghost would be angry.
The monk asked, “What is the eye of the patch-robed monk? The Master said, “This question is inappropriate. The monk asked, “What is it after it has become appropriate? The Master—

[The monk] asked, "What can one do? [The Master] said, "A rare encounter once every thousand years. [The monk] asked, "How does one attain freedom from all conditions? The Master said, "Standing before the multitude.
[The monk] asked, "How about when one is not separated [from conditions]? The Master said, "Standing before the multitude.

[The monk] asked, "Who is the person of great peace and bliss? The Master said, "Not seeing a single dharma. [The monk] asked, "On what basis do you designate them as a person? The Master said, "Thank you, Dharma brother."
**Inquiring into the Words:** A questioner asked, "What is the person who is always present? The Master said, "Why are you running about so restlessly? A questioner asked, "What is Shoushan?
The Master said, "The eastern mountain is high; the western mountain is low. [The questioner] asked, "What is it like for one among the mountains?
The Master said, "It happens exactly when the staff is not there. A questioner asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "There is fire within the brazier, yet it is without intention."

He brushed it aside. He wandered freely wherever he pleased, moving horizontally and vertically at will. A monk asked, "What is it like for one on the Way? The Master said, "Sitting and watching the beauty of the mist and clouds;
they do not compete with the white clouds. A monk asked, "How is it when not even a single hair has been stirred? The Master said, "Meeting a traveler with pierced ears on the road.
The monk asked, "And after it has been stirred? The Master said, "There is no need to hesitate further. A monk asked about the "stringless" [lute]. The Master said, "One..."

[The student] bowed and requested the Master’s voice. After a long silence, the Master asked, "Do you hear it? [The student] replied, "I do not hear it. The Master said, "Why do you not ask with a loud voice?
[The student] asked, "A student has long remained in deep delusion; I beg the Master for a single encounter. The Master said, "This old monk has no leisure for such things.
[The student] said, "Does the Monk have no skillful means? The Master said, "If you wish to walk, then walk; if you wish to sit, then sit."
Zuò asked, "What is the phrase that transcends both the ordinary and the sage? The Master said, "Venerable An of Mount Sōng. Zuò said, "Is this not the ultimate point of the Master?
The Master said, "Master Ràng of Mount Nányuè. Zuò asked, "A student has newly entered the monastic community;
I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "How long has it been since you arrived here? Zuò replied, "It has already been..."

[The Master asked about] winter and summer. The Master said: "Do not mistakenly present this to others. A questioner asked: "When there is a person who has come having exhausted everything, will you still receive them?
The Master said: "Setting aside the 'exhaustion,' who is that one person? The questioner said: "The wind is high and the moon is cold. The Master said: "..."
"How many people are sitting or lying down in the Sangha hall? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "I have been cheated by this old monk.

A monk asked, "What is the mark of the Brahma-sound? The Master said, "The braying of donkeys and the barking of dogs. He then said, "If you wish to attain intimacy, first of all, do not bring questions to ask.
Do you understand? The question is in the place of the answer; the answer is in the place of the question. If you bring a question to ask..."
"The old monk is beneath your feet. If you hesitate, there will be no connection. At that time, a monk came forward and bowed; the Master struck him.
The monk then asked, "What is it like when one hangs up one's staff in a secluded crag? The Master said, "Wrong. The monk said, "Wrong. The Master struck him again. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "The daughter-in-law rides the donkey while the mother-in-law leads her. The monk asked, "I do not understand."

"In what category of phrase is this statement included? The Master said, "It cannot be contained within the three essentials; how could it be encompassed by the four propositions? [The student] asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "Heaven is long and earth is enduring; the sun and moon shine together. [The student] asked, "What is the one phrase of Caoxi?"
“The people of the world have heard [of you], but I do not know who it is that hears a single word of the Master.
The Master said, “It does not go outside the three gates. [The monk] asked, “Why does it not go outside the three gates? The Master said, “To be made known to the people of the world.
[The monk] asked, “What is the Master’s eye that does not deceive people? The Master said, “Look! Look! Winter is coming. [The monk] asked, “Ultimately? The Master said, “Look!”
“How is it? the Master asked. The monk said, “I have heard from afar that the Master has no thread upon which to hang anything;
yet now that I have arrived, why is there a mountain to be guarded? The Master said, “What do you say? The monk gave a shout.
The Master also shouted. The monk bowed. The Master said, “I grant you thirty blows. Subsequently, he resided at Guangjiao and Baoying for three years.

At the Dharma Seat. On the fourth day at the hour of the horse (noon) in the twelfth month of the Renchen year of the Chunhua era of Emperor Taizong of the Song dynasty, he ascended the hall and spoke this verse:
"This year I am sixty-seven; Old and sick, I pass the days as circumstances allow.
This year I shall record the matters of next year; Next year I shall record the day of today. In the fourth year, the dates did not differ from his prior record. He again ascended the hall.
He took his leave of the assembly and spoke a verse, saying: "O children, wandering aimlessly through waves, How many Ganges Rivers have you already crossed?

Avalokiteśvara points to Maitreya; Mañjuśrī can do nothing about it. After a long while, he said: "The world of white silver and the body of golden hue— Sentient and non-sentient share one single truth.
When light and darkness both cease, there is no longer illumination; At the hour after noon, the entire body is revealed. It was after noon.
He passed away peacefully. His body was cremated, and his *śarīra* relics were collected to build a stupa.
Chan Master Zhen of Guanghui in Ruzhou once served as a garden supervisor under Fengxue.

Fengxue asked him, "During the Huichang persecution of the Dharma, where did the Dharma-protecting virtuous monks go? The Master replied, "They were always in the midst of the marketplace; yet, nevertheless—"

No one recognized him. The cave-dweller said, "You have attained thorough penetration. The Master prostrated himself. On the day he entered the hall to assume his position, a monk asked, "What is the realm of Extensive Wisdom?
The Master replied, "Before the small temple, behind Ziqing. The monk asked, "What is the patriarchal style of the Master's house?
The Master replied, "A hoe, a rake, and a spade."
A monk asked Chan Master Man of Changxing Monastery in Fengxiang Prefecture, “What is the site of the ancient buddhas?
The Master said, “As soon as you walk, you step right upon it. The monk asked, “After stepping upon it, what then? The Master said, “The ice melts and the wall crumbles.
The monk asked, “Why is it so? The Master said, “A gentleman within the city; a common child outside the walls. [Another monk] asked, “When the Great Function manifests before one, how is it?”
The Master said, "Rolling through the bustling marketplace.
A monk asked the Abbot of Lingquan Monastery in Tanzhou, "What is the Master’s livelihood? The Master said, "Not a single thing.
The monk asked, "I do not understand; what is used in daily life? The Master gave a shout. The monk bowed. The Master struck him. [Question: What is this?
The former master said: "The horse-herder’s wife on the sands of Jinshe—what is the meaning of this? The teacher said: "Countless people outside the East Gate. [The student] asked:
"What if one understands it in this way? The teacher said: "Many pass back and forth across Tianjin Bridge."
Chan Master Shanzhao of Taiyuan, of the Shenyuan Court in Fenzhou, was a successor of Chan Master Nian of Shoushan in the ninth generation after the Southern Peak (Nanyue).
He was the son of the Yu family of Taiyuan; he shaved his head, received full ordination, and traveled with a staff.
He traveled as a wandering monk, staying briefly wherever he went, striking out according to the occasion, and visited seventy-one *kennshi* (masters).
Later, he arrived at Shoushan and asked, "What is the meaning of Baizhang’s folding his mat? Shoushan said, "The dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, and the entire body is revealed."
[The Master] asked, "What is your understanding? Xiangyan said, "Where the Elephant King walks, foxes have no place to roam. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Rising from his prostrations, he said, "The moon in the empty expanse of the ten thousand ages' azure pool—only after repeatedly searching for it does one finally come to know it.
Someone asked, "What principle did you perceive that you were so immediately convinced? The Master replied, "This is precisely where I let go of my body and life. Later...

He traveled through Hengzhou, Xiangzhou, and the regions of Xiangyang and Mian. Whenever he was invited by local magistrates to take charge of famous monasteries, he was requested eight times in succession;
yet he remained firm in his refusal, declining to respond. Only after the passing of Shoushan did the clergy and laity of the Western Road dispatch the monk Qichong to invite him to serve as abbot.

The Master had closed his quarters and was sleeping with his head on a high pillow. Fenzhou Cong pushed open the door and entered, admonishing him, saying: "The Great Matter of the Buddha-Dharma is of primary importance; retiring in tranquility is but a minor detail.

Fengxue feared he would fail to respond to the prophecy and worried that the fundamental teaching would fall into extinction. Fortunately, there was the former Master, but the former Master has already passed away.
You are one who possesses the strength to shoulder the Great Dharma of the Tathāgata; at such a time as this, why do you wish to sleep peacefully? The Master [woke].
He sprang up, grasped Cōng’s hand, and said, "Were it not for you, this teaching would never have been heard. Prepare my departure immediately; I shall go.
Upon arriving, he sat in formal meditation upon a single mat for thirty years, his feet never crossing the threshold. He ascended the hall and said:
"Under the gate of Fényáng, there is the Lion of Xīhé, who crouches at the entrance. Whenever anyone approaches, he bites them to death. What skillful means are there?"
To enter the gate of Fenyang and see the person of Fenyang—if you see the person of Fenyang, you are fit to be a teacher to the Buddhas and Patriarchs;
if you do not see the person of Fenyang, you are all nothing but people standing dead on the spot. Is there anyone who can enter it now?
You must enter quickly, lest you bring your whole life to naught. Do not fail to see the guest at Longmen; take care that you do not meet with a mark upon your brow.
"E! [The Master] said. "Which one is the guest from Dragon Gate? He pointed them all out at once, then raised his staff and said, "Withdraw quickly!
Withdraw quickly! Take care! Ascending the hall, he said: "The former sages taught that a single phrase must possess the three gates of the One;
a single gate of the One must possess the three essentials. Which phrase possesses these three gates and three essentials? Understand it well! Each of you should reflect upon this."

Have you attained stability yet? When the ancients of old went on pilgrimage, if they heard a single kōan (in-yuan) and had not yet clarified its inner meaning, they would find food tasteless and sleep uneasy;
they would urgently seek resolution, never regarding it as a minor matter.
This is why the Great Awakened Elder appeared in this world for the sake of the one great cause. Consider this well.
From the time I first set out on my travels, it was not for the sake of wandering through mountains, playing with the water, or viewing the splendors of provincial capitals.

My single robe and daily food have all been for the purpose that the Sage’s mind might be fully realized; thus I have driven myself across the land to resolve what is profound and subtle, and to transmit and propagate the teachings.

Seeking out those of vast learning and prior realization, and drawing near to those of high virtue, is for the purpose of continuing the lamp of the Buddha’s mind, perpetuating the ancestral lineage, exalting the sacred seed, and guiding those with future potential.
To benefit oneself and others, one must not forget the traces of the predecessors. Is there anyone present now who would discuss this?
If there is, come forward; let us all deliberate together. A monk asked: "What is the phrase for receiving a beginner?"

The Master said, "Do not mistake the bridge of a donkey’s saddle for your father’s chin. Zhang Maochong, the Grand Guardian, asked, "Regarding Kāśyapa Mātanga entering the Han, the accounts have already become overly verbose.

He asked, "If one can turn things over, they are the same as the Tathāgata. Since the myriad phenomena are 'things,' how does one turn them over?"

[The monk] said, “I have attained it. The Master said, “Having eaten the meal, you possess not a shred of wisdom. [The monk] asked, “When there is not a single thread of silk, the Dharma-net is boundless.

Where is there that does not receive this grace? But tell me, how do you express the power of receiving this grace? In a long silence, he said: 'A drop of spring rain is as slippery as oil.
A monk asked, "What is the student's own *dharmakāya*? The Master said, "Carrying firewood every day is no easy task."
[The monk] asked, "This belongs to the great assembly. What about that which belongs to the student? The Master said, "Three lifetimes and sixty kalpas.
[The monk] asked, "As you open your bedding and spread out your bowl every day, how do you repay the kindness of the donors?

The Master said, "I am nearly driven to death by this one question. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then I thank you for your offerings. The Master said, "What kind of person's breath are you breathing?"
[The monk] prostrated. The Master said, "Come back for another meal tomorrow. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the 'fuzzy ball at the head of a rapid torrent' mentioned by the ancients?
The Master said, "The clouds part and the moon shines bright. He asked, "What is the meaning of the 'bottom-stone at the head of a rapid torrent'?
The Master said, "The roof collapses and the blue sky is revealed. [The monk] asked, "How does one fully comprehend this? The Master said, "[The same as before]."

Pervading above and penetrating below. [The Master] asked: "Suppose a fire breaks out in one place; let us say you can extinguish it. But what if fires break out simultaneously in all eight directions?
The Master said: "Quick! The monk asked: "Is there still a way to escape? The Master said:
"If you seek an escape, you will be burned to death. The monk bowed. The Master said: "Even if you do not seek an escape, you will still be burned to death. [To the assembly: The First Phrase.

If you can speak the first phrase, you have burst forth from within the stone. If you can speak the second phrase, you have been summoned forth. If you can speak the third phrase, you will not even be able to save yourself.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A white cat with fierce claws and talons;

raised upon the dais, it leaves no trace of insects. This is clearly the method for establishing oneself atop a tree; one must strictly avoid giving words of permission to outsiders. "What is this 'giving words of permission'? [The Master] asked.
This is a phrase that arises from the external; do not err in citing it. A monk entered the room and asked, "At such a time as this, is there still a teacher?
The Master said, "The lamp has shone throughout the night; where is it not clear? The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is it?
The Master said, "Tomorrow is Cold Food Festival."
Chan Master Yuanlian of Guanghui Monastery in汝州 (Ruzhou) was the son of the Chen family of Quanzhou. He went to visit Shoushan, who asked, "Where have you recently come from?
The Master replied, "From Hanchang. Shoushan held up his fist and said, "Is there such a thing as this in Hanchang?
The Master said, "What kind of bowl is this that makes a sound? Shoushan said, "Blind! The Master said, "Exactly so," and gave a single clap. Then he departed.
[The Master] went out. On another day, he asked again: "When a student has personally reached the Treasure Mountain and returns empty-handed, what then?
The Mountain said: "A torch before every door. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and said: "I no longer doubt the tongues of the old monks throughout the world.
The Mountain asked: "How is it that you understand? Tell me and let me see. The Master said: "Only..."
"This is river sand from the ground," he said. The Master replied, "Do you understand? The Master then bowed.
Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "A red banner flutters atop the bamboo pole.
The Minister Yang Yi asked, "There is no Maitreya in heaven, and no Maitreya on earth; I wonder where he is?"
The Master said, “It is like knocking on bricks and beating tiles. [The monk] asked, “Fengxue said, ‘At the sands of Jinsha is the horse-herding woman.
What is the meaning of this? The Master said, “Even if I were to speak further, it would not equal it. [The monk] asked, “What is the true person of no station?
The Master said, “A wooden board above, iron below. [The monk] said, “In that case, the fault has its place. The Master said, “The Judge has laid down his brush. The monk [departed].
[The Master] prostrated. The Master said, "Drag him out! He asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Two is not enough. He ascended the hall.
Linji’s two head monks of the two halls met each other and simultaneously let out a shout.
Everyone, tell me: was there a guest and a host, or not? If you say there was, you are nothing but a blind man. If you say there was not, you are likewise a blind man.
Neither existent nor non-existent. Ten thousand miles away at Yuzhou. If you can speak here, I shall give you thirty blows;
if you cannot speak, I shall likewise give you thirty blows. When a monk reaches this point, how does he emerge?

The mountain monk rolled up his sleeves. After a long silence, he said, "How bitter! Frogs and earthworms leap as high as the Thirty-three Heavens, only to crash into the summit of Mount Sumeru and shatter into a hundred pieces.
He took up his staff and said, "A troop of unperforated iron hammers—retreat quickly, retreat quickly!

Xu Langzhong was appointed to the post of Transport Commissioner; while traveling through Western Sichuan, he went to visit the Master. It happened that he was received by the Master at the Buddha Hall.
Xu said, "First pay homage to the Buddha; first pay homage to the Elder. The Master said, "A shrimp swallows a large tiger. Xu said, "If that is so, then I shall not pay homage.
The Master said, "Director of the Bureau of Judicial Review, you have fallen into a trap of words.

Xu said, "Elder Xu possesses the single eye. The Master then brushed him with his sleeve. Xu said, "Today I have seen through it," and he prostrated himself. —Recorded during the Renzong era of the Song dynasty.
On the twenty-sixth day of the first month in the year of Bingzi during the Jingyou era, he displayed four circular diagrams, each inscribed with the characters for tiger, dog, rat, and ox.
He hung them at the door of his quarters, and subsequently passed away on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth month.
Chan Master Zhisong of Sanjiao at Tiancheng Monastery in Bingzhou was a native of Fanyang.
He visited Shoushan and asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Shoushan replied, "At the foot of the City of King Chu, the Ru River flows eastward.

At these words, the Master attained realization and composed the *Three Yuan Verses*, which begin: "It must be used, it must be used directly; Let not the mind and intellect waver. For three years..."
The Lion’s Roar: The species of foxes has vanished from the ten directions; I possess the nature of True Suchness (Tathatā), yet it remains hidden like a figure behind a curtain.

Once the gates of the six sense-doors are shattered, the Seal of Vairocana is revealed. This adamantine essence of true bone is worthy of praise; with a single sweep away of the six objects of dust, there is forever no obstruction.
The vast and empty world takes emptiness as its substance; within that substance, non-action (wuwei) is the true arrival home. Upon hearing this, Shanwen then requested [instruction].
They went to drink tea. [Zhaozhou] asked, "Were these three verses composed by you? The Master said, "Yes.
Yunmen said, "Suppose someone were to instruct you to manifest the thirty-two marks—what then? The Master said, "I am no wild fox spirit. Yunmen said, "Save your eyebrows.
The Master said, "How many have you already lost, Master? Yunmen struck him on the head with his bamboo staff and said, "This..."
The Han dynasty fell into chaos long ago; it remains so even now. Entering the hall, he said: "Mañjuśrī wields his sword and traverses Mount Wutai;

the Tang Emperor Ming blocks all paths to stop such demonic delusions. Since the Buddhas of the three ages have not yet emerged from the vehicle of the teachings, they are like fish swimming beneath the net."
The Dragon Gate is difficult to cross; the hook is cast across the four seas. This extraordinary discourse for catching the fierce dragon is intended solely to seek out those of true knowledge.
If one were to proclaim the fundamental principle, Mount Sumeru must be ground to dust; if one were to speak of Buddhas or Patriarchs, the waters of the great ocean would surely dry up.
When the precious sword is brandished, its radiance extends ten thousand miles. I grant you this single path to speak with universal penetration.
"Severing the throat—where can people draw breath? A monk asked, "Those of dull faculties delight in the lesser Dharma and do not believe they can become Buddhas;
after becoming a Buddha, what then? The Master said, "Grasping a qilin in the water. The monk said, "If that is so, then one immediately ascends the high seat.
The Master said, "Riding an ox up to the Thirty-three Heavens. [A monk] asked, "The ancients raised their mallets and brandished their fly-whisks."
"What is the meaning? The Master said, "Riding a donkey, one does not wear boots. Question:

"What is 'seizing the person but not seizing the environment'? The Master said: "There is a road to one's hometown, but no one is there. Question: "What is 'seizing the environment but not seizing the person'?
The Master said: "Secretly transmitting the Emperor’s decree; accompanying him for a hundred stages. Question: "What is 'seizing both person and environment'? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
The Master said, “A headless shrimp with its feet pointing to heaven. [The monk] asked, “What is it like when both person and environment are not wrested away?

The Master said, “In the south of the Jin Temple, the alley of long willows. [The monk] asked, “Regarding the ancient saying, ‘The eastern mountains and western ridges are green,’ what is its meaning?”
The Master said, "The Persian’s nostrils are large. [The monk] asked, "If that is so, then Kāśyapa in India and our Master here in this land [are one].
The Master said, "Vajrapāṇi’s palm is broad. [The monk] asked, "Regarding the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion, which one is the True Eye? The Master said:
The Stone Buddha of Kaifeng claps his hands and laughs; the Lady of Jin Temple knows how to sing. [The monk] asked:
"When Linji pushed over Huangbo, why did the *vina* receive the blow? The Master said: "A dog that is truly upright does not steal oil.
[The monk] asked: "How is it that a rooster carries away a lamp-stand? The Master said: "Use it when you need to. [The monk] said: "Please, Master, use it."

The Master said, "Drag out this dead man! Zheng, the Minister of Works, asked, "When one plays ball atop a hundred-foot pole, or when one’s waist is bound by a thread at the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom precipice—what then?
The Master said, "Planting your feet in Youzhou; wrestling in Guangnan. Zheng was speechless.
The Master said, "I have seen through this fellow. Zheng said, "For twenty years I have been within the borders of Jiangnan; this time, however—"

He saw Chan Master [Xuefeng]. The Master said, "A blind old woman blowing on a fire. [The monk] asked, "When it is said that 'one should not stand on either side, nor need one establish a middle way,' what is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "Elephant tusks come from Guangnan. The monk said, "I do not understand. I beg the Master to point directly.
The Master said, "A leather ball from the barbarian lands costs eight hundred coins. [Later, the Master] ascended the hall. He said, "Cold, warmth, coolness, and heat—put on your clothes."
"Eating a meal—of itself, nothing is lacking. Why all this fuss about seeking something? It is simply that people are unwilling to take responsibility.
Is there anyone here now who can take responsibility? If there is, do not fail the mountains, rivers, and the great earth.
Be careful. Question: "The Patriarch came from the West; the Tripitaka went to the East. What matter should be clarified by these? The Master said: "The Buddha Hall and the Patriarch’s Hall."
The monk Shu was repairing the Sangha Hall when an old monk covered it up, saying, "In that case, you have fully clarified today's affair. The Master asked, "What is today's affair?
The monk then gave a shout; the Master then struck him. A monk asked, "What is the place where a student applies his mind?
The Master said, "Shave your head clean and wash your bowl thoroughly. The monk asked, "What is the place where a student walks and acts? The Master said:

Before the Sangha Hall, behind the Buddha Hall, he ascended the seat for the formal discourse. He cited a verse by Fayan: "Seeing mountains, they are not mountains; seeing water, how could it ever be otherwise?
The mountains, rivers, and the great earth—all are but a single orb of the moon. Great Master Fayan has not yet left the Nirvana Hall. Sanjiao, however, does not agree with this:
"The mountains, rivers, and the great earth—each uses its own awl and blade. [He remained standing] for a long time.
Take heed.
Zen Master Zhisong of Tiefo Monastery in Xin Prefecture had a fellow practitioner arrive. Upon seeing him, the Master asked, "Do you still remember our acquaintance?
As the head of the visiting group hesitated, the second monk struck the head with his sitting cloth (*zuoju*) and said, "Why are you not quick?"
He replied to the Master. The Master said, "One arrow, two targets. The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from?

The monk said, "From Mount Tai. The Master said, "Have you seen the Dragon King? The monk said, "Try saying it yourself, Master. The Master said, "If I were to say it, it would be like ice melting and tiles shattering.
The monk hesitated. The Master said, "You do not believe my words. [The monk] asked about a deceased monk’s transition: "Toward what [direction] does he go?"
"Where has he gone? The Master said, "Dingpo does not run away; a swift opportunity is hard to encounter.
Chan Master Huizhi of Shoushan in Ruzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said:
"A three-foot staff and a broken tile basin. [The student] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The bottom of the bucket has fallen off.

[The student] asked, "What sayings did the sages of the past have? The Master said, "Thus have I heard. [The student] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Believe, accept, and practice accordingly."
Chan Master Chuping of Renwang Monastery in Chizhou asked Shoushan, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
Shoushan gave a shout. The Master prostrated. Shoushan raised his staff. The Master said, “Old monk, you have no world!
Shoushan threw down his staff and said, “It is difficult to deceive one with clear eyes. The Master said, “The grass-robbers are utterly defeated.”

The envoy replied, "How would one dare to nest upon the head of a hawk?

The Master said, "If you do not become a dragon atop the staff," and he followed this by striking his sitting mat once. After the tea was finished, the envoy rose and said, "Just now, I have inadvertently offended you, Master."
The Master said, "Du the Zen Guest from Jiangnan, what are you looking for with a second bowl?
When the Prefect Yang Yi asked, "The Master of Mount Huizhao at Lukmon in Xiangzhou said, 'Entering the mountains one does not fear tigers;
on the main road, however, one must guard against people. What does this mean? The Master said, "The gentleman is broad and open. A monk asked, "What is..."
Lumen Mountain. The Master said, "The large is large; the small is small. [A monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person among the mountains?
The Master said, "Eyes askance, lying flat on one's back."
The layman Wang Sui, the Chancellor, visited Shoushan and attained the meaning beyond words. From then on, his practice was profound and clear.

As he approached the end of his life, he wrote this verse: "The lamp in the painted hall has already been extinguished; To whom can I point my finger and speak? Coming and going are fundamentally ordinary;
The spring breeze sweeps away the lingering snow."

Chan Master Chiming (Buchu Yuan) of Shishuang in Tanzhou,
a successor in the tenth generation under Nanyue and a dharma heir of Chan Master Fenyang Zhao,
was born into the Li clan of Quanzhou during the Yongping era of Emperor Taizong of the Song dynasty.
In the *xi* year of the Dinghai cycle, he was young and served as a scholar. At the age of twenty-two, he entered the monastic life at Yijing Temple on Mount Xiang.
His mother, who possessed virtuous conduct, encouraged him to travel abroad. The Master had joined eyebrows and prominent eyes, and was tall and robust.

Yet, whenever he encountered the strict standards of the monastic rules, he was rebuked by the senior elders for being too young for the monastic community (*conglin*). The Master leaned against a fence and laughed, saying, "A dragon..."
"The trampling of an elephant is not something a donkey can endure. He constantly carried a box of antiques on a bamboo staff as he traveled between Xiangyang and Mian.
Accompanying Shou Zhi, he entered Luoyang. Hearing of the great reputation of [Yuan] Fenyang, he went to pay him a visit.

Fenyang looked at him and silently took note of him, yet for two years he did not permit him to enter his inner quarters. Every time they met, he would scold and revile him, or disparage the various other schools.

Furthermore, whatever he taught was all nothing but vulgar matters of worldly custom. One night, [a disciple] complained, saying, "Since arriving at this Dharma assembly, two summers have passed, yet I have received no instruction.
My worldly thoughts and labors only increase; the years and months slip by in a flash, and my own fundamental task remains unclarified.
I have lost the benefit of leaving the household life. Before he had finished speaking, Yang stared at him intently and scolded, "This is a wicked teacher! How dare you deceive and exploit me?"
In anger, he raised his staff to drive him away. The Master (Fayan) was about to step forward to rescue him, when Yang covered the Master’s mouth.

At that moment, the Master attained great enlightenment and said, "Now I know that Linji’s Way transcends ordinary sentiment. He served [Yang] for seven years before taking his leave. He then relied upon Tangming Song.
Song once said to the Master, "The Palace Secretary Yang Dainian possesses lofty insight and is steady and authentic in his entry into the Way; you must go see him. Thereupon, the Master...
He went to see him. Nanwen asked, "We do not know each other face-to-face, yet from a thousand li away we share the same wind.

The Master said, "Recently I have received an invitation from the Mountain Gate. Nanwen said, "You are truly a master of deception. The Master said, "I left Tangming last month. Nanwen said, "Just now I regretted asking you.
The Master said, "A true adept. Nanwen then gave a shout. The Master said, "Exactly! Nanwen shouted again. The Master reached out his hand.
He made a sweeping gesture. Nian stuck out his tongue and said, "Truly a dragon-elephant. The Master said, "What words are these?
Nian called for the guest master to bring tea, saying, "It turns out he is one of our own household. The Master said, "That too is unnecessary. After the tea was finished, he asked again.
"What is the one phrase by which you, the Senior Monk, benefit others? The Master said, "It is urgent. Yuan Nian said, "If that is so, it is like a bride in a long skirt dragging through the mud.
The Master said, "Who could equal you, Inner Secretary? Yuan Nian said, "A master, truly a master. The Master said, "I grant you twenty blows.
Yuan Nian tapped his knee and said, "What kind of place is this? The Master clapped his hands and said, "It is also [a place for such]."
"You must not let this pass," [Zhao]zhou said. Yuanwu laughed loudly. He asked again, "Do you remember the karmic conditions for Tangming’s awakening at that time?
The Master said, "Tangming asked Shoushan, 'What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
Shoushan replied, 'At the foot of King Chu’s city, the Ru River flows east. Yuanwu said, "Regarding these words alone, what is their underlying intent? The Master said, "Upon the water."
While hanging up a lantern-ball, Yang Yi said, "If it is so, then I have failed the ancients. The Master said, "If you harbor doubts, Inner Secretary, then seek instruction elsewhere.
Yang Yi said, "A three-legged frog leaps into the sky. The Master said, "Let it leap as it pleases. Yang Yi then laughed heartily.

He was lodged in the refectory, where he questioned the Master day and night on matters of doubt. When Zhizheng heard these previous words, he went to visit him, regretting that he had not met him earlier.
In the evening, [Dao’an] saw the Prince of the Household, Li Gungzunxu, in the palace and said, "Recently I met a man of the Way who is truly a lion of the West River.
Li replied, "I am constrained by official protocol; how can I go to pay my respects? Dao’an remained silent.

Upon returning home, he said to his teacher, "Lord Li is one among those who follow the Buddha-dharma. Having heard that the wind of the Way has arrived from afar, he has a desire to see me, yet for this very reason—"
The Master was not granted an audience. He passed by with his attendants. At dawn, he went to pay his respects to Lord Li. After the Lord had read the visiting card, he sent a page to inquire:
"If you can speak the Way, you may meet with the Senior Monk. The Master said, "I have come today specifically to pay my respects."
He further sent a youth named Bei, who said, "The inscription on the stele is carved in white characters; one must plant green pines along the road.
The Master said, "If it were not for this auspicious day, such an occasion would surely be difficult to encounter on other days. The youth stepped forward again and said, "The Commandant says:
'In that case, I shall go to meet you, Venerable Sir. The Master said, "From head to toe. The official then emerged, took his seat, and asked, "I have heard that in the West..."
"There is a golden-haired lion in the river. Is this so? The Master asked, "Where did you get this news? The official gave a shout. The Master said, "A wild jackal howling.

The official shouted again. The Master said, "Exactly so. The official laughed heartily. As the Master was taking his leave, the official asked, "What is the one phrase for the Senior Monk as he departs?
The Master said, "Take good care of yourself. The official said, "How is this any different from other places? The Master [remained silent].
[The Master] said, "How about you, Commandant? The official said, "I give the Senior Monk twenty blows. The Master said, "Solely for the sake of its circulation.
The official shouted again. The Master said, "Blind man! The official said, "Go well. The Master responded, "Yes, yes.

From then on, he went back and forth between the gates of Yang and Li, taking the Dharma as his friend. After a long time, he took his leave to return to Hedong. He said, "I have a phrase to entrust to you."
"Did Tang Ming understand? The Master said, "The bright moon shines upon the traveler at night. Yuan'an said, "That does not quite fit.

The Master said, "It may still be bearable before midnight, but after midday, it brings even more sorrow to people. Yuan'an said, "Why has the Vajra statue in front of Kaibao Temple recently broken into a sweat?
The Master said, "Do you know why? Yuan'an said, "As you are about to depart, Master, surely you have something to bestow upon us?"
The Master said, "Layer upon layer of mountain passes. Nan'an said, "In that case, I shall follow you, Venerable Sir.
The Master let out a single sigh. Nan'an said, "A true lion cub; a great lion’s roar. The Master said, "Let go, yet he draws me back again.
Nan'an said, "Just now I lost my footing and fell, only to be helped up by a servant boy. The Master said, "When will there ever be an end to this?"

Nian laughed loudly. When the Master returned to Tangming, Lord Li sent two monks to question him. At the end of his reply, the Master drew a pair of feet and wrote the names of the visiting monks to return it.
Lord Li composed a verse, saying: "The black brush has traveled over a thousand li; the golden coffin reveals a pair of feet.
Humans and devas can hardly fathom this; take care, O red-bearded barbarian! The Master then returned south because his mother was elderly. Upon arriving at Rui...
In the capital of the province, at the time when [Changsha] was the head of the assembly at Dongshan, Chan Master Cong resided there.
Previously, Fenyang had said to the Master, "I have traveled everywhere visiting the descendants of Yunmen, yet I have harbored a regret for not having seen Cong.

For this reason, the Master stayed with him for three years before traveling to Mount Yang. Yan Dainian then sent a letter to Huang Zong, the Governor of Yichun, requesting that he invite the Master to come forth.
The World-Honored One preached the Dharma. Shouyan, having received the transmission of the lineage, ascended the hall after his arrival. Holding up his staff, he said:
"All Buddhas of the past, all Buddhas of the present, and all Buddhas of the future;

the twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven, the six patriarchs of the Tang land, and all the old monks of the world—all have been transformed into this staff of Nan-yuan. You people, toward..."
Where shall one find a place to settle the body and establish one’s livelihood? Look! Look! This staff has already pierced through the skulls of you all.
Is there anyone here who can discern its pain and itch? If there is, come forth and leap before the assembly! If there is none, Nan-yuan has lost his advantage today.
(He lets out a shout and strikes the ground with his staff. He descends from the seat. Entering the hall: When a single speck of dust is raised...
The entire great earth is completely released. From a single hair-tip lion, ten billion hair-tips manifest ten billion hair-tip lions;
from a single hair-tip, thousands and tens of thousands of heads appear. Simply recognize one head. Then, he raised his staff and said:
"This here is Nan-yuan’s staff. That one is the single head. [The Master] gave a shout, struck the ground with his staff, and descended from the seat.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "An old man develops an illness.

A monk asked, "What is the phrase for receiving a beginner? The Master said, "One stroke, two pieces. [The monk] asked, "What is the phrase for testing a patch-robed monk? The Master said, [He remained silent].
Hanshan and Shide asked, "What is the phrase for when the true command is being exercised? The Master said, "Coming in thousands, going in tens of thousands.
They asked, "What is the phrase for establishing heaven and earth? The Master said, "The heavens are high and the seas are vast. A monk asked, "How is it when one sits side by side with the Master?
The Master said, "A thread passes through yellow leaves. He ascended the hall and said: "Heaven and earth share the same root as I; the myriad dharmas..."
“I am the one body. He then held up his staff and said, “This is Nan-yuan’s staff; which one is the body?
After a long silence, he said, “To cross the river, one must use a raft; once on the shore, the boat is not needed. With a shout, he struck the ground with his staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said, “The sands of Ganges River Buddhas, the lands of the sands of Ganges River—altogether...”
It has been swallowed whole by the staff of Nanyuan. Among those sentient beings, none perceive it and none know it.
You monks, where are your nostrils? If you know their location, you may carry your staff across your shoulders and gaze at the clouds in the sky.
If you do not know, there is porridge and rice upon your long benches. (He lets out a shout. An official asks: "What is it?"

[Nan]yuan asked about the "realm. The Master said, "Digging a pond, one awaits the moon in autumn; planting bamboo, one screens out the sun in summer. He asked, "What is it like to be a person within this realm?

The Master said, "The young gentlemen of the city possess every kind of nobility; the practitioners of the Way beneath the forest trees are poor in every respect. A monk asked, "I have long been ignorant of the pearl in my robe;
I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "The grass-robbers are utterly defeated. The monk said, "There is no way to escape. The Master said—
[The student] said, "My feet do not move from their place. The Master asked, "I have heard it said in the teachings:
