[He ascended the hall for formal discourse: "Because heaven is impartial, it constantly covers all; because earth is impartial, it constantly supports all. Because the sun..."
Because the moon is impartial, it is ever-luminous throughout the four seasons. Because *nirvāṇa* is impartial, the noble and the ordinary are not two.
Because the human mind is impartial, there is no contention between high and low. [The Master] took up his staff, struck once, and said: "All you practitioners of Chan, this very staff—”
Day and night I have been preaching the Dharma-gate of equality for all of you. Do you hear it? If you do hear it, I can guarantee that your journey as wandering monks is complete.
If you say you do not hear it, I nevertheless grant that the eye at the crown of your heads is upright.
Why is this? Because this Dharma is equal, with no high or low; this is called Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. After a long silence, he laughed.
He said: "The text below is long.
Chan Master Chongzhen of Puci Monastery in Runzhou, a successor of Chan Master Jinshan Ying, was asked by a monk: "What is the realm of Puci? The Master said: "It emerges."
Upon entering the gate, he saw Mount He-lin. [The monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person within this realm? The Master said, "As soon as you enter the gate, you see Elder Chen.
Chan Master Zhonghe of Ruizhu in Taiping Prefecture was asked by a monk, "Regarding those who have attained their seat and donned their robes, they all understand what lies beyond."
"What is the matter regarding the vehicle of our school? The Master said, "Simply know that ice is water. [The monk] asked, "Is there anything further, or not?
The Master said, "Cease asking how water becomes ice. [The monk] said, "To play with the tide, one must be a man who plays with the tide. The Master said, "This monk has come from Zhejiang."
Chan Master Huixian Yuan-tong of Mount Jinshan in Runzhou was the son of the He family of Yongjia. He left home to become a monk at the age of four.
Later, he studied under Master Ying at Yingsheng Temple and attained realization. He first propagated the Dharma at Taiping and Yinjing, then presided over Mount Jinshan.

Subsequently, he retired to Niuwang (Ox Head) Mountain before being invited to serve as abbot at Yuantong on Mount Lu and Xuedou in Mingzhou. A monk asked: "When you propagate the fundamental tenets of our school, from whom did you receive the Dharma?"
The Master raised his whisk. The monk said, "At the head of the Iron Cauldron City, you once received certification; by the edge of the Green Creek cliff, the ancestral lamp shines.
The Master gave a stroke with the whisk and said, "If your hearing is not true, you will call a bell a cauldron.

In the *Renxu* year of the Yuanfeng era of Emperor Shenzong of the Song dynasty, the Master passed away at Niutou (Ox Head). His entire body was enshrined in a stupa on the Western Ridge. He was sixty-seven years old and had been a monk for [X] years.
63. A monk asked Zen Master Xianzhong Zuyin of Shifosi in Yuezhou, “What is the Immovable Honored One?
The Master said, “A monkey on a hot griddle. The monk asked, “What are the thousands of millions of transformation bodies? The Master said, “Adding incense and changing [the water].”

[The Master] sprinkled water, lit a lamp, and swept the floor. [A monk] asked, "What is the Dharmakāya Lord Vairocana? The Master said, "The hitching post for the horse. [The monk] asked, "What connection is there?
The Master said, "I would tie this fellow to death! [Another monk] asked, "One who knows how to kill the Buddhas and patriarchs is truly an adept.
What is the sword that kills the Buddhas and patriarchs? The Master said, "I do not behead those already dead. [The monk] asked, "How so?"
"This is the Preceptor’s sword. The Master said, "An order is not executed twice. [The monk] asked, "What is birth through mutual conditioning?

The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. [The monk] asked, "What is birth through conceptualization? The Master said, "A rabbit gazing at the moon. [The monk] asked, "What is birth through continuous flow?
The Master said, "Without interruption. [The monk] asked, "What is form and emptiness? The Master said, "A five-colored screen."
Ascending the hall: "Tut! Tut! Tut! The fish and dragons at the bottom of the sea have all dried up; a three-legged toad flies up into the sky; a shell-shucked turtle lives amidst the flames.
Ascending the hall: "When it is time to point, one does not point; black and white remain undistinguished.

When it is time to reach [the goal], one does not reach it; mud and water are blended together. A pillar leaps and bounds, entering into a lantern—let him do as he pleases for now. But what about your eyebrows?"
For what reason, then, is it dragged beneath one's heels? Even if you were to understand this clearly, it would still be like a monkey wearing a bamboo hat;
if you do not understand it, how is it any different from a crooked leg wearing boots? Nevertheless, though this is so, many laugh at me.
"Those who understand me are few.

While residing at Jingzhu Monastery in Hangzhou, Chan Master Zhenjing visited Jinshan. He then asked, "I have a superficial understanding of the sutras and treatises, yet I do not believe in Chan at all.
I pray that the Master will resolve my doubts. Jinshan replied, "Since you do not believe in Chan, how can you claim to understand the sutras?"

"Meditation (dhyāna) is the mainstay of the sutras; the sutras are the net of meditation. By grasping the mainstay, the net is set right; by understanding meditation, one sees the sutras. The Master said, "Explain meditation for me so that I may observe it.
Dongshan said, "What follows is a long discourse. The Master said, "If it is thus, then the sutras and meditation are of one essence.
Dongshan said, "The Buddha and the Patriarchs do not have two minds. It is like a hand forming a fist, or a fist opening into a hand. Because of this, the Master [attained realization].
Having attained realization, he then composed a verse: "For over twenty years I have used my mind in vain speculation, Several times I have tried to extinguish this heart.
Now, in my decline, I have met one who knows me: Li Bai was originally a scholar."
Chan Master Gongchen of Xiyushan in Anji County ascended the hall: "Lingyun saw the flower; there was a film over his eyes.

Xuansha knitted his fingers; he suffered a misfortune upon his own person. Not realizing this, he simply passes the time in such a manner. Naturally, body and mind are at peace. He ascended the hall again:
"Principle arises because of phenomena; the mind follows the objects of perception. When both phenomena and objects are forgotten, there are a thousand mountains and ten thousand rivers."
"How can one attain the perfect state? After a long silence, he said, "Do not gouge out flesh to create a sore.
The Master had thirty volumes of the *Zuyuan tongyao* (Essential Passages from the Patriarchal Source) which circulated in the world.
A monk asked Chan Master Shanduan of Panyu Temple in Kunshan, Suzhou: "When there is birth and there is extinction, these are all ordinary phenomena.
But what is it like when there is neither birth nor extinction? The Master said: "Kunlun wears boots and stands in mid-air. The monk asked:
"Is this not the point of teaching others? The Master said: "The stone maiden adorns her hair with flowers and sleeps amidst the flames. The monk said: "May the assembly bear witness."
The Master said: "Look further at the earthen ox fighting its way into the sea.
Chan Master Wenjian Jizhen of Guangjiao in Ningguo ascended the hall and said: "One who wishes to become a patriarch must thoroughly understand the phrases of light and darkness.
Blinking one's eyes in the dead of night is entirely a hollow proclamation; Śākyamuni was merely being overbearing when he was born."
Looking around in all four directions, he pats his chest and claims sole supremacy. Again, walking seven steps in every direction—who else knows this clearly? In secret, who will cause awakening?
From that time until a thousand or ten thousand years later, counting them as grains of sand in the Ganges, one blind man leads a multitude of blind men; blind and blind, they support one another.
On that day when you meet Old Yama, exert yourself and look into the void. At that moment, cease your crying and shouting; there is no boiling cauldron.
In this cold place, do not remain empty-stomached and haughty. Simply lift your chopsticks and turn them over on your plate; send this message to future generations:
do not be deceived by Xu Liu.
When the lay practitioner Li Duanyuan was a child in the government academy, he frequently read Chan texts. Although he later married and entered official service, he remained devoted to the Dharma.
However, being resolute in his commitment to the ancestral way, he subsequently built a dwelling resembling an *āraṇya* (monastery) in the rear garden and invited Jinshan Ying to reside there.

Morning and evening he consulted and studied with him, forgetting even to sleep or eat. One day, Ying looked at the Master and said, "Were it not for the power of manifesting [through skillful means], how could you have reached such a state?
Yet, alas, you still lack a point of entry. The Master asked, "Are heaven and hell ultimately real, or..."

"No. "Please, Master, explain this clearly. Ying said: "The Buddhas speak of existence within non-existence; it is like seeing flowers in the sky with one's own eyes. Your Excellency seeks non-existence within existence;
it is laughable to grasp at the moon in water with your hands. Seeing a prison before your eyes, you do not avoid it;

hearing of heaven beyond your mind, you wish to be born there. You fail to realize that joy and fear reside in the mind, while good and evil constitute the external environment. Your Excellency need only understand this."
"The mind of itself is naturally free from delusion. The Official asked, "How does one bring the mind to such a state? Ling said, "Do not deliberate upon good or evil at all.
The Official asked, "After no longer deliberating, where does the mind go? Ling said, "Please, Excellency, return to your residence for now. The Official said:
“Just as when a person dies, where does the mind go? Zhiyong said, “If you do not know life, how can you know death? The official said, “As for life, I already know it.
Zhiyong asked, “From where does life come? The official was at a loss for words. Zhiyong rose, thrust his hand toward the official’s chest, and said:
"It is right here. What more do you intend to deliberate upon? The official said, "I have understood. Yǐng asked, "How have you understood it?
The official said, "I only knew how to hurry along the journey, unaware that I had missed the way. Yǐng pushed him away and said, "A hundred years are but one dream."

I have only just awakened this morning. Thereupon, I spoke this verse: "At thirty-eight years of age, I was dazed and ignorant. Now that I possess knowledge, how am I any different from my former ignorance?
The waters of the Bian River flow on, the embankments of Sui remain faintly visible. Master, you must return; the arrow-like waves rush eastward."

Chan Master Liaoyue of Dongting was the dharma successor of Chan Master Liaoguang of Jianfu in Suzhou. A monk asked, "Without relying on verbal explanations, I request the Master to grant me instruction.
The Master said, "The assembly all sees you asking in such a manner. The monk asked, "Is this itself it? The Master said, "Rarely encountered is one who pierces through..."

A monk asked Zen Master Baoxuan of Huangyan in Taizhou, a successor of the Zen Master Yiji:

"What? The Master said, "Knowing it yet deliberately committing it. The monk bowed; the Master then struck him.
Chan Master Shizi Jingduan of Xiyu, Anji Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Longhua Yue, was the son of the Qiu family of that same prefecture. When he first encountered Nongshi...
The Master revealed the essentials of the mind. Having gone to visit Longhua, he received his seal of approval and subsequently returned to his hometown.

He fashioned a lion’s skin from dyed fabrics and wore it at that time; thus, he was known as Master Duanzi. Prime Minister Zhang, admiring his Way, personally invited him to open a dharma center at Wushan, where his transformative influence spread widely.
On the day he ascended the hall, when the Vinaya Master reached the point in the proclamation where one turns back and pushes over [the screen], he kicked it over.
"I have not yet recited the Lotus Sutra in its seven fascicles; the cry of the fisherman was heard first. The Master stopped him, whereupon he ascended the seat.
After offering incense for the Emperor, he raised his voice and chanted: "Originally a lone fisherman of Xiangxiang, wandering west, east, north, and south.
The assembly responded with a chorus of acclaim. The Master looked at them and laughed, saying: "Behold clearly the Dharma of the Dharma King."
Such is the Dharma of the Dharma King. [He] then descended from his seat. Master Duan ascended the hall: "Master Duan, Master Duan! As abbot, I am carefree and free from afflictions.
In the morning, I attend the assembly of several dozen monks; at night, I gaze upon the single bright moon, shining clearly.
I urge all people to diligently study the Way, so that they may recognize the priceless treasure within their robes. Upon the terrace of Shanguang Hall, the snow has just melted, washing it clean."
The peaks and ridges are even more magnificent; Elder Guangjiao has arrived. He ascends the hall and says: "Floating clouds have dispersed, and the sky is a deep azure;
the spring colors have melted away, and the mountains are all the clearer. I cherish this Chan elder, as serene as water; he comes at times to accompany me through the remainder of my life.
The Master arrives at Zhiyuan in Huating. The assembly requests him to ascend the hall. He says: "Originally a lion from Xiachuan, I have come here..."
"Roaring amidst the clouds: the Buddha-dharma is not something to be deliberated upon. It would be better to perform a somersault. He then performed a somersault and descended from his seat.
The Master arrived at Zhangnan and visited Chao of Shangfang. A nun came to take her leave. The Master said, "Come back tomorrow at the third watch of the fifth watch.
Early the next morning, the Master sat there with his face smeared with red powder. When the nun entered and saw him, she was startled.
He then attained enlightenment. Chao You composed a verse that says: "How laughable is the old bald slave of Wu Mountain, Skillfully applying rouge and powder to receive the nun!
Vast and boundless is the universe, with countless people; Which man among them can truly be called a hero? The Master presided over four small monasteries in succession.
They were dilapidated and desolate, such that others could not endure their hardships, yet the Master alone found joy therein. He first resided at Chang...
At that time, there was one known as Houtou (Head-Turner) who deluded the ignorant and common folk; offerings poured in upon him like mountains.

He happened to encounter the Master, who struck him on the head. Houtou could not fathom this. The Master looked at him and said, "A dragon’s head with a snake’s tail. Houtou remained speechless, fleeing in shame and perspiration.
Once, while at the residence of Grand Marshal Pin, he encountered a sorcerer whom everyone considered a divine marvel; the Master [encountered him] alone...

When he spoke of refuting [the opponent], the latter was immediately known to be spurious; he was subsequently executed, and the assembly finally acknowledged the Master’s lofty discernment and far-reaching insight.

Renowned dukes and high officials delighted in associating with the Master. The Master would often compose verses in jest; though they appeared humorous at first, upon careful reflection, they were found to contain profound meaning.
Yuanzhao was originally summoned to reside at HuiLin Temple in the capital; at that time, the Master went to visit him, and Yuanzhao came forward to welcome him.
Zhaowei said to him, "Are you not Master Duan Shizi? The Master assumed the posture of a lion. Zhaowei probed him with colloquial language, and the Master responded immediately with a gāthā.
Zhaowei laughed and approved of him. At that time, Chancellor Zhang Gong was presiding over the administration and wished to have the Master reside in the capital.
Upon hearing this, the Master returned home without informing anyone. He later styled himself the Monk Anxian (The Peaceful and Leisurely) and personally established two...

Taoqi said, "When I die, bury me here. Having been free from illness or distress throughout his life, on the fifth day of the twelfth month of the Guiwei year of Song Huizong’s Chongning era (1103), he suddenly told the assembly of monks, "My karmic conditions have ended today.
He requested a bath, wrote a verse of farewell, and sang several verses of the "Fisherman's Song" (*Yufu ci*). With a single laugh, he passed away. The assembly interred him at Guyun Monastery.
His secular age was seventy-four and his monastic seniority (sang-lao) was forty-nine.
He was the twelfth-generation descendant of Nanyue and the dharma heir of Chan Master Cuiyan Zhen.
Chan Master Zhenru Muzhe of Daopei in Tanzhou was the son of the Wen family of Wenchuan in Fuzhou.
A monk asked, "Regarding Zhaozhou’s 'The cypress tree in the courtyard'—what is its meaning? The Master said, "Last night the wind grew fierce; the solitary traveler already feels the cold first.

The monk asked, "The former master did not say those words; how would you explain it then? The Master said, "Only when the traveler sets out does he know suffering. The monk said, "For ten years I have wandered..."
"In the midst of the red dust, today he reveals his body alone. The Master said, "Adding frost to snow. Question: "What is the Buddha in the city? The Master said:
"Standing out without a banner amidst a crowd of ten thousand people. Question: "What is the Buddha in the village? The Master said: "A mud-pig and a scabby dog. Question:
"What is the Buddha in the mountains? The Master said: "Where no one comes or goes. Question: "What is... [The text ends here.]
Regarding the "separate transmission outside the teachings," the Master said: "It cannot be translated. Question: "What was it like before Niu-t'ou had seen the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said: "The hairs on one's body stand on end. Question: "What was it like after he saw him? The Master said: "Sweat breaks out on the forehead. Ascending the hall, he said:
"When the moon arises as one, the vastness of heaven and earth—who suffers the wrong? "When the moon arises as two, east, west, south, and north..."
The north vanishes into nothingness; the moon gives birth to the three virtues. Wealth specifically heads southward to pay respects.

Therefore it is said: "If let go, the Tathāgata radiates light; if held fast, the dust and mud hide the brilliance. But tell me: is it letting go, or is it holding fast? After a long silence, he said:
"The three dots of the circle and the water—ten thousand things are naturally fresh and new. He ascended the hall and said: "An ancient Buddha said: 'In the past...'"
Śāriputra, you previously turned the wheel of the Four Noble Truths—this was like falling into a pit or dropping down a moat.

Now, you turn again this most wondrous, unsurpassed Great Dharma Wheel—this is like adding mud on top of earth. Is there anyone present here now who, without traversing the steps, has uniquely transcended all things?
After a long silence, he said: "Looking out from beyond the heavens, who is the one within?
Ascending the hall, he said: "Alala! What is this? I recall that year when the hearth was broken; when the staff suddenly struck, I finally realized I had betrayed myself.
He struck the incense stand once with his staff and said: "Duo! Duo! Ascending the hall, he said: "Reaching into the void to chase an echo—how wearying is your diligence!"
"Divine! Upon awakening from a dream, one realizes it was not real; what further matter remains? The old man Deshan is upon the eyebrows and eyelashes of you all. Do you yet realize this?
If you do, then you have awakened from the dream and realized it was not real.

If you have not yet realized it, you are merely clutching at empty space and chasing echoes—there will never be an end to it. Even if you were to be bold and clear-sighted here, it would still be like climbing a mountain."
[The monk] entered to pay tribute. [The Master asked: "Is there anyone who transcends all things? After a long silence, he said, "Do not falsely display your cleverness. [The monk] asked:
"When the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas, why was it that he could not attain Buddhahood? The Master said: "..."
"Kusha kills people. He ascended the hall and said: "The white clouds are limpid; the waters flow into the vast ocean. All phenomena are fundamentally at rest—what further matter is there?
Therefore it is said: there is the provisional, and there is the real; there is illumination, and there is function.
When you people reach this point, how do you tread upon it? After a long silence, he said: "As long as there is a path to ascend, those of superior stature will walk it."
Ascending the hall, he said: "This mountain monk originally possesses no accumulated wealth; I simply have enough porridge and enough rice. When I am weary, I immediately sleep.
Let me do as I please, whether divining east or west. Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients said, 'One Śākyamuni, two Yuanhuo, and three Buddhas;
all the rest are merely bowl-dropping ghosts. Huiguang, however, does not agree. One Śākyamuni, two Yuanhuo."
The Sambuddha is always a *tuoqiu*. Do you all know where the light of wisdom falls?
If you do know, I grant that you possess iron eyes and copper pupils; if you do not know, do not say, "How many times have we been startled by perilous winds and waves?
For my small boat has once traveled across the Five Lakes. Ascending the hall, he raised his staff and said: "When a single speck of dust arises, the entire earth..."
[He] gathers it all in completely. He strikes the desk once and says: "The World of Wondrous Joy shatters into a hundred fragments.
Now tell me: where is the Tathāgata Acala right now? If anyone can recognize this, they may be said to have ascended to wondrous enlightenment without moving a step.
If you do not yet recognize it, he enters nirvana within the eyebrows and eyelashes of everyone here. [He] strikes the desk once again. [End of Text]
The Hall. To know without thinking; to understand without deliberation. "The price of rice in Ilung is high; the radishes in Chenzhou are large.
Ascending the hall, he picked up his staff and said: "This staff of Zhizhai sometimes becomes the Vajra King’s precious sword."

Sometimes he acts as a lion crouching on the ground; sometimes he acts as a probe or a blade of grass for a shadow. Sometimes he does not even use it as a staff. Do you all understand this thoroughly?
If you do understand it, you will be like a dragon gaining water or a tiger relying on its mountain—appearing and disappearing, rolling up and unrolling, applying it freely in every direction.
If you have not yet understood it, it is very much like trying to escape one’s own shadow in broad daylight. [Ascending the hall, the tenth discourse.]
Now we gather together as one; each and every one studies non-action (*wuwei*). This is the field for selecting Buddhas; with an empty mind, you shall return having passed the imperial examination.

Under the Gate of Wisdom’s Radiance, one is directly uprooted and ascends, bypassing all formal categories. Since you have all arrived here, the winds and clouds are spread across the earth and your fangs and claws are already formed;
you merely lack the thunderous roar to burn off your tails. Now, for all of you, I shall strike a sudden bolt of lightning.

"Depart! With his staff, he struck the meditation seat and descended from it. On the eighth day of the tenth month of the year Yihai in the Shao-sheng era of Emperor Zhezong of the Song dynasty, the Master, free from ailment, spoke this verse:
"Last night at the third watch, wind and thunder suddenly arose; The clouds dispersed across the vast sky, and the moon sank behind the front creek.
After a long silence, he took leave of the assembly and passed into stillness. Upon cremation, there were *śarīra* relics about a peck in volume, each as large as a bean.
The eyes, teeth, and claws remained undecayed. His disciples divided the pagoda between the capitals of Chang’an and Tanzhou.
At Nan Yue Xilin, Chan Master Chong’ao was asked by a monk: "When one question and one answer are exchanged, the roles of host and guest are clearly defined.

But when there is neither question nor answer, how does one distinguish them? The Master said, "Those sitting remain seated; those standing remain standing. [The monk] said, "If one understands it in this way..."
"How is it? The Master said, "The tongue should rest against the upper palate.

The monk bowed. The Master said, "Do not try to evade it. Zen Master Zhuzhu of Shigudong in Qizhou ascended the hall for a discourse. As questions and answers multiplied, they moved further and further away from the Way.

Why is this? The Way does not belong to knowing; knowing is deluded perception. The Way does not belong to seeing; seeing is the root of delusion. When knowing and seeing are not clear, [one is far from the Way].
Encountering phenomena, they are towering and formidable, linked in an unbroken chain as the root of birth and death.

If one can cast them beyond the great void, worldly thoughts will naturally be forgotten in an instant, and the true mind will be directly revealed. These words are spoken for the sake of those with inferior faculties.
When fellow practitioners meet, there is nothing that is not acceptable. When sitting, the ten directions all vanish; when walking, the six realms follow conditions. Nevertheless.
Furthermore, you must know that there is a single path for turning the body; only then will you be able to find one among the assembly who can turn the body.
Come forward, and I, this mountain monk, shall provide testimony for you. If there is no such person, I, this mountain monk, shall suffer defeat today.

Thus, our Great Awakened World-Honored One practiced asceticism on the Snowy Mountains, attained enlightenment at Magadha, and ascended to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to preach the Dharma for his mother—this is the filial piety of Śākyamuni. Having attained great liberation, he...

There he saw his compassionate mother, weeping immeasurably. This was the filial piety of Maudgalyāyana.
But what is the filial piety of Xinghua? After a long silence, he said: "Today, Xinghua does not ascend to heaven, nor does he enter hell; he is at the Hall of Dharma."
In the center, upon the seat of the Lamp King, he preached the Dharma for his mother to repay her labors. He then asked: "Tell me, where is my mother now? He continued:

Chan Master Shao Deng of Shengquan in Fuzhou was the son of the Chen family of Gutian in his native prefecture. At the time of his birth, an extraordinary fragrance filled the room and a purple cap covered his head.
At the age of seven, he studied various sutras and treatises as if they were the result of past habituation. At ten, he took leave of his parents to enter the monastic life.

In Li, he took Kāifú Zhǐ as his teacher, where he received the tonsure and full ordination. Later, he traveled to Yùquán; upon their first meeting, they were like a needle meeting its eye—a perfect accord.
He subsequently returned to his native village and lived in profound seclusion. Prefect Ding invited him to reside at the Pagoda Cloister on Mount Tuó.
Suddenly, one day, he requested a bath and changed his robes. When the drums were struck and he ascended the seat as the assembly gathered, he spoke this verse:
"At fifty-three years of age, I have no attachment to going or staying. Facing the moment of death, what need is there for idle chatter? He then passed away in solemn stillness.
After two nights with his eyes closed, he suddenly awoke upon hearing the sound of a bell; his four elements felt light and at ease, and thereafter his body would frequently emerge [from the coffin].

Śāriputra. During the Yuánfēng era, there was a great drought in his native prefecture. The Prefectural Governor requested that he perform a rain prayer. The following day, a sweet rain fell in great abundance. He moved to reside at Shèngquán (Holy Spring).

The traces of the fish have already departed from the path. This is because those who go out from here and enter there do not reach their destination, and those who come from elsewhere do not arrive at this place.

Chan Master Zhi Xing of Yanfu at De’an was a native of Western Sichuan. He visited Yuquan to clarify the ground of his mind.

Initially he resided at Jianyuan, then moved to Longhua at Huangmei, and finally settled at Yanfu. The Master’s speech did not discuss the ultimate principle, and his conduct did not involve formal cultivation.

Jie’s person did not conform to formal decorum, and the multitude took no pleasure in seeing him. After his passing, his spiritual manifestations were unfathomable; both monastics and laypeople followed and revered him, fashioning an image to worship it.

Chan Master Zuyin Zhideng of Jingshan, a successor of Chan Master Daowu Zhen, was a native of Jinyuan. He succeeded Daowu at the very age he first established himself [as a monk].

He subsequently opened the Dharma and propagated the Way; those who followed him were like clouds. He preached the Dharma for thirty years. In his later years, he retired to Jue Temple on Mount Yan-shan.
He has a two-volume *Yulu* (Recorded Sayings). The Censor-in-Chief Zou once wrote a preface for it, stating:

"Recently, while I was in Zhongtao, I once discussed the famous monks of the realm with Master Yuan of Li Tao. Master Yuan said: 'Among those I have encountered, there is Zu Yin, who is truly [a master of the lineage].'"
He was one who possessed the Way. To behold his countenance was like gazing upon trees at the end of autumn; to listen to his expositions was like hearing the tide at midnight.

Although such words are not recorded in the *Xinxiu xuandeng lu* (Newly Compiled Record of the Lamp), the few lines remaining in the preface to the *Zhengyan ji* (Record of Correct Words) allow us to form a vivid image of this man.

Today the Sangha points to a deer as a horse; they sing of nine as ten, deceiving all people. The true command of Magadha is impenetrable as water;

It is utterly beyond seeing and knowing; its brilliance transcends both past and present. This is truly because when the mind harbors the measure of the sage, it falls into seeing and knowing;
thus, hearing does not transcend sound, and seeing does not surpass form. If one can turn the light back to reflect upon itself, what Buddha-way could there be to attain?
What sentient beings are there to be saved? [The Buddha] hid his body within the flames; he surged from the east and sank in the west, surged from the south and sank in the north;
he rode a horse upon motes of dust and sat in the Great Place of Enlightenment. Nevertheless, one must by all means avoid mistaking the bridge of a donkey’s saddle for the collar of one’s father.

Later, he arrived at Yangshan, where he remained submerged among the masses, unnoticed by all except Foyin, who alone regarded him as extraordinary. At that time, the Master was resolutely determined.
While he was studying calligraphy, Yinzhi scolded him, saying, "Your original purpose in studying the Way was to resolve the matter of birth and death.
Instead, you are occupied with words and brushstrokes; what benefit does this have for the Way? Thereupon, the Master abandoned his studies and relied upon Dayang Hongzhi at Daopei for ten years.

Daopei’s teaching was as imposing as a towering wall, yet the Master alone received his seal of approval. When Daopei accepted an imperial summons to reside at Xiangguo Temple in the capital, the Master...

The first [monk] asked, "What does the teaching mean? The Master said, "When one grasps the meaning, one forgets the words. The first monk said, "It seems you are still taking the intent of the teachings into your heart; this is a sickness.
The Master replied, "How great is the sickness of those who speak of the Buddha-realm and the Dharma-realm? The first monk was again unable to respond. The following day, he suddenly passed away.
At that time, people called the Master "The One Who Killed the Head Seat. This occurred during the Dazhong era of Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang dynasty.
Finally, at Mount Xinfeng, he attracted and guided his disciples.

Subsequently, he flourished in the Dongshan of Gaoyang in Yuzhang, where he provisionally established the five ranks, skillfully received practitioners of the three capacities, extensively expounded the single sound, and widely propagated the myriad natures. He drew forth the precious sword horizontally.
He pruned the dense forest of various views with wondrous foliage that widely propagated the Dharma;

he severed the myriad forms of forced interpretation and gained a profound and clear understanding of Cao Shan’s essential intent. His sublime songs and excellent maxims harmonized the Way of ruler and subject through the interplay of the partial and the absolute.
Thus, the original wind of Dongshan was disseminated throughout the world, such that the masters of all quarters unanimously honored him, calling it the Caodong School.
The Master said, "It was the anniversary of Yunyan’s death, so we were preparing a vegetarian feast. A monk asked, "What instructions did you receive from Yunyan?
The Master said, "Although I was with him, I did not receive any instructions. The monk said, "If you did not receive any instructions, why did you prepare this feast?
The Master said, "How could I dare to go against him? The monk asked, "When you first met Nanquan, why..."
Ma, however, prepared a vegetarian feast for Yunyan. The Master said, "I do not value my late teacher's moral virtue or his Buddha-dharma;
I only value that he did not explain it through to me. [Ma] asked, "Since you, Master, are preparing a feast for your late teacher, do you still acknowledge him?"
The Master said, "Half-accepting and half-refusing. The monk asked, "Why do you not accept it fully?
The Master said, "If you were to accept it fully, you would be failing your former teacher. A monk asked, "I wish to see the Master’s original teacher; how may I see him?
The Master said, "When our years and teeth are similar, there will be no obstruction. As the monk was about to offer further words, the Master said, "Do not follow in his footsteps; ask for another."

Question: [The monk] remained silent. (Yunju spoke on his behalf: "If that is so, then you have not seen the Master's original teacher. [The monk asked Changqing: "What is it that is like the teeth of a year-old calf?
Changqing said: "The ancients spoke thus; what are you seeking here, O *śrāmaṇera*? Question: "When cold and heat arrive, how can one avoid them? The Master said:
"Why do you not go to a place where there is neither cold nor heat? [The monk] asked: "What is this place where there is neither cold nor heat? The Master said: "When it is cold, freeze to death."

"Ācārya! When it is hot, the heat will kill you, Ācārya! [The Master] ascends the hall and says: "Is there anyone here who does not repay the four debts of gratitude and the three realms of existence?
The assembly is silent. He speaks again: "If you do not realize this meaning, how can you transcend the afflictions of beginning and end?

You must ensure that mind after mind does not touch objects, and step after step has no fixed location. Only when there is constant, uninterrupted continuity will you attain correspondence with the Way. You must exert yourself!"

Do not let your days pass in vain. [The Master] asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from wandering the mountains. The Master said, "Have you reached the summit? He replied, "I have.
The Master said, "Is there anyone at the summit? He replied, "There is no one. The Master said, "If that is so, then you have not reached the summit.
He replied, "If I had not reached the summit, how would I know there is no one? The Master said, "Why do you not stay for a while? He replied, "I..."
He did not decline to stay. A person from India was unwilling to accept this, and the Master said, "I have always harbored doubts about this fellow.
Once, while the Master and Chief Seat Tai were eating fruit on the Winter Solstice, he asked: "There is a thing that reaches up to heaven and down to earth; it is as black as lacquer.
It is constantly present within activity, yet it cannot be contained within activity. Tell me, where does its fault lie?"
"Where? Tai said, "The fault lies in the midst of active functioning. (Tongan Xian added, "He does not know. The Master called to his attendant and had the fruit table removed.
He asked Xuefeng, "Where have you come from? [Xuefeng] said, "From Tiantai. The Master said, "Did you see Zhiyi?
[Xuefeng] said, "Yicun is liable to receive an iron staff. He asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "It is much like being startled."
Jixi asked, "Regarding the story of the snake swallowing the frog: should one save it, or should one not save it? The Master said, "If you save it, its two eyes will not see;
if you do not save it, its form and shadow will not be revealed. There was a monk who was ill and wished to see the Master. The Master went to him.
The monk said, "Master, why do you not save the sons and daughters of others? The Master said, "Who are you?"
[The monk] said, "The man and woman of such-and-such a household; they say that this person is a great icchantika.

After the Master had remained silent for a long while, the monk asked, "What is it like when the four mountains press in from all sides? The Master said, "In recent days, I too have passed beneath the eaves of people's houses.
The monk asked, "Do you yield to them or not? The Master said, "I do not yield. The monk asked, "Where then would you have me go?"
The Master said, "Go into the parched fields. The monk gave a single sigh and said, "Take care," whereupon he sat and passed away.
The Master struck his head three times with his staff and said, "You only know how to go like that; you do not know how to come back like this.

Because he did not light the lamp during the evening assembly, a monk came forward to ask a question. After the monk withdrew, the Master ordered an attendant to light the lamp and then called out, "The one who was just now..."
The Master called to a monk to come forward. The monk approached; the Master said, "Bring me two or three catties of flour and give it to this venerable elder.
The monk shook his sleeves and withdrew. From that moment on, he attained realization. He subsequently gave away all his robes and possessions to provide a vegetarian feast for the assembly.
Three years later, he took his leave of the Master. The Master said, "Farewell. At that time, Xuefeng was standing in attendance and asked, "As for this monk—"
He took his leave. "When will you return? the Master asked. The monk replied, "He only knows how to go; he does not understand how to come back.
The monk returned to the hall and passed away while sitting beneath his robes and bowl. Fengshang reported this to the Master, who said, "Even so, he is still three lifetimes behind me.
He then asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the pagoda of the Third Patriarch. The Master said, "Since you have come from..."
“[The monk] said, ‘I have come from the place of the Patriarch. What do you want to see me, Old Monk, for?
The Master said, ‘The Patriarch is indeed distinct, but you, student, are not distinct from the Abbot. The Master said, ‘I, the old monk, wish to see your original teacher; can you show him to me?
The monk said, ‘That too must wait until the Abbot himself puts his head out. The Master said, ‘Just now, the old monk was away for a short while.’”
An official asked, "Is there anyone practicing the Way? The Master said, "Wait until you become a man, and then you shall practice.

A monk asked, "When meeting someone, one does not bring it forth; when the intention is raised, one knows it immediately—at such a time, how is it? The Master then pressed his palms together and placed them upon his head as a mark of reverence.
He asked a monk, "What have you come to do? The monk replied, "I have come to serve my teacher with filial piety. The Master said, "In this world, what..."
"Things are most filial and obedient. The monk had no reply. Ascending the hall, the Master said:
"There is one person among a thousand or ten thousand people who does not turn his back on anyone and does not face anyone. Tell me, what kind of countenance does this person possess?

Yunju stepped forward and said, "I am going to the meditation hall. The Master sometimes said: "Only when you realize the matter that lies above the Buddha will you have even a fraction of the words [to speak]."
A Case. A monk asked, "What is speech? The Master said, "When you are speaking, you do not hear it. The monk asked, "Does the Master hear it?
The Master said, "When you are not speaking, then you hear it. [The monk] asked, "What is the correct question and the correct answer?
The Master said, "It is not spoken from the mouth. The monk asked, "If someone were to ask, would the Master still answer? The Master said, "Yes."
[The monk] had never asked this before. [The monk] asked, "How is it that those who enter through the gate are not the treasure? The Master said, "It would be well to stop asking.

[The monk] asked, "How many people have been willing since you, Reverend, appeared in the world? The Master said, "Not a single person has been willing. [The monk] asked, "Why is it that not a single person has been willing?
The Master said, "Because each and every one of them possesses a bearing like a king. The Master then questioned the lecturer on the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra*.
The monk said, "It cannot be known by wisdom; it cannot be cognized by consciousness. What kind of statement is this? He replied, "It is a statement praising the Dharmakāya.
The Master said, "To call it 'Dharmakāya' is already praise itself. [The Master] asked, "Constantly and diligently wipe away [the dust]."
"Why was it that he did not receive his robe and bowl? May I ask who was worthy to receive them? The Master said, "One who does not enter the gate.
[The monk] asked, "As for one who does not enter the gate, would they still receive them? The Master said, "Even so, although it is thus, I cannot help but give them to him.
He further said, "Even if one directly says, 'Originally there is not a single thing,' one has still not yet deserved his robe and bowl."
"You tell me: what kind of person is worthy of this? Here, one ought to be able to deliver a turning word. Now tell me: what kind of word can be delivered?
At that time, there was a monk who offered ninety-six turning words, none of which accorded with the Master’s intent; only his very last turning word finally satisfied the Master.
The Master said, "Why did you not speak like this sooner, *ācārya*? Another monk was listening secretly. Only...
He did not hear the final turning of the wheel and consequently requested further instruction from that monk. The monk was unwilling to speak.

Thus they followed one another for three years, yet he never once raised the topic. One day, due to illness, the monk said, "For three years I have requested you to raise the previous story, but I have not received your compassion.
If it cannot be grasped well, it must be abandoned as wrongly grasped. He then took up a blade and said, "If you do not raise it for me..."

He then said, "Even if it were brought forth, there would be no place to put it. The monk bowed in gratitude. There was a master of a hermitage who was unwell;

When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? The Master said: "After the fire, a single stalk of thatch. A questioner asked:
"Master, you usually teach people to practice the 'Bird Path. I do not yet understand what the Bird Path is. The Master said: "Not meeting a single person."
[The monk] asked, "How should one practice? The Master said, "You must simply proceed with no self-interest beneath your feet.
[The monk] asked, "As for practicing the 'Bird Path,' is that not the original face? The Master said, "Disciple, why are you so upside-down? [The monk] asked, "In what way am I upside-down?
The Master said, "If you were not upside-down, why would you mistake the servant for the master? [The monk] said, "It is like this..."
"What is this original face? The Master said, "It does not travel the path of birds.

The Master said, “So it is, so it is. A questioner asked, “From what do the myriad dharmas arise? The Master said, “They arise from inversion.

The Master said, “Why do you act with inversion? A questioner asked, “Why can unmoving grass conceal a fragrant elephant? The Master said, “Acarya.”
"Fortunately, you are a master. He asked again, "What does Caoshan do? [The monk] asked, "The three realms are in turmoil and the six destinies are shrouded in darkness;
how can one distinguish their colors? The Master said, "One does not distinguish their colors. [The monk] asked, "Why does one not distinguish their colors?
The Master said, "If one were to distinguish their colors, that would be delusion. The Master heard the sound of a bell and said, "A-ye! A-ye! A monk asked, "What is the Master doing?"
"What is it? the Master asked. The monk said, "It struck my heart. The monk had no reply. He asked the Rector (Kanna): "Where have you come from?
He replied, "I have been pulling the vinegar tub away. The Master said, "If you reach a dangerous place, how will you pull it then?
The Rector had no reply. He asked Jin-feng Zhi: "What have you been doing? He replied, "I have been building a house. The Master said, "Is it finished yet? He replied, "This side..."
[The monk] said, “I understand. The Master asked, “What about that matter over there? [The monk] replied, “I shall inform the Master on the day the work begins.

Question: "Do the eyebrows and eyes still recognize one another? The Master said, "They do not recognize each other. Question: "Why do they not recognize each other?"

[The monk] asked, "When one is able to exhaust all things, what is it like after this exhaustion? The Master said, "Only then does one know that this sword exists.

[The monk] asked, "Regarding characteristics (*lakṣaṇa*), what is the reality (*tattva*)? The Master said, "Characteristics themselves are reality. [The monk] asked, "How should this be manifested? The Master held up his whisk.

"Most precious. The Master said, "No one puts a price on it. Question: "How can one manifest it when there are no words?
The Master said, "Do not manifest it here. Question: "Where then does one manifest it? The Master said, "Last night, three coins were lost from the head of the bed.

Question: "What is it like before the sun has risen? The Master said, "Cao Shan has also come this way. Question: "What is it like after it has risen? The Master said, "Cao Shan has also come this way."
The Master said, "It is still half a month's journey behind Cao Shan. He asked a monk, "What are you doing? The monk replied, "Sweeping the floor.

[The student] said, "Not carved. The Master said, "You must know that Cao Shan is a master craftsman.
[The student] asked, "What is the retinue of Cao Shan? The Master said, "White hair covers the head; atop it is a single flower.

[The student] asked, "An ancient worthy said, 'Throughout the entire world, there is only this one person. I do not yet understand who this person is. The Master said, "There cannot be a second moon."
[The monk] asked, "What is the second moon? The Master said, "I want you, elder brother, to determine this for me.

[The monk] asked, "What is the first moon? The Master said, "Dangerous! The Master asked Seat-Holder De, "When a Bodhisattva is in meditative concentration and hears of an elephant crossing a river, from which sutra does this come?
[De] replied, "It comes from the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*. The Master said, "Did he hear it before entering concentration, or did he hear it after emerging from concentration? [De] replied, "Both."
[The monk] continued the flow [of the water]. The Master said, “It is the Way; it is indeed the Way, yet you have only spoken half of it.

It is like a region plagued by *gū* poison; one must not let even a single drop of water touch [the person].
Question: "What is the Master of the Dharmakāya? The Master said: "To say that there is no one in Qin. [The student] asked: "Is this not it? The Master said: "Kill! Question:

Question: "Who is it that remains forever submerged in the ocean of birth and death?

Question: "I wonder what kind of person can receive them? The Master said: "One who carries an iron cangue. Question: "When snow covers the thousand mountains, why is one solitary?"
The peak is not white. The Master said, "You must know there is that which is extraordinary within the extraordinary. [The monk] asked, "What is the extraordinary within the extraordinary?
The Master said, "Not falling into the colors of the various mountains. A practitioner in paper robes came to visit. The Master asked, "Are you not the practitioner in paper robes?
He replied, "I dare not say so. The Master said, "What is the matter beneath the paper robe? He replied, "Once the single cloak is hung upon me..."

[The Master said: "The substance: all phenomena are entirely thus. The Master asked: "What is the function beneath the paper robe? The student stepped forward, responded with an assent, and then stood there and removed his clothes.
The Master said: "You only understand going in this way; why do you not understand coming in this way? The student suddenly opened his eyes and asked:
"If the singular, numinous true nature does not rely on a womb, what then? The Master said: "That is not yet wondrous. The student—
[The student] asked, "What is the wondrous? The Master said, "Not borrowed, not lent. Having said this, he paid his respects and passed away. The Master then presented this verse:

"The nature of awakening is perfectly luminous, a formless body; Do not take cognitive views and falsely distance yourself from true awareness. If thoughts differ, you will obscure the profound essence."

When the mind deviates, it does not dwell as a neighbor to the Way; when emotional attachments divide the myriad dharmas, they sink into the realm before one. When the discernment of consciousness becomes manifold, the original truth is lost.
If you can fully understand these words, you will clearly see that you are the person of old, free from affairs.
He asked Upādhyāya Qiáng: "The Buddha’s true Dharma-body is like empty space; responding to things by manifesting forms, it is like the moon in water. How is this so?"
[The monk] spoke of the principle of "responding," saying, "It is like a donkey looking down a well. The Master said, "You have spoken quite well;
you have only managed to express eighty percent of it. [The monk] asked, "How about the Master? The Master said, "It is like a well looking down at a donkey.
A monk related: Yueshan asked a monk, "How old are you? The monk replied, "Seventy-two. Yueshan said, "Is it seventy-two? The monk said, "Yes. Yueshan then—
[The Master] struck him. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The first arrow might still be excusable; the second arrow shoots deep into the person.
[The monk] asked, "How can one avoid being struck by this staff? The Master said, "Once the royal decree has been issued, the feudal lords must clear the way.
[Another monk] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Fill the ditches and block the ravines. Yunmen asked, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said—

The Master said, "Why not say: 'Bearing fur and wearing horns'? The Official bowed. This was the Great Officer Lu Xian.
A monk asked Nanquan, "What is your surname? Nanquan said, "It is Wang. The monk asked, "Does Wang have any kinsmen? Nanquan said, "The four ministers are not obscure.
The monk asked, "In what position does Wang reside? Nanquan said, "Moss grows on the palace steps. Later, a monk cited this question and asked the Master [Linji] about it.

The "Dragon Roars Within the Skull" [koan]. A monk asked, "What is the Way-man? Yanguan said, "Eyes within a skull. The monk did not understand, so he went to ask Shishuang.

On a summer night during the *xinyou* year of the Tang Emperor Zhaozong’s reign (the year 901), he asked the administrative official, "What date is it today?
He replied, "The fifteenth day of the sixth month. The Master said, "Throughout my life of wandering as a pilgrim, wherever I have gone, Cao Shan..."

He calculated ninety days as one summer retreat. On the following day at the hour of the Dragon (7–9 a.m.), he departed on foot on his travels. At that very time, he burned incense, sat in meditative composure, and passed away.
He had lived sixty-two years in the world and held thirty-seven years of seniority (*lǎ*). His entire body was interred on the western slope of the mountain.
He was posthumously titled Chan Master Yuánzhèng, and his stupa was named Fúyuán.
Chan Master Daoying of Yunju in Nankang was a native of the Wang family of Yutian in Youzhou. He left home to become a monk at Yanshou Temple in Fanyang during his childhood.
At the age of twenty-five, he received full ordination as a bhikṣu. His master ordered him to study the *Śrāvaka* precepts (*piānjù*), but this was not to his liking;

[The Master] said: "Do you say that the Tathāgata still possesses a *uṣṇīṣa*? [Question: What is it like when [the robe] cannot be lifted at the head of Dàyǔ Lìng?

The Master said, "Dharma-teacher, you say that Vimalakīrti held up the world with his palm. A monk asked, "I know there is [the Truth]. The Master said, "... (The text ends here).

"It is difficult to find even a single one [who is]. [The monk] asked: "When the toad lacks the power of reflecting back and the jade hare lacks the intention to accompany the moon, what then?

The Master said: "Even the sovereigns Yao and Shun still have their transformative influence remaining. [The monk] asked: "How can one attain this? The Master said: "It is difficult to find even a single one [who has]."

"As your body is at ease, you may go. The Master said, "Only when you are no longer deceived by another body will you succeed" (Fayan added: "Who is troubling you?"). Baociyu praised the Master’s portrait, saying:
"The sun rises over the connected mountains; the moon is full before the door. It is not that there is no body; it is simply that he does not wish to reveal it in its entirety."
One day, the Master was sitting inside his tent. A monk asked, "It is not that you have no body, nor do you wish to reveal it entirely;

He was eighty-nine years of age and seventy-five years since his ordination.

When Chan Master Xiu Jing of Huayan Temple in Jingzhao was serving as the *karmadāna* at Luopo, one day he struck the gavel for a communal work session (*pǔqǐng*) and said, "Those in the upper hall shall carry firewood;
those in the lower hall shall hoe the earth. The First Seat asked, "What is the Holy Monk doing?"
The Master said: "He does not sit upright upon the dais; he does not respond to the dualistic promptings. The Master visited Dongshan and asked, "A student has no path of principle;
I cannot avoid being driven by emotional consciousness. Dongshan replied, "Do you even see any such path of principle?"
The Master said, “There is no way to perceive it. Shan said, “From where have you derived this conceptual consciousness? The Master said, “I am asking in earnest.
Shan said, “In that case, you must go to a place ten thousand miles away where there is not a single blade of grass.

The Master said, “Is one permitted to go to such a place as ‘ten thousand miles away where there is not a single blade of grass’? Shan said, “You must go in just this manner. The Master carried out [the task].
Chai Ci. Dongshan seized him and said, "What is it like when we meet on a narrow path? The Master replied, "Turning this way and that; turning this way and that. Dongshan said, "Remember my words:
if you go south to dwell there, you will have a thousand followers; if you go north to dwell there, you will have only three hundred.
When he first resided at Huayan on Mount Dongshan in Fuzhou, the assembly filled one thousand. Not long after, during the reign of Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang...
[The Master] entered the imperial capital and extensively propagated the profound wind [of the Dharma]. His disciples numbered no more than three hundred.

Emperor Zhuang asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "Having exhausted the search through the treasuries of the Dragon Palace, the multitude of meanings cannot fully explain them.
[The Emperor] asked, "Why does one who has attained great enlightenment still become deluded? The Master said, "A broken mirror does not reflect again; fallen flowers are difficult to retrieve."
Shangzhi asked, "The Great Army has prepared a *Tianwang* (Heavenly King) vegetarian feast seeking victory, while the rebel army has likewise prepared a *Tianwang* feast seeking victory.

Zhuangzong invited the Master into the palace for a meal. There he saw that all the great masters and virtuous monks were reciting scriptures, yet only the Master and his disciples remained silent.

[The Master] sat. The Emperor asked, "Master, why do you not read the scriptures? The Master replied, "When the Way prevails, the imperial edict is not transmitted; when the times are peaceful, there is no need to sing songs of great peace. The Emperor said, "Since you are a junior, why do you instead call yourself 'Elder' (Changlao)? The Master said, "A dragon or phoenix cub at three years of age;
a veteran court official for a hundred years under Your Majesty. Later, the Master traveled through Heshuo and stayed at Pingyang.

He manifested his parinirvāṇa. Upon cremation, śarīras were obtained, and four stūpas were erected: one at Jinzhou, one at Fangzhou, one at the Xiaoyao Garden on Mount Zhongnan, and one at Huayan Temple.
By imperial decree, he was posthumously titled Chan Master Baozhi, and his tomb was named the Wúwéi (Non-action) Stūpa.

The Master struck him. The monk said, “Within the Way of benevolence and righteousness, what fault is there in prostrating? The Master said, “Since your point of origin is not clear, you must undergo strict discipline.
Question: “When the eye does not reach the realm of form, how is it? The Master pointed to the incense altar and asked, “What is this before you?
The monk said, “Please explain this in detail, Master. The Master said, “It will not hinder you from being scrutinized by others. Question: “Regarding every person...”

The student asked, "Is there anyone who is not mad? The Master said, "There is. The student asked, "Who is this one who is not mad? The Master said—

Touzi said, "Tuo Hui’s eyes were not yet open on the road. He asked a monk, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "From Min Province. The Master said, "The long journey must have been difficult. The monk said, "It was not difficult; as soon as one moves a step, one arrives. The Master said, "Is there anyone who does not move a step? The monk said, "There is. The Master said, "How can such a person arrive here? The monk had no reply. The Master drove him away with his staff. [Question: What is the meaning of this? [Answer: It is to test whether the student has realized the Way or not. If they have realized it, they will not be moved by the Master's words. If they have not realized it, they will be unable to respond. This is why the Master used his staff to drive him away. Furthermore, the Master’s question, "Is there anyone who does not move a step? is to see if the student can transcend the duality of movement and stillness. If the student can transcend it, they will not fall into the trap of the Master's words. If they cannot transcend it, they will be stuck in the trap of the Master's words. This is why the monk had no reply. Therefore, one must realize that the Way is not something that can be attained through movement or stillness. It is only when one transcends both movement and stillness that one can truly arrive at the Way. This is the meaning of Touzi's teaching. This is called "the gate of the Way" and "the gate of liberation. If one enters this gate, one will naturally attain liberation. If one does not enter this gate, one will remain bound. Therefore, one must strive to enter this gate. This is the essential point of Touzi's teaching. One must not mistake this for mere intellectual understanding or verbal cleverness. "How is it when the mirror-like mind is unmoving? The Master said, "You lack the power of a great man.

[The student] asked, "What is the power of a great man? The Master said, "When facing the mirror, the mind does not move. [The student] asked, "Why did you just now say that one lacks the power of a great man?

The Master said, "In one's own house, one speaks only of how easy it is to be a guest; it is only when reaching the river that one realizes how difficult it is to catch fish. [The student] asked, "What is..."

[The monk] asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "I see carriages and horses passing through. [The monk] asked, "What is it like for one who is on the Way? The Master struck him. The monk bowed; the Master then shouted.

A monk asked, "How does one accord with the Way throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said, "To accord with the mind is to accord with the Way. [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, how is it?
The Master said, "It would still be tolerable to add mud upon earth, but to seek water apart from the waves is truly pitiable."

Question: "What is the indestructible body? The Master said: "It is precisely this very learning. [The student] said: "People do not understand; I pray the Master will point it out directly. The Master said:
"How much was there of deviation just now? Question: "An ancient said, 'True reality is established through delusion;

from delusion, true reality is revealed. Is this so? The Master said: "Yes. [The student] asked: "What is true reality? The Master said: "That which is not mixed with food. [The student] asked: "What is... (the question is left unfinished).
[The student] said, "Delusion. The Master said, "Arising from inversion and grasping at conditions. [The student] asked, "Setting aside these two paths, how can one attain the perfect and eternal?

The Master said, "If you do not revere the Goddess of Merit, who would begrudge the Woman of Darkness? [The student] asked about the "Single Path" of Jiufeng, which is known throughout ancient and modern times.
"The vehicle of the ultimate source—please, Master, proclaim it! The Master held up his whisk. The monk said, "The assembly is listening intently;
we pray you will grant us a skillful means. The Master said, "In clear waves, fish and dragons do not appear; in swift surging waves, the wind is high. The hook reaches deep and low.
[The monk] said, "If one had not studied long, how could one know this today? The Master said, "Human life has no fixed abode; the image vanishes, yet it remains perfect within the mirror."
A questioner asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Ask someone else. The questioner said, "If that is so, then my entire being is it.
The Master said, "One must wear Mount Sumeru upon the crown of one's head."
When Chan Master Tong of Beiyuan in Yizhou first visited Jia Shan, he asked: "The Dharma is not before the eyes; its intent lies within the eyes.
It is not the Dharma of the present moment, nor is it that which reaches the ears or the eyes. Is this not the Master’s own teaching? Jia Shan replied:
The Master then overturned the meditation seat and stood with his hands folded. Dongsan rose and struck him once with his staff;
the Master then descended from the seat. Next, he visited Dongshan. Dongshan ascended the hall and said, "Severing the host, one does not fall into a secondary view.
The Master stepped forward from the assembly and said, "One must know there is a person who does not keep company. Dongshan said, "That is still a secondary view."
The Master then overturned the meditation seat. Deshan said, "What will you do, Senior Monk? The Master replied, "I shall wait until my tongue has rotted before I speak to you, Reverend.
Later, as he was taking leave of Dongshan and preparing to enter the mountain passes, Dongshan said, "Be careful on Flying Ape Ridge;
it is steep and must be watched closely. The Master remained silent for a long while. Dongshan called out, "Dharma-heir Tong! The Master responded, "Yes? Dongshan said, "Why did you not enter?"
The Master departed from Lingji. Thereupon, he attained realization and never again entered Lingji. Later, while presiding over the assembly, he ascended the hall and said:
"Venerable elders, what matters are there? Come forward and discuss them! Those of the highest capacity do not require such methods.
As for those of middling or inferior capacity, you must strip away the thresholds and bases of the gates until they are bare and empty; do not let them sink into the mud and water. However...
First, you must quickly put an end to your affairs. You must simply learn with a mindless state; otherwise, all manner of things will result in mere intellectual understanding.
What connection does that have with the Gate of the Patch-robed Monks? A monk asked: "If one must learn with a mindless state, how should it be done?"
The Master said, "I do not care about being tied up. Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A sheer cliff originally has no moss. [He] sprinkled ink to depict mottled patterns. Question:
"When two dragons contend for the pearl, who is the one that obtains it? The Master said, "The one who obtains it loses it.
[The questioner] asked, "How is it for the one who does not obtain it? The Master said, "Give me back the pearl! Question: "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
Wuming asked, "When one cannot turn [the situation] around, what then? The Master said, "The merit has not yet reached it. A monk asked, "What is the person of great wealth and honor?
The Master said, "Like the treasure-store of a Wheel-Turning King. The monk asked, "What is the person who is utterly destitute?
The Master said, "Like the apron-string of a wine shop. A monk asked, "When water cannot wet [it], what then? The Master said, "Dry."
*Pò pò dì.* [The student] asked: "What is it like when one blow brings about completion? The Master said: "It is not a mere coincidence. [The student] asked:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "A withered pine painted on a wall; wandering bees compete to gather its pollen."
He manifested his passing. Later, by imperial decree, he was posthumously titled Chan Master Zhengzhen (Certified Truth).
When Chan Master Daquan of Dongshan questioned the former Dongshan, "What is the essential method for transcending and leaving [samsara]?

Dongshan replied, "Dharma brother, smoke rises from beneath your feet. The Master attained realization on the spot and no longer traveled elsewhere. Yunju entered the discussion, saying, "In the end..."
"I dare not fail you, Reverend; smoke is rising from beneath your feet. Dongsan said, "Every step that is originally so is the arrival of merit.
When Dongshan passed away, the assembly requested [Dongsan] to follow in his footsteps as abbot. A monk asked, "When the Buddha entered the royal palace, was this not the Great Sage returning?
The Master said, "Huming did not descend to be born. The monk said, "But what about the six years of ascetic practice?"
The Master said, "An illusory person presents illusory affairs. [The student] asked, "What is it that is not illusory? The Master said, "It cannot be found even in the royal palace.
[The student] asked, "Regarding the pure practitioner who does not enter nirvana, and the precept-breaking bhikṣu who does not enter hell—at such a time, what is it?
The Master said, "When all have been saved without leaving a trace, he returns to transcend nirvana. [The student] asked, "When the eye reaches out for a thousand li, this is..."
"What is your style? The Master said, "That is your style, O *ācārya*. [The monk] asked, "I do not yet know what the Master’s style is like.
The Master said, "I do not spread out the eyes of *vaśavartin*."
The Chan Master Xiandeheshang of Jingzhao was a man of unknown origins. His life and deeds were remarkably extraordinary; he had no fixed dwelling place.

Having realized the mind through Dongshan, he lived among the common people in Minchuan. He possessed no ritual implements and did not observe monastic regulations. Throughout both winter and summer, he wore only a single robe.
Day after day, he would go along the riverbanks to gather shrimp and clams to sustain himself. At dusk, he would simply stay overnight at the eastern [shore].
At the Shrine of the White Horse on Mount Shan, the local residents called him the "Shrimp Monk. When Huayan Jingwen heard of this, he wished to determine whether the man was genuine or not.
He first hid himself within the paper money offerings. Late at night, when the Master returned, Jingwen grabbed him and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master immediately replied, "The wine stand and platter before the deity. Jingwen let go of him and said, "..."
It was no mere coincidence that he shared the same roots as myself. Later, when Emperor Zhuangzong summoned him to the capital, Chang’an, the Master had already arrived there beforehand.
Every day he would sing and play his own instruments, or feign madness, wandering through mud and snow until no trace of him remained.
His final whereabouts were never known.
Master Daoyou of Youqi in Taizhou was asked by Jingqing, "What is the 'Lesser Father'? The Master said, "There is no target.
Jingqing said, "Is it because there is no target that he is called the Lesser Father? The Master said, "What fault is there in that? Jingqing said, "As for the Lesser Father himself, how is he?
The Master said, "What kind of mental activity is this, you who ask? [Another] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master—

[The monk] said, "You do not believe this is a sentient being. The Master said, "A student of the Way must have great faith. [The monk] said, "If one forms a conceptual resolve (*adhimukti*), one will immediately succumb to various delusions.
[The monk] asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Wherever there is a path that can be ascended, those who are superior to others also travel upon it.
[The monk] asked, "What is one who is on the Way? The Master said, "One who understands how to drive away the clouds and possesses faith. One day at the time of the midday meal, the Master...
Entering the hall, he struck the wooden gavel and said, "I inform the assembly. The assembly raised their heads; the Master said, "Now, eat your rice.

When the Master was about to pass away, a monk asked, "After the Master’s hundred-year life has ended, where will you go? The Master replied, "Far, far away," and having finished speaking, he sat and passed away.
When Master Qianfeng of Yuezhou ascended the hall, he said: "The Dharma-body has three kinds of illnesses and two kinds of lights;
you must penetrate each one thoroughly before you can return home and sit in peace. You must know that there is yet a 'further' opening above this.
Yunmen stepped forward and asked, "Why does the person within the hut not know what is outside the hut? The Master laughed heartily. Yunmen said: [and prostrated].
This was still a point of doubt for the student. The Master asked, "What is the state of your mind? Yunmen said, "I also wish for the Master to understand me.
The Master said, "You must be thus before you can sit securely. Yunmen responded, "Yes, yes. He ascended the hall and said, "If you cite one, you cannot cite two;
to let go of one is to fall into the second. Yunmen stepped forward from the assembly and said, "Yesterday..."
A man came from Tiantai and was heading toward Jingshan. The Master said, "The head cook must not be called for general labor tomorrow," and then descended from his seat.
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "Tiantai. The Master said, "I heard it was said that the Stone Bridge has been split in two—is this true?
The monk asked, "From where did the Master receive this news? The Master said, "I thought it was the Flower Peak (Huading)."
"A guest before the peak is originally a person from the level fields and manor. [Someone] asked, "How does one go forth beyond the three realms?
The Master said, "Call the monastery steward to drive this monk out! The Master asked the assembly of monks, "In transmigrating through the six destinies, what kind of eye do you possess?
The assembly had no reply. [Someone] asked, "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? The Master said, "Old..."
A monk asked, "What about this? [The Master] said, "Let us set aside your question, Master. The Master said, "Even when the old monk asks, you are still at a loss;

what need is there to speak of talk that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? [The monk] asked, "Regarding the verse: 'The Bhagavans of the ten directions / Follow the single path to the gate of Nirvana.'"

Chan Master Foji Benkong of Hangzhou first traveled to Mount Tiantai. He once said, "If there were someone who could seize my vital pivot (*ji*), that person would be my teacher.

At that time, he was thirteen years old. Four years later, he visited Jiashan. As soon as he entered the gate, he saw the *karmadāna* (rector).

The bright window speaks; I shall tell you at once. On the following day, Jia Shan ascended the hall and asked, "Where was the one who arrived yesterday?

[The Master] was crossing the waves. Xie invited him to come further, asking, "What do you think of this? The Master said, "I have long dwelt among crags and valleys, unattached to pines and vines.

A questioner asked, "What is it like when suchness is unmoving? The Master said, "When will there ever be an end to this? The questioner asked, "How is that so?

[The monk] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Oṃ. [The monk] asked, "What is the point of acting for others' benefit to the ultimate degree? The Master said, "A diligent entrustment."
A later person asked, "Why did Piṇḍola go to receive offerings from all four continents with a single body?
The Master said, "A thousand rivers reflect the same moon; ten thousand households encounter spring together. He then spoke a verse:

"The precious lunar orb atop Dragon King Mountain Shines upon heaven and earth, piercing through the dark clouds. The Venerable One does not move from his original singular substance, Yet its reflection appears in a thousand homes and ten thousand directions."
Jiachun. A monk asked Master Bajiao of Yingzhou, "How should one apply the mind throughout the twelve hours of the day?
