A monk asked Chan Master Huiju of Shizang in Dingzhou, "What is the meaning of the West? The Master said: "The trees bear the color of the Canglang River;
the mountains stretch across as a single streak of green. [The monk] asked, "What is the monastery? The Master said: "It is just this."
[The monk] asked, "What is it like to be among those within a monastery? The Master said, "How? How? [The monk] asked, "If a guest should suddenly arrive, with what will you receive them?
The Master said, "Go drink tea."
Chan Master Zhongyun Zhihui of Jingzhao Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Baishui Ren. He was the son of the Gao family from Xianning.

During his childhood, he delighted in visiting Buddhist temples and vowed to leave the household life; his parents could not dissuade him. He received the tonsure under Guifeng Wen and later went to visit Baishui.
He alone mastered the subtle words [of the Buddha] and secretly penetrated the secret keys [of the Dharma]. He returned to Luo and chose a site at Zhongtan to establish the Wenshi Monastery.
His constant practice was to provide water and administer medicine. There was a bhikṣu suffering from white leprosy whom everyone loathed;

only the Master treated him by massaging and washing him as usual. Suddenly, there appeared divine light and extraordinary fragrance. When the others marveled at this, the bhikṣu vanished without a trace, leaving behind only his scabs.

The fragrance was pungent and intense; they subsequently gathered it together and fashioned a statue of Avalokiteśvara to enshrine it within. Later, the Master suddenly desired to return to his former residence at Mount Guifeng in Zhongnan.
One day, while strolling idly among the crags and grottoes as he usually did when resting, he suddenly beheld a set of monastic robes, a rosary, a copper pitcher, and a palm-leaf hat.
Upon touching them, they immediately crumbled to pieces. He said to his attendant, "These were the ritual implements from my previous life."

[He] arrived here and established a temple to repay his past karmic causes. While he was clearing away the weeds, auspicious clouds shrouded the sun, gathering at the mountain peak and remaining there for a long time without dispersing;
consequently, it was named Mount Chongyun (Heavy Clouds). Fierce beasts all withdrew of their own accord, and when the dragon pool was filled to open a path, the dragon also moved elsewhere.
Later, during the reign of Emperor Mingzong of the Later Tang, the imperial plaque was granted with the name Changxing. Disciples...
Zhencui. A monk asked, "What is it to return to the root and attain the essential meaning? The Master said, "Already forgotten; one does not recall the arising of dust.
The monk asked, "What is it to follow illumination and lose the source? The Master said, "The home is raided by thieves.

The monk asked, "Regarding 'not recalling the arising of dust,' what is the single path for advancing forward? The Master said, "Grass has already grown beneath your feet; ahead lies a pit ten thousand fathoms deep."
Question: "The essential path is level and open; how does one tread upon it? The Master said: "If I were to point it out to you, you would go off toward the east, west, south, or north.
Question: "What is the Scale of the Heavy Clouds? The Master said: "Examine the whole world as you please.

Question: "What are words that cut through iron? The Master said: "Better to die than to violate them. Question: "What is Kāśyapa? The Master said: "Better to die than to violate them. (Note: This response repeats the previous answer, likely indicating a thematic continuity regarding the gravity of the matter.)
He heard these matters directly from the master himself. The Master said, "Chongyun cannot remember. Question: "What is the realm of Chongyun?
The Master said, "In all four seasons, flowers cluster thickly; throughout the three months of winter, strange grasses remain green. The Master expounded the Dharma for over forty years.

While he was still of humble status, the Military Commissioner Wang Yanchao often accompanied the Master on excursions. Desiring to become a śramaṇa, the Master gazed at him intently and said, "You..."

"The worldly conditions are profound; you shall serve as the boundary wall for my house. Later, when the Duke of Wang was stationed at Yongxing, he performed the rites of a disciple toward the Master.

When the Master was about to pass away, he first took leave of the Duke of Wang, entrusting him with the protection of the Dharma-gate. The Duke wept and said, "Can the Master truly bear to abandon his disciple?
The Master smiled and said, "Even if one borrows a thousand years, it is but a single parting. Upon returning, he composed a verse and showed it to the assembly.
He said, "I have a single room that my parents built for me; I have lived here for eighty years. Lately, I have noticed it is falling into ruin, and I intended to move elsewhere early on.
However, such matters involve likes and dislikes; I shall wait until it collapses of its own accord, so that there will be no obstruction for either side.
Thereupon, he sat in the full lotus posture and passed away on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month of the Bingchen year in the Xiande era of Emperor Shizong of the Later Zhou dynasty.
He lived to the age of eighty-four and had been a monk for sixty-four years. His stupa was erected at his home mountain.
Chan Master Youzhang of Ruilong Monastery in Hangzhou was the younger nephew of the Tang Prime Minister Xiahou Zhi.

At the beginning of the Dazhong era, when his uncle, the Grand Master of Ceremonies (Sikong), was sent to govern Guangling, the Master was seven years old and was visiting Huizhao Temple, where he heard [the recitation of]...
Fahua was determined to seek ordination as a monk. His paternal uncle initially refused, but when Fahua ceased taking food and drink, his uncle had no choice but to grant his permission.
He took Huiyuan as his teacher. Later, he traveled to various Chan assemblies at Shushan and Baihui, where he received the essential instructions of the mind-transmission from all of them.
In the *Renchen* year of the Xiantong era, he arrived at Jiangling. Master Tengteng instructed him, saying:
"Go to Tiantai and seek a quiet place to dwell; stop wherever you encounter peace. Later, he met Master Hanzhan, who patted him and said:
"Forty years from now, there will be a Bodhisattva beneath Mount Jingshan who shall rule over Jiangnan. At that time, my Way—"

Prosperous indeed! He subsequently arrived at Mount Tiantai and established the Fudang Monastery in Jing’an Township. This fulfilled his own words of "leaping about. He later resided at the Yilong Monastery.

During the Jiachen year of the Zhonghe era, when famine and pestilence ravaged the region of Zhejiang, the Master collected and buried the remains of the deceased throughout the three prefectures of Wenzhou, Taizhou, and Mingzhou;
he was then known as the Great Being Pizeng. Xuefeng once went to visit him and left behind a *tāla* fan.

He brushed aside [the invitation] and departed. In the *Bingyin* year of the Tianyou era, Qian Shangfu dispatched his envoy Tong Jian to bring robes, incense, and medicinal herbs into the mountains to extend an invitation.
Upon arriving at the prefectural courtyard, he was appointed as the Great Master Zhide and lodged in the Hall of Meritorious Ministers. The Lord personally inquired about the Dharma every day.
The Master requested that a *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* (Golden Light) ritual site be established annually on Mount Tiantai, with the clergy and laity from all the commanderies participating.
The assembly met and dispersed after more than a month (the Great Assembly of Radiance began with him).

As he was about to take his leave and return to the mountains, the King felt deep affection and built Rui Long Monastery within the palace precincts (King Wenmu later renamed it Bao Shan Monastery), inviting him to propagate the Dharma. At that time, the Chan school flourished;
thus, the prophecy of Hanhan was fulfilled. Ascending the hall, he said: "In years past, this old monk traveled abroad through Jiangwai, Lingnan, Jing, and Hu."
There is no one among those who know me or have visited the various monasteries who has not come to inquire after me.

This is because today I am gathered with you all, and each of you wishes to know the destination of the Way. Yet, throughout all quarters, there is never any divergent teaching; it simply instructs each person to bring their frantic mind to rest and cease seeking from others.
Simply follow the direction and let nature take its course—yet there is no "nature" to be taken as real. Use it according to the occasion, and yet...
There is no time when this can be applied. Even if you were to show compassion and speak with bitter candor, you still could not call day night;
even with further skillful means, you ultimately could not point east and call it west. Should you be able to do so, that would merely be a supernatural feat of wonder and has nothing to do with me.
As for those who merely parrot words, failing to reflect upon themselves and recognize their error, they are simply attempting to pluck flowers from the sky.
"Can you take the moon from the waves and put it back where it was? You should each withdraw for a moment and reflect.
If you suddenly agree, only then will you know that Old Man Rui-long had no choice but to go to such great lengths. Do you agree now?
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the realm of Rui-long? The Master said, "Do you not see it? The monk asked, "What is the realm?"
[The Master] said, "A person of middling capacity. The Master said, "Those who come later are to be feared. [The monk] asked, "When it is vast and empty with no clouds, what is the mid-autumn moon?
The Master said, "The best is when there are no clouds. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then a single wheel is suspended on high, and ten thousand lands behold it together.
The Master said, "It is difficult to speak with one who squints their eyes. The fourth year of the Tiānchéng era of Emperor Míngzōng of the Later Táng dynasty, the *Dīnghài* year.

In the [first] month, he requested a site for the stupa from the Supreme Father (Yi Sun-sin). The Father ordered Lu Renzhang to select a superior location at Xiguan to construct the stupa and establish a monastery, renaming the "Tiantai Yilong" as "Yiji.
Upon the completion of the stupa, the Master entered the official residence to take leave of the Supreme Father, entrusting him with the protection of the Dharma.

He passed away peacefully on a predetermined date. The Supreme Father mourned him deeply and dispatched the Sangjeong (Chief Administrator of Monks) to assemble the virtuous elders residing in the city to welcome [the remains].
He was brought to the pagoda. His age was eighty-seven and his years of ordination were seventy.

Chan Master Kuanghua Zangyu of Baoci Monastery in Tanzhou, successor to Chan Master Longya Dun, was asked by a monk: "What is it like when the eye and the mind see each other?
The Master said: "What would I say to you? He was further asked: "What is the place of true seeing? The Master said: "Not separated by even a hair’s breadth."
[The student] said, "If that is so, then I have seen [the truth]. The Master said, "Nanquan had a truly fine place to go. [The student] asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?

“Where have you come from? he asked. “I have come from Sleeping Dragon,” he replied. The Master said, “How long have you been there? “I have passed through both winter and summer.

Chan Master Shenzhe of Hanzhushan in Xiangzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Master’s deepest place?
The Master said, "As soon as a single inch-nail enters the wood, nine oxen cannot pull it out. The monk asked, "What is the Eye of the True Dharma?
The Master said, "The spirit-tree in front of the gate. The monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "A poor child holds [his mother's] breast."
Zi Du was crossing a river when his wife and children followed after him, vying for his affection. He asked a monk, "Existence is not it; non-existence is not it;

[The Master] said, "For now, rejoice that there is no connection. [The monk] asked, "How is it so? The Master said, "At this point of intimacy, please ask another question.
[The monk] said, "I, your disciple, cannot say it; I beg the Master to speak. The Master said, "Come on another day, and I will tell you. [The monk] asked, "Why do you not say it right now?
The Master said, "I cannot find a person capable of grasping these words. He then questioned a monk: "Zhang..."
"King, Li, Zhao—these are not your original surnames. What is your original surname? The monk replied, "I share the same surname as the Master.
The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment that you share the same surname, what is your original surname?
The monk replied, "Wait until the Han River flows backward, and then I will tell the Master. The Master said, "Why do you not say it now? The monk replied, "The Han River [is flowing backward]."
"Is it still flowing? The Master ceased speaking. A monk asked, "What is it like when one recognizes [the nature] in accordance with conditions?
The Master said, "What is there to ask? [Another] asked, "What is the true person of no station? The Master said, "How could you manage by making other arrangements?
The monk asked, "What is it like when there are no arrangements? The Master said, "The true person of no station. A monk asked, "What is the true scripture? The Master said, "A."
Mida. A monk asked Zen Master Xichuan Cun: "The student understands how to ask about the enigmatic phrase; I pray that the Master will manifest the 'startling' faculty.

"Will the Master receive me? The Master then struck him.
Zen Master Kuangyi Dingjue of Ziling in Fengxiang Prefecture, a successor of Zen Master Huijing of Huayan, first arrived at Panlong. Seeing a monk, he asked: "The azure pool..."
"Clear as a mirror. Where does the coiled dragon dwell? The Dragon said, "Sunk in the sand, its bottom is unseen; floating on the waves, it is full of rugged peaks.
The Master did not approve. The Dragon asked the Master to speak. The Master said, "The golden dragon soars far beyond the azure heavens;

how could it be hindered within the pool by the mechanism of the jade wheel? The Dragon approved. After he took up residence there, a monk asked, "Before one has yet taken human form, what is one doing?"
[The Master] came forward. The Master said: "The stone ox walks step by step through fire; looking back, it need no longer chew the grass at midday. A questioner asked:

"When the path of intellect and consciousness is severed and thought and deliberation are both forgotten, what is it like? The Master said: "Ceasing imprisonment only increases wisdom; nursing an illness only brings ruin to the body."
A monk asked National Teacher Wei of Tong’an Temple in Hongzhou, successor to Chan Master Man of Jiufeng: "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "The divine tree by the roadside; all who see it raise their hands in prostration. The monk asked, "What was it like after he saw him? The Master said, "Inside the room."
"No spirit-bed; the whole family does not wear mourning. A question was asked: "Regarding the meaning of the Patriarch and the meaning of the Teaching—do they coincide or do they differ?
The Master said: "The Jade Hare has never known the meaning; how could the Golden Crow ever consent to shine at night? A question was asked: "What is the single song of Tong’an? The Master said:
"The numinous lute does not share the melodies of the human world; those who know the sound, how could they pass through the hundred gates? [He] said: "..."
"Who, I wonder, can harmonize with this? The Master said, "When the wooden horse neighs, listen to it from there; when the stone man claps his hands, who hears it?

A monk asked, "What is it like when one encounters a true知音 (zhīyīn—a 'connoisseur' or 'one who understands')? The Master said, "The connoisseur does not pass through the ears. How could those who have attained be the same as those who merely hear?
One day, as the Master was touring the mountains, the assembly followed behind him. The Master said, "The lush green bamboos before the steps, beneath the courtyard tiles..."
Yellow Flowers. An ancient said, “True Suchness is Prajñā. Tong’an, however, was not like this. A monk asked, “The ancients were also like this, Master.
The Master said, “Not coveting the taste of fragrant bait, he may truly be called a dragon in the azure pool. [The monk] said, “The eyes of those in all quarters do not doubt Yuanming.
The Master said, “Dharma brother, you sit with eyes closed during the Mid-Autumn festival, yet you laugh that the moon has no light. [The monk] said, “The steps...”
"Green bamboos in front; yellow chrysanthemums beneath the steps. What about that? The Master said, "Annam has not yet submitted; how could the northern frontier be conquered? The monk bowed.
The Master said, "His fame is heard everywhere. The Master asked a monk, "At dawn and at dusk, you seek food and drink;
you have no place to hide your body. Do you say there is such a principle? The monk asked, "How about you, Master? The Master struck him once with his whisk.
The monk said, "Clapping hands to challenge a man—this is merely boasting of being a skilled hand. The Master said, "Holding a whip and tilting one's cap—is that you, O *śrāmaṇera*?
The monk said, "Where can the Way of ancient and modern times hide itself? The Master said, "How about you, *śrāmaṇera*?
The monk said, "Take care," and then departed. The Master said, "Not yet."
When the Monk Xiangcheng of Jingzhao Prefecture first visited Chan Master Beiyuan Tong, he asked: "What is it like when one appears as two?"

The Master said, "A five-colored pennant is planted before the peak of Chao-yi. The monk asked, "How is it when there is no involvement with literary colors?
The Master said, "Right now, he has come across the river on purpose. A monk asked, "Regarding the one path above, I ask the Master to proclaim it."
The Master said, "A fishing line cannot pull out a hook. [The monk] asked, "Does Niutou still grasp the meaning of the Fourth Patriarch?

The Master said, "When writing in sand, the dot below the character falls as a thousand characters. [The monk] asked, "What is it like after the dot has fallen? The Master said, "I shall separately take another pinch to represent humans and devas.
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then everyone possesses it. The Master said, "And what about you? [The monk] asked, "The bag is empty."

The silk thread binding the ants is severed; the crumbs gathering flies in the kitchen are cut off—at such a time, what is there to do? The Master said: "Day after day one discards [what is real] without seeking it, yet pursues it through delusion to obtain it.
This was the seventh generation under Qingyuan.

The Seal of Understanding. Opening the Dharma at Shanglan. A monk asked, "What is the bladeless sword of Shanglan? The Master said, "None.

When Chan Master Huimin of Tongan in Hongzhou first visited Dongshan, he asked, "By what do all the sages take their life?
Dongshan replied, "By non-interruption. The Master asked, "Is there anything further beyond this? Dongshan said, "There is. The Master asked, "What is that which is further?
Dongshan said, "It does not follow from interruption. At these words, the Master attained realization. After he took up residence [at Tongan]:
A monk asked, "I request a single phrase from the Master. The Master said, "Remember it well.

At Mount Lumen in Xiangzhou, Zen Master Zhi-xing Tan was asked by a monk, "What is the ground of ultimate reality? The Master replied:
"Jambudvīpa in the south; Uttarakuru in the north. [The student] said, "If that is so, then we are of one family in this matter. The Master said, "Mount Sumeru stands between us.

Master Xingyin of Foshouyan on Mount Lu was a native of Yanmen. He first visited Lumen, where he attained profound spiritual resonance with his teacher.
Subsequently, he traveled to the northern reaches of Mount Lu, where there was a cliff resembling five fingers and a stone cave below it about three zhang in depth.
The Master took up residence therein and was consequently known as the Monk of Foshouyan (Buddha-Hand Cliff). Although the Prince of Jiangnan summoned him three times, he steadfastly declined.
He was invited to open the hall at Qixian, but before a month had passed, he returned in secret to his mountain retreat.
A monk asked, "What is the manifestation of the physical body? The Master held up one finger. Later, manifesting a slight illness, he said to his attendant monk, "At noon today, I shall depart.

A monk asked, “What is the matter beneath the patched robe? The Master said, “Mystery. While the Master was sitting with Elder Rui, a monk asked, “Since two Honored Ones do not appear together in the world, why do you two both occupy the abbot’s quarters?
The Master said, “Even ‘one’ is not. He had a verse that said: “Liangshan is one.”

A Melodious Song. Difficult for those outside the school to harmonize with. For ten years I have sought a true friend, yet never once have I met one. Questioning the passing of a deceased monk: "Where has he gone? The Master said: "When did the deceased monk pass away? [The questioner] said: "What can we do about seeing him off? The Master said: "A strand of silk thread upon the flames of a red furnace; amidst the dense clouds, he does not nod his head. *Upasarga* (Supplementary Verse): A Melodious Song. Ascending the hall: "The hook is cast across the four seas; it is intended only for the fierce dragon. This profound mechanism beyond the mundane is for seeking a kindred spirit.
Ascending the hall: "A thousand fathoms of line are cast; the intent lies in the deep pool. A single phrase spans the void, while the white clouds remain distinct. A solitary boat is rowed alone."
He did not violate the clear waves, yet he traveled freely across the sea; it was rare to encounter one with such clear discernment. A questioner asked, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe?
The Master said, "Not revealed by all the sages. As the Master approached his passing, he presented this verse:
"The crimson flames conceal my body; Why need a new stupa be used? If there is someone who truly appreciates it, Within the ashes, the absolute reality is sought."
Chan Master Changjue of Pujing Monastery in Dongjing was a dharma successor of Chan Master Guizong.
He was a native of the Li family in Chenliu. In his youth, he studied Confucianism, yet he had no desire for official rank.

His mind delighted in mountains and rivers; he first visited Guizong, and upon hearing the Dharma, he attained realization. Thereupon, he sought to leave the household life. Not long after, he returned.
When Zong was about to pass into *parinirvāṇa*, he summoned the Master and patted him on the head, saying, "You have a karmic affinity with the Dharma;

in the future, you shall deliver the multitude, for no one can fathom your capacity. He then entrusted the matter of his tonsure to the various disciples. The Master arrived in the *Ren-shen* year of the Later Liang (*952 CE*) and shaved his hair.
The following year, he received the full precepts at the Amṛta Altar of Donglin Temple. He subsequently traveled to Mount Wutai and then returned.
In the capital, while residing alone for two years outside Lijing Gate, there was a lay devotee from the north named Mr.

Zhang who invited the Master to receive his offerings. Mr. Zhang had long investigated the principles of the Daoist source; he therefore sought instruction from the Master, who then guided and inspired him according to his capacity.

Under these words, Mr. Zhang attained awakening and realization. He prepared a mat and invited the Master to stay overnight. At the deep of night, he and his wife secretly peered in and saw the Master...
His body filled the entire mat, with both his head and feet protruding from it. When he ordered his maidservants and attendants to look at him, they saw him exactly as usual;
their reverence and admiration redoubled, and they said, "We, your disciples, are an elderly couple. We now wish to donate the front hall of our residence to supplement this chamber for the Master.

The Master joyfully accepted the offer. By the year Wuzi of the Chengtian era during the Later Tang dynasty, it had become a large monastery complex, and the imperial plaque was bestowed upon it naming it Pujing (Universal Purity).

The Master, considering that the capacity of the times was shallow and dull, feared it would be difficult to sustain the ultimate meaning. He thought that if he were to reveal it to those who were not fit vessels, they would incur the blame of slander and resentment;
thus, he preferred not to strive to propagate the Dharma. Every month on the third, eighth, and thirteenth days, he provided bathing facilities for monks and laypeople by the tens of thousands.
The Master once said to his disciples, "If only the gate of wisdom remains unobstructed, how could blessings ever be hindered? One day, he provided...
While serving as an official, Tao Gu visited the monastery to pay his respects and asked: "The sutras state that when one is free from all marks, one is called a Buddha.
Yet, before our very eyes, all manner of marks are in profusion; how can one be free from them? The Master replied, "Official, what have you seen? Tao was delighted and held him in high esteem.
From then on, although princes, dukes, and great officials repeatedly recommended him for robes, official rank, and the title of Master, he declined them all.
On the second day of the twelfth month of the Xinwei year of Emperor Taizu’s Kaibao era of the Song dynasty, he manifested illness. On the eleventh day, he addressed the assembly;
having completed his final instructions, he passed away reclining on his right side. He was seventy-six years of age and fifty-six years since his ordination.
Chan Master Defu of Yunding in Huainan was a successor of Chan Master Huguo. When he first visited Huguo, he asked: "The Buddha’s seal is the direct source;
I am unable to pluck leaves or guide branches—what then? Huguo said: "Cease grasping at the clouds and trees for three autumns."
"Indeed! Cease playing with the solitary moon-disk in the azure pool. Thereupon, the Master suddenly resolved his doubts.
The Military Governor of Chengdu invited him to ascend the seat in the official yamen. A general from the music corps came forward to pay his respects;

rising, he looked back toward the mounting platform and said, "I do not ask about 'drinking up the waters of the West River in a single gulp,' but I request the Master to swallow this mounting platform before my feet. The Master extended both hands.
He called out, "Polish it finely and bring it here! At this, the attendant had a sudden and profound awakening.
Master Daoyang was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Jian of Dayang.
A monk asked Master Cong of Shimen in Xiangzhou, "After Daoyang passed away, where did he go? The Master said:
Riding an ox without wearing a hat; sitting upright without walking crookedly.
A monk asked Chan Master Qianian of Beichen in Tanzhou, "What is the source of the Great Way? The Master said, "The myriad streams cannot mix it.
The monk asked, "How is it when one is uniquely liberated? The Master said, "Piercing clouds and penetrating rocks. [The monk] asked, "How is it?"
"This does not fall into the trap of ancient or modern phrases. The Master said: "The fifteenth and the sixteenth; the sun and moon pursue one another.
Chán Master Shàoyuàn of Shímén in Xiángzhōu was a successor of Chán Master Shíchén of Shímén. Initially, while serving as a field overseer at Shímén, Shímén asked him: "What is..."
"A water buffalo at the edge of the field. The Master said, "Its horns turn and thunder across heaven and earth; where the morning sun shines, there is spring everywhere.
On another day, the Gatekeeper asked again, "Is the water buffalo well? The Master said, "It has never lacked grass and water.

[The Gatekeeper] asked, "What about its work in the field? The Master said, "Deep plowing and shallow sowing. [The Gatekeeper] said, "It is acting according to the Dharma. The Master said, "I have never acted recklessly."
After he had taken up residence, a monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style do you succeed? The Master said:
"Throughout the ten directions there is no divergent path; it surpasses Fenglin. [The monk] asked: "The former master has already returned to the Wild Goose Pagoda;
please, Master, proclaim the single phrase of Dangyang. The Master said: "Holding the sun and moon within the palms of an asura; treading upon a mud-dragon with the feet of a yakṣa."

Question: "The golden dragon does not breathe forth the mists of the mundane world; I pray the Master will reveal the phoenix-like pivot. The Master said: "The white-browed one does not extend his hand;
the road to Chang’an is level and plain. Question: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said: "A cloth bag containing a tortoise.
Question: "What is the realm of Shimen? The Master said: "A solitary peak facing Fengling. [The questioner] asked: "How about this?"
[A monk] asked, "What is it like for one who is within this realm? The Master said, "The remaining snow on the crags reflects its brilliance everywhere.
[A monk] asked, "What is the Master’s secret functioning? The Master said, "Dripping water is not the essential point; across a thousand mountains, he reveals no body.

[A monk] asked, "How is it when [the karmic winds] come from the four quarters and eight directions? The Master said, "A barefoot Persian sniffs at the sky. [A monk] asked, "Regarding the transfer of a deceased monk..."
"Transformation! To what place does it go? The Master said: "The ashes fly and the smoke vanishes; white bones reach to the heavens.
While the Master was applying moxibustion to a sick monk, the monk asked: "At this very moment, how is it? The Master said: "The single pulse of universal penetration is much like a shooting star.
A monk asked: "What is the mind of the ancient Buddha? The Master said: "A white ox lies exposed on the ground by the green stream."
Question: "How can one cross the river of birth and death? The Master said: "The wind blows the lotus leaves; the duckweed floats. Question:
"What is the single phrase of the separate transmission outside the teachings? The Master said: "A goat-headed carriage enters Chang'an. Question:
"How can one speak of the Way amidst the waves of birth and death? The Master said: "The hand-bag lies across the body, cutting off all green pecks; the clear stream is ever constant."
While reclining in the spring sun, [a monk] asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The mountains are deep and the waters are cold.

[The monk] asked, "What is one who is on the Way? The Master said, "A golden mallet strikes a golden drum. [The monk] asked, "When the sky is overcast and the sun does not emerge, where has its radiance gone?
The Master said, "An iron snake lies across the main road; its entire body is black as smoke. [The monk] asked, "What is the Essence (the *Zong*)? The Master said, [as before].
Regarding one phrase from the *Zhongjing* (Sutra of the Middle): The Master said, "The spark of stone burns the mountain at night; the great earth joins its palms in unison. Question:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "A stone ox blocks the ancient road; a wooden horse gallops across the high tower."
A monk asked Chan Master Huigan of Beichen in Tanzhou, "What is the phrase by which all the sages benefit others?
The Master said, "The red sun faces ten thousand households; its light illuminates, yet it has no mind. [Another] asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? The Master said:
Shihu Liulixin. Dongyuan Tongmiao asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A foot is short;
an inch is long.
Chan Master Shouzhen of Lingzhu in Ezhou was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "The monk’s staff carries [the answer]."
"Snow reaching to the heavens. The vase fills with the springs of the great earth. A questioner asked, "When neither delusion nor enlightenment enters the various objects, what is it like?
The Master said, "From where do the objects come? The questioner said, "In that case, there are no objects at all? The Master said, "A fellow who has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake."
A monk asked Chan Master Shanjin of Shuzhou, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “The character for ‘king’ (王) with no dot. The monk said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “Dot!
[The monk] asked, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, “The mountains are cold and the waters are frigid.
The Master had a staff and composed a verse about it, which says: “A single staff facing the four directions, To test [the student] when the opportunity arises.”
The dragon-elephant’s head and horns are slightly raised and lowered; lightning strikes upon its back.
A monk asked Chan Master Yiqin of Chengtian Temple in Jiazhou, “What is the realm of Chengtian?
The Master said, “Two rivers flank a blind fellow; a range of mountains hides a barefoot barbarian. [The monk] asked, “What is ultimate reality?”
The Master said, "The scholar's kerchief is black.
A monk asked Zen Master Yicheng of Qingfeng in Fengxiang Prefecture, "The non-arising of the three periods of time—of what person is this the realm?"
The Master said, "White clouds join the snowy peaks; the bright moon blends with the fishhook. [The student] asked, "I wonder, is there anything further beyond this?
The Master said, "There is. [The student] asked, "What is this matter that lies beyond? The Master said, "The numinous light pierces through the color of lapis lazuli;
when the great earth is illumined, it is free from even a trace of a spot. [The student] asked, "What is the house style of Qingfeng? The Master said, "Toward..."
Fire eating sweet melon.
A monk asked Zen Master Zhidu of Guangde Mountain in Xiangzhou: "How was it before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "He put on his clothes and ate his meals. The monk asked, "How was it after he saw him? The Master said, "He put on his clothes and ate his meals. [Question: Like what?
"What is Mount Guangde? The Master said, "When facing the sun, flowers bloom easily; when turned away from the shade, snow melts with difficulty.
[The monk] asked, "What is it like for one among the people of the mountain? The Master said, "If the morning mist does not emerge from the gate, the evening mist travels a thousand miles."
Shouze Shi of Shimen in Xiangyang was a native of Taiyuan. He had resided at Shimen for over thirty years, and the monastic communities held him in high esteem.
Once, while a monk was requesting tea, he asked, "What is the one stroke by which the Head Seat benefits beings?
The Master replied, "I still remember it from just now. The monk asked, "And how about right now? The Master said, "Serve some fine tea."
One day, carrying a hoe, he entered the garden. A monk asked, "Among the three bodies [trikāya], which one goes to perform manual labor?
The Master stood with the hoe propped against him. The monk said, "Is it not you yourself who are doing so? The Master took up his hoe and walked away.

Chan Master Qi Chong of Guyin in Xiangzhou, successor to Chan Master Guoyin Yan of the ninth generation under Qingyuan, was asked by a monk: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said:
The people of the north wear fur coats, while those of the south wear them. A student said, "I do not understand this principle; how is it so?
The Master replied, "A deaf person leans his ear, and a mute person sings."
Chan Master Jingxuan of Dayang Mountain in Yingzhou was a successor of Chan Master Liangshan Guan.
He was a native of the Zhang family of Jiangxia. Having relied upon Master Zhitong for his ordination, he became a full monk at the age of nineteen.

Upon hearing the definitive meaning of the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* (the *Yuanjue jing*), no one could surpass him in the lecture halls; he subsequently traveled to various regions. Initially, he arrived at...
Liangshan asked, "What is the formless site of enlightenment? Pointing to Guanyin, he said, "This was painted by the scholar Wu.
As the Master was about to offer a word in response, Liangshan hurriedly asked, "This one has form;
which one is formless? The Master then attained realization and prostrated himself. Liangshan said, "Why do you not utter a single phrase? The Master replied, "To speak—" and thereupon left.
He did not decline, fearing that the paper and brush might be exhausted. The Master laughed and said, "These words shall go upon a stele. The Master offered this verse:

"In my former days as a beginner, I studied the Way in delusion; I sought out knowledge across ten thousand waters and a thousand mountains. Though I tried to discern the ancient through the present, I could never fully comprehend it;
To speak directly of 'no-mind' only made my doubts increase further. Now, having been pointed out by you, Master, the mirror of the Qin dynasty, I see clearly my parents before they were born."
At the time of his birth, he realized as if it were today: "What is there to be gained? At night, the black chicken is released and flies with the snow.

Yangshan said, "The lineage of Dongshan can be relied upon," and for a time his reputation resounded throughout the land. After Yangshan passed away, he took leave of the stupa and went to visit Dayang Jian.
Jian yielded his seat to him, and he presided over the monastery. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Dayang? The Master said, "The cry of a feeble crane and an old monkey."
The valley’s resonance: Sparse pines and cold bamboo lock in the blue mist. [A monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person within this realm?

The Master said, "How? How? [The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s house style? The Master said, "A full flask cannot be poured out; throughout the great earth, there is no one with the means. [One day] he ascended the hall and said:
"Lofty and towering ten thousand fathoms—this path of birds is difficult to traverse. Upon the edge of a sword and thin ice, who is fit to tread?"
Treading upon the wondrous phrases of the primary vehicle, the path of language is difficult to describe. Regarding the gate of non-duality, Vimalakīrti remained silent.
Thus, when Bodhidharma came from the West, he sat facing a wall for nine years until he finally met one who understood his music. Today, Dayang is also most groundless. Take care! Question:
"What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said: "Red dust rises from the bottom of the vast ocean. You must...
On Mount Mi, water flowed across the summit. The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Hongshan. The Master said, "Is the late master still there?
The monk said, "He is. The Master said, "His presence is not denied; however, ask him to come forth so that I may meet him.
The monk said, "Well? The Master said, "This one is merely an attendant. The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Go and drink tea. He then ascended the hall for the discourse.

All you virtuous practitioners of dhyāna: you must clarify the phrase of ordinary non-arising, the phrase of wondrous mystery and lack of partiality, and the phrase of essential clarity and inexhaustibility.
The first phrase penetrates a single path; the second phrase has neither guest nor host; the third phrase carries both together.
To speak the first phrase is for the lion to stretch; to speak the second phrase is for the lion to turn back and leap; to speak the third phrase is for the lion—
Crouching on the ground: "longitudinally" means pervading the ten directions; "seizing" means sitting and cutting off everything at once.
At this very moment, how do you communicate a message? If you cannot communicate a message, tomorrow you shall present it to the King of Chu.
Question: What is the ordinary phrase of non-arising? The Master said: White clouds cover the green mountains; atop the green mountains...

[The student] did not respond. [The student] asked, "What is the phrase of the wondrous origin that is without partiality? The Master said, "In the jeweled palace, there is no one who does not stand in attendance;
if one does not plant the *wútióng* tree, the phoenix will have no reason to come. [The student] asked, "What is the phrase of the manifest essence that is inexhaustible?
The Master said, "When the hand points to the void, heaven and earth turn; returning to the source, the stone horse emerges from the gauze cage. [The student] asked, "What is the lion’s yawn?"
The Master said, "Ultimately there is no intention to look back; how could one willingly fall into the ordinary? [The student] asked, "What is 'the lion’s backward leap'?
The Master said, "Moving forward and returning, all is returned to the Father; though manifold activities arise in great function, the essence remains without deficiency.

[The student] asked, "What is 'the lion crouching on the ground'? The Master said, "Utterly transcending the mechanism of coming and going; throughout past and present, it undergoes no change. [The student] asked, "How about this?"
"This is a person of great realization. The Master said, "It cannot be categorized as being like empty space. [The student] asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body?
The Master said, "A white ox spits out the brilliance of snow; a black horse bears a black rooster. Ascending the hall, he said:

"Letting go of the hand on that other side, beyond the thousand sages, the roots and sprouts grow long in the Patriarch’s Hall and at Shaoshi. A heron leaning against a snowy nest is still tolerable, but look further at the white horse!"

With the feathers of a crane, the beak of a hawk, and the body of an egret, it yet keeps company with crows and ravens. High it enters the misty heavens; low it flies along the willow banks. Returning at evening, look closely: it is vaguely like a wild goose amidst the clouds. Caoshan’s "Three Kinds of Falling" states: "These three phrases must be understood through the transformation of positions before they can be attained. First, 'becoming a water buffalo' is falling into the same category.
The Master said: 'This is the speech of a śramaṇa changing his body; it is a matter within the realm of different categories.
If one does not comprehend this meaning, there will be an obstruction. It simply requires that one’s single thought be free from self-interest; then there is a path for emerging from the body.'"
Second, not receiving food is the "falling into nobility. The Master said: "You must first realize that side, and only then come to this side to practice.
If you do not leave this station empty, you will sit fixed in nobility. Third, not severing sound and form is the "conforming fall. The Master said:
"Because one does not understand sound and form, one falls wherever they are. You must find a way to emerge from within sound and form."
"What is the one phrase beyond sound and form? He replied: "Sound is not sound by itself; form is not form by itself. Therefore it is said:

Centrality and Rectitude: Behold the bright moon, the mirror of the Qin era; it is dimly present like a lamp beneath the sun.

"How can samādhi manifest a name? Yang said, "So it is, so it is. You should believe this:
the original substance is fully manifested; principle and phenomena are non-dual. Protect and maintain this well. Later, a monk asked, "What is the realm of Luofu?
The Master said, "Lofty and towering, it reaches the edge of heaven; majestic and imposing, it anchors the shores of the sea. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said:
White clouds dispersed from the summit; black smoke rose from beneath his feet.
When Master Xigui of Baima in Xiangzhou first questioned Dayang, he said, "I, a student, am ignorant and deluded; I beg you to point out a path of entry for me.
Dayang remained silent for a long time, then called out to the Master. The Master responded, "Yes? Dayang said, "I give you a path of entry. At these words, the Master—
There was a provincial governor who, after staying with the Master, asked: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "A well-trained dog wearing a collar;
when asked, it hides its six limbs like a tortoise. [The Governor] asked: "At such a time, what is it like? The Master said: "An archer and bow inside a cloth bag. [Another] asked:
"If one seeks neither in the Buddha nor in the Dharma, where should one seek? The Master said: "A villager kneeling and prostrating before a stone lion. He then said: "..."
"What is the meaning? The Master said: "A vegetarian feast is being held beneath the village tree. Ascending the hall, he said: "If you run too fast, you will miss it;
if you walk too slowly, you cannot catch up. What can these men of vast capacity do? If there is anyone here with many words and a glib tongue, please come forward!
A monk asked: "I do not ask about the full sentence; what about half a sentence? The Master said: "Cast yourself down! The monk threw himself off. The Master said: "Too late!"
"This is one phrase. The Master said, "One cannot grasp even half a phrase. Question:
"What is the gate of profound stillness? The Master said, "Do not make a fuss, do not make a fuss."

A monk asked Zen Master Hui of Dayang in Yingzhou, “When the Han Emperor won seventy-two battles and became the great hegemon of the world, you, Master, faced the assembly without employing so much as an inch of blade.
By whose grace and power did you achieve this? The Master said, “The brilliant sun faces the eaves; the myriad phenomena are viewed as one.
The monk said, “If that is so, then the golden crow [the sun] gathers its exquisite luster, and the jade hare [the moon] dwells deep within auspicious clouds. The Master said, “A single drop…”
[The Master] poured forth his impartial intent. [His] single thought penetrates all directions. A question was asked:

"What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: "My coarse cloth robe is patched layer upon layer; my daily hoe is polished turn after turn. [The questioner] asked: "When a guest of superior standing arrives, how do you attend to them?
The Master said: "If it is needed, then use it. A question was asked: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said: "The sun."

The sun rises in the east; the moon sets through the western door. He further showed them a verse, saying: "Morning after morning the sun rises in the east; night after night the moon sets through the western door.
Today, the imperial house of the Great Song is entirely composed of those of golden branches and jade trees."
Chan Master Baoyin Lingyun of Yunmen Mountain in Yuezhou ascended the hall and said: "Last night clouds and rain dispersed across the vast sky;

the moon shines amidst the myriad phenomena of the universe. Within this numinous light of the myriad phenomena there is neither inside nor outside—how can one penetrate a single phrase that clarifies this?
Have you not seen when a monk asked Master Dage, 'When the moon rises above the clouds, what is it like? Dage replied, 'Three.'"
Three children embrace a flower drum. Do not come to block my path to the goal. The moon rises at the edge of the clouds;
what worldly matter does this clarify? Three children embrace a flower drum. To conceive a thought is already to be separated from it.
Do not come to block my path to the goal; you must have a way to emerge before you can succeed. If you have no way to emerge, you are like a black ox lying dead in stagnant water.
A single phrase regarding one’s origin—how do you speak of it? No need to stand for long.
Zen Master Yunjing Haipeng of Huai’an Army was asked by a monk, “What is a person of great doubt? The Master said:
In Pipa Rock, they stared at one another and asked, "What is the person who has no doubts? The Master said, "'Thus have I heard.
Sumeru is ground to dust. He was asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
The Master said, "Bodhidharma met Emperor Wu of Liang; Kāśyapa Mātanga encountered Emperor Ming of Han."
Furthermore, a monk asked Chan Master Jianming Jicong of Fuzhou, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "This question is not in vain. The monk asked, "What is the realm of Dongchan? The Master said, "The water of samādhi has never left its old shore."
How could the red dust of the world dare to enter the surging waves?
Chan Master Yiqing of Touzi in Shuzhou was the son of the Li family from Qingshe. At the age of seven, he displayed extraordinary intelligence;

he went to Miaoxiang Monastery to leave the household life and received full ordination after passing the scriptural examinations. He studied the *Śataśāstra* (Treatise on the Hundred Dharmas), but before long, he sighed and said: "The path of three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* is far..."
"What benefit would distress bring? he thought, and so he went to Luoyang to listen to the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*. His understanding was like pearls strung together.

Once, while reading the verses of the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, he reached the passage on "the self-nature of the mind" and had a sudden realization, saying: "The Dharma transcends words; how can it be expounded?

He immediately abandoned his studies and traveled to the assembly of the Master. At that time, Yuǎnjiàn resided at Huìshèng Yán. One night, he dreamed of a blue hawk, which he took as an auspicious omen. When dawn arrived—
The Master arrived. Yuanjian received him with courtesy and directed him to contemplate the kōan concerning the outsider’s question to the Buddha: “Did you ask for words or not ask for words?
After three years had passed, one day Yuanjian asked him, “Do you remember the pivot of this dialogue? Try to bring it forth. As the Master was about to respond, Yuanjian covered his mouth.
At that moment, the Master attained clear and thorough enlightenment. He then prostrated himself. Yuanjian said, “You have wondrously awakened to the profound mechanism.”
"Yes," [the Master] said. "Even if you have it, you must spit it out. At that time, Attendant Ziji was standing nearby and said, "Master Qinghuayan, today it is as if a sick man has broken a sweat.
The Master looked back and said, "Shut your mouth! If you chatter further, I shall immediately vomit.
From then on, another three years passed before Jian emerged from Dongxia to show him the fundamental principles of the school; [Ziji] understood them all with wondrous accord.
He presented him with leather sandals and a straight-cut robe bearing the mark of the Great Sun on the crown, and instructed him, saying: "I entrust you with the legacy of the Great Sun;
continue his lineage and do not linger here for long. You must skillfully uphold this. He then wrote a verse to send him, saying: "Mount Sumeru stands in the great void."

The sun and moon revolve in mutual support; the myriad peaks gradually lean toward one another. White clouds are just beginning to transform; the wind of Shaolin rises amidst the thickets. The bamboo curtain at Caoxi is rolled up;
the golden phoenix roosts in the dragon’s nest. How could the imperial moss be crushed by carriage wheels? Let us rely on the excellence of Yuan Tong.
When the Master arrived there, he did not inquire about anything; he did nothing but indulge in sleep. An attendant reported to Xiu, "There is a monk in the hall who sleeps every day;
we ought to carry out the regulations. Xiu asked, "Who is it? The attendant replied, "The Senior Monk Qing. Xiu said, "Not yet. Wait until I have investigated him.
Xiu then took up his staff and entered the hall. Seeing the Master fast asleep, he struck the meditation bench and scolded him, saying, "This..."
[Zhaozhou] said, "There is no spare rice in the kitchen to give to the Senior Monk (shangzuo) to eat and fall asleep.
Xiu said, "What am I to do, Master? Xiu said, "Why not go practice Chan? The Master said, "Fine food is not for the hungry man to eat.

Xiu said, "But many people will not agree with you, Senior Monk. The Master said, "Even if they agreed, what would that avail? Xiu said, "Have you ever met anyone who has seen [the Buddha-nature], Senior Monk?"
"Who has come? The Master replied, "Fushan. Xiu said, "No wonder you are so stubborn and unruly. He then took [the Master's] hand and laughed together before returning to the abbot’s quarters.
From this point on, his reputation for the Way became widespread. Initially he resided at Baiyun, and subsequently moved to Touzi. Entering the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"If one speaks of this matter, it is like a phoenix soaring into the sky, leaving no trace; it is like a wild goat..."
Hanging from the corner, where can one seek its traces? The golden dragon does not dwell in the cold pool; how could the jade hare take refuge in the shadow of the moon?

Should host and guest stand opposed, one must shake one's head beyond the world of Primordial Sound. When questions and answers are set forth, they are still merely raised as chants along the original path.
If you can do this, you are still halfway there. If you further fix your gaze, there is no need for us to meet.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If the Dharma-gate is raised, both ordinary and sage leave no trace. When the gate of the multi-storied pavilion opens, one meets another at a separate door.
Even if one attains awakening by rolling up the curtain, how can one avoid being a bystander? Encountering peach blossoms in spring only increases the eye-disease.
Therefore, the ancients said: 'The path that goes upward is not transmitted by the thousand sages. You worthy ones, since it is not transmitted, why [is there this] iron..."
The Ox walked through the land of Silla and then shouted: "Those who attain realization must know that there is a startle in the dark.
A monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed? The Master said, "Before the Nameless One (Wei-yin), a single arrow pierced through two layers of mountains.
The monk asked, "What is the matter that is transmitted? The Master said, "It is entirely because of the moon over Huai that it can illuminate Yingyang."
In the spring, [a monk] said, "If that is so, then one enters the water and sees the long man. The Master said, "One knows only that the jade of Jing is extraordinary;
how can one discern the heart of King Chu? The monk bowed, and the Master struck him with his whisk. He then asked again, "Is there anyone else who wishes to ask a question?"
[The Master] said, "As if there were none. [The monk] said, "Both parties have found their advantage. He asked, "Master, just now you took up the incense to offer prayers for the Emperor’s long life.

Tell me, how many years old is he this year? The Master said, "The moon embraces the vermilion cassia far away; the stars bow toward the North Star on high. [The monk] said, "The Southern Mountain rises straight, its longevity equal to Heaven;
the vast waves of the Eastern Sea compare to the source of his merit. The Master said, "Two phoenixes court the golden palace; the green pines..."
The ancient resonance was lofty. [A monk] asked, "The Sage’s longevity has already received the Master’s instruction; as for the matter of governing and transforming heaven and earth, what is it?

The Master said, "It is better to seal your mouth and withdraw; this is how one repays the Imperial Grace. [He ascended the hall and said: "Silence sinks one into the realm of darkness; speech falls into a deep pit.
To attempt to grasp it is like the vast distance between heaven and earth; to abandon it is to be lost for a thousand births and ten thousand kalpas. The great waves are vast and boundless, white..."

Waves surge to the heavens. The Bright Pearl that Subdues the Sea—by whom shall it be gathered and held? After a long silence, he planted his staff and said: "A hundred fragments! Ascending the hall, [the Master said:
"In a solitary village or a humble inn, do not hang up your flask and bowl. The profound gateway of the Patriarchs and Buddhas must be traversed directly with the body cast across.

Already this is like Su Qin striking a barrier; seeking a path, it is difficult to turn back. When Xiang Yu faced the river, how could he escape his destined fate? O virtuous practitioners of Zen!..."

"Arriving here, to advance is to fall into the realm of celestial demons; to retreat is to sink into the destiny of ghosts. To neither advance nor retreat is to stand right in the midst of the waters of death.
How, O worthy ones, can you attain stability? After a long silence, he said: "Let the three-foot snow fall as it will;
it cannot suppress the single inch of the numinous pine. The Master composed the *Five Ranks* (*Wuwei*) with a preface: "Now, the vast sky is of one color..."

How can the stars and moon be distinguished? The great earth is without partiality; yet withering and flourishing differ of their own accord. Thus, the Dharma is not a dharma distinct from itself—how could delusion and enlightenment ever reach it?

The mind is not of itself the mind; it is provisionally proclaimed by means of words and images. These words are comprehensive, perfect, direct, and ultimate; they are inclusive and harmoniously penetrating.
This Dharma does not fall into the trap of right or wrong, nor is it concerned with the myriad phenomena. Once the profound intent is integrated, [all distinctions vanish].
Regarding the moon in the water: the source of the school’s lineage blends with the golden river; it does not fall, remaining in empty stillness. The path returns to the subtle wonder.
The verse says: In the center, there is deviation: the stars and Milky Way turn across before the bright moon. Colored vapors intermingle at night while heaven has not yet dawned;

within the hidden, all is revealed; in the dark, all is complete. In deviation, there is the center: at midnight, when the day breaks, one is ashamed of one's own reflection. Amidst the hazy mist, what can be discerned?
Divided, yet indistinctly merged, it does not fall into the mirror of the Qin era. Coming from the very center: a fire-cock sits upon the phoenix terrace.
The primordial path leans against the void, connecting the channels above; through the clouds on the bird-path, one emerges from the dust.

Reaching through the simultaneous: snow-reeds enshroud the body, leaving no room for evasion. A natural warrior, neither side is harmed; in secret, all is perfectly prepared. Arriving through the simultaneous: [he] understands.
The person who runs does not touch the Way; in general, picking it up and presenting it to you is quite different. Only when one does not fall into right or wrong is it truly wondrous.

At the end of the fourth month in the year of Guihai during the Yuanfeng era of Emperor Shenzong of the Song dynasty, the Master manifested slight illness. He sent a letter to take leave of the local officials and patrons.
On the fourth day of the fifth month, after ascending the seat to bid farewell to the assembly, he spoke this verse: "Holding the position in two places, there is nothing [to be done]..."
"May this assist the Way. Take care. With these words, he ceased his writing and passed away. He was cremated, and five-colored śarīra were obtained, identical to sacred relics.
They were enshrined in a stupa behind the Sanfeng Hermitage to the north of the temple.
Chan Master Shanji of Liangshan in Dingzhou, successor to Chan Master Liangshan Yan:
A monk asked, "What is it like when one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha? The Master said, "Do not let your eyes grow dim.
A monk asked, "When will you, Honored One, attain Buddhahood? The Master said, "Do not force the noble to become base. The monk said, "Why? [The Master replied: "Because..."
"What is it that you refuse to accept? The Master said, "Better nothing at all than a good thing. The Master offered this verse on Lu Zu’s wall-facing:
"Lu Zu’s samādhi is most effortless: As soon as he sees a monk approach, he faces the wall.
If one is a person who knows the heart and understands the Way, It is not necessary to raise an eyebrow for them to understand completely."
Chan Master Chiyu of Tianping Mountain in Xiangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Daowu Xuan. A monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he inherit? The Master said:
"The drumstick strikes both ends of the drum. He was further asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: [The same].
The Turnip of Zhenzhou and Tea Contained in a Stone. A scholar asked, "When the Dharma is motionless, what is it like when it moves?
The Master said, "You have come from Lufu. The scholar said, "I have not taken a single step. The Master said, "How did you manage to get here?"
The official said, "Master, why do you speak in your sleep? The Master said, "I grant you twenty blows.
An official asked, "When there is no neighbor to separate us, why do we not see one another? The Master said, "Whom should I blame? While the Master was walking along the corridor...
Seeing a monk, he pointed at him with his staff. The monk stepped forward to take it, whereupon the Master struck him.
[He was] a successor of Chan Master Qing of Touzi, the eleventh generation under Qingyuan.
Chan Master Daokai Fuyong of Tiantong Monastery in Tokyo was born into the Cui family of Yizhou. From childhood, he studied the practice of fasting (*pi-gu*).

He lived in seclusion at Mount Iyang before traveling to the capital, where he registered his name at Shuitai Temple. There, he underwent the *Lotus Sūtra* examination and received ordination. He then visited Touzi at Haihui Monastery and asked:
"The words and phrases of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are like the common tea and rice of daily life; apart from these, what else is there?"
“Is there a place for people? he asked. The Master said, “You speak of the Emperor’s decree within the realm; does it still require Yao, Shun, Yu, or Tang?
As the teacher was about to offer a word in reply, the Master struck his mouth with his whisk and said, “From the moment you first conceived this thought, you already deserved thirty blows.
The teacher attained immediate enlightenment. He bowed twice and was about to depart. The Master called out, “Wait a moment, Kalyāṇamitra! The teacher turned back.
[The Master] did not look back. The Master said, "Have you reached the stage of non-doubt? The Teacher immediately covered his ears with his hands.

Later, while serving as the head cook (dianzuo), the Master said, "Managing the kitchen duties is no easy task. The Teacher replied, "I dare not [complain]. The Master asked, "Do you cook the porridge? Do you steam the rice?
The Teacher replied, "The laborers wash the rice and light the fires; the practitioners cook the porridge and steam the rice. The Master said, "Then what do you do?"
"What is it? the Master asked. The Teacher said, "Out of compassion, Preceptor, let him go in peace. One day, while attending on Touzi, they were walking through the vegetable garden.
Touzi passed his staff to the Master; the Master took it and walked along with him. Touzi said, "It is only right that you should act this way.
The Master said, "Carrying the Preceptor’s shoes and holding his staff would not be considered an overstep either. Touzi said, "There is someone else accompanying us. The Master—
[The Master] said, "That one person did not accept the teaching; you may leave. When evening came, [the monk] asked the Master, "The talk from this morning was not yet finished.
The Master said, "Please, Venerable Sir, bring it up. The monk said, "Born in the hour of the Rabbit (Mao), born in the month of the Dog (Wu).

The Master immediately lit a lamp and approached. The monk said, "Your coming up and going down has not been in vain at all. The Master said, "Being by the side of the Venerable Sir, it is only right that it be so."
The Master said, "Every household has its slaves and servants. The Teacher said, "The Master is advanced in years;
we cannot do without him. The Master said, "How diligent you are! The Teacher said, "I have my share of gratitude to repay. After he took up residence there, a monk asked:
"A tune without a melody, not falling within the five musical notes; its resonance issues forth from the azure heavens—please, Master, blow and sing it.

The Master said, "The wooden cock crows at midnight; the iron phoenix calls as the day breaks. The monk said, "If that is so, then a single line of this song contains the resonance of a thousand ages;
all those like clouds and water in the hall are connoisseurs of this sound. The Master said, "A tongueless child is able to join in the chorus. The monk said, "A master of the school!"
The Eye and Mirror of Humanity and Heaven. The Master said: "Forbid the grasping for two pieces of skin. Question: "At midnight it is perfectly bright;

at dawn, nothing is revealed. What is this matter that is not revealed? The Master said: "The boat is full, yet empty; the fisherman sleeps amidst the reeds. Question: "What is the家风 (household style) of Cao Dong?
The Master said: "The corded seat is rotted by wind and rain; weeds grow within the abbot’s quarters."
Qin asked, "What is the direct source? The Master said, "Grass has already grown beneath your feet; every step you take falls upon a perilous slope. He ascended the hall and said:
"By day, one enters the garden of Jeta, where the bright moon hangs in the sky. By night, one climbs Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, where the sun overflows the eyes.
Crows and ravens are like snow; solitary geese form flocks. Iron dogs bark as they soar toward the heavens; mud..."
The oxen fight and enter the sea. At such a moment as this, the ten directions gather together; how can "self" and "other" be distinguished?
Within the arena of the ancient Buddhas and under the gate of the Patriarchs, everyone extends a hand to receive the visiting masters who come and go.
O virtuous ones, tell me: what matter is accomplished by this? After a long silence, he said: "Planting in abundance a tree without shadow, to leave behind for those who come after."
The Master ascends the hall. As soon as he has mounted this seat, he has already entered the realm of worldly toil. To fix one’s gaze upon it further would only reveal one’s own flaws.
That single phrase of the separate transmission robs the thief of his home; yet to claim not to lose the fundamental source is for the fox to remain attached to its den.

Therefore, True Suchness, ordinary beings, and sages are all but words of a dream; Buddhas and sentient beings are both merely figurative designations. Reaching this point, turn the light back within.
Reflecting back. Taking it up with a letting-go of the hand. One cannot avoid the cicada clinging to a withered tree; weeping until tears are spent, they do not turn their heads back.
Entering the hall, he said: To call it "one phrase" is already to bury the ancestral wind. To accommodate the present age is to let the common path waste away.

Therefore, to clarify the position by means of function, one employs function within the essence; to clarify function by means of position, one brings essence into the sphere of function. If even this essence...
Use the "Double Illumination. It is like a door with two panels; one must not fixate upon either panel. Have you not heard the Old Man of Xinfeng say:
"The peaks and ridges are exquisite and unique, yet the cranes do not pause in their flight. The numinous trees stand tall and remote, yet the phoenixes have no place to perch.

Only when one has achieved the task but does not dwell therein can the lightning-flash of the moment be difficult to pursue. Any question involving deliberation is already ten thousand miles from the truth. [Ascending the hall: ... [The assembly] ... Ascending the hall.
I shall not ask about what happens before the thirtieth day of the twelfth month. But as for the matter of that very thirtieth day—how will it be?
O virtuous ones, when you arrive at this point, even the Buddhas cannot help you;
the Dharma cannot help you; the Patriarchs cannot help you; the old monks of the world cannot help you; and even I, this mountain monk, cannot help you.
"You have attained it. Even Old Man Yama cannot help you; you must simply exhaust this present moment.
If you can exhaust this present moment, then even the Buddha cannot do anything about it; the Dharma cannot do anything about it; the Patriarchs cannot do anything about it;
the old monks of the world cannot do anything about it; and even I, this mountain monk, cannot do anything about it. Yama..."
"Old Master Luo—there is nothing that can be done about him. Everyone, tell me: what is the principle for exhausting the present moment?
Do you understand? 'Next year there will be new branches again; the spring wind’s vexation shall never cease. A monk asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "The hornless mud ox gallops through the night gate. He ascended the hall. The bells and drums resounded.

The announcement has not yet been heard; a single sound startles those within their dreams. Perfect, constant, and quiescent, there is no other matter—whom can one call a separate gate of Avalokiteśvara?
After a long silence, he said: "Do you understand? Cease asking the guest atop Mount Potalaka;
the warbling of the oriole cuts through the clouds of the sea-mountain. Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "If you can realize it here, all are the Buddhas."

This establishes the limit of phenomena. Even if you can cause the east to surge and the west to subside, and exercise mastery over rolling up and unfolding [the teachings], you have not yet seen a trace of the news from before the Seven Buddhas.
You must know that there is one person who does not receive it from others, who does not undergo instruction, and who does not fall into stages or ranks.
If you recognize this person, the business of a lifetime of study is finished. He then suddenly called out to the assembly, saying: "If you look on with a fixed gaze even longer..."
Without the need for formal greetings, he ascended the hall. After a long silence, he said: "The green mountains constantly move their steps;

the stone woman gives birth to a child at night. He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall again, he said: "To speak of the Way through provisional words brings it down to the present moment.
Even if a tongueless person could speak and a legless person could walk, they still would not yet be in accord with that One Person. Do you understand? The Dragon..."
The practitioners of poetry leaned their ears toward him; as the tiger roared, they pondered in vain. A student asked, "What is the 'comprehensive' statement?

The Master said, "The wondrous function is fully deployed, encompassing the entire world; the wooden man takes a leisurely stroll, emerging from amidst the flames. The student asked, "What is the style of your house, Master?
