Everywhere, by the side of the brazier, three or five of them gather their heads together, opening their mouths to chatter incessantly, saying, "This is it..."
This is a statement of public talent. This is a statement that strikes out from within the situation. This is a statement that speaks of phenomena.
This is a statement of essence. You, the masters and mistresses of your own house, having finished eating your rice, do nothing but talk in your sleep.
They immediately say, "I have realized the Buddha-dharma. You should know that traveling on pilgrimage like this—when will you ever find rest?

Furthermore, there is another type who, as soon as they hear mention of a place of rest, immediately closes their eyes within the realm of the five aggregates (skandhas), making their living inside a rat's hole.
Sitting beneath the Black Mountain, they experience it within the realm of ghosts, saying, "I..."
"You have found a way of entry. Have you seen it in a dream? If one were to kill ten thousand people like this, what sin would there be?
This is called 'beating [the drum]. If you do not meet a true master, you will ultimately remain nothing but a hollow charlatan.
If you truly have a place of realization, bring it forth and let us deliberate together; do not let your time pass in vain. You do not recognize good from evil; you are merely babbling."
Chattering away, you huddle together to spin webs of sophistry. Do not let this old monk catch you; if your answers do not match the test, I shall break your waist with my staff.
Do not say I did not warn you: is there any blood beneath your skin? Why do you go everywhere seeking only to suffer humiliation?
These are all nothing but packs of wild foxes—what are you all doing here? With his staff, he drove them all away at once.

The three virtues and six flavors are offered to the Buddha and the Sangha. Ascending the hall: The eyelashes span horizontally across the ten directions;
the eyebrows extend upward through heaven and earth and downward through the Yellow Springs. Mount Sumeru blocks your throat. Is there anyone who understands?
"If you can understand this, you will drag Campāpura under your control and fight neck-to-neck with Silla. Ascending the hall, he said:
"In Jiangxi, they speak of ruler and subject, father and son; in Hunan, they speak of 'he' not being like that. Here, in my place, it is not like this at all."
After a long silence, he said, "Do you still see the wall? Ascending the hall, he said, "Go! Go! You are merely obstructing one another.
When will there ever be an end to this? He then asked the assembly, "In saying this, am I at fault? A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The first thing is not to ask. The monk said, "Yes. The Master scolded him, saying, "You do not even grasp the words!"
Question: "Today we made offerings to the Arhats; will the Arhats return? The Master said: "If you had not asked, I would not have spoken. The questioner said:
"I request the Master to speak. The Master said: "Joining palms at the three gates; burning incense within the Buddha Hall. Question:
"What is the fundamental matter of a patch-robed monk? The Master said: "To the south there is Xuefeng; to the north there is Zhaozhou. The questioner said: [No further response.]
“Please, Preceptor, do not use flowery words. The Master said, “Do not lose the point of the question. The monk said, “Yes. The Master struck him. The monk asked, “I have heard it said of old:
‘If you understand, then things are like one family; if you do not understand, then teeth are parted from tusks.

How does one attain this state where things are like one family? The Master said, “Why are you running about in confusion? He ascended the hall and said, “From the beginning, this has simply been a...”
What is it? Now, having no choice but to do so, I shall speak to you all: Throughout the entire earth, what thing exists that could serve as an object of opposition or a condition for you?
If there were even a needle-point that could act as a separation or an obstruction for you, bring it here to me!
Then tell me, what would you call a Buddha or a Patriarch? What would you call the mountains, rivers, the great earth, the sun, and the moon?
"Stars! Taking what as the four great elements and five aggregates? To speak of me in such a way is called the talk of an old woman from a common village.

If one were suddenly to encounter a genuine traveling monk who, upon hearing such words, were to grab him by the leg and drag him down the steps—what fault would there be in that? Nevertheless, on what principle does one act in this manner?"
Do not speak such nonsense here just to satisfy your own tongue; one must be a true man before this will do.
If you are suddenly found out by this old fellow at his very heels, and he breaks your legs where there is no place to go, what crime would that be? Since it is so.
"Now, is there anyone who still wishes to ask a question regarding the essence of the School? Once this old man has answered one turn, you may go east or west as you please.
Just as a monk was about to ask, the Master struck him in the mouth with his staff and descended from his seat.
A monk asked, "What is it like when a lion yawns? The Master said, "Setting aside the yawning for a moment, try to roar! The monk responded, "Yes? The Master said, "..."
"This is the cry of a rat. [He] ascended the hall. "I have a phrase; I do not dare hope that you will understand it. Is there anyone who can bring it forth?
After a long silence, he said, "I thought it was a red-bearded barbarian, but there is also one with a white-bearded barbarian.
He then descended from his seat. [He] ascended the hall. "Out of necessity, I shall treat this like a dead horse. What is this thing I am pointing out to you?"
"East is west; this is south, this is north; this is existence, this is non-existence; this is seeing, this is hearing;
this is upward, this is downward; this is 'so,' this is 'not so. This is called the talk of an old woman in a village of three households."
"How many of you are there? [The Master asked. "If you are equal to this state, then you are equal; if not, then you are not. "Svāhā in stillness!
With these words, he descended from his seat. [Later,] while ascending the hall, he said: "The old masters of all quarters say that one must know there is a matter beyond sound and form.
Such talk as this deceives the men and women of the world. Within these three bays of the Dharma Hall, I am alone."
This is merely your own deluded imagination. You have never even dreamed that the essential tenets of my original Master remain here. How can you possibly digest the offerings of the faithful?

On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, each and every one of you must settle this debt before it is possible. No matter how much you may leap about, it is up to you all to exert yourselves individually.
Take care! Question: "If not a single dharma exists before one's eyes, can one still escape birth and death?"

"No. The Master said, "You will not escape this until the year of the donkey. A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Go. The monk said, "I do not understand; I beg the Master to speak of it.
The Master said, "Your credentials, Layman, are clear; why seek a further judgment? [The monk] asked about Vimalakīrti’s silence:
"Is that the same as speaking or not? The Master said, "Receive this one question with full attention. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then..."
The same was said. The Master asked, "What did you just say? A monk asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said, "A flower-and-medicine railing.
[The monk] asked, "How is it when one understands it in this way? The Master said, "A golden-maned lion.
While ascending the hall, he heard the bell toll and said, "The world is so vast; why does the sound of the bell penetrate everywhere?"
Tiao ascended the hall and said: "One must not add frost to snow. Take care. He then descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Those old bald slaves from all quarters sit upon their crooked wooden meditation seats, seeking fame and profit; when asked about the Buddha, they answer as if they were the Buddha themselves."
Questioning the Patriarch and answering the Patriarch is like passing the mouthful of food from one person to another among the wives in a village of three households;
what good or evil could they possibly recognize? If everyone were like this, even water would be difficult to digest. Ascending the hall, he said: "Everyone possesses their own luminosity;
yet when looked for, it is not seen, shrouded in darkness. He then descended from the seat. The Master entered the capital and stayed at...
At the Shouchun Hall, the Emperor asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "The Emperor has issued an imperial decree; this monk-monk responds.
While the Master was at Wende Hall for a vegetarian feast, Attendant Ju asked, "Has the fruit on Lingshu matured yet?
The Master said, "In what year did you begin to believe that it grows? Ascending the hall, he said, "All of you, you have come here for no reason..."
"What are you looking for inside? This old monk only knows how to eat rice and defecate; what else does he know how to do?
You all travel on foot to various quarters to study Chan and inquire about the Way. Let me ask you: what is it that you have realized by studying in those various places?
Try to bring it forth and show me. He continued, "In the meantime, can you find your father inside your own house? Look behind this old man’s backside!"
Having found a mere drop of saliva, you chew it up and take it for yourself, saying, "I understand Chan; I understand the Way.
Even if you could recite the entire Great Canon, what would you do with it? The ancients, driven by necessity, saw that you were wandering aimlessly and said to you:
"Bodhi and Nirvana are but things that bury you; they are stakes to pin you down. Furthermore, they saw...
"You will not. I tell you: it is neither Bodhi nor Nirvana. To know such matters as these is already to miss the point.
Yet you still seek commentaries on such things. From the very beginning, everyone has been like this; how could it have reached this day?
When I was traveling as a pilgrim in the past, there were certain people who provided me with commentaries; they were not bad."
"My mind has been seen through by you in a single day; it is nothing but a source of laughter.

It is because I have not died for three or five years that I am in such a state—my legs have been broken by a single blow of the axe. Nowadays, there are many throughout the various quarters who exert themselves in worldly affairs;
why do you not go among them? What are you seeking here with this dry dung-stick? The Master then stepped down from his seat and, with his staff—
At that time, [the Master] struck him and sent him away. [The monk] asked, "How can the myriad dharmas be resolved into one? The Master said, "Do not let the question be lost.
[The monk] asked, "What is it like when one finds life within death? The Master said, "Three thousand miles by day; eight hundred miles by night.
[The monk] asked, "The great assembly has gathered like clouds; what should they discuss together? The Master said, "Today, let go; the command has been issued. A monk [asked].
[The student] prostrated. The Master struck him. [The student] asked: "What is the student's own self? The Master said: "I fear you do not know. [The student] asked:
"What is the phrase for penetrating the Dharma-body? The Master said: "The seas are calm and the rivers are clear. A Daoist asked:
"Sight and hearing are without sound and without form; the Old Lord has already explained this. I request the Master’s instruction on Yunmen’s single phrase. The Master said: [He struck him.]

"The road to the Western Heaven is far indeed. The scholar remained silent. As the Master was about to descend from his seat, the scholar said, "I ask the Master once more to proclaim the essential tenets.
The Master said, "Let those who can speak come forward. The assembly had no reply. The Master said, "In that case, you would be failing the host.
He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, when the great assembly had gathered and settled, the Master took up his staff and said, "No..."
Having attained it, first understand it here. Look! The three gates are upon the pillar. Then he descended from his seat and addressed the assembly:
"No matter how you speak horizontally or vertically, you are not yet descendants of the School Gate. As for those who are true descendants of the School Gate..."
"This is the sound of a very hot bowl. "The teachings of the Three Vehicles and Twelve Divisions of the Canon speak of dreams; Bodhidharma came from the West speaking of dreams.
If there were an elder master opening the hall to preach the Dharma for others, what fault would there be in killing hundreds of thousands of millions of people with a sharp sword?
He also said, "I thought there must be some principle for such talk. [He] addressed the assembly, raising his staff.
[The Master] brandished his whisk, snapped his fingers, and raised an eyebrow; each question and answer was not at all in accord with the Supreme Vehicle (shangxiang zongcheng).
A monk then asked, "What is the Supreme Vehicle? The Master said, "From the underworld to Jambudvīpa, everyone can speak of it.
But as for sitting in the morning audience in the bustling marketplace, or the worms in the cesspool by the pork stall—do they still transcend the Buddhas and surpass the patriarchs?"

The Patriarch said, "What about *mā*? A monk said, "Some do not accept it. The Master said, "As for those who do not accept it, it is not that it exists when there is deliberation and does not exist when there is no deliberation.
If one relies on such talk, one understands the matter only through its phenomenal form (*lakṣaṇa*)."
To speak directly, you have not yet arrived; your understanding is biased and stunted. To the assembly:
I usually say that all sounds are the Buddha’s voice, all forms are the Buddha’s form, and the entire earth is the Dharma-body. Yet you have mistakenly formed a view within the Buddha-dharma.
Now, when you see a staff, simply call it a staff; when you see a house, simply call it a house. Addressing the assembly, [the Master] said:
"To act yet there is no acting; to employ yet there is no employing. He then picked up his staff and said: "If it were not 'employing yet there is no employing,' what would you call this staff?
Addressing the assembly again, he cited Danxia: "When the hundred members of the body all fall apart, one thing remains steadfastly present."
[The Master] said, "Changling, the staff must be efficacious. What do you call the 'hundred skeletal parts'? From where have they come?
Addressing the assembly, he raised the passage: "All worthy sages and saints, by means of the unconditioned dharma, possess distinctions. The Master said:
The staff is not the unconditioned dharma; nothing at all is the unconditioned dharma. Addressing the assembly, he cited Master Zhigong:
"At the hour of Chou, when the cock crows, a single round light has shone for long. The Master said: "I do not ask about what is behind your head;
from three thousand miles away, bring me a single phrase! Addressing the assembly, he cited Mazu calling to a monk, and Zhaozhou offering tea.
The meaning of "entering the water": Xuefeng rolling the ball, Guizong dragging the stone, the character "eight" on the head of a sūtra, and the National Teacher’s water bowl.

"The Arhat’s written characters," "The place where all Buddhas emerge," and "On the water above the mountain to the east"—these are all teachings shown to the assembly during the time of the Ultimate Vehicle.
One reaches the point where everything met with the eye is unimpeded, and one realizes that names, bodies, and phrases—all phenomena—are empty.

Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are merely names, yet even these names cannot be apprehended. This is called being fully endowed with the nature-sea of samādhi; yet it is still [merely a description].
When there are no winds, the ripples cease; one simply attains the forgetting of cognition within awakening. Awakening is itself Buddha-nature. Such a person is called "one who has nothing to do.
Yet you must further know that there is still a "further-reaching opening" beyond this. Addressing the assembly: There is nowhere that is not the preaching of the Dharma.
When the bell is struck and the drum is beaten, it cannot but be so. If it were merely like this, then nowhere would be the Dharma.

"It exists. It is not that it is non-existent in all places. [The Master] addresses the assembly: "It cannot be said that it exists when being spoken of, and that it is non-existent when not being spoken of.

If one considers this from the perspective of formal instruction (*ti-chang*), it has not yet reached the mark; however, within the context of guiding others, it is acceptable. [The Master] addresses the assembly:
"He brings together birth-and-death and nirvana into a single mass. Then, picking up his fan, he asks: "What is this? It is not a mere combination.
To achieve it as a single mass—how unsharp and dull this is! Even if you were to do so, it would still be making a living inside a ghost cave.
Addressing the assembly, he raised a case: A monk asked Nanquan, "When Niutou had not yet met the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds carry flowers to offer him?
Nanquan said, "Step by step, he was treading upon the stages of the Buddhas. The monk asked, "After he had seen [the Patriarch], why did they no longer [offer them]?"
[The monk] offered flowers in his mouth. Nanquan said, "Even if he did not come, he would still be one line of difference from Old Master Wang.
The Master said, "Nanquan only knew how to climb higher step by step; he did not know how to let go from the void. The monk asked, "What is climbing higher step by step?
The Master said, "The World of Fragrant Accumulation. The monk asked, "What is letting go from the void? The Master said, "To fill it."

Filling the ditches and blocking the ravines. Addressing the assembly: If you ask about the two characters "Buddha-dharma," they extend east, west, south, and north; they traverse freely in all directions.

He said, "At the hour of the rat tomorrow, I shall depart. When the appointed time arrived, he held a night conversation with seven people, including Yunmen Shuang, Wenmen Shunfeng, and others.
As the attendant announced that it was the third watch, the Master asked for incense to be burned; he joined his palms and passed away.
He had lived sixty-eight years and spent forty-eight summers in the monastic community.
Chan Master Zifu Quan of Shaoyang was asked by a monk: "I do not ask about the Dharma-gate; I request the Master’s mind-seal. The Master said: "I will not answer this question.
The monk asked: "Why do you not answer? The Master said: "It does not accord with what was previously stated. The monk asked:

"At the place where one cannot encounter [the Buddha] face-to-face, how does one look into the mirror and utter 'Heh'? I beg the Master to bestow half a verse, so as to spare future generations from doubt. The Master said: "The Peak."
The previous phrase transcends the "Tamer of Men" (the Buddha). [A monk] asked, "How is it that you have gone against [the truth] for kalpas?

[The Master] said, "If that is so, then people know of the eastern mountains and western ridges; but I wonder, in the courtyard of Zifu, whose wind and moon are they? The Master said, "For now, take my previous words."
On the day Master Huang Yunnyuan first opened the hall at Guangzhou, he struck the rope seat with his hand and said, "Do you all recognize this vast Mount Sumeru seat?
If you do not recognize it, I, the old monk, shall ascend. The Master then sat.
A monk asked, "What is the realm of the Great Han? The Master replied, "Songs and chants fill the roads. He then said, "The ancients..."

The Way. It has never been absent from what meets the eye. Why do you not speak when the opportune moment arrives? This mountain monk is not like that: it has never been absent from what meets the eye;
yet when the opportune moment arrives, what would I say? Take care.
Chan Master Lun of Longjing in Guangzhou ascended the seat for the opening of the hall. Raising his whisk, he said: "Do you understand? If you do, you add a head upon your head;
if you do not, you must sever your head to live. A monk asked: "What is the house style of Longjing?
The Master said: "Jackals, wolves, tigers, and leopards. A monk asked: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "Diligently plow the fields."
[The Master] said, "The student does not understand. The Master said, "The harvest has already been gathered. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Yellow Clouds.
The Master said, "What is the phrase that expresses the state of being languid, charming, and doting, yet supporting others, within those Yellow Clouds? The monk was speechless.
He addressed the assembly, saying, "What is the phrase for taking one's ease upon the long benches? Speak it forth!"
Coming, Chan Master Shuang of Yunmen Mountain in Shaoshan ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Ten thousand years to the Emperor's person.
The monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya? The Master said, "A radish growing on a silver incense stand."
Chan Master Wumen of Baiyun in Shaoyang ascended the hall and remained silent for a long while. A monk came forward and asked, "The single path of Baiyun is entirely due to this very day.
The Master said, "It is not so; it is not so. The monk asked, "How about you, Master?

The Master replied, "On the single path of Baiyun, the grass grows ten feet deep," and he immediately descended from his seat. A monk asked, "If I were to extend a question, would you still answer? The Master said, "Black."
The pods hang from the tree tops; the wind blows, yet no melody is formed. Question: When receiving the offerings of a donor, with what should one repay them?
The Master said: "By becoming an ox or a horse."
The Master of Guang (the Prince) asked Chan Master Jingfa Chang of Shaoyou, "What is Chan? The Master remained silent for a long while.
The Master [of Guang] could not fathom this, and consequently bestowed upon him the title [Chanxiang]. A monk asked, "When the sun and moon shine brightly again, what then?

The Master said, "Though the sun and moon are bright, they do not reflect beneath a covered basin. A monk asked, "Since it is already a 'Golden Mountain,' why dig into the stone? The Master said, "To reveal the gold within the stone."
The Master said, "Jinshan carves stone. A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "A journey of more than one hundred thousand miles.
Chan Master Man of Wenmen Mountain in Shaoyang was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The *svastika* is inscribed upon his breast."
[The monk] asked, "What is the Patriarch? [The Master] said, "He does not travel westward.
Someone pointed to a painting on the wall and asked, "Since it is a thousand-foot pine, why is it still under the eaves? The Master said, "How about 'a mustard seed containing Mount Sumeru'?
[The monk] asked, "When one sees the horn through the wall, one immediately knows it is an ox—what then? The Master struck him. [The monk] asked, "As for suchness..."
"What is the family style of the Master? The Master said, "Have you ever studied the classics? Question:
"When the Prince was first born, why did he not recognize his parents? The Master said, "He was utterly transcendent and noble."
A monk asked Chan Master Yingzhou Dayong Yin, "What is the water of Dayong? The Master said, "Give me back a single drop.
A monk asked, "When Maitreya descends to be born in the future, what will it be like? The Master said, "The three-spring grass within Maitreya’s palace.
A monk asked, "What is true emptiness? The Master said, "Remove the attachment to Yang. [The monk] asked, "What is... [The Master said: "... (The text here is incomplete).
"Wondrous Function. The Master then clenched his fist. The monk said, "The wondrous function of true emptiness—how far apart are they?

The Master brushed it away with his hand. [The monk] asked, "I do not ask about the long snake or the crescent moon; what of the single horse and solitary spear? The Master said, "Do you understand at the base of the Maja Bridge?
[The monk] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "In front of Shengshou Temple. [The monk] asked, "Since it is already 'Great Acceptance' (Dairyo)..."
"Why did you drive out the monk? The Master said, "The great ocean does not tolerate dust; a small stream is full of weeds. A questioner asked, "What is the single path of the ancient Buddhas?
The Master pointed to the ground and said, "I am not asking about this. The Master then said, "Go. The Master was scheduled to travel elsewhere with an elderly practitioner.
Due to certain circumstances, he did not go. The practitioner said, "The Buddha’s word is not twofold. The Master replied, "It is so."
He said: "The Dharma has no single direction.
Chan Master Changshou of Luoshan in Guangzhou was asked by a monk: "What is the territory of the Great Han? The Master said:
"When the jade dog barks, the sky is not yet dawn; where the golden rooster crows, it is the beginning of the fifth watch. [Another monk] asked: "When Danxia visited the laywoman..."
"How is it when the son does not carry the basket? The Master said, "He must also come here for one more turn. Question:
"What is the realm of Luoshan? The Master said, "A thousand fathoms of spreading water."
Chan Master Changbao of Yunmen in Shaoyou ascended the hall and said: "The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it simply dislikes discrimination.
Is there anyone here who discriminates? At that time, a monk asked: "Among the lands of the ten directions, there is only the One Vehicle Dharma. What is this One Vehicle Dharma? The Master said:
"The sun and moon are clearly manifest. The monk said: "I do not understand, Teacher. The Master said: "A clear breeze fills [the world]."
At Linxi in Yingzhou, Chan Master Jingtuo was asked by a monk, "What is the Dharma-body? The Master said, "Guests from the four seas and five lakes.
The monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, "An eye of clarity laughs at you. [End of Question]
“What is the person who has been here from the beginning? The Master said, “The wind blows dust all over one’s face. “Before Niu-t’ou had met the Fourth Patriarch, what was it like?
The Master said, “When wealthy and noble, there are many guests. “How was it after he had met him? The Master said, “In poverty, one cuts off all social visits.
“Who is the Buddha? The Master said, “At the crossroads. “What is the Dharma? The Master said—
[The student] asked: "In a village of three families, are the Buddha and the Dharma one or two? The Master said:
"The pillar crosses the Three Rivers, yet still harbors lingering resentment. [The student] asked: "What is the seamless stupa? The Master said: "The city of Fuzhou. [The student] asked:
"And what about the person within the stupa? The Master said: "Longxing Temple."
A monk asked Chan Master Guangwu of Shaoyou, "What is the one phrase by which you, the Master, benefit people?
The Master said, "Using the wind to blow the fire.
A monk asked Chan Master Hui of Huayan in Guangzhou, "I have heard an ancient saying: 'Where the deluded mind has no place, that is bodhi.'"
"Right at the very moment of delusion, does bodhi exist or not? The Master said, "The sound of your coming has already been reflected. The student said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "When the deluded mind has no place to abide, that is bodhi."
A monk asked Chan Master Zheng of Changle Mountain in Shaozhou, "Who can grasp the patriarchs' mind-seal?
The Master said, "The stone man’s skillful hand remains. The monk asked, "Does the student have a share in this as well? The Master said, "The wooden man adjusts what is uneven."
While Master Guanyin of Yingzhou was digging a well, a monk asked, "How deep is the well? The Master said, "It reaches your nostrils.
A monk asked, "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "Guanyin of Yingzhou. The monk asked, "What was it like after he saw him?
The Master said, "Guanyin of Yingzhou. A monk asked, "What is the wondrous power of wisdom of Avalokiteśvara? The Master said, "Guanyin of Yingzhou."
The Master said, "The wind strikes the broken window and it rings.
A monk asked Zen Master Linquan of Shaoyang, "What is the master of the forest springs? The Master said, "The white stone beneath the cliff."
[The questioner] asked, "What is the house style of the forest springs? The Master said, "Welcoming guests and attending to visitors.

[The questioner] asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Far, far away. [The questioner] asked, "How is it when one understands it in this very way? The Master said, "One who, over a long time, forgets all conditions."
How could one harbor feelings of coming or staying?
Zen Master Xiu of Yunmen in Shaoyou was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Right now, what is the meaning? The monk said, "Exactly so. The Master then gave a shout.
Chan Master Fajie of Huangbo in Ruizhou was asked by a monk, “What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, “To serve as a model for all people under heaven. The monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Thick eyebrows and large eyes.
He ascended the hall and, after a long silence, said, “If you can recognize the Huangbo screen, the business of your lifelong pilgrimage is finished. Take care!”
A monk asked Chan Master Kang Guoyao of Tangzhou, "What were Mañjuśrī and Vimalakīrti discussing when they conversed?
The Master said, "Only when you realize it beyond the skull will you understand. The monk asked, "An ancient said, 'Realize it within the skull. What does that mean?"
The Master said, "Have you realized this yet? The monk replied, "If that is so, then a man from afar has met with the Master.
The Master said, "Do not speak such idle words.
Zen Master Fēng of Gǔshān in Tánzhōu was asked by a monk, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style do you succeed? The Master—
He said: "The plum blossoms bloom on the snowy peaks; the old monk in the cloud-cave is startled. Entering the hall for formal instruction, he said:

"Before the mechanism of the spirited horse, there is something extraordinary; upon the traveler’s arm, something is suspended. Since you have come as a guest from beyond the clouds, try to see this for me, old monk!
At that moment, as a monk was just about to step forward, the Master struck him and said, "Why did you not show your head earlier? He then descended from his seat.
A monk asked Chan Master Kuangguo of Yingzhou Lohan Temple, “What is the ‘hair-blistering sword’?
The Master said, “When you have passed away, if someone suddenly asks where you have gone, how will you respond?
The Master said, “In the future, when you meet a true adept, you shall explain it clearly to them. The monk asked, “Who is a connoisseur? The Master said, “The connoisseur.”
[The Master said: "That is not it; do not ask in such a way. [The monk asked: "How is it when one 'borrows light by boring through a wall'? The Master said, "Wrong. [The monk said:
"But what can be done about his bitter resolve and single-minded devotion? The Master said, "Wrong, wrong."
Chan Master Lin of Cangxi in Dingzhou was asked by a monk: "The Dharma abides in its place; the characteristics of the world are eternally constant. Where has Master Yunmen gone?
The Master said, "Do you see him? The monk said, "A mistake. The Master said, "A mistake, a mistake.
[Another monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, "Not a mistake. The Master composed a verse on account of certain events, which begins: "Heaven and Earth..."
The direct path of the past—no one of these times can forcibly alter it. To produce intellectual understanding within this state is like adding eyebrows upon eyebrows.
Chan Master Qingbing of Dongshan in Ruizhou was a native of the Li clan of Quanzhou. He went to study under Yunmen.
Yunmen asked him, "Where did you come from today? He replied, "Huilin. Yunmen raised his staff and said, "When the Great Master Huilin departed in such a manner, did you see him?"

Mo said, "I have deeply understood this question. The Master looked to his left and right and simply smiled. From that time on, the Master entered the inner chamber and received the seal of realization.
The Ruler of Jinling invited him to reside at Guangmu Monastery; before long, he was commanded to enter the Chengxin Hall to compile the essential sayings of various quarters.
After ten years, he was welcomed to reside at Dongshan. On the day of the opening of the hall, the Rector struck the gavel and declared: "The Dharma assembly is attended by dragons and elephants."
"Assembly, you should contemplate the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*). The Master said, "What a wonderful message! I only fear you will misunderstand it.
At that time, a monk asked, "The 'Single Tune of Yunmen' was personally sung by the Master; what is the matter with Xinfeng today? The Master said, "I must say it anyway."
Chan Master Wutong Ji of Beichen Monastery in Qizhou ascended the hall and, picking up his staff, said:
"The Buddhas of the past, future, and present, as well as the Bodhisattvas as numerous as motes of dust—all appear simultaneously upon the tip of this staff and turn the Great Dharma Wheel."
"They all pass right through the nostrils of everyone here. Do you see them? If you do, bring them to me.
If you do not, you are very much like a man standing there already dead. After a long silence, he said, "The wind is calm and the waves are still; it is better to return to the hall.
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Huangzhou. The Master said, "Where did you spend the summer? The monk replied, "At Zifu. The Master said, "Zifu (Blessing)."

"What supports it? he asked. "Two layers of public cases," the monk replied. The Master said, "But what can you do while it is still in Beichan’s hands? The monk said, "If it is in your hands, then take it back.
The Master struck him immediately. The monk was dissatisfied; the Master followed him out and drove him away. [Another monk] asked, "What is the Buddha?"
The Master said, "Facing each other across a thousand li.
A monk asked Zen Master Yongping of Nantianwang in Luzhou, "What is the meaning of the West?
The Master said, "I do not scatter sand. [The monk] asked, "What is the realm of Nantianwang? The Master said, "View it as you please. [The monk] asked, "How about..."

"This is a person from within this realm. The Master said, "For now, take up the previous dialogue. [The monk] asked, "Having fought long on the battlefields, why is it that you have not achieved fame or merit?
The Master said, "It is simply because [the hardships] of sleeping in frost and lying in snow are too deep. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then let us cease the hostilities."
[The Master] said, "I am returning to court with my hands bound. The Master [Dongyang] said, "Commander, you have not yet arrived.
A monk asked Chan Master Lang of Yong’an in Hunan, "What is the house style of Dongyang? The Master said, "As soon as you enter the gate, you see it.
The monk asked, "How is it that one sees it as soon as one enters? The Master said, "The guest is the host who recognizes the host. The Master asked.
"What is the ultimate discourse? The Master said, "The suffering of separation from those one loves.
A monk asked Zen Master Mingzhao of Xiangtan in Hunan, "What is the realm of Xiangtan? The Master said, "The mountains connect with Mount Deyue;
the waters join the Xiao and Xiang rivers. The monk asked, "Who is the person within this realm? The Master said, "One should simply know the times."
Question: What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "A hundred delusions merely weary the spirit.
A monk asked Zen Master Cheng of Mount Daimian in Qingcheng, West Sichuan: "What is the Wheel-Summit Peak? The Master said:
[The mountain] rises straight up to the edge of the misty peaks. [A monk] asked, "What is the matter that transcends this? The Master said, "Three feet and five inches underground.
[Another monk] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The drum beats *dong-dong* before the Xingyi Gate.
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Three thousand blows in the morning; eight hundred blows in the evening."
A monk asked the Chan Master Pǔtōng of Xingyuan Prefecture, "How does this assembly today compare to that on Vulture Peak?
The Master said, "It shakes heaven and earth. The monk asked, "What is the realm of Pǔtōng? The Master said, "In front of the courtyard, the bamboo is luxuriant through the three winters;
inside the door, there is no lamp, yet it is bright at midnight."
Chan Master Jingyuan Zhen of Dengfeng in Shaoyou ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said, 'Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are all True Suchness.
If you, the assembly, attain True Suchness, then mountains, rivers, and the great earth will be hidden away. If you do not attain it, then you contradict the ultimate words of the ancients.
Is there anyone among you who can express this? Come forward and speak! If you cannot speak it, it is better that each of you simply..."
Return to the hall. Take care. A monk asked, "How was it before Bodhidharma had come? The Master said, "In the villages of three families, two by two and three by three.
The monk asked, "And after he came? The Master said, "A thousand crooked paths are not equal to one straight line.
A monk asked, "I do not ask about the mark of the extinction of all phenomena; what is the mark of the world? The Master said, "The true does not conceal the false."
A question was asked: "What is the one phrase of the Master for the sake of others? The Master said, "Without exerting effort.
Chan Master Dafan Yuan of Shaoyou, upon seeing a sacred image of a Buddha, asked a monk, "How old is this sacred monk?
The monk replied, "He is exactly the same age as the Master. The Master shouted, "This fellow is a thorough scoundrel; it is no easy thing to say such a thing!"

A monk asked Zen Master Yuan Guang of Yaoshan in Lizhou, "The lamps of Yaoshan form a continuous line; to which generation do you belong? The Master said, "Everyone who meets me says they have retired from office;
yet I have never seen a single person beneath the forest trees. Another asked, "Do you still receive those who do not traverse the waters or the land?
The Master said, "Suru suru. The Master asked a newly arrived monk, "Have you come from the south, or have you come from the north?"
The monk said, "From the north. The Master said, "Without falling into words or explanations, speak quickly, speak quickly!

The monk said, "I am a man of the Way from Fujian; I am well-versed in our local dialect. The Master said, "Go join the assembly. The monk said, "It is indeed so. The Master said, "Jump around some more! and struck him.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "What are you saying?"
A monk asked Zen Master Yunzhen of Ehu in Xinzhou, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Are you not a monk asking this question?
The monk asked, “Where have you recently come from? “From the Two Zhe,” he replied. The Master said, “Have you brought the ‘Blow-Off’ sword with you? The monk spread out both hands.
The Master said, “I thought you were a transcendent immortal of Lanke; it turns out you are merely a gambler.”
Question: "What is the house style of鹅湖 (Ehu)? The Master said: "The guest is the host's counterpart. [The questioner] said:
"If that is so, then I shall thank you for your hospitality. The Master said: "It is difficult to lay out Chen Fan’s couch."
A monk asked Chan Master Qingyao of Kaixian on Mount Lu, "What is the meaning of 'the lamp never ceases from one to another'?
The Master said, "The green willows are planted in succession. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Singing a hollow name beneath a rootless tree.
A monk asked about the single phrase of Piyun that the Master had personally sung: "What is the matter for Changqing this morning? The Master said, "Every household contemplates the world."
Yin asked, "What is the realm of 'Piercing the Clouds'? The Master said, "A single flask of green water placed beneath the window;
with this as one's livelihood, one passes through several autumns. He asked, "What is the realm of Changqing? The Master said, "The old monk in the hall has hair as white as snow.

He asked, "Since these two realms both return to the same source, there must be a distinct principle. The Master said, "Wherever one goes, people harbor doubts. [Question on the Ancients] asked: "What is the ancient [principle]? The Master said, "In every place, one meets those who cause doubt."
"Cold spring water in the mountain stream—whom can reach it? The Master said, "Dry. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then you have reached it. The Master asked, "How deep is it?
Chan Master Qinghai of Fengguo in Xiangzhou was asked by a monk: "The verdant bamboo stalks are all True Suchness (Tathatā). How is this so?"
“This is True Suchness (Tathatā). The Master said, “A guest who can turn iron into gold hears the name but does not see the form.
[The monk] said, “If that is so, then I shall take my leave with gratitude. The Master said, “Your former delusions persist even to this day. Question:

I have heard it said of old, ‘When you see the moon, cease looking at the finger; when you return home, stop asking about the path. What is this ‘home’? The Master said, “Try bringing up the *huatou* (critical phrase) and see.”
Question: "If you let it pass, you are speaking of the east as the west; if you do not let it pass, how would you speak? The Master said: "Two years are the same spring.
A monk asked Chan Master Ciguang of Shaoyang: "'This very mind is Buddha'—these are words of guidance and instruction. How about one who does not follow in the footsteps of those predecessors?"
"How do you instruct others? The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment the directions of east and west, what is the matter with north and south?
[The student] said, "In that case, I am unable to fathom it. The Master said, "A dragon’s head and a snake’s tail."
A monk asked Chan Master Huizhen of Shuangfeng in Shaoyang, “What is the one phrase of the Master for the sake of others outside of the formal time?
The Master said, “Have you finished eating the staff yet? The monk bowed; the Master then struck him.
A monk asked Master Mì, the Chan Master of Bǎo'ān in Tánzhōu: "What is it like when a mustard seed rolls onto a needle? The Master said: "Where would it land? The monk asked:
"What is it like when one does not strike against the sharp edge of words? The Master said: "Tiantai and Nanyue. The monk asked:
"What is it like when one goes off in just this way? The Master said: "Jiangxi and Húnán."
A monk asked Chan Master Yunmen Faqiu of Shaoyang, “What is the Great Way that came from the West?

The Master said, “At that time, deluded thoughts have continued unabated until now. The monk asked, “What is the Sword of Yunmen? The Master said, “The vast sky does not encase its sharp, gleaming edge.
The monk asked, “And what of one who employs it? The Master said, “The four seas are purely clear; the sun and moon shine bright.”
Question: "What is the Way? The Master said: "Above the head and below the feet. Question: "What is one who is on the Way?
The Master said: "Go freely east or west. Question: "What is the color-changing mani jewel? The Master said: "Color is not non-existent."
"What is this pearl? [The student] said, "I do not understand; I specifically request your instruction. The Master said, "The clouds have the momentum to leave the mountains;
the water has no sound as it enters the ravine. [Someone] asked, "How was it before Niu-t'ou saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "A fragrant breeze blows away withered flowers. [The questioner] asked, "How was it after he saw him? The Master said, "It rains even more new and beautiful ones."
A monk asked Chan Master Yuan of Mount Fotuo in Shaoyou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Copper heads and iron brows.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Sifting soil and tossing up dust."
A monk asked Chan Master Shen of Ciyun Mountain in Lianzhou, "What is it like when the precious mirror faces the courtyard?

The Master said, "Heaven and earth both lose their color. The monk asked, "What is the one phrase transmitted outside the teachings? The Master said, "Knocking on the teeth for fear of startling them."
A monk asked Chan Master Jian of Huacheng on Mount Lu, "What is the Master’s Eye of the True Dharma? The Master said, "A person from Silla has lost his way.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Bhagavāns of the ten directions [enter] the single path to the gate of Nirvāṇa. All you practitioners of Zen!"
Furthermore, what is this gate of nirvāṇa? Is it that we gather here for a short while and that constitutes the gate of nirvāṇa?
Do not misunderstand! All you practitioners of Zen, do you all understand it in this way? Or is there some other deliberation?
Here, I have already reached a point where I can do nothing else; I speak thus to you all because there is no alternative. It is already so.

This state is already bluntly set aside; what further benefit would there be in attempting to step forward? O practitioners of Zen, simply remain free from affairs; you will naturally find peace and joy.
Let things proceed spontaneously according to their true nature, acting with mastery as conditions arise.

Do not go about visiting the doorways of others to seek understanding or to commit [doctrines] to memory. You will be bound by them and lose your freedom; thus, you will be born [into further delusion].
Bound by death, when will one emerge? How precious it is that time passes in an instant; this very moment is the next life. One must strive with all speed.
At that time, a monk asked, "When birth and death arrive, how can they be avoided? The Master said, "The crackling of firewood and the bursting of bamboo startle the ears.
The monk said, "I do not understand; I pray the Master will point directly. The Master said, "The house dog's barking is fierce at night."
Xiu asked, "What is the path of bodhi? The Master said, "The moon shines upon the deep old room. Xiu asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "I do not wish to describe it to people. Xiu asked, "Why is it so? The Master remained silent.
The Master said, "Family scandals are not to be broadcast abroad. [The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s usual phrase for benefiting others?
The Master said, "Appointing to office according to one's talent. [The monk] said, "In that case, I have no share in this. The Master said, "Let the heart not betray the person.
[The monk] asked, "Ultimately, what kind of matter does the Buddha-dharma accomplish? The Master said, "A fine question. None."
A person replied, “I have attained it. The Master said, “Does the Master not possess skillful means? The person said, “The clouds have the appearance of emerging from the mountains;
the water has no sound of plunging into the ravine. Question: “What is the pivotal bolt of the higher realm? The Master said: “Drawing the sword to stir the Dragon Gate.”
Chan Master Huguo of Mount Lu in Nankang ascended the hall and said, "Is there anyone who can explain the dialogue?

Come forward and ask before the assembly. At that time, a monk came forth and bowed. The Master said, "Tomorrow morning, you shall present it again to the King of Chu," and he immediately returned to his quarters.
