The Master said, “The high question receives the low answer. The monk asked, “What was it like after he saw him? The Master said, “The wind whistles; the rain falls. He ascended the hall.
A monk asked, “Your fame resounds through the universe, and we have known you for a long time. Please allow us to briefly glimpse the family style of the Snowy Ridge. The Master—
The Master said, "That is not it; speak further. The monk spread both hands open. The Master struck him. The monk bowed. The Master held up his staff and asked, "Does the assembly understand?
Words are not repeated, nor are commands enacted twice. He then descended from his seat. He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from?
The monk replied, "From the Eastern Capital. The Master said, "Have you seen the Son of Heaven? The monk replied, "He comes out once every year."
At Jinming Pool, the Master said: "Courtesy may be excused; lack of courtesy is difficult to tolerate. Begone! Zhimen asked:

"I do not ask about the passing of summer and the coming of winter, but what is it like when meeting beneath the grove? The Master said: "Listen for the jade water-clock before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion.
Zhimen said: "What can be done? The Main Peak is high, while the Altar Peak is low. The Master said: "Strike the drum upon the summit of Mount Sumeru!"
Jinzhong Yue was a youth who traveled with Xuedou Xian to the mountains of Huai. Hearing that Master [Huairang] resided at Wuzu, he wished to test him;
however, while Xian was reluctant to go forward, Yue went on ahead. He went directly to the master’s quarters. The Master asked, "What is your name, monk? Yue replied, "Qiyue.
The Master said, "How does it compare to Mount Tai? Yue was speechless. The Master then struck him and drove him away.
The next day he went to visit him again. The Master asked, "What are you doing? Yue turned his head and presented a circular diagram (*maṇḍala*).
The Master said, "While the hearth is still hot, put another one on top. As Yue hesitated, the Master seized his staff and drove him out the door. A few days later...
Yue went to visit him again. He then raised his sitting cloth and said, "When spread out, it encompasses the great trichiliocosm; when not spread out, not even a hair's breadth remains.

"Is it when it is spread out? he asked, "Or is it when it is not spread out? The Master suddenly descended from his rope bed, seized him, and said, "Since you are an old acquaintance, why must you act like this?
Yue was again left speechless. The Master then struck him out. This was when the Master reached the end of his life.
Dayu leaned on his staff, conversed with a smile, and passed away.
At Fuchang Monastery in Jiangling Prefecture, Chan Master Chongshan was asked by a monk, "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master said:
Observing the celestial bodies at night, [a student] said, "The student does not understand. The Master said, "Look at the mountains in the daytime.

[Another] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "In the east, jia-yi is wood. [The student] said, "If that is so, then I would rather have my bones ground to powder.

The Master said, "It is easy to open a mouth for the beginning and the end, but difficult to preserve a heart through the cold of winter. [Another] asked, "Amidst the vast expanse of dust and defilement..."
"How do you distinguish the master? The Master said, "The Son of Heaven in Chang'an; the General beyond the frontier. [The student] asked, "If that is so, then power is held firmly in one's hand.
The Master said, "One does not execute those who are innocent. [The student] asked, "What is the dharma that does not shift? The Master said:
"Dead people do not practice *zazen*. [The student] said, "I, a student, do not understand. The Master said, "The *nāga* is always in meditative concentration (*samādhi*).
[The student] asked, "Setting aside the throat, lips, and mouth, I beg the Master to speak quickly. The Master said, "Fuchang’s mouth is narrow.
[The student] asked, "Why, Master, is your mouth narrow? The Master said, "Give me back my words. [The student] asked, "What is it like to be free from the trap and snare?"
[The monk] said, "The head is large and the hat is small. He asked, "What is the meaning? The Master said, "Staggering sideways while wearing boots backward.
[The monk] asked, "When the golden crow rises in the east and the jade hare sinks in the west, what then? The Master said, "A scholar does not ride a donkey."
[The student] said, "If that is so, then I thank the Master for his guidance. The Master said, "You must still be more careful.

[The student] asked, "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "A prayer-bead rosary. [The student] asked, "What was it like after he saw him? The Master said, "The monk Tieqing.
[The student] asked, "What is it like when one enters the battlefield without first displaying martial skill? The Master said, "I shall strike you, old monk!"

[The Master] beat the drum for the retreat. [A monk] said, "If that is so, then the battle lines are being drawn and the banners are being unfurled. The Master said, "I humbly pray you may enjoy the offering.
He ascended the hall and said, "All the Buddhas of the dust motes throughout the entire universe and the great earth are all here at Fuchang.
[Holding up his staff and drawing a line with it,] he said: 'As for preaching the Buddha and preaching the Dharma—if you understand this, come forth and I will provide you with verification.'"
"If you do not understand, the flowers must bloom through the night; do not wait for the morning breeze to blow. He then descended from his seat.
A monk asked Zen Master Zhìyīn of the Fourth Patriarch’s Monastery in Qí Prefecture, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya?
The Master said, "An ancient pine tree, weathered and gnarled. [Another monk] asked, "When leaves fall and return to the root, what then? The Master said, "Year after year..."
Flourishing and Withering.
A monk asked Chan Master Xinghua Fenneng of Xiangzhou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Long hair; the monk's appearance is ugly."
A monk asked Chan Master Huiman of Tianmu Mountain in Tangzhou, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “An old peach pit. The monk asked, “What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, “Break it open; there is a person inside. Another asked, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, “Every three years there is an intercalary month. The monk asked, “What matters are you discussing? The Master said, “The ninth day [of the ninth month].”
The Double Ninth Festival.
A monk asked Chan Master Jian Fozhi Tong of Ezhou, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body?
The Master said, "A parrot yearns for Western Qin. The monk bowed; the Master said, "Listen to this verse: 'Yunmen penetrates the Dharma-body; the Dharma-body...'"
A man from where? The wild geese return north of the sandy barriers; the parrot yearns for Western Qin.
A monk asked Chan Master Zongben of Xiangzhou Yanqing: "What is it like when the fish has not yet leaped through the Dragon Gate? The Master said:
He waved his hand and entered Chang’an. [A monk] asked, “After leaping over, what then? The Master said, “Though Chang’an is pleasant, it is not equal to Mount Dàlóng in Dǐngzhōu.
A monk asked Zen Master Bǐngxián of Mount Dàlóng in Dǐngzhōu, “Regarding the words of our former master, how does one penetrate the Dharmakāya?
The Master said, “The phrase before the ten-thousand-fathom peak does not level with the white clouds. [Another monk] asked, “What is the movement of the heavens?”
The *Kun* verse: The Master said, "Piercing through the Dragon Palace, he overturns the great ocean; opening his palms, he turns the sun and moon and topples Mount Sumeru.
Question: "What is it to be a renunciant? Master: "Deep. Question: "What is the Dharma of renunciation? Master: "Suffering."
The Venerable Shangzuo Yan asked, "What is the seamless stupa? The Master said, "Bricks, tiles, mud, and clay. He asked, "Who is the person within the stupa?
The Master said, "One who has teeth and wears hair. He asked, "What is the mark of a great man?
The Master said, "Never having fashioned a likeness. He asked, "What is the mark of an old man? The Master said, "Lacking the strength to grasp a staff."
Question: "Regarding Dongshan’s 'three pounds of flax,' what is the underlying meaning? The Master said: "An eighty-year-old grandmother does not bother with makeup.

Chan Master Guizong Guangzuo of Zhi Men in Suizhou, a successor of Chan Master Xianglin Yuan, ascended the hall and said: "When Deshan entered the gate, he was struck with a staff; when Linji entered the gate..."
He gave a shout and said: "Tell me, what does this mountain monk employ here? Is there anyone who understands thoroughly?
It would be better to return to the hall and warm oneself by the fire. Take care! Ascending the hall: For these past two or three days, there has been fine spring rain;
it may truly be called a torrential downpour. To ordinary people, water is water; to devas and humans, water is lapis lazuli; to fish and dragons, water is...
A cave-dwelling. When hungry ghosts see water as fire, you monks—what do you call it? If you call it water, you are the same as ordinary people in their perception.
If you call it lapis lazuli, you are the same as devas in their perception. If you call it a cave-dwelling, you are the same as fish and dragons in their perception.
If you call it fire, you are the same as hungry ghosts in their perception. As for you, in your daily practice, how do you perceive it?
How is it so? Therefore it is said: "If one is a person who has attained [realization], the fire of the Way does not burn the mouth, and the water of the Way does not drown the body.
Do you eat even a single grain of rice less every day when you take your meals? Furthermore, an ancient said:
"All day long one wears clothes and eats food, yet one has never bitten into a single grain of rice, nor has one ever hung on a single thread of silk. Even though this is so—
Furthermore, you must actually arrive here before you may attain it. If you have not yet reached this ground, do not merely engage in empty verbiage. Question:
"When it is said that 'the mark of the cessation of all dharmas cannot be proclaimed in words,' what is it like? The Master said: "A fine question. [The student] said:
"In that case, it pervades the earth and fills the heavens. The Master said: "It is just another heap of dung. Question: "What is the seamless [reality]?"
[The Master] points to a pagoda. The Master says, “Its four corners rest upon the ground. [The student] asks, “What is it like for the person within the pagoda?
The Master says, “The nostrils weigh three *jin*; the scale cannot lift them. A monk asks, “Before King Vairocana (Viyūnapati), who was it that first attained awakening?

The Master says, “Why do you not ask the pillar? The monk says, “If one understands it in this very way, what then? The Master says, “Two heads and three hands. A monk asks about King Vairocana... [text fragment].
"A single sound resonates; when the wondrous form has already manifested, what then? The Master said, "A double case. Question:
"Since it is the Universal Eye, why does one not see the Universal Worthy (Samantabhadra)? The Master said, "Seeking cleverness results in clumsiness. The Master had a whisk made of tortoise hair.
When a student brought it to offer to the Master, how did the Master respond? The Master said, "I have a staff made of rabbit horns to give you."
The *ācārya* said, "If that is so, then one will receive a reward for one's offerings. The Master said, "Thirty years from now, this story will spread far and wide.
He ascended the hall and addressed the assembly: "Venerable elders, the autumn is now cool; this is precisely the time to advance on the Way and engage in decisive discernment.
If you have any lingering doubts, come forward before the assembly, and we shall deliberate together with you. When the principle is long, one follows it. Thus, Zhaozhou’s eight..."
Tenth: I still practice traveling on foot, solely to satisfy the monastic community and, moreover, not to carry a one-sided board.

If there are those who can do so, please present your realization before the assembly. Should anyone attempt to scrutinize or judge from the sidelines, you must conceal your edge within your presentation—suddenly striking with the staff, suddenly shouting.
Sometimes he manifested a circular halo; sometimes the elephant king suddenly turned back to offer itself; sometimes the lion suddenly reversed its steps;

sometimes he let out a great lion’s roar; sometimes he snapped a walking staff; and sometimes he overturned a meditation seat. "I simply ask you to provide such displays—does anyone have anything like this? The assembly remained silent.
It is further said: "If you are a descendant in the lineage of the Gate of the Patriarchs, you must observe the pivotal function (*ji*) of the patriarchs;

only then can you truly be their offspring. You must not merely consume the patriarchs' food and wear the patriarchs' robes while passing your days in negligence, then claim, 'I am a wandering monk (*caryā-bhikṣu*).
Such a person is called nothing more than a bhikṣu in name; they pointlessly exhaust the offerings of the faithful before King Yama."
In time, there will surely come a day when you are called upon to pay the price for your straw sandals. Do not say that you have gained the advantage;
one day, when your eyes fall to the ground, you will enter hell as swiftly as a shot arrow. What, then, is the point of scheming? Let each person simply look after their own interest.
Nor am I a dull-witted fellow. [I have] stood long. [Ascending the hall: If you desire to seek much, I fear it will hinder the Way.
As for you, venerable elders, have you yet accomplished your work on the Way? If you have not yet accomplished it, then all your thousand kinds of clever explanations are of no avail.
It does not benefit his mind; he engages in ten thousand kinds of deliberation as to what the principle might be. Thus the ancients said: "If you have no mind, I shall also rest.
When the weather is fine and dry, one refuses to go; one must wait until the rain drenches the head.
Question: "What is the essence of *prajñā*? The Master said: "A clam contains the bright moon. Question: "What is the function of *prajñā*? The Master said: "A rabbit carries the moon in its breast."
Tai asked: "The three months of spring have already passed, and the nine months of summer are now approaching. I, a student, am not yet clear; I beg the Master to point directly. The Master said:
"I would strike your head until it breaks into seven pieces! The student said: "I know that the Master is earnest with deluded disciples, but what can I do?
I, a student, simply do not understand. The Master said: "It is not the fault of the sun or the moon. A student asked: "Before the world existed, was there still Buddha-dharma?"
[The student] said, "There is none. The Master said, "For one moment less, there is no birth; for one moment more, there is no death.

[The student] asked, "I do not ask about raising the mallet, holding up the whisk, or raising the eyebrows and blinking the eyes. Please, Master, proclaim the path that goes beyond. The Master said, "Why do you carry a cangue and plead your own case?
[The student] said, "If it is so, then I thank the Master for his skillful means. The Master said, "A crime is not punished twice."

Question: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whom does the lineage of this school follow? The Master said: "Layer upon layer of mountain passes and roads. Question: "What is the purpose of this assembly today?
The Master said: "Playing the lute for a cow. Question: "The true source has no trace or sign; how can one speak of its ancestors? The Master said:
"A person is made clear within the words. Question: "If that is so, then clouds rise on the southern mountain while [the sun shines] on the northern mountain..."
It was raining. The Master said, "The willow flowers meet the warm breeze. A monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, "A monkey tying up a dew-pillar.
He ascended the hall and said, "A thousand people pushing at the gate is not as good as one person pulling the bolt. A monk then asked, "What is it like when a thousand people push at the gate?
The Master said, "Waiting by the stump for a rabbit. The monk asked, "What is it like when one person [pulls the bolt]? The Master said, "A single arrow piercing the seven layers of armor."

[The Master] pulled open the gate. The Master said, "You do not have such hands and feet. A monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "The most bitter is *huanglian* (Coptis). He asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "The sweet is *gansao* (licorice). He ascended the hall. As soon as the drum had ceased, [the Master said,] "Rarely does one encounter a true adept.
A monk came forward and prostrated. The Master said, "The drum is beaten for the three armies. The monk said, "A long serpent."

The moon of stillness ceases its manifestation; a lone horse and single spear are in vain for achieving merit. The Master said, "The ice melts and the tiles crumble. [The monk] replied, "Yes. The Master said, "Suru suru.
He asked, "In the Hall of the Empty King, who serves as the attendant? The Master said, "Lohitya Buddha. He ascended the hall.
Nanquan said, "Since my youth, I have raised a water buffalo. When I intend to let it go toward the east of the stream..."

"Let them loose! Even if you let them loose, they will inevitably eat the water and grass belonging to the king. If you intend to let them loose on the west bank of the stream, they will still inevitably eat the water and grass belonging to the king.
It would be better to let them graze a little here and there; then he will not see them at all. Therefore, Master Yunmen said:
"On the level ground, there are countless dead people. To pass through the thorn-brake forest is to be a master.
Even if you were to cut off both the ordinary and the holy, and exhaust all existence and non-existence, it would still only be a rat entering a rice jar.
You do not yet know that there is a 'hole above'. Then a monk asked, "What is this 'hole above'? The Master struck him and said, "I have already been..."
He took a piece of excrement and smeared it across [the monk’s] mouth, saying, "Why do you come here to bite my hand?

The monk hesitated, and the Master immediately drove him away. Ascending the hall, he said: "Divine prescriptions and secret arts are not transmitted from father to son. This mountain monk has a medicinal formula:
black beans are good for making sauce. He then descended from his seat. A monk asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master replied, "It fills the eyes."
[Dongshan] asked: "What is dust? [Qingyuan] asked: "How is it that form is empty? The Master said: "Selling scallions in a garlic garden. [Qingyuan] asked:
"'An emanation is not the true Buddha, nor is it the one who preaches the Dharma. I do not yet know who it is that speaks these words. The Master said: "The mouth and lips of the pillar are missing.
[Qingyuan] asked: "What is the bottomless alms bowl? The Master said: "Hang it on the wall. [Qingyuan] said: "Not yet."
[The monk] asked, "What will you serve for the morning and evening porridge? The Master said, "A clay bowl and bamboo chopsticks. [The monk] asked, "What is the Buddha?

The Master said, "Crying out in innocence while clutching a stolen goods. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Mountain clouds and wild pheasants. [The monk] asked, "What is it like before the lamp was lit?
The Master said, "In the empty kalpa, there were no idle people. [The monk] asked, "What is it like at the very moment the lamp is lit? The Master said, "The light fills the room."

[The monk] asked about "Dīpaṃkara. The Master said, "A spark has entered the Ox and Dipper constellations. [The monk] asked, "What is it like after lighting the lamp? The Master said, "The patch-robed monk runs all over the world.
[The monk] asked, "How is it when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master said, "It is merely a piece of copper. [The monk] asked, "How is it after it has been polished?
The Master said, "Just put it away. [The monk] asked, "I, a student, have a question; I do not know whether you, Master, will [answer it]. The Master said, "... (text fragment).
[The student] replied, “There is none. The Master said, “A crane in the south; a fox in the north. [The student] asked, “What is the meaning? The Master said, “Watch within the three months.
[The student] asked, “When was it that Sudhana entered the pavilion? The Master said, “At the very end, with earnest diligence.
[The student] asked, “Ultimately, how does one bring him down? The Master said, “It would be better to retreat three steps back. [The student] said, “If so, then the ancients...”
"Not before; people nowadays do not wait until later. The Master said, "The King of Qin struck the *qin*. [The student] asked, "I have been pondering this all day long;
it is simply because of the remaining snow in the courtyard. How can this snow be made to melt away? The Master said, "Spring will arrive in due course.

[The student] said, "If that is so, then at the rising of the red sun, everything will be washed away. The Master said, "Adding frost upon the snow. [The student] asked, "What of closing the door to practice within?"
"Regarding 'The carriage and the time'—how is it? The Master said, "Have you attained accomplishment yet? "Regarding 'Leaving the gate and the tracks meeting'—how is it?

The Master said, "Under the workshop of Lu Ban. Question: "I have heard it said in the teachings: 'When one person gives rise to the true and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions is entirely dissolved.
Since this is empty space, how can it be dissolved? The Master said, "One who returns to the source merges [with it]."
[The monk] said, "I understand. [The Master] said, "If that is so, then where a single bubble arises, all waves are the same.

The Master said, "Look closely at the previous story. Master Guanzhou Luohan was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The ox-headed *ābhaṇḍa* (tomb-warden). [The monk] asked, "What is the Dharma?
The Master said, "Swords and blades; trees and mountains. [The monk] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-Dharma? The Master said:
"A red flame within a well; a floating bubble in the sun. [The student] asked, "How should one comprehend this? The Master said, "Pointing far toward the sun beyond the Fusang tree.
[The student] asked, "What is the original mind? The Master said, "You have already missed it."
Chan Master Xianlin Xin of Qingcheng in Guanzhou was asked by a monk: "What is it like when face-to-face presentation occurs? The Master said:
"It strikes right at the nostrils.
[He was] a successor of Chan Master Chushi Dongshan.
Chan Master Liangya of Fuyan in Tanzhou served as the First Seat under Dongshan. Following a small-scale instructional session (*xiao can*), a monk stepped forward and asked, "What is the Buddha?
Dongshan replied, "Three pounds of flax. After the session concluded, Dongshan went to the master’s quarters and said to him, "Was my answer to that monk’s question appropriate?
The master replied, "It happened to coincide with my shaving my head. Dongshan said, "So you knew all along..."
Acting with such deportment, he brushed out his sleeves and departed. The Master said, "This old fellow! I thought I could not penetrate this koan.
Thereupon, he presented a verse, saying: A cow's head painted in five colors, With a forehead marked in gold.
On a clear spring day in the second month, All farmers take it as their model. At Cold Food Festival, celebrating the New Year, Iron coins by the three or five hundred. The mountain sees...
He deeply approved of this. While residing at Fuyan, a monk asked, "What is the master’s house style? The Master said, "As soon as you enter the gate, you see it.
At Kai Fu De in Jingnan Prefecture, Zen Master Xian was asked by a monk, "What is it like when one cannot leave or depart? The Master said:
The Son succeeds to the Father’s legacy. [A monk] asked, "What is the livelihood of a patch-robed monk? The Master said, "Planting fields in one's ears. Ascending the hall, he said:
"There is no need for thought to know, and no need for deliberation to understand. When both knowledge and understanding have vanished, what matter is there to discuss?"
After a long silence, he said: "When a single leaf falls, the whole world turns autumn. A monk asked, "I have heard that you, Master, once raised your hand while gesturing across the river;

what was the meaning of that? The Master said, "Sailing with the sails unfurled within one's own bedding. The monk said, "In that case, clouds rise from the southern mountain and rain falls on the northern mountain.
The Master said, "One cannot step upon it."
A monk asked Chan Master Song of Baoji in Tanzhou, "What is the meaning of 'the Northern Dipper concealing its body'?
The Master said, "An old man of a hundred years enters a lacquer jar."
Chan Master Muzhou Qianming asked Dongshan, "What is it like when the mechanism is halted and the performance ends? Dongshan said, "A puppet show beneath the water.
The Master asked, "Who is the player? Dongshan said, "The one for whom the mechanism has been halted and the performance ended. The Master said, [I understand.]
"If that is so, then those who know the sound do not harmonize," [the Master] said. Mountan said, "What is the matter of one who knows the sound?
The Master said, "A great month has thirty days. Mountan said, "Not yet; speak further. The Master said, "I deserve to receive a severe blow from the Master's staff.
Mountan desisted. [Another asked: "Regarding the record of old at Vulture Peak, whom do you succeed this morning? The Master said, "Chu."
The mountain rises abruptly; the Han River flows to the east. [A monk] said, "If that is so, then you are a successor of Dongshan.
The Master said, "Your perception of the matter is not true; you call a bell a water jar."
A monk asked Chan Master Tong of Guangji Monastery in Dengzhou, “When all conditions have ceased, what is it like?
The Master said, “A three-legged toad flies up into the sky. The monk asked, “What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, “The three peaks of Mount Hua are small.
The monk asked, “What is the meaning of this? The Master said, “The blue river flows with rolling currents.”
A monk asked Chan Master Hongjiao of Dongping Mountain in Shaoyou, “What is the barrier that transcends upward?
The Master held up his whisk. The monk said, “I do not yet understand; I beg the Master to point it out again. The Master said, “This is not your realm.
The monk said, “Does the Master have no expedient means? The Master said, “A second offense will not be tolerated.”
Chan Master Zongsheng of Liaoshan, successor to Chan Master Letan Qian, ascended the hall and said: "The sound of the bell is clear, the sound of the drum is resonant;

heard morning and evening, cease your deluded thoughts. If you recognize this, it is merely labor in vain to seek another path. Do not say that this mountain monk has no skill—*tu!* (a shout of rebuke)."
A monk asked Master Xiang, the Lotus Peak Hermit of Tiantai and Dharma heir of Chan Master Fengxian Shenshi, "What is the bellowing of the snow-clad mud ox? The Master said, "Listen.
The monk asked, "What is the neighing of the Yunmen wooden horse? The Master said, "The sound. On the day he passed away, he took up his staff.
He addressed the assembly, saying, "When the ancients reached this point, why were they unwilling to stay? The assembly had no reply.

The Master then said, "Because on their journey they could not gain strength. He spoke again, asking, "Ultimately, how is it? Holding his staff across his shoulder, he said, "Carrying my knotted staff slung over my shoulder, I look back at no one;
I go straight into a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
A monk asked Chan Master Chongsheng of Jiangzhou, "What is the samādhi for a student’s own use?
The Master said, "Carrying my staff slung across my shoulder. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Treading firmly with every step."
Chan Master Huìyuǎn of Dégshān in Dìngzhōu, successor to Chan Master Yù of Shuāngquán, ascended the hall and addressed the assembly: "The infinite dharma-gates are all already fully complete."
Nevertheless, although this is so, one must first attain thorough and detailed understanding before proceeding. As for the other expedient means, the sages of old appeared in succession, saying:
"After the transmission of the lamp, the worthy ones shall stand shoulder to shoulder. Thus it is said that they succeed the Patriarchs; therefore, mind-to-mind transmission continues.
The seal of the mutual correspondence of dharmas: how is it transmitted? How is it sealed? Raising his whisk, he said:
"This is what humans and devas have realized together. If it is thus, you shall provide mutual testimony. As for those who have not yet understood, please ask your questions.
A monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "The iron gate is a perilous path. (End)

Master Xia ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The ninety-day period of restraining the feet has now concluded; what is the ritual for the *pravāraṇā* ceremony? The Master said, "A monkey chasing a butterfly, pausing every nine steps.

The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master presented a verse: A monkey chasing a butterfly, Pauses once every nine steps. If you wish to know the ultimate meaning, Look at the monkey’s face.
Two children carry a wooden drum; the one on the left beats it while the one on the right dances. In an instant, they manifest hundreds of thousands of forms.
I show this clearly to you—take note! Question: When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? The Master said: "A tortoise drills through a wall. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]:
"Resting upon stone and rinsing one's mouth with flowing water—this is the spontaneous functioning of the true nature. One does not see the ancients..."
This is the Way. Pushing aside mists and sweeping away snow, one blends with the mica-like clouds; digging through rocks and shifting pines, one finds the *fuling* fungus.
At such a time, what more need be said? All you practitioners of Zen, do you wish to understand? Listen to this verse: The long sky clears after the snowfall;
wild geese fly across the vast fields. Patches of cloud, fragment by fragment, drift westward and eastward.
A monk asked Chan Master Bin of Mount Hanzhu in Xiangzhou, "What is the Eye of the True Dharma? The Master said, "Blind.
The monk asked, "What is the pivot of the Master's gate? The Master held up his whisk. The monk then gave a shout; the Master struck him.
Question: "What are the teachings of the Three Vehicles? The Master said: "Shang Daren (The Superior Man). Question: "What is the meaning of this? The Master said:
"Hua Sanqian (Transforming the Three Thousand).
[This is the record of] Chan Master Piyun Ji, successor to [Master Xuefeng].
A monk asked Chan Master Zhao of Kaixian on Mount Lu, "I beg the Master to grant an instruction regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school.

The Master said, "Where the white clouds are severed, one sees the bright moon. The monk said, "That is still a point of doubt for me, a student. The Master said, "When the yellow leaves fall, one hears the sound of pounding clothes.
The monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "A single stream of cold mountain brook; there, one gains strength."
[The Master] said, "How about one who employs [the Way]? The Master said, "A hundredfold shattering. Ascending the hall, he said:

"The regulations of the monastic groves and the family style of the ancient Buddhas consist of one session of inquiry and one request, one bowl of congee and one meal of rice. But tell me, what do you understand by this?
As for all of you, whose minds do not rest and whose thoughts do not abide—if you can rest where there is no resting, and have no thought where there is abiding..."
[The Master] reflected: "This accords with the principle of non-arising. To speak in such a manner would crack open the mouths of others.
A monk asked Master Tianbao of Jinling, "What is it like when white clouds embrace a secluded rock? The Master said, "Not your realm.
A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Divide five into three. The monk said, "I, your student..."
[The monk] did not understand. The Master said, "A nose-ring and a needle-case.

Chan Master Xilang of Taoyuan Mountain in Cizhou, successor to Chan Master Shunfeng Shaor, was asked by a monk: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: [A nose-ring and a needle-case.]

[The Master] said, "If the One Who Came from the West had any intention, he would have cut off this old monk's head. [The monk] asked, "Why is it that he did so? The Master said, "Have you not heard it said:
'For the sake of the Dharma, one may sacrifice one's body'?"
A monk asked Chan Master Zhishan Fayun of Anzhou, "What is the Dharma site of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, "The mountains are green and the waters are blue.
[He was] a successor of Chan Master Banyue Rou.
A monk asked Zen Master Zhanchan of Lantian County, “What is the gate of Great Samādhi? The Master said, “Carrying firewood and picking vegetables; entering the hall.
“A mountain is formed by relying on the first basket of earth; a long journey depends upon the first step.
Elder, you have just now come from the side of the hearth—is this the same as the first step, or is it different? If you say they are the same, then you do not understand ‘non-transmigration.’”
If you say they are distinct, they neither meet nor shift. Elder, how do you understand this? Do you understand yet?
Here is not there, and there is not here. Tell me, are these one place or two places? Are they shifting or non-shifting?
This coming and going is not coming and going. If one attains clarity regarding this, then past and present are as one;

from beginning to end, it is naturally so. Moment by moment there is impermanence; thought after thought, there is eternal cessation. Therefore it is said: "By observing the direction, one knows that person is departing; yet the one who departs does not reach any direction.
Elder, you have just now come in such a manner; please now depart in such a manner. *Chan*.
Master Xichuan Xuefeng Qingshan, successor to Chan Master Miaoshengzhen, ascended the hall and said:
"Yesterday was one; today is two. Do not use thought or deliberation. You must quickly have a sudden flash of realization.
Otherwise, you will miss it for the rest of your life, leaving you with nothing to hold onto. *Duḥ*!"
Chan Master Yunhuo of Xifeng in Jizhou was a dharma heir of Chan Master Qingliang Ming.
He was the son of the Zeng clan of that prefecture. In his youth, he sought instruction from various masters;

in his later years, he visited Chan Master Qingliang and asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? Qingliang replied, "Clouds shroud the trees at the gate of the sea. [The Master] asked, "After he appeared in the world..."
"How is it? Liang asked. "It is to split open the Iron Ring Mountains," the Master replied. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.

Liang certified his realization, and he returned to reside at Baolong Monastery, where disciples gathered like clouds. Emperor Zhenzong of the Song dynasty sent an envoy to summon him, inquiring about the essentials of the school.

He was retained in the Imperial Garden for some time; there he sat in meditation without food. The Emperor marveled at his extraordinary state and bestowed upon him the title Yuanjing (Perfect Purity). When he took his leave to return, he was presented with a great abundance of precious gifts.

Long [received the honors], yet the Master declined them all. He composed poems to honor his conduct and changed his posthumous title to "Xiangfu" (Auspicious Symbol) to commemorate the Master’s dwelling.
Once, when someone asked about the essential principles of the *Yi* (Book of Changes), the Master said: "The spirit arises from the formless and is perfected through the formed.
Only by proceeding from the existent to the non-existent can one then accord with the Way of the wondrous, perfect, and true enlightenment. Thus...
From the forty-nine hexagrams up to the eleven thousand five hundred and twenty, they exhaust the principles of the world and fully realize human nature;
this is no different from the teaching of our Sage. On the day he manifested his entry into nirvana:
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The heavens are not high and the earth is not thick; from this point on, people of this age will not be able to see through it.

Just wait and see on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month: as before, he will face south and gaze at the Northern Dipper. He then passed away peacefully. Upon cremation, śarīras were obtained, and a stupa was erected.
The Complete Works of the Five Lamps, Volume 312;
The Complete Works of the Five Lamps, Volume 33.
Compiled by the Monastic Subject (Chao Yong), Abbot of Shenggan Chan Temple in the Capital.
Verified and presented for imperial inspection by the Abbot (Subject Monk) Chaokei of Kyoto’s Ancient Kegon-ji Temple;
Yunmen School.
Chan Master Dongshan Xiaocong of Ruizhou,
a descendant of the ninth generation under Nanyue and a successor of Chan Master Wenshu Zhen,
was the son of the Du family of Shaoyou. While traveling to study under various masters, he served at Yunju.
Dengtou saw a monk mention that the Great Sage of Sizhou had recently appeared near Yangzhou.
Someone asked, "Since he is the Great Sage of Sizhou, why has he instead appeared in Yangzhou? The Master said, "A gentleman loves wealth."
He took it according to the Way. Later, a monk brought this up to Master Xiang of Lotus Peak. The Master was greatly surprised and said, "A descendant of Yunmen still remains!
At midnight, he gazed toward Yunju and prostrated himself toward him. After taking up residence there, he ascended the hall. A monk asked:
"Before Bodhidharma transmitted the seal of the mind-ground, and before Śākyamuni untied the jewel in his topknot—if at that time one were to ask about the meaning of the West, would it still be so?"
"Is there the meaning of the West coming, or not? The Master said, "In the sixth month, the rain pours down; it broadens the hearts of the myriad people.

The monk said, "If so, then the clouds disperse and every house has the moon; spring comes and flowers bloom everywhere. The Master said, "From the soles of your feet down to the Golden Wheel Ocean, how much distance is there?
The monk was speechless. The Master then said, "The Patriarch came from the West specifically to sing of this matter. From... [text ends]
This Elder did not realize it. Therefore, that which enters through the gate is not the family treasure. To mistake the shadow for the head—is this not a great error?
Since the Patriarch came from the West specifically to sing of this matter, why must he further speak at such length before the assembly?
Take care! Question: "Where does one plant the rootless tree? The Master said: "It abides eternally for a thousand years."
One day, a monk asked, "What is the phrase that transcends sound and form? The Master said, "Jambudvīpa; Uttarakuru.
The monk said, "In that case, this student knows how to acknowledge your kindness without failing. The Master said, "How deep are the four great oceans? A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?

The Master said, "When principle prevails, one follows it. The Master ascended the hall and instructed the mountain monks, saying: "Speak! The monks remained silent. The Master said, "I am teaching you mountain monks to speak!"
What can be attained? The ancient is the present; the present is the ancient. Therefore, the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* says:
"Pines are straight and thorns are crooked; cranes are white and crows are black. Do you understand this yet?

Even so, it is not necessarily the case that pines are invariably straight, thorns are invariably crooked, cranes are invariably white, and crows are invariably black. Dongshan said: "Right here there is also that which is crooked."

Pine trees. There are those with straight bases and thorns; there are those that are black at the bottom like cranes; there are those that are white at the bottom like crows. After standing for a long time, he ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "When a student can neither advance nor retreat, what then? The Master said, "Cradling one's head, one weeps to the blue heavens. The monk was speechless.
The Master said, "Do you know where the alms bowl and the cooking pot have fallen? If you..."
"I know where it lands; it depends on how you ask. Thirty years later, he ascended the hall unexpectedly and asked:
He cited Xianshan, who said: "The bottom is covered in red dust; the peak rises with white waves. The rock-mother gives birth to a rock-child;
tortoise-hair grows inch by inch. If you wish to study Bodhi, simply look at this appearance. After a long silence, he said: "Do you still..."
Do you know where it has fallen? If you do not know where it has fallen, look at Bodhi; it has already entered the Sangha hall.

I have stood long enough. Ascending the Hall: The spring cold is freezing and solid. There was fine snow last night; do you see it? The great earth is covered in vast white snow, yet the spring wind remains as cold as ever.
It is easy to speak of Chan and speak of the Way, but difficult to become a Buddha or a Patriarch. Be careful.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The morning cock announces the dawn; after the gruel, it is already bright. The lanterns are still dozing, yet the pillar is wide awake.
He added: "When it is wide awake, I say directly it is wide awake; when it is clearly distinct, I say directly it is clearly distinct. Tomorrow and the day after."
Do not mistake a servant for a lord. Be careful. Addressing the assembly on account of a matter: When the sky is clear, roof the house; when the weather is dry, reap the grain.
Having paid the king’s taxes early, one beats the belly and sings the *bāgē*. Question: Regarding Deshan’s [practice of] striking immediately upon entering the gate—
This is still merely following a model or copying a pattern. When Linji entered the gate, he immediately shouted; this cannot avoid being like pressing one's eyes until flowers appear.
Apart from these two paths, I do not know how Dongshan would have acted for others. The Master said, "It has been a long time since the sky cleared and it rained; lately, clouds have been rising.
The student asked, "If someone asks about the fundamental principle (zongzhi) of Dongshan on another day, how should the student respond?"
The Master said, "The vegetables in the garden are very withered; I shall carry water to sprinkle upon the *bōlǒng* (spinach).

On the eighth day of the sixth month in the *gengwu* year of the Tiānshèng era of Emperor Rénzōng of the Sòng dynasty, the Master manifested illness. He maintained a fast for seven days. Ascending the hall to bid farewell to the assembly, he recited this verse on the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*):
"Do not be bewildered in your study of Chan and the Way; Penetrate through to the Dharma-body, and the Northern Dipper will be hidden. I am now old and decrepit."
He was extremely frail and emaciated; seeing others, he lacked the strength to deliberate. "Only my spade knows my intent; when planting pine trees, I shall ascend Mount Kongara once more.
Having spoken these words, he passed away peacefully. Seven days later, his body was cremated, and five-colored śarīras were obtained.
He was enshrined in a stūpa on Mount Kongara.
Chan Master Faguang of Gaoyang in Ruzhou, successor to Chan Master Qin of Nantai, was asked by a monk: "What is the great compassion of a thousand hands and eyes? The Master said:
Falling into a pit or tumbling down an embankment.
A monk asked Chan Master Jiecheng of Shishuang in Tanzhou: "The ancients said, 'Rolling up the curtain to face the bright day;
shifting the seat to face the green mountains. What is meant by 'rolling up the curtain to face the bright day'? The Master said, "Bring me the pure pitcher. [The monk] asked, "What about..."
He moved his seat to face the green mountains. The Master said, "Return it to its original place. Ascending the hall, he said: "Outside the mind there are no dharmas;
outside dharmas there is no mind. Flowing freely in accordance with conditions, do not hesitate further. As soon as you all step onto the path leading to the hall—"
"You had better go back. What is the point of waiting for a second ladle of foul water to be splashed upon you?
Chan Master Zhixian of Dingshan, a successor of Chan Master Deshan Xuanjian of Yanshou, was asked by a monk: "What is it like when one sees the mind as soon as one sees form? The Master said:

The horned bow bends like the moon; the precious sword is as sharp as frost. [A monk] asked, "How should one understand this? The Master said, "The golden armor resembles fish scales; the vermilion banners are like flames.
[Another monk] asked, "I have come from afar to seek your guidance; I beg you, Master, to grant me an audience. The Master said, "I will not receive you.
The monk said, "If that is so, then my question was in vain. The Master said, "Rare is the guest who comes with pierced ears; many are those who mark the boat after it has drifted away."
A person asked, "The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas; why was it that he could not attain the Way of Buddhahood?
The Master said, "Gazing greedily at the moon in the sky, he lost the pearl in his palm.
Question: "What is it like when the military deadline is urgent? The Master said, "Dust covers his face at the crossroads. Question: "Why is it so? The Master said, "Because he knows."
[The monk] intentionally committed an offense. [Another monk] asked, "What is the discourse on the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*)?

The Master said, "The stone sheep and stone tigers chatter away. [The monk] asked, "What kind of teaching is this? The Master said, "Long passages cannot exhaust it; short verses are beyond human hearing.
[Another monk] asked, "What is 'one invocation of *Namo Buddha*'? The Master said, "All thereby attain the Way of the Buddha."
Zen Master Heishui Yiqin of Mount Emei, successor to Zen Master Heishui Jing, ascended the hall.
A monk came forward and prostrated. The Master said, "The great earth shatters into a hundred fragments," and immediately descended from his seat.

Chan Master Hetan Huicheng of Hongzhou, successor to the Fifth Patriarch Chan Master Jie, was asked by a monk: "That which sees is form; that which hears is sound. Apart from these two paths, please, Master, speak another word.

The Master said: "An ancient temple with a new plaque. [The monk] asked: "How does this not act as a phenomenon among the myriad dharmas? The Master replied: "It is not a phenomenon among the myriad dharmas."

"Companion," [the Master] said. "Who is this person? The teacher replied, "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. One day, the teacher saw a monk wearing his patched robe (*kaṣāya*) and said, "How excellent these needle and thread!
The monk replied, "I simply want it to be sturdy. The teacher asked, "Why do you 'beat the grass to startle the snake'?
The monk said, "When a guest arrives, one must see to them. The teacher said, "There is only this; is there anything else? The monk replied, "Clouds arise."
On the ridge, the Master said, "Not yet; speak further. [The monk] said, "Water droplets on the rock face. [Someone] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Mañjuśrī is Mañjuśrī himself; liberation is liberation itself."
Chan Master Zibo of Dongshan in Ruizhou was the son of the Wu family of Hefei, Luzhou.

He possessed extraordinary features from birth. At a young age, he left home to become a monk at Puning Temple. He once served as the head administrator of Wuzu Monastery. One day, the abbot required fresh ginger for medicinal purposes;
he insisted that the master must first return the payment before it would be given. Zibo held this precept in high regard. Later, he followed Master Cong at Dongshan, where he encountered Cong...

He passed away. His final instruction was that his teacher should succeed him on the seat. Upon ascending the hall, he said: "Everyone here is like this—how calm and still the wind and waves! Where did you get such a notion?
Suddenly, when encountering vast surging waves and white billows reaching the heavens, at such a time as that, it would be difficult to find even a single helmsman.
Is there anyone among you who can take the helm? No one in the assembly responded. The Master said, "What a pity! This has ruined an entire shipload of people."
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Long waist, short legs. When Yiqian was returning to Guizong, one day he went out with a staff in hand.
Seeing the District Magistrate riding up on horseback shouting his command, the Master stepped aside onto the left side of the road. The Magistrate’s horse knelt and would not move.
The Master said, "This beast, however, recognizes people. The Magistrate, realizing this, prostrated himself before the Master, and the horse then proceeded.
A monk asked Zen Master Siguang of Beizhou North Pagoda, "What is the transformative and adaptable practice of a patch-robed monk?
The Master said, "Surging eastward, submerging westward. The monk asked, "What is it like after this transformation? The Master said, "The soil is rich; the eggplants are tender.
Another monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Writing the right character with the left hand. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master—
It is said: "Crooked head, willow legs.
The Dharma-body verse of Chan Master Duan of Fourth Ancestral Hall in Qizhou says: "A lamp-wick pricks the stone man’s foot;
In haste, go and invite the master physician Zhou. On the road, he meets Master Pang, who asks him: 'In the sixth month, the sun is scorching dry.'"
A monk asked Zen Master Zhinyong of Yungai in Tanzhou, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

The Master said, “The inscriptions on the ancient temple stele are difficult to read. The monk asked, “What is the purport of this? The Master said, “All who try to read them knit their brows. A monk asked, “What is the realm of Yungai?
The Master said, “At the mountain peak, golden screens are drawn; beneath the pines and vines, jade curtains hang. The monk asked, “How about [the meaning of this]?”

This is a person from among the assembly. The Master said: "Few are the gentlemen in purple robes; many are the old monks with snow-white crowns. Ascending the hall, the Master looked at the great assembly, gave a shout, and said:
"O virtuous Chan practitioners, is it not the case that guest and host are clearly distinct? Is it not the case that there is first illumination and then function?
Is it not the case that illumination and function are simultaneous? If you understand it in such a way, the Linji school’s tradition will be leveled."
"Sunk in the sea of suffering. Since you do not understand it in this way, how then do you understand it?
After a long silence, he let out a shout and struck the meditation seat once. Ascending the hall for discourse: "Yesterday was the third, today is the fourth.
Seizing the vital ford, releasing and gathering—limitless seekers of Chan are utterly at a loss. He let out a shout.
A monk asked Chan Master Tong of Haihui in Shu Province, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, “A persimmon bucket and a straw hat. The monk said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “When walking, it is carried on the head; when sitting, it hangs on a high wall.”
A monk asked Chan Master Miaoyuan of Dongshan in Ruizhou, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “The head and brain are the same.
A monk asked Chan Master Zixiang of Yitai in Qizhou, “What is the realm of Yitai? The Master said, “On the roads, nothing is left behind.
The monk asked, “What is one within the realm? The Master said, “The dog of Jie barks at Yao.”
A monk asked Chan Master Huaiqing of Tiantong in Mingzhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Dust does not settle in the eyes. The monk asked, "How should one comprehend this? The Master said, "Water does not remain in the ears.
The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall prostrate myself. The Master said, "The eastern house lights the lamp; the western house sits in darkness."
A monk asked Chan Master Shuzhi of Baoyan in Yuezhou, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “An earthen body and wooden bones.
The monk asked, “What is the underlying meaning? The Master said, “Five-colored gold ornamentation. The monk said, “If that is so, I shall prostrate myself.
The Master said, “The *zhilu* staff of Tiantai.”
A monk asked Zen Master Xiu of Wuzushan in Qizhou: “It is said that ‘there being no dharma to be spoken, this is called preaching the Dharma.

Since there is no dharma to be spoken, with what then do you preach? The Master said: “The frost is cold and the ground is frozen. The monk said: “Śūnyatā-born (Gavāmpati) could not understand while sitting in the mountain cave;
he caused the heavenly flowers to stir and come rushing from the earth. The Master said: “The sun rises and the ice melts. The monk hesitated, and the Master said: “Ha!”
"Why do you not offer a word? The monk remained silent. The Master said, "A cart should not be pushed sideways; principles must not be judged with partiality.
Master Bian of Baima in Xiangzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "When water comes, the river swells. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma?
The Master said, "When the wind comes, the trees move."
Chan Master Zhishu of Shuinan in Suizhou ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to know the path of liberation, the cock has crowed and the sky is already bright.
The cypress tree in front of Zhaozhou’s courtyard knocks down the dates from Qingzhou. Tsk!"
Chan Master Qiyue of Shangfang in Anjing Prefecture, successor to Chan Master Fuchang Shan, was asked by a monk: "What is bodhi? The Master said: "Brick heads and roof tiles. The monk asked:
"What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "Bitterness. He ascended the hall and said: "Gathering up yellow leaves, I burn them into blue smoke."
"Sleeping in one's robes on a bamboo cot at midnight; after the morning gruel, the evening session is dismissed with three strikes of the board. Who can further speak of the Zen of the Patriarchs?
He then descended from his seat.
A monk asked Chan Master Changtan of Yuwang in Mingzhou, "What is existence within existence? The Master said, "The Golden River."
At the Peak. [A monk] asked, "What is 'nothing within nothing'? The Master said, "Before the Hall of Prajñā. Ascending the hall, he said: "A thousand flowers compete in bloom;
a hundred birds sing in spring—this is the phrase that points upward. The Buddhas appear in the world; the spiritual friends give rise to compassion—this is the phrase that points downward.
What is the phrase that does not involve either of these two paths? If you can recognize it, you will breathe from the crown of your head. If...
The consciousness cannot grasp it. It is like plowing a stony field with an ox made of earth. [The Master] struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Chan Master Ruixin of Jingshan in Runzhou was asked by a monk: "I have a great affliction because I have this body.
Before my parents were born, I do not know where this body was. The Master said: "Throughout vast kalpas, it has had no location. If..."

[The opponent] argued that [the concepts of] arising, ceasing, and extinction were proven to be incorrect. [The Master] said, "If that were so, then although it pervades the ten directions, the mind would not be present in all places.
The Master said, "Shaking a stake in the mud. He ascended the hall and said: "That which is prized in the mundane world are the Jade of He Shi and the Pearl of Lord Sui.
I call the Golden Mountain 'donkey dung and horse manure. That which is prized in the supramundane world are True Suchness and Liberation."
"Bodhi and Nirvana—Jinshan calls these 'a boiling pig in a bowl clinking. Now tell me, when speaking in such a manner, where does it land?
It is not a matter of a mind of grasping or rejecting; it is not about valuing right views or hating heterodox, inverted ones.
Do you all wish to know? A fierce tiger pays no heed to meat on a table; how could a roaring furnace cast the needle within one's bag?
Chan Master Yishu of Yaoshan in Lizhou, successor of Chan Master Qianmingxin, was asked by a monk: "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master said:
"A great tree wrapped in a great bark. The monk asked: "How is it after he appeared in the world? The Master said: "A small tree entwined with a small bark. [Question: "What about suchness..."
"What is the Immovable Honored One? The Master said, "The Four Kings cannot lift him up.
Chan Master Zhimen Zu was a dharma successor of Chan Master Mingzhou Xuedou Chongxian;
he was the son of the Li family of Suining and entered the monastic order under Puan Xian. He received [the precepts].

After completing his studies, he took up the sutras at the lecture hall to investigate principles and exhaust the ultimate source. His interrogations were as swift as whirling blades, and his quick-witted eloquence was peerless;

all recognized him as a vessel of the Dharma and unanimously urged him to travel south. He first visited Zhi-men, whereupon he extended his inquiry, saying, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, how can there be transgression?
Zhi-men called for the Master to come forward. As soon as the Master drew near, Zhi-men struck him across the mouth with his whisk. The Master—
As he was about to open his mouth, the gate struck him again. The Master attained sudden enlightenment. He went forth to reside at Cuifeng.

Later, when he moved to Xuedou and ascended the Dharma seat for the opening of the hall, he looked toward the assembly and said, "If we speak of the fundamental matter, there is no need to ascend the high Dharma seat to meet one another.
He then drew a circle with his hand and said, "Everyone, follow the mountain monk’s hand and look. Immeasurable..."
The lands of all Buddhas appear simultaneously before him; he gazes upon each one with meticulous detail.

Should there be any limits yet unknown, he cannot avoid being mired in the mud and water. Then, he ascends the seat. After the head monk has struck the gavel, a monk steps forward. The Master calls him back, saying:
"The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye of the Tathāgata rests entirely upon this day. To let it go is for tiles and pebbles to emit light; to hold it fast..."
When he took his place, even genuine gold lost its luster. With the authority in his hand, he could kill or give life at will; those who were capable of such action all came forward to testify.
A monk stepped forth and asked, "Having departed from the ancestral seat of Cui Feng, you have now arrived at the Dharma site of Xuedou.

Pray tell, are these one or two? The Master said, "A horse that lacks the thousand-li stride cannot falsely claim to chase the wind. The monk said, "If that is so, then the clouds disperse and every house has its moon."

Yue asked, "Master, you are a man whose head is like a dragon’s but whose tail is like a snake’s. Since the staff and the shout have already been manifested by Deshan and Linji, how do you, Master, benefit people?
The Master said, "I let one move pass. The monk hesitated, and the Master immediately shouted, saying, "I wonder if it is merely thus, or if there is something more?
The Master said, "If one does not truly shoot the tiger, one's efforts are in vain and the arrows are wasted. [The monk] asked about blowing the great Dharma conch and striking...
The Great Dharma Drum: The high officials presided over the assembly. [A monk] asked, "How is it right here? The Master said, "The pure breeze has not ceased its coming.
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then I have met the Master. The Master said, "Once a word has been spoken, even four horses cannot overtake it. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "I let this one matter pass. Then, surveying the entire assembly, he said: "With humans and devas gathered here in such numbers, what matter should we together clarify?
How can it be that the vehicle of our school is simply a matter of alternating roles as host and guest, or racing through questions and answers?

The vast style of our tradition is sovereign in its majestic power, its brilliance illuminating past and present; it holds fast heaven and earth. Even the thousand sages could only say: 'It is known by oneself.'"

Chan Master Hai-lin of Yuehua Mountain in Shaozhou was the son of the Deng family of Duzhu in Qujiang County of that same province.

In his youth, he studied Confucianism, but later turned to the study of Buddhism. He was proud of his poetic talent, yet gradually came to realize his own limitations. He went to visit Baoshou at Dongshan, who recognized his potential and subsequently entrusted him with a great responsibility.
He returned south and built a hermitage at Bailian on the old site of the mountain; followers from the fourfold assembly flocked to him.
His realization was profoundly deep. Later, he retired to the West Hall. When an imperial edict selected men of renowned virtue to reside at Baolin Monastery, he firmly declined.

He then built a brick *śarīra*-stūpa for himself at his hermitage, saying, "I shall return my bones to this place. The site was Mount Yuehua, the location where the monastery of Lang flourished the Dharma.
When the Master arrived and caused great prosperity there, everyone considered him to be the reincarnation of Lang.
